reviews.title: YES, these are made of genuine silk satin, my skin knows the difference
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 24, 2021
reviews.text: I'm not sure why a couple of the top-rated reviews say these pillowcases aren't real silk, and those reviewers didn't explain why they thought that. ?? I think it's possible those people are actually used to polyester microfiber satin, which is often falsely called "silk" these days, and has a more slippery feel than real silk. (Also, most silk pillowcases are sold individually, and the description one these is clear about the price being for one single case only, so if you need a pair, make sure you purchase two!) I am absolutely certain that the Yanibest pillowcase I received is genuine 100% silk; I have very sensitive skin, and silk is the best fabric for it, being made of a protein fiber that's very similar to skin, rather than a non-absorbent plastic fiber like polyester, or a too-absorbent plant fiber like cotton. (Next-best fibers for my skin include bamboo rayon or viscose, Tencel lyocell/eucalyptus lyocell, linen, modal, and rayon and viscose made from other types of wood.) Wearing or lying on silk makes my skin feel so soft and smooth, never too dry or too oily. So I know just by that alone that this pillowcase is real silk. And of course, silk is great for hair care too, as it won't suck the moisture out of your hair the way cotton pillowcases do, and also reduces friction so you get less tangling. For anyone who can't tell that way, you can simply cut a little bit of extra fabric from an inside seam and burn it. Silk, again, is a protein fiber, so when burned it smells like burnt hair and crumbles to ash; polyester will smell like burnt plastic and just melt. The quality is VERY nice for a ~$25 silk pillowcase! Reviewers saying it should be better quality for the price are definitely not used to buying real silk. This is a GREAT price for a real silk pillowcase, especially one made with a nice hidden zipper and a substantial fabric weight. The teal color is also gorgeous - a very rich sea-blue color, exactly what I wanted. Since silk is protein fiber, it requires different, more gentle care than your typical plant or plastic fiber fabrics do. Make sure you use a silk-safe detergent; I use Soak for my smaller handwash silk items, and Woolite Extra Delicates for larger things like bedding that need to go in the washing machine. Never use heat - cold water only, and air-dry only if you put it in the dryer! For pillowcases, I turn them inside out and zip mostly closed, just leaving enough of an opening that I can unzip it again after; then put them in a mesh lingerie bag and wash on the most gentle cycle in cold water, and tumble dry on the air only setting, still inside the lingerie bag, to avoid friction from the sides of the dryer and other items. Don't use any fabric softener, it's not needed and will leave a coating on your silk. You can also line dry or dry flat - the fabric will come out a little stiffer, but will soften up again quickly with use. I love silk fabric so much, and I hope these tips help some of you enjoy your silk more too! I very much recommend these pillowcases, and I'm about to order several more colors.

reviews.title: surprisingly pretty, launders well (will wrinkle), daughter loves it.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 23, 2021
reviews.text: My 6 has hair down to the small of her back so nightly braiding and wrapping is a thing, but sometimes her sleep cap works off since she wrestles sleep every night in a no holds barred cage match. I picked up a silk pillowcase and kicked myself as soon as the order was shipped - oh no!! I could have gotten her a satin one at half the price!! But then the pillowcase arrived and I opened it. This thing is pretty!! I wasn't sold on the flower print, but they'd been out of the color I wanted when I'd placed the order, and since it was for a kid - I didn't too much care about what it looked like. (bad mom, I know) But this print was really pretty and elegant with so much shading and detail. it kind of looks, well, splotchy and not so attractive in the pictures but in person the floral pattern itself is lovely and it has so many colors - peach, mauve, touches of lavender, black, gray, rose and cream. It sounds weird but it's really a soft almost water-color effect of shading that honestly works with just about every quilt and duvet cover we own. Bonus, right? As to the material - couldn't be happier. two washes in, pillowcase still looks nice. It gets chucked into a lingerie bag and washed alongside kid's bed linens then hangs to dry. it came out wrinkled to heck and back, but who cares! I put it over a hanger, took a moment to smooth it out and left it alone, by the time it's back on her pillow most all of the wrinkles are worked out of it. No complaints. The zipper is a nice touch, I don't know how sturdy it will be in time, but I imagine it's a necessity to keep the pillow from slipping out in the night. Sewing seems sturdy and tidy (I appreciate that sort of thing) without any threads hanging or messy serge work and the zipper seems well-set in the material. I liked it enough I ordered a couple extra so she'd have a spare and I'd have one for myself.

reviews.title: More powerful than expected
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 27, 2022
reviews.text: I needed a pair of clippers to body clip my horse this spring that wouldn't break the bank. In the past I've used an old pair of Wahl Stable Pros that are going on 20 years old now. The rotary motor in those clippers is still going strong, but the plastic piece that moves the blades keeps cracking, and getting replacement parts is a challenge. So I bought these Ion clippers, which seemed the closest to my old clippers and use the same blades, the big difference is they are cordless. I couldn't body clip my horse in one sitting with these because the battery only lasts 2-3 hours, but they got the job done over the course of 2 days, and were almost as powerful as the old Stable Pros. Gotta admit I was skeptical on their power, and they exceeded my expectations. Being cordless was a nice feature too, neither me or my horse got all tangled up in a cord for once! They were not as easy to clean (take apart) as the Stable Pros, but since I only plan to use them once a year, that doesn't bother me too much. Overall a good purchase, hopefully they last multiple years like the Stable Pros did.

reviews.title: Like a standard waffle maker
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 30, 2018
reviews.text: Like a standard waffle maker, the Presto Super Waffle Bowl features heated top and bottom sections that are connected by a hinge. But, it also boasts a unique concave shape that allows you to create thick and fluffy four-inch ‘bowls,’ which can be filled with just about anything, including eggs, bacon, syrup and butter, ice cream, or fruit. According to the website, all you have to do is allow the machine to preheat, pour in the batter of your choice (no special batter required), close the lid, and then allow it to bake. Then, when the time comes, its nonstick grids help ensure everything’s easy to remove. If you’re not in the mood for waffles, the Presto Bowl also works with a variety of other foods and ingredients, such as brownie batter, cinnamon roll dough, pizza dough, rice, and bacon—you can even make quesadillas. You have to admit that this concept seems appealing, and if it works exactly as described, that the device could live up to its promises of being easy to use, while making breakfast and other meals more exciting. A Quick Note About Presto Super Waffle Bowl’s Manufacturer In business for more than three decades, Telebrands is far and away the largest As Seen on TV company in the industry, with hundreds of products to their name. Recent examples include California Charcoal, Pocket Hose Brass Bullet, Atomic Beam Glove, and Red Copper Pan. Telebrands held a D+ Better Business Bureau rating, based on more than 320 closed customer complaints, as of 2/16/18. Although a company rep responded with a resolution in each instance, common complaints appeared to revolve around lower product quality than expected, as well as less-than-stellar support experiences. My Bottom Line About the Presto Super Waffle Bowl The Presto Super waffle maker comes to us from a company with decades in business, who offers free S&H and who stands behind the product with a 30-day refund policy (although you’ll be responsible for return shipping charges if you’re dissatisfied with its performance). So, it seems you might not have much to lose by giving the product a try. On top of this, the identical 03500 model seemed to come with almost wholly positive online customer feedback, which could be a good indication you’ll experience much of the same if you choose to hand over your hard-earned money. However, based on what we learned while browsing online marketplaces like Google Shopping, Amazon, and Walmart.com during our research, it appears Telebrands (or more specifically, their Bulbhead division) sells the exact same product at exactly half the price. Even if you wanted to go directly through Presto, their branded version was available for just a few bucks more. So, if the price is your number one factor when purchasing, either of these might represent solid options. But if you're looking for the lowest cost option possible (although certainly much more labor-intensive than using a device like Presto), you can cook seven-inch batter circles in the oven for four to five minutes, remove, drape them over an inverted cup, and allow to cool before filling with the food of your choice and enjoying.

reviews.title: So Cool!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on February 6, 2017
reviews.text: Okay seriously, this thing is AWESOME. I got it in the afternoon and immediately used it to make waffle bowls that night for dinner. And the next morning for breakfast. And then for lunch. And then for dinner. Granted, it was not just plain waffles the whole time. I was experimenting! I used the basic waffle recipe out of the booklet that came in the box, and it turned out perfectly without any cooking spray or complications. I got a beautifully toasty waffle bowl in 3 minutes. Fresh out of the maker, the waffles are fluffy and easy to bend if you want to use them taco style, which is what I did for breakfast with some butter, powdered sugar, and a fresh banana folded in waffley goodness. We also tried filling them with a variety of berries and other fruits (thawed from being frozen in bags) and topped it all off with whipped cream. There are so many good things to try, I don't think you can go too far wrong here. If you like your waffles a little more crispy-crunchy, you can cook them a little longer in the maker, or just let them warm a few minutes in a 200 degree oven while you keep making more. They are still very tasty, but become firmer and unbendable, which I think you would want if you're using softer fillings such as yogurt or ice cream. I also tried other things besides waffle mix. For lunch I made a potato bowl. I tried using both hash browns and tater tots (the frozen bagged ones, microwaved to thaw first), and they both worked. Obviously they take longer to cook, and you have to position the potatoes with more care to make a complete bowl since they won't flow up to the edges like a batter will, but still. Tastiness! You can fill a potato bowl with eggs or just top it off with salt and cheese. For dinner I made cornbread bowls for chili, and they turned out super yummy! The jiffy cornbread mix actually has a recipe on the box for making it waffle style instead of traditional style. Very easy! It was so fun making bowls that I ended up with a few extras in the freezer, so I'll get to see how they are when re-heated. Next up on my list: brownie bowls and cookie bowls! I got this thing mostly for the novelty of it, and I gotta say I'm glad I did. It's been a lot of fun, and a lot of deliciousness the last two days!

reviews.text: I was starting a YouTube channel and wanted to use my Boya M1 Lavalier Mic with my Canon T3i DSLR camera. What I didn't know was that the amount of poles or pins on your 3.5 mm jack matters to what your device can and cannot read. So while my phone read 4 poles, my DSLR could only read 3 (TRRS vs. TRS). As a result, I could never my camera to register my mic. This little adapter fixed that issue perfectly. I just plugged my Lav Mic jack into the adapter and then plugged the adapter into the mic jack on the DSLR. Worked great and I now how good sound. If you have a problem like this, splurge on this $10 adapter, b/c some of the cheaper adapters are terrible. Hope this helps!

reviews.title: Cost saving replacement, installation can be a bear…
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 24, 2021
reviews.text: These housings work very well - they are nearly identical to the factory parts, and that is where the problem lies. Removing the originals was a big problem, as the threaded studs which hold them in place are only press-fit into the plastic of the housing. When I tried to remove the nuts, at least one stud on each started to spin, with no effective way to hold them still. In the end, I had to cut the studs off to get them out. The studs in these new housings are also press-fit, and done very poorly. Gentle pressure on the studs while installing caused multiple studs to fall right out. Eventually I used epoxy to secure all the studs in place, so they would stay during install and hopefully won’t be a problem if I need to ever remove them again. So, a 15 minute job required an hour and a half due to poor engineering. That said, they are cost saving replacements, simply copying the poor design of the original manufacturer. A dab of glue before you crawl under your truck will save you some time and hassle.

When I tried to loosen one of the nuts, the stud started to turn with it. I ended up leaving the nuts on the studs. Then I used the nuts from the factory lights to secure these lamps in place. reviews.text: Update: this case does NOT offer full protection as I had previously thought. Less than a week after I put it on, my phone dropped and the screen completely shattered. I’m very disappointed! I’ve dropped my phone many many times with other cases and never had this issue! This iPhone case with cross body strap is great! I was debating between getting this one or the Bandolier one that costs way more from a department store, but I’m very happy I chose this one. This is actually very comparable to the Bandolier crossbody case. It fit my iPhone 11 perfectly. I ordered the black one and the strap has a trendy gold chain that attaches to a black leather strap and is adjustable in length. The black leather strap sits comfortably on the shoulder, while the gold chain appears half way down and connects to the matching gold loops on the case via large lobster clasps. The clasps attach and detach easily, so on a night out, I can easily remove the strap and slip my phone in my purse. The case itself is very sturdy and offers great protection with bumpers on all sides. Im still able to easily press the volume up/down or power button with ease. It doesn’t get stuck like some other cases I’ve seen. The case is very lightweight and easy to hold. The leather back side has a single card slot with a push button closure, and I’m able to fit my credit card, my ID, and some cash in it so it doubles as a wallet. That’s great for when I need to run a quick errand and don’t want to lug around a big purse. The leather-like material isn’t the best.. i made the mistake of adding too many credit cards, so it stretched out a bit, but it gets the job done. The case itself is not too thick or bulky, yet very sturdy. As a busy mom on the go, this was a great option to have my phone on me and not have to constantly be searching for it.

reviews.title: Very close to perfect....but not perfect.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on June 26, 2011
reviews.text: As usual I searched online before making this purchase like with alot of important items in life that I purchase. And this item is very important! I've heard both the parents' AND plumbers' stories of items "flushed into neverland" by toddlers. So it was on the top of my list to get the right seat lid lock the first time. Just before I began my search, my wife had purchased one of those units that you have to stick with adhesive onto the seat. What happens to the adhesive residue when your kid turns 18 and you finally want to remove it? I'll tell you what happens. You spend the weekend using a chemical to remove that residue that not only harms your plastic seat but also your not-so-plastic nostils! Not for me, thanks! Well, if you feel the way I do about these issues, then this unit is the one for you. The positives? Easy to assemble...including instructions and spacers provided to fit your bowl edge width. With what is provided in the box, it really should fit all toilets. Also, the unit is easily removable so I can take it off on the day the cleaning person (not my wife...we actually have a cleaning person) comes to tidy the bowl. And, when you know how to use it, you can work it at 3am just fine. The negative that made me only give it 4 out of 5 stars? I had to "shim" the flip top portion that rests on the very top of the upper outside of the seat. When I attached it without shimming, the unit would open at will without activating the (un)-lock lever. Hey, maybe it was just my toilets. All three in my house are only about a year old and may be "slimmer" in that area than an older toilet...who knows? But honestly, the shimming was easy. I used that rubber shelf liner. I cut a piece the length and width needed and wrapped it about three or four times around and then used a good tape to secure it and that provided the "tightness" to keep it from opening at will. I really do like this unit. I think I read the unit is rated for children up to 4 years old. When my son figures out how to open it?....we'll move to staight duck tape!

reviews.text: If this fits your toilet, it will work great. Would be nice to have adjustment on top. My seat cover is solid wood, so rather thick and the arm fits snug over the seat cover. A plastic seat cover will likely have more play and could be opened probably up to an inch.

reviews.title: Works great but limited to certain toilets
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 21, 2022
reviews.text: We had one of these for our firstborn and bought another for our second. We moved in the meantime and threw out the original. I know what you are thinking…but saving and then packing a hunk of plastic that hung on the outside of our toilet was not really prioritized in our family nor did I think to keep a toilet lid lock in our family mementos. Anyhow I bought a replacement and it did not fit our Koehler, but if it does fit your toilet it’s much better than the 3M tape top locks or the strap locks…and works especially well if you only have one child.

reviews.title: Works exactly as advertised
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on February 19, 2012
reviews.text: After multiple iPhone dunks in various toilets around our house, as well as cloggings from who knows what (I REALLY don't want to know what was flushed) it was time to go hard core. As always, I read reviews for as many different products as I could find that do the same thing, and settled on buying three of these. The only criticism I saw was addressed by some smart user's suggestion to add some tacky material to the lip of the toilet bowl (like the stuff you line drawers with) if your lock slips (and only one of mine did, due to toilet design). Easily and quickly installed all three locks and waited for the gremlin to appear to see how he would react (and more importantly, if he could open or break it). As I sat watching from behind the door, I heard the pitter-patter of tiny, cloven feet approach the toilet...him thinking no one was around to see his evil dunking deeds. But lo...as the miniature, but amazingly dextrous hands went to open the toilet seat per usual...something held! It worked! IT WORKED! GLORY DAY IT HELD! I observed from the shadows as the expression on the would-be evil doer's face went from devilish grin to complete shock and surprise at this new and unfortunate (for him) development. He fiddled with it for a few seconds, head turned sideways like a puppy dog, with a puzzled look...then I guess it finally sunk it that once again he was being thwarted, and this was by design, so he gave up! YES!! Knocked off one star because this is cheeeeeeeeep plastic people. I'm actually shocked the 15 mo old did not just break it when he pulled on it. Seems like it would have just snapped, but nope. The house iPhones can sleep peacefully now.

reviews.title: Good so far
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on September 28, 2021
reviews.text: It was a bit of a faff to install and the instructions were stapled to the bag of parts, so there was no way to open the bag without ripping the instructions. However, once I got it installed, it certainly looks to be holding the toilet closed securely. The catch to open it is a bit tricky but I think that's a good thing because it should be resistant to even the most determined toddler. So far so good!

reviews.title: Broke the toilet seat- very disappointed
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on February 23, 2022
reviews.text: Initially easy to install and does what it says- the toilet lid is effectively 'locked' which does prevent my 1 year old from throwing all his bath toys/toilet rolls/self in to the toilet pan. However, where the underside sits on top of the toilet pan, it raises the toilet seat fractionally. Despite my husband and I being well within the bounds of a healthy BMI; the toilet seat has cracked from the pressure. Very very disappointed as will now have to fork out for another toilet seat as well as find an alternative method of thwarting my sons favourite toilet fishing games. Broken toilet seat= badly designed product.

reviews.title: It's a good idea, but not brilliant in practice
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on March 14, 2016
reviews.text: It's a good idea, but not brilliant in practice. I was able to secure it fairly easily to the bowl of the toilet, but we have quite a thin lid and needed to stick some thick padding to the top to make it fit the toilet seat, otherwise it could still be lifted quite a bit. My 16 month old was also able to open the lock with a quick wrench on the seat. We still have the lock fitted and we do use it at bath time when it prevents casual lifting and has made the toilet far less interesting as a result. But to be honest it's not a great fit for our loo and hasn't been terribly necessary. Update: We gave up on this after a couple of weeks. It's too easy to open by wrenching the toilet seat - perhaps because it doesn't fit our toilet brilliantly but I don't think it would be all that secure in any case. In the end, the minimal benefit if provided in keeping the lid shut wasn't worth the hassle of cleaning it and opening it when we wanted to use the toilet. I wouldn't recommend it for kids, but perhaps it would be helpful for people with thirsty dogs...

reviews.title: Incredibly useless, don't waste your time.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on January 28, 2018
reviews.text: This is sadly as useless as everyone else states it is. I ignored the reviews because we have a thick resin seat so thought it would fit. Not only does it fall off because it is really big and baggy but it can easily be taken off by a 3 year old. I'm baffled as to what toilet this was made for....maybe the giant at the top of the beanstalk as the size toilet that this clip has been designed for???

reviews.title: Good idea, will work best with a thick lid and toilet rim
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on July 31, 2021
reviews.text: Firstly the good part. This comes with extra parts to adjust to the thickness of the rim of your toilet. Ours had a bit too much movement around the rim of our toilet and didn't quite hold the lid down enough...no fault of product, our seat and lid was a budget fitting and unusually thin. Sadly it broke within a week.

reviews.title: Set Up Problems
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 31, 2022
reviews.text: The product comes with a fancy, colorful brochure, the brochure was weak about useful installation tips and instruction (normally I would not even need to reference an instruction manual). As an example, it came with a bag of bolts/screws for installation including two long, interesting/unusual "expansion screws" for which I could not figure out what they are for (Note: I have purchased and installed countless # of solar light systems). It also was not clear whether I could install the solar panel flat against a wall surface (for air circulation) vs. having to use the pre-installed installation bracket which creates about 6 inches of space behind the solar panel. I also experience multiple issues with only 1 of the lamps. Despite 2 days of full sun panel charging, 1 lamp keeps flashing red lights (which is indication of an error) and would only light up when I completely un plug the lamp from the solar panel. If I unplug the lamp from the solar panel, the lamp would stay fully lit for hours. The other lamp works well when connected to the solar panel. I also tried the USB cables to help troubleshoot, but still have issue. I wrote to the company twice across a 6 day period, using the company email that was provided in the brochure. Still no response to help troubleshoot the one lamp.

reviews.text: I really like this solar light! It’s made of durable black medal, not plastic, and has a tempered glass covering the light. The lights are very, very bright! That means that suppose you want put a spot light on your special tree or illuminate your house, you have two lamps to position the way that you want. I use mine in my back yard as security lights. It comes with a remote, but I use the dusk to dawn feature. However, you have to have the remote to turn the unit on. I can see clearly what’s going on in my back yard. reviews.title: Started out great, but........
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on May 6, 2020
reviews.text: Got the lights charged them up and tested in a dark basement, lit very well and all functions on the remote worked flawlessly. Set up the lights outside turned them on and remote stopped working, changed batteries tapped on the remote could not make adjustments or turn off lights, Finally after about 45 min I could get one of the lights to be controlled by the remote but the other light is stuck on. Overall I was happy with the product, but this remote issue needs to be fixed or the product will be returned. I can only rate this product a 3 star but will adjust if the company steps up and fixes this remote issue. EDIT: I am happy to say I have found the issue, you need to be in front of the lights for the remote to work properly all the time, yes it does sometimes work from the side or behind but not always and this was my issue. Now that I am aware I just wanted to update, and will also update my rating to 5 star. Will probably buy another set sometime in the near future.

Responsible for attaching the wheel to the car, a wheel hub assembly is a pre-assembled unit that features precision bearings, seals and sensors. Also called a wheel hub bearing, hub assembly, wheel hub unit or hub and bearing assembly, the wheel hub assembly keeps your wheel attached to your vehicle and allows the wheels to freely turn enabling you to safely steer. The wheel hub assembly is also critical to your anti-lock braking system (ABS) and the traction control system (TCS). Besides bearings, it contains the wheel speed sensor that controls your vehicle’s ABS braking system and traction control system. ABNORMAL NOISES Excessive inner or outer tire wear is a sign that there could be something wrong with your tie rods ends. STEERING WHEEL VIBRATION A damaged tie rod end can cause the front end to come out of alignment and handle poorly. ILLUMINATED ABS LIGHT A loose tie rod end can cause vibration or looseness in the steering wheel which can worsen during acceleration or turns. POTHOLE DAMAGE Abnormal noises like squealing while turning corners or clunking from the front end can be an indication of a damaged tie rod end. Read more

reviews.text: After reading the reviews, and seeing the prices of some of the other laptop portable desks there was no way I was going to spend a lot of money on something that (1) I didn't know how long I would really be using it, (2) Weighed more than a desk and (3) cost more than $30 dollars. So.. it fits my 14.5 Lenovo Ideapad with room to spare. Heavy duty plastic top, with 2 deep wells, which will not hold my Android. Appear to be made to hold smaller items (paper clips, small pen),. There are 2 cushions underneath which are covered with a soft material which is filled with what feels like small round foam balls. It sits comfortably on bare legs. Haven't had it long so I can't really attest to durability/longevity, but again it serves its purpose at an affordable price.

reviews.title: Not ideal for a laptop or being moved around during use
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 7, 2022
reviews.text: I spent some time looking through the options of a lapdesk for my new MBP I'd bought. I already have a simple rectangular board that has a sliding mouse tray, but it tends to cut into my legs when sitting the way i do (not the way most people would be sitting). It was also not really safe to have the tray component out while on my lap, so I decided to look at lapdesks with the cushion bottom as that should keep it elevated and stable. The one feature that made me get this one over others was that it purports to have a lip designed to keep your item from sliding towards you. So it said. While that is true, even with the thin bottom half, my MBP slid right over it! Now, the lip alone wasn't the reason the Mac moved, however. the Reason it moved is because the plastic shell of this thing is too slick for simple rubber feet. This, unfortunately, was not something one could know/test without having the item in hand. This combination issue (especially the risk of the laptop falling backwards onto the ground!) let to a quick decision to return an otherwise nicely designed item. The feel of it is good all the way around and if you're reading a book, then perhaps this is better for you than a laptop. IDK how a tablet would fair, but if it's not any taller than the lip, then it may fare well. That lip is probably a half inch thick at most, but no less than a third of an inch. I wanted to like it as the surface area was good, but it's just not worth the risk for my use.

But the other issue is the smaller bits are made of two pieces, the bit and the hex shank that fits in your impact drill. reviews.title: “And if you gaze long enough into an abyss, the abyss will gaze back into you."-Nietzsche
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 16, 2015
reviews.text: Universal digs into the vaults and bring us ten films that immerse us into a world of alienation, despair, cynicism, disillusionment, melancholy, desperation, pessimism, paranoia, moral corruption and ambiguity. The Film Noir 10 Movie Spotlight Collection gives us a nice mix of major classics of the genre (Double Indemnity, Touch of Evil, Criss Cross, and The Killers), minor classics (This Gun For Hire, The Blue Dahlia, and Phantom Lady), and lesser but very good noir films (The Glass Key, Black Angel, and The Big Clock). The ten movies are spread across six single-sided dvds and packaged in a standard size dvd keepcase. The keepcase has two double-sided hinged trays inside the case for the dvds (no spindles). My copy also had a cardboard slipcover over the case. The outer case is not clear so here is a a breakdown of the disc contents: Disc One: 01 This Gun For Hire (1942) is based on the Graham Greene novel ‘A Gun For Sale’ and stars the classic screen duo of Alan Ladd and Veronica Lake in their first of seven pairings. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks relatively clean. There are specks of dust here and there but nothing that distracts me from the film. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: A trailer for the film. 02 The Glass Key (1942) is not the 1935 original with George Raft. This remake is based on the novel of the same name by Dashiell Hammett and again stars Alan Ladd and Veronica Lake in their second pairing. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks relatively clean. There are specks of dust here and there but nothing that distracts me from the film. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: None Disc Two: 03 Double Indemnity (1944) is one of the very best films of the film noir genre. I personally rank it second to only The Maltese Falcon. The film is based on James M. Cain’s novella of the same name and stars Barbara Stanwyck and Fred MacMurray. Be on the look out for Edward G. Robinson in one of his best roles as a supporting actor. It is amazing to think all three actors were originally not interested in appearing in the film. They all needed to be persuaded to appear in film that turned out to be one of their greatest performances. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks great. Audio: There are English and Spanish Dolby Digital 2.0 mono tracks. They are clear sounding and I have no complaints. Subtitles: English SDH, Spanish, and French Extras: This film has a bunch of goodies… * Audio Commentary by Film Historian Richard Schickel. * Audio Commentary by Film Historians Lems Dobbs and Nick Redman. * A 2 ½ minute introduction by film historian and host of Turner Classic Movies, Robert Osborne. * Shadows and Suspense: An excellent 38 minute documentary about the film. * A trailer for the film. Disc Three: 04 Phantom Lady (1944) is based on the Cornell Woolrich novel of the same name. He written the novel under the pseudonym William Irish. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and is the worse looking in this set. All of the other films are relatively clean looking but this one is loaded with dust specks and scratches. Some of the scenes are not that bad and others are very dirty and look horrible. I’m guessing parts of the film may have been damaged beyond the point of restoration or Universal forgot to clean up this one. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: None 05 The Blue Dahlia (1946) stars Alan Ladd and Veronica Lake in their fifth pairing (the third and final on this set). Be on the lookout for Hugh Beaumont (Leave It To Beaver) in a supporting role. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks relatively clean. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: None Disc Four: 06 Black Angel (1946) is based on the Cornell Woolrich novel of the same name. Be on the lookout for the great Peter Lorre as Marko the nightclub owner. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks relatively clean. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: A trailer for the film. 07 The Killers (1946) is partly based on Ernest Hemingway’s short story of the same name and stars Burt Lancaster (his film debut), Ava Gardner, and Edmond O’Brien. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks relatively clean. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: A trailer for the film. Disc Five: 08 The Big Clock (1948) is an adaptation of the Kenneth Fearing novel of the same name and stars Ray Milland, Maureen O'Sullivan, and the incredible Charles Laughton. Be on the watch for Elsa ' The Bride of Frankenstein' Lanchester. Video: The movie is presented in a solid 1:33 full frame transfer. The film is in black & white and looks relatively clean. Audio: The only audio track is English Dolby Digital 2.0 mono. It is clear sounding and I have no complaints Subtitles: English SDH Extras: None 09 Criss Cross (1949) is probably my second favorite film in this set and easily ranks in my film noir top ten. reviews.title: STYLISH COLLECTION OF FILM NOIRS
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 5, 2015
reviews.text: A superb collection of "film noirs", five from Universal and an equal number from Paramount and apart from the 1958 "Touch of Evil", all made in the classic and appropriately black and white era of the forties. Probably only a few outright classics ("Double Indemnity", "The Killers" and "Touch of Evil") but all wonderfully well made and intriguing from beginning to end. Billy Wilder's "Double Indemnity", one of the all time greats and the Orson Welles more recently reconstructed and rediscovered gem "Touch of Evil" both get a single disc while the other eight films are scattered across the other four, two to a disc. These two are the only ones with significant extras and they are substantial with "Indemnity" containing three audio commentaries and a first rate 40 minute documentary. Two separate commentaries accompany "Evil" with one featuring the stars Charlton Heston and Janet Leigh and there a couple of short "making of" featurettes. All the films in this collection are stacked with interest, fascination and excitement and they all range from better than good to excellent. They all contain the fine Hollywood craftsmanship of the time, move with style and pace and have storylines which will have you engrossed throughout. From the stunning debut and early film career of Alan Ladd (matched with the intriguing Veronica Lake) in "This Gun For Hire", "The Glass Key" and "The Blue Dahlia" to the powerful screen presence of Burt Lancaster in "The Killers" (an astonishing debut performance opposite Ava Gardner) and "Criss Cross", these films won't disappoint. The two Lancaster films were directed by one of the best, if not the best, film noir directors Robert Siodmak, and he is also represented by the 1944 gem "Phantom Lady". This was the real discovery for me: a fantastic thriller with an excellent Ella Raines and with a limited budget, just marvel at the way Siodmak has created it with such marvellous, inventive and stylish filmmaking. And the unforgettable scene where Elisha Cook Jr. reaches an orgasmic fury during a drum solo is priceless! To round out this collection, Ray Milland does battle with a couple of newspaper tycoons (the sticky, slimy Charles Laughton and George Macready) in the complicated but fascinating "The Big Clock" with Elsa Lanchester as an eccentric painter stealing every scene she's in. And Roy William Neill getting a break from all those Universal Sherlock Holmes programmers, with "Black Angel", beautifully made with a fine performance from Dan Duryea in one of his more sympathetic roles. An appreciation of fine filmmaking during the studio factory years with not only fine directors and actors but terrific writers (eg Raymond Chandler, W.R. Burnett, Albert Maltz, Jonathan Latimer, Anthony Veiller), outstanding cinematographers (eg John F. Seitz, Russell Metty, Franz Planer) and great music composers (eg Miklos Rozsa, Victor Young, Henry Mancini) all in collaboration to create top of the list movies for art and entertainment.

reviews.title: COULD NOT POSSIBLY BE BETTER
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 2, 2019
reviews.text: LOOOOOOOOOVE THIS WATCH. FINALLY, a women's watch that isn't the equivalent of wearing an Instant Pot on your arm. This one is so petite, but it doesn't look like a kid's watch. Why has this been such a difficult feat for manufacturers? The best watch I've ever owned was a digital Armitron I think in the '80s. It was small, very low profile (even lower than this one), and had all the digital functions. When it finally died, they had long since stopped making it. I went with Timex after that, and haven't been happy with most of their stuff. BIG is NOT okay! Their smaller watches were expensive and fragile (bands ripped apart easily), and the last one perpetually slipped around my arm so that I could no longer see it. Took two hands to see the time. My little Armitron here came without instructions, which I knew going in. (I bought an open box to save a few bucks). There are YouTube videos that explain everything you need to know and which may be helpful for visual people like myself. It's not hard to figure out, but it is just different enough from Timex to throw you off a little here and there. HOURLY CHIME: I love the optional hourly chime. Helps me keep track of my day better. (Hit MODE button once to get to the alarm, then hit the upper right button until you see a little bell). STOPWATCH: I use the stopwatch every day when I run, and LOVE that it doesn't have laps! (Update: I think it actually does have laps). You can pause the stopwatch using the top right button, OR pause it (to check your time) while keeping it running in the background using the top left button. Hit the top left button again to get back to the active stopwatch. TIME ZONE/24HR: Love the second time zone and optional 24-hour clock for us nurses out there (hit the top left button to switch back and forth). Love everything about this watch. Even though it's small, it doesn't look like a kid's watch. It's too classy for that. Oh, and love all the wonderful colors it comes in. I got "pink/rose gold," but I definitely wouldn't call the band pink. It's more like a very faint peach, and the rose gold is beautiful. That's for more dressy occasions. Also got navy for everyday wear, and purple for fun. I'll keep ordering new colors as they release them. Thank you, Armitron! Don't ever stop selling this watch, and don't change it in any way! It's PERFECT. UPDATE 2-22-22: Still wear these watches 24/7. I inherited 18 very nice watches from my mother, and have only worn one of them once. This one is just that good. I change a lot of watch batteries (by no means an expert tho), and this one is more of a challenge than most. There are four tiny screws to open the back--which is great, much easier than popping the back off--and two even tinier screws to remove a metal frame over the battery. Once replaced, you have to short circuit the connection to get it going. It takes CR1616 batteries, which are inexpensive. I wear my purple watch a ton, and constantly change modes and use the light, so the battery lasted me a little less than 2 years. The two I purchased in fall of 2019 are still going strong. (It is now Feb 2022). I'm about to add a black one to my collection.

I didn't know what size wire I should go with before hand. I considered 12 Gauge, 14 Gauge, 16 Gauge and 18 Gauge. reviews.title: Well-made leather phone holster but magnet-closure is a fai l & sizing overstated
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 5, 2019
reviews.text: This thing is well-made and looks really nice. Leather this thin appears impossible so I'm guessing they've skimmed the surface off leather & backed it with PU or textile. It should hold up for a year or two: acceptable for the price. But only for a naked phone. And that's a shame, cause it does look nice. Sizing: the Amazon listing claims it will hold a Samsung S8+ in a case. Not a chance. Maybe the slimmest of silicone sleeves, but that's it & unlikely. In an Otterbox or equivalent the flap won't close. Closure fail: if the flap did close, it wouldn't stay closed. The magnet closure is a joke: any fridge magnet is stronger than this. The cost is so low I haven't the heart to return it: shipping costs more. I'll try bending a crease in the front flap & see if I can glue on velcro. That might make it usable. It's too bad because it's a nice-looking holster & there are times when I'm in pants that won't accommodate the phone, which is admittedly large. It needs to ride on my belt then in a holster. But there's no way I'm carrying a computer this expensive around without a protective case, and anyone making a holster for a device worth more than $500 should expect that they'll want that kind of protection. They aren't going to carry a naked phone. Suggestions: if you're going to claim you've made room for a phone with a case on, please provide photographic proof of that, so we know what we're buying. And for goodness sake, don't provide magnetic closures unless you're prepared to do it right. By way of example, pick up an Otterbox case & see how a real magnet closure works. An inexpensive product that doesn't work isn't cheap: it's useless. Spend the money for proper rare-earth magnets, charge a bit more & sell something you can be proud of. In future I know this manufacturer can make a pretty product. I won't expect it will necessarily be useful, & I'll be leery of purchasing from them again.

reviews.title: I would also find out which I liked better for future reference
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 17, 2016
reviews.text: I picked up an iPhone7 to replace a flip phone I had for many years. For the flip phone, I had used a Canon camera case that had a belt loop to contain the phone. I wanted a similar type of pouch for my new iPhone. After looking through the many options on Amazon, I decided to get two different ones, the one from Kingsource and "De-Bin," one for each of the two pairs of pants that I alternate. I would also find out which I liked better for future reference. This review is for the Kingsource. There are lots to like about this holder. It appears to be real leather and smells like it. The lining appears to be leather, too. The sewing is really good. The biggest drawback is that the material is extremely thin, about the thickness of two pieces of paper. Unfortunately, the belt loop and belt clip are only attached to the leather. I saw one review that said this construction caused his holder to fall off after a short use. I would not be surprised. Between the exterior and the liner is some sort of backing. To prevent a sudden loss of my phone, I drilled a hole through the material and threaded a thick string through. A clip (from a badge holder) was added to the other end to be clipped to a belt loop. Then if the holder suddenly separates from the belt clip, I would notice something dangling from my belt loop. I would not hesitate to buy another one after this one wears out. But I just wish the outside material is thicker, maybe twice to three time. I would be willing to pay quite a bit more. Then it would have the quality of my Canon camera cases. Many people pay much more for a phone case that just goes around the phone itself than what this Kingsource holder costs. The manufacturer can also solve this potential longevity issue very simply with little extra cost. Then they can sell it to us for just a minor increase. First, use thicker material for the belt loop and clip. Second, sew the belt loop and clip all the way through to the lining. Then the loop attachment would be across three layers of material, with almost no danger of failure. Now, if only Amazon can notify the manufacturer of the suggested design change ...........

reviews.text: I have a black protective case which I had to slightly modify on the left side by using a file. It needs to fit flush against the side of the laptop. So depending on what kind of protective case you have, you might need to make sure that it allows for the ENTIRE length of the device to fit flush against the Macbook. That being said, its space grey, matches the laptop which is amazing. It uses 2 USB ports, but has 2 USB-C ports, an HDMI out cable that works great on my 4k TV. It has 2 USB 3.1 ports, a memory card reader and a micro card reader as well so you don't need an adaptor for the mini ones that are the typical ones used today that have a 256GB or higher space. It was $99 when I purchased it, which was in my opinion pricey because of the other models available. That being said you get what you pay for. This is a GREAT product, looks sleek and was made for the MacBook Pro. I have the 2016 13" MacBook Pro with the touch bar, basically the best you could buy in the early summer of 2017. Soon after a new upgrade was released but the differences were only slight. I was so in love with my new MacBook and at how easily it was to port around and how quiet it was that I wanted to only put the best of the best on it. This is the best adaptor for the laptop. With USB-C on the macbooks you only get 4 ports, 2 on each side, so this totally takes up an entire side. Since the power cord is USB-C I was curious if you could charge only on one side (the right side but nope, left or right, you can simply plug in the device and then plug in the power cable to one of the two USB-C ports on the device. I have plugged in 2 USB 3.1 hubs and connected about 8 devices all through this hub and all worked perfectly. The HDMI out supporting 4k was pretty surprising. Now granted I have a mid level 4k TV, used a new HDMI cable but just for some reason expected a 1080p resolution but was surprised that it was 4k resolution, making the text on icons super easy to read. I could use my 65" TV as an extended monitor no problem. Though, I really don't but its pretty good if you want to play video. I use plex and I also use Apple TV (currently the 4 that doesn't support 4k), so its nice to plug in directly and get higher resolution as the apple TV is limited to 1080p and most programs can't transcode video from one format into 1080p in real time so they are usually 720p so the sake of your CPU. I use Stream2Me and Air Play HD on my apple TV along with Plex on my apple TV and the comparison between airplay is completely noticeable with the HDMI being much clearer. Even using 3rd party applications like Air Parrot 2, having a great wireless ac network, that covers my whole house, sometimes it's just easier to plugin an HDMI cable. I have used the HDMI out at several conferences and meetings and the fact that the HDMI input is located on the top makes it much easier. So nothing but good things to say about this. I would mention the issue with the cases and it needing to be flush. I will attach pictures showing what I mean.

reviews.title: Alligator clip review. Strong springs!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on May 10, 2020
reviews.text: Alligator clips review I picked these up to make test leads and power jumpers. Some of these: I had to flatten the rivet so they didnt fall apart, some of the jaws were out of alignment, some have gaps in the teeth that make it hard to hold tiny wires. Soldering these. I had no issue with this, but I felt some type of residue and dripped them in flux. I had a lot of slag on the iron and on top of the solder so I know this helped. The ones with screws... some of the screws were stripped out and short of the little tabs, I would not bother trying to crimp these at the metal at that end is rather thin. I'm not sure what size these actually are. The imagery shows metric but I checked charts for AWG to metric and my wire was always to large to fit through the solder hole. I soldered them inside by the spring. I put flux on everything, wet the clip with solder, wet the wire with solder, then used the tabs to hold the wire. I then put on a seperate clip to hold down the wire and act as a heat sink. I used .032 solder to start filling in the gap, then moved to the bigger solder so I could fill things in before melting anything. I used these clips as heat sinks but they do not work that well for that. I've used others in the past that did. They will fill my needs, but they aren't the greatest.

reviews.text: This is my 2nd countertop ice maker. My 1st one was a different brand, no longer available. This unit is a little smaller in size but that was a plus in my consideration when I needed a new one! Another plus is this one has a self cleaning function which is appreciated. The directions stated I didn't have to use distilled water but due to the excessive hardness & minerals in my area, I only use distilled water in my icemaker. This machine when turned on quickly gets to work producing ice! Those are the good things! The rest of my review are the items that are not deal-breakers but don't fit my needs as well as my 1st machine. This water reservoir is a little small as is the basket holding the formed ice. We live in the South so iced beverages are necessary! The filled basket only fills, maybe, 3/4 glasses. Of course then it begins to quickly make more. The base of machine is not chilled so ice begins melting as soon as it is dumped. This is a big drawback for me as our other machine, while not a true freezer either, kept the ice nearly frozen for hours. The noise. Both machines have been noisier than expected! Lots of clunking sounds as ice is shifted into basket. Lots of other random noise which have guests questioning what is happening in my kitchen!! I will definitely keep a countertop ice maker in our home. Would be easy to use in a camper. So, I like the smaller footprint 👣 but don't like the smaller reservoir or basket. reviews.title: Was great while it worked - but it is unrepairable
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 7, 2022
reviews.text: Ice makers in freezers are a catastrophe, I've never had one work reliably. A relative got a countertop one and raved about it, so we tried it out. It was pretty good. It was relatively quiet. During the freezing portion, I didn't notice any noise unless I was standing right there. When the ice was frozen and dumped into the bucket, it obviously made noise as the ice dropped onto the other ice and the water refilled, but that was like 30 seconds every 90 minutes or so. The capacity to make ice was pretty good. At the time, we had season tickets to the local AHL team and tailgated a lot, plus hosting a bunch of BBQs at the house. We do have a chest freezer available, so we'd make ice continuously for a day or two beforehand and bag it and put it in the chest freezer and it made plenty to put in the coolers. I'd say if anything, the listed production is a little low. The bin is a bit on the small side for such large capacity. I mean, it doesn't freeze things any faster, it just makes more, so I'd get home from work, and get 3 or 4 loads in before letting it go overnight and it would be full and just refreezing the melted ice. The weekends we'd run it all day long and have plenty of ice available for the week. In that respect, the water capacity and the ice capacity were pretty well matched. For about a year, it was great. Our problem came with the sensor that stops making ice when the bin is full. It is just a little metal knob sticking out the side near the top of the bin, presumably attached to a thermocouple or other sensor inside. It would trigger kind of randomly, regardless of how much ice there was. It got worse over time, so that if it had any ice at all, it would trigger so that when the current batch of ice was done, it wouldn't refill the water and start the next batch. So, rather than having to empty the bin every 6 hours or so, every 90 minutes I'd have to walk over and pinch the metal knob between my thumb and middle finger for a couple of seconds to get the next batch to go. I tried a bunch of things to alleviate it, like wrapping it with some wiring to add more bulk and make it less sensitive, or wrapping the knob with a few twists of wire and hanging the other end out of the machine into the kitchen air or eventually trying a glass of water at room temp. None of that worked. I eventually took it apart to see what else I could do, and just tossed it. The problem is there are almost no screws - the insulated part where the ice bin sits is molded in and not removable. Removing screws and prying apart the case, the entire interior between the case and the ice/water is filled with insulation, it looks like expanding foam. I still ranked if 3 stars because it was great and maybe we just got a bad sensor or maybe someone else in the house damaged it somehow (not sure how, it still seemed solid, and due to the foam there isn't really any place it could move). If it were really meant to last a year, I'd put it at 1 star, but I could have just gotten unlucky.

reviews.title: Good for karate and weaving
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 6, 2022
reviews.text: I bought these for a wildly disconnected pair of purposes. One, to use to do four dent weaving on a ridged heddle loom. Two, for a stick to use for bojitsu practice indoors in the winter. It works for both. For weaving, it is sturdy enough to support 32 inches of stitches across the length of the loom lifted together for a weaving pattern. For here, strength was a primary concern. If it was prone to bowing or warping it would not have worked for the purposes as the warp threads would have been lifted unevenly or unreliably. I used cotton as a tie to the threads and it worked without a hitch. High marks for strength. For bojitsu, smoothness was a main concern. I needed to be able to slide my hand along it from position to position. I knew it would not be long enough for some things, and that was an intended trade-off for being able to work in a smaller space. I did need to be able to switch grips however, and that requires smooth wood and that I can do with this. Hi marks for even, smooth wood. If you are concerned about fiber catching, don't be. So, thus far these have worked for both purposes to which I set them, odd as those purposes may be. I can say these look great, no signs of damage, splitting, or trouble on the wood at all. I can say, if I wanted to use them for something like a banner, I would not hesitate. They’re quality.

reviews.title: an abundance of frustration; a story
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on February 11, 2021
reviews.text: I was hopeful this would be the beginning of many repeat purchases & was excited (albeit skeptical) to find this item at such a reasonable price. I was initially thrilled, less $$$ than my previous brand & tasted good: Heck Yeah! Sadly, my excitement was short-lived. I quickly came to realize the pods are flawed. The majority of the time the pods basically explode in the Keurig. Hot water is released into the pod but doesn't stream coffee into the cup. As a result, the pod fills with hot water until it erupts from the foil top. A maddening, hot mess! Allow me to tell a little story. Don't judge me. After a typical 4.5 hours of restless sleep, I'm jolted awake by the relentless shriek of the alarm. Hit the snooze button 4 times until begrudgingly I drag my achy, exhausted self out of bed. Shuffle across the bedroom floor having the previous days mascara smeared down my cheek. I'm forced to acknowledge my snooze button addiction has (again) cost me the breezy morning I envisioned & I regretfully submit myself to my situation. The stark reality is that I have under 28 minutes to get myself in appropriate condition to face yet another day of hell, oops I mean another hectic day. Anyhow... outside, 4 a.m. & still dark. I'm standing in my robe, being pelted with a mixture of snow & painful little ice balls. I wait (at least11 minutes) for my Prima-Donna K-9 to find the absolute best place to have "a poopie". After the spoiled furball gets her treat (she successfully did a poopie) I'm smiling to myself as that precious 1st cup of coffee of the day calls to me like an old friend. The dog is smugly chomping her peanut butter biscuit & I set my lucky coffee cup on the Keurig. A sideways glance from the four-legged mutt & I know she knows. The thing I'm anticipating will be much better than that dry, stale peanut butter morsel she's already devoured. She looks at me with jealous eyes, saddened by the fact that she has no thumbs & cannot possibly partake in this cup of rejuvenation I'm preparing. Setting my coffee pod in place, I deliberately dismiss the fact that only 14 minutes remain before I must begin the journey to my expectant but, paying master . In this moment I realize I am thankful for my thumbs & remain blissful. I push the "brew" button....... Let me tell you, in this moment, hell hath no fury like that of a woman whos coffee pod explodes. My sad tale continues to this very day. Regularly now, I ask myself; will my morning, (thus my entire day) be doomed at the hands of another faulty coffee pod? I am forced to contemplate how badly I need my job. Perhaps I should say heck with it all and go back to bed?! Will I be forced to face the day without any life-fuel at all? Can I endure yet another mocking stare from my drooling companion, as she happily licks the remnants of peanut buttery deliciousness from her mouth while I glare at my empty (not-so-lucky) cup? I haphazardly wipe coffee grounds from the entire surface of my kitchen while cursing these blasted inexpensive, large quantity, off-brand coffee pods. I tell myself I absolutely will not experience another morning such as this. But I do. So many mornings. I made this purchase obviously, because I am frugal. Spending 46 bucks for 18 pods is insanity! With this purchase, I thought I'd discovered the secret to mortal happiness; 120 pods for under $30! But they have become the bane of my existence! Considering my aforementioned frugality, I cannot simply walk away from this, I have entered into a 120 pod commitment! A sane woman would toss this nightmare in the garbage & return to her previous state of contentment while casually sipping her (not-exploded) expensive cup of joe. But, as you might have guessed I am not quite a sane woman. So I continue what has become the morning disaster, with approximately 108 more to go until I might shout "good riddance!" to this seemingly endless supply of cruel pods. However, if I must confess a silver lining, it is that on the rare occasions that the pod maintains its' integrity and provides me with the expected, perfect cup of coffee, I am momentarily stunned into quiet appreciation for the little things. Smiling as I take a sip, I burn my tongue and start cussing. Life is hard.

reviews.text: Update: included a pic so you can see wht I did with these. It has been very windy but they have stayed up and from the street look pretty okay. Update: I went over the 'seam' between the four pieces with clear tape to keep them steady during wind and rain. They seem pretty durable. I will try to put up some pics of the window that I used these on, making a 'pane' out of four. ... I used these to create a barrier between the screen of a window on a patio of a neighboring house and the inside. The glass had been knocked out so I used four of these for each window. reviews.title: Good quality, but I didn't pay attention to the thickness

reviews.text: These are some really nice sheets of plastic! They came well packaged, and I feel like you can tell they're pretty good quality. However, I did a dumb and wasn't paying attention to their stated thickness (I was needing something that was closer to a quarter inch thick); so these weren't 100% what I was looking for. But they will definitely make good acrylic sheets for some other project! The one thing I did find in experimenting with these was that if you try to cut them with scissors (probably just a dumb thing to do in general, but like, live and learn), they might shatter just a little bit. Not the whole piece, but some chunks of it. I had better luck with an exacto knife, going over the lines I wanted to cut out a few times. So, the moral of the story is that these are good quality acrylic sheets, but they're rather thin, so be aware of which ones you're buying; and if you need to cut them at all, try a really sharp blade before you resort to the scissors. reviews.title: semi-pro car code reader for home mechanics and even proffessional mechanics
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on August 19, 2021
reviews.text: I own a OBD USB interface cable which requires a computer and software - this works but the free software is difficult to find and not very reliable or feature rich. The all in one cheaper code readers only read your main ECU codes (i.e. they won't read things like ABS and transmission codes etc. So I decided to spend a bit more and a better all in one unit, and having used this for some time now, I'm so glad I did. This won't be for everyone as it is a lot more expensive than a simple code reader, but it does provide a lot more. It's an android based, touch screen unit. In general use, you plug it into the car, and it will then probably auto recognise your vehicle then auto scan it and generate a report for you. The unit stores a history of reports, so no need to try remembering what the previous code where if you fixed something then cleared them all down. As it's android based, you can connect it to Wifi (I use home wifi and sometime my phone as a hotspot), which allows to enter an email address which emails a link to a cloud hosted report - professional enough for sending to customers for trade mechanics. You can click a code on the unit to trigger an internet search for more details, but the unit does have pre-loaded description of most codes (i.e. for any codes found, you get the code and a brief description). It's super simple to use, you don't need to study the user guide as the android mobile phone like interface is very intuititve. The only minor negative is that scanning all the different systems takes a couple of minutes so isn't super fast. As a home mechanic, I'm not sure if that's just because the OBDII system takes this long to work through scanning all the different areas, or this unit itself is a little slow. However it's definitly not painfully slow. At a guess, I suspect the time required is because this unit is able to scan all the subsystems of the car where the cheaper units only scan the main ECU codes.

reviews.title: Top quality in the $10 and under range
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on September 3, 2020
reviews.text: I decided to write this review after spending hours agonizing over which notebook to get for my first bullet journal, to help others who may be doing the same. EDIT TO UPDATE: [I liked this notebook so much that I quickly burned through the first one and just ordered a second. I've updated my review with some info I forgot to share the first time, along with info from my extensive pen tests.] My Minimalism Art 120gsm dotted journal just arrived and though I was nervous about the purchase based on some of the negative reviews, I'm very pleased with the notebook. 😊 Mine has none of the defective issues others experienced. Some key points: * The cover is textured, which should resist fingerprints. I bought the red, which is a beautiful cool-red color. * The notebook arrives shrink wrapped, so there's no chance of scuffs or marks during transportation. * The hard cover is stiff enough that I can write on my lap or a soft surface without needing to put a clipboard behind it. * The binding of the notebook is indeed stitched, not glued. This is obvious on the first Index page and the center spread. (Note: Based on a prior review I looked up instructions for how to properly break in a hard cover book, and did that when it first arrived. So hopefully I won't have the same issues with pages coming loose that some others noted. I will update this review if I do in the future.) * The margins are nearly exactly the same on every page (I did a flip-through), with a variance of about 1/16". I find this totally acceptable and wouldn't have even noticed had I not been looking for it. * The dots correctly align across left-right spreads throughout the book. I checked at least 20 spreads and did a flip-through. * The first and last pages are blank, which make for a nice custom title page and a pen test page. (I'm waiting for my fineliner pens and brush markers to arrive from Blick, so I can't do a pen test yet. I'll update this review if I experience any ghosting or bleeding. That is the most important issue for me and why I purchased the Minimalism Art notebook with 120gsm paper instead of the popular Moleskine (60gsm) or Leuchtturm (80gsm) brands.) * The dots are easily visible -- for reference they're about a 50% greyscale color. (The dots are a bit dark for my personal preference -- I prefer closer to 30% -- but I don't find them distracting. And the page numbers would probably be difficult to read if the ink was that light.) * The page numbers are easy to read and are the same color as the dots. The numbering starts on the first page *after* the Index, so you truly have 122 pages of writing space. Note: There is some inconsistency in the placement of the page number in the allotted margin space, but again this probably isn't something I would have noticed if I hadn't been looking for it. And honestly, for the inexpensive price I don't care about this. * The index is 2 pages long, with room for 60 total line items. Most people will probably find this suitable for 122 pages of content. (That is a bit small for my use, so will be extending the index to fill one more page. I personally don't find it inconvenient to have to draw some lines on a page to make an index. I bought a rolling ruler for hand lettering, so that should make the task easy. Others may find that task irritating if they need a longer index.) * The two bookmarks are made of grosgrain ribbon (textured) instead of satin ribbon (smooth). I personally prefer this, as the grosgrain is more sturdy and I find it holds its position better when marking on the diagonal. Note: Because of the shrinkwrap the ribbons do arrive crimped where the bottom of the notebook ends. I think this would be the case with any new bookmarked notebook. (I easily ironed the ribbons straight. It took less than 2 minutes). * The elastic band is firm without being too tight. One nice thing about the packaging is that the notebook comes with the elastic band fastened around the back cover, not the front. So the notebook doesn't arrive with any indentation made on the front cover from the strap, like some others do. EDIT: [* The notebook does lay flat, but it takes a bit of coaxing on some spreads. Given the low price (I've seen journals upwards of $30), I find this acceptable. ] [* The paper color is a nice soft ivory, not a creamy yellow. It appears to be white until you put a white paper next to it.] [* The expandable pocket is easy to use and feels securely attached. I even fit rolls of washi tape in there, though doing so means the book has to be fastened with the elastic band to stay closed.] [*Note: The only drawback I can see is that notebook does not have a pen loop. Personally I'm fine with that and keep all my pens in a pouch anyway. But for some that may be a deal breaker.] So all in all I'm rating this a 5-star notebook. It is definitely top quality in the $10 and under price range. (If I later find there are bleeding or ghosting issues (EDIT: see below), or binding problems, I'll change the rating accordingly.) EDIT TO UPDATE: *A word on pens, bleed thru and ghosting: When just writing, I had no trouble with bleed through with anything except cheap dollar store alcohol markers, which bled completely through and onto the page behind it. Sharpie brand markers were fine. When actually coloring with pens, doing a full saturation test (going over the same area 3-4 times), the Sharpies bled through and there was some minor ghosting with the following: -- dark colors of water-based Tombow Dual Brush pens -- dark colors of Zebra Mildliner pens -- dark colors of Sakura Moonlight Fine Point pens -- dark colors of Staedtler Triplus Fineliner pens -- Staedtler Pigment Liner micron pens (but Sakura Pigma micron pens did *not* ghost) A word on gel pens: -- For some reason this paper does not like Sakura Gelly Roll pens. While Gelly Rolls typically write smoothly on loose leaf paper, they skipped and dragged on this notebook paper. However, Sakura Moonlight pens write smoothly (different formulation). -- Papermate Ink Joy gel pens are just that: a joy to write with on this paper, the smoothest of all the brands I tried. -- Uniball Signo was also smooth writing. -- Pilot G-2 0.7 skipped and dragged sometimes. So after using the Minimalism Art 120gsm dotted journal as a bullet journal everyday for the past month, my 5-star rating still stands. And the price can't be beat.

reviews.title: Good Enough, Could Be Better
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 1, 2022
reviews.text: I looked at a few bag hangers and this seemed to be a good option. I knew that I'd need to make a mount for it so it'd have a solid connection to the studs in my wall. I made an 18"x30", 1.5" thick plywood board and secured this mount to it using 3/8" bolts. The board is then secured to the studs in the wall with (6) 4" structural screws. The connections are solid and I don't think it's going anywhere as the ratings are way above a 130lb bag. With that being said, I did a lot of work on my end to make this mount viable. On top of that, it came wrapped in a weird, green fabric and only one provided screw. The rest must have fallen put of the box during shipping because the box was beat up. I think the seller likely mass produces these in China and then ships a bulk box to Amazon and they box them individually. Packing is terrible. As another reviewer said, the arm on the mount does flex a bit when the bags in use. Not a lot, but you can see it if you look at it. I find this as an added benefit because that means less stress on my studs in the wall. Not worried about it, but it might help over time. Do NOT buy this if you're expecting to open the box and mount it on your wall. It might not come with all of the screws, which are crap anyways and the studs in your wall are likely 24" apart so you'll need a wooden board like I used to secure it. It's an affordable option that can be made to work. It does look very clean on the wall as well and that's what I was looking for.

We had to use plenty of Teflon tape on the threaded male nipples going into the housing so it would not leak. We had it all hooked up, and then it started dripping. reviews.title: Used for high iron content well
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on February 4, 2021
reviews.text: I installed this on my well which I use for irrigation. We are in an area with a high iron content, so whatever the water hits gets discolored. I also got a 20k gallon pool and used the well to fill it once it was placed in the ground. The filter helped with discolored water, but it wasn't perfect. The pool guys said it made a difference in the water, but I still shouldn't drink the water. The filter is pretty dark and dirty after running 20k gallons through it, so it at least helped out a good amount. The housing is easy to install, as long as you know a little about installing plumbing pipe. The hardest part is screwing on the blue part with the filter inside - it is not light. Not easy to spin on yourself, it took me a few tries to get the threads to seat properly. A second set of hands would make it simple, but not required. I did have to dig a hole and put a bucket in the ground for my setup, it was easier than redoing more of the PVC and keeps the setup a little lower for when I finally cover it during the winter. The problem with this is I can't use the tool provided to tighten or loosen the housing. Oh well. Overall, I sure hope this helps in the long run. I will definitely be replacing the filter before summer (pool in December) when the sprinklers start up again.

reviews.title: Great Quality Overall
