reviews.title: Must read!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 18, 2021
reviews.text: The media could not be loaded. I ordered this for value and testing purposes. I have a bar and a bunch of freeloader friends that never pay for my beer. So, I took out the beer tap and replaced it with a Fruit Punch tap. I use this pump, hooked up to a fuse and an ON/OFF switch (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED) This pump uses air line pressure to turn on. Simple - When I open my tap to get my fruit punch (I mix Poland spring water with 16 packages of mix in a gutted out 7.75 gallon keg) the pump detects a loss of pressure in the line and turn on. This set up is a similar setup in RV's and Boats on a 12volt system. This pump I ordered with the correct voltage and amps, and I have an inline fuse then the shut off switch. It is installed inside my kegerator and mounted to the wall. The reason for the on/off switch is my thoughts is that if a line pops under pressure I wont have fruit punch everywhere if it OFF. Trust me on this. I ordered this in June, and over the course of 4 months using a rubber 3/8 water line, the slight pressure made a bubble on the side closest to the pump exit, so I am using a braided hose.. That works great now. Peace of mind. Fast forward to today. 9 months later. The pump for some reason is staying on. (See Video) and it is getting hot with just a minute of use. It is inside a cold fridge, there is no way this should be so hot to the touch like it is. There are no air leaks in the lines or you would see red fruit punch everywhere (there is some frozen as you can see form the old hose mishap) so why is it staying on? Its a good thing I installed the off switch. Now I need to see about a replacement or warranty. In the video I have the switch on, pouring fruit punch into a jug, then I stop the tap and you can hear the tone of the pump change, but it still stays on even though I have the tap off. UPDATE: Pump just stopped working.. I got about 1 year and a half out of it.. I turn the power switch on and I can hear a faint humming when on. When I turn it off the hum stops.

reviews.title: Easy to use, flexible, light color makes it almost unnoticeable
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 5, 2022
reviews.text: I live in a 25+ year old house with original wooden sash windows. The windows have pretty significant air leaks where the top portion and bottom portion meet. Unfortunately, I used some clear tape to better seal it and then had to remove it when my house got painted (peeling off a lot of window paint in the process!). I have used a similar product to this in the past but it was gray and I could never find the off-white in the big box home improvement stores. This caulking cord fit my needs perfectly. The color almost matches the window trim so it is almost completely unnoticeable. It is easy to use and manipulate - simply cut the lenth you need and then determine the width you need. The product is slightly over 1” wide and consists of 6 ‘strips’ that can be separated by simply pulling them apart. You can use 1 strip width or up to 6 strip width (and any where in between). For my needs I used 2 strip widths in order to ensure proper sealing. It makes a HUGE difference in drafts (pretty much eliminated all draftiness completely). It is easy to remove wthout taking pain off the window. I did 11 windows on the first floor and used only about 1/3 of the roll. Fortunately the windows upstairs don’t have nearly the draftiness as the downstairs windows, but I can easily do ALL the windows in my house and have some leftover. $16 to pretty much eliminate draftiness is a bargain and I have no doubt that I will save way more than that in energy costs this winter… plus the color makes it almost unnoticeable which I love. Hope this is helpful info!

reviews.title: Great concept..not as great implementation
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on May 7, 2021
reviews.text: I had to give this a solid 2 star review. The fact that it did actually stick to the wall and it did functionally cover a gap, prevented me from going any lower. Unfortunately I had high expectations on this product, and maybe that was part of the problem. It's pretty embarrassing, but I'm horrible at caulking around objects and trim. This was like the answer to all my problems! A ray of sunshine on an otherwise stormy covid day. I don't know what I was thinking when I ordered this product.... That I was going to be able to unroll this thing around a toilet with ease? That I could bead it along the edge of the bathtub where it meets the floor and it would be perfectly symmetrical and stand out just like a pro did it? In my minds eye, I could see my wife looking at my work with trembling lips and her eyes would start tearing up in joy. I would be a hero! I immediately ordered this thing and went to bed dreaming of puppies. When the item arrived, I was a little disappointed that the color wasn't as white as I'd hoped. Not that I mind the darker caulk you understand, it's just that the brightness would pair with the porcelain in the bathroom better than an off-white color (see pic). This was far from a deal breaker though. I could make this work! So when I tried to unwind the very first strip, I found that it was kind of hard to unravel. It was sticking to itself. Being the handy guy that I am, I whipped out my razor knife and helped it out a little---which turned out to be more than a little. It turned out to be just about the whole thing. In order for this thing to work efficiently, you would not only have to be able to unravel it without sticking, but you would need to be very careful and not stretch it either. If you stretch it, then it would be similar to using a gun and beading the caulk while applying different pressure. Not much more to say on this (at least without crying). Maybe the shipping caused it to stick and meld together, but whatever the reason, I was never able to pull off more than a foot and by the time I got that section off, it was not the same size from end to end. It was stretched out in places. I spent more time to separate this thing from itself than I thought it was worth. This might be fine for outdoor stuff- like around your shed or under window sills, but if you value your marriage don't bring it into the house :(

reviews.text: I got all my He-Man stuff back in 1982. With that in mind, I think this is a really good Greyskull for those of you who want the one you had as a kid, but don't want to splash out for an antique one. It has all the old play features, elevator, trap door, locking jawbridge, turret gun, flag, weapons, windlass, and even the original stickers to put inside. The sculpt is good. The plastic is really tough. Vintage figures fit in there just like I was back in 1982. Awesome! The one place this falls down is that the paint application is almost not there at all. There is like no significant paint on this thing anywhere. Even the vintage one, which was just spray painted, managed to catch some of the angles of the stone and make the castle look spooky. This new one is very flat. The included image (with the 2 castles) shows what I am talking about. The castle on the left has an awesome paint app. Lots of weathering and atmosphere added here. The one on the right, the new one, is just flat looking. I wound up modding mine to enhance the texture. The second image (with 1 castle) is the one I painted. Be prepared to either DIY your own paint job or just get it for the great sculpt and play features.

reviews.title: Billig Produktion von Mattel
reviews.date: Reviewed in Germany on June 23, 2021
reviews.text: Ich kann die ganzen positiven Rezessionen zu dem Castle Grayskull aus der Origins Line von Mattel überhaupt nicht nachvollziehen. Kommen wir zuerst zu den wenigen positiven Punkten. Verpackung ist super, sieht gut aus. Amazon verschickt im Mattel Umkarton und hingestellt sieht es ganz okay aus, aber neben 200x und Vintage Grayskull keine Augenweide und das liegt an folgenden Punkten. Die beigelegte Temple of Darkness Sorceress ist in Sachen Billigkeit, aus Kunststoff gefertigt, nicht zu überbieten. Die Gelenke sind eine Katastrophe und dann liegt die auch noch lose in der Verpackung, kein Blister, keine Karte, einfach nichts. Wie bei Lego, hat man hier auch Leute gefunden bei Mattel, die genau sehen wo man sparen kann, um auch den letzten Cent rauszupressen. Das Castle an sich, sieht ganz okay ist von außen, das Material und die Innenansicht ist eher für 3 jährige geeignet. Mir ist bewusst das wir hier nicht über Sammelfiguren und Zubehör von Super 7 sprechen, sondern um Figuren von der Stange, aber den Wegwerf Kunststoff für 70-90€ an den Mann zu bringen, find ich hart. Gegenüber dem 200x Castle Grayskull hat man sämtliche Sound Effekte eingespart, es gibt nichts an Effekten oder Licht. Ganz klarer Rückschritt zum Mattel Vorgänger. Gegenüber dem Vintage Castle Grayskull ist die Optik und gesamte Qualität eine Katastrophe und wir sprechen hier über Qualität von vor 30 Jahren, die das heutige Modell nicht erreicht. Bei dem Plastik der 200x Version hat man schon ordentlich gespart, aber selbst das war noch richtiges Hartplastik, wenn auch an den Seiten reichlich dünn. Aber bei weitem besser, als dieser Weichplastik Mist. Die ganze Innen Deko sieht aus wie ein Spielset für 3 jährige und fühlt sich auch so an. Kann man über die Figuren und Fahrzeuge der Origins Line bis jetzt die Qualität angesichts des Preises noch weglächeln, kann ich mir bei UVP 89,99€ nichts schön reden. Lieber das Vintage Grayskull oder 200x kaufen. Das Vintage Grayskull hat die wesentlich bessere Optik und Qualität und das 200x Grayskull die wesentlich bessere Bespielbarkeit, dank der vielen Effekte. Ich hab mir als Horde Fan nochmal eine Fright Zone in meinem Leben gewünscht, aber gemessen an der Qualität die uns Mattel im 21. Jh. präsentiert, kann ich darauf gerne Verzichten und die Vintage Fright Zone muss ohne Freund auskommen. Preis-Leistungsverhältnis katastrophal für den Kunden und Gewinnorientiert topp für den Hersteller. Zum Verschenken an Kinder durchaus geeignet, wenn man bereit ist das Geld in die Hand zu nehmen. Die Qualität ist erbärmlich, die Haltbarkeit gut und die Optik vom Karton super.

reviews.title: Flimsy but suction is pretty good. Chimney too short for 9ft ceiling. Find another! LEDs dimmed out!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 1, 2021
reviews.text: Allocate about THREE HOURS to remove the sticky film used to protect the thin stainless steel. VERY time consuming to remove. NOT worth the hassle. Additionally, it HIDES any small dents in the metal which will become obvious after removing the film! The finish is terribly easy to smudge, so don't touch it! Flimsy, but suction is pretty good. Chimney too short for 9ft ceiling unless 3ft above stove is OK where someone 5ft tall won't be able to reach it. 22gauge sheet metal is TOO thin for this range hood. It hangs on the wall warped. Suction is good but pretty noisy on high. The LED lights are inadequate and only good for use as a night light! In addition, there is no diffuser so the LED light reflects off of cookware and back into the eyes. The LEDs create two spots on the stove and do not spread light over the stove surface to properly illuminate it. UPDATE: The control panel buttons have a VERY loud beep that send my dog running. No way to turn off annoying beeps! Here's the fix: Under the cover of the black control box on the control circuit board can be seen the noisy piezo buzzer. Take a 4mm screw and run it into the hole in the piezo. That will pop the cover and break off the piezo element; voila! Took unit off the wall and many of the screws holding it together are loose as a goose; causes parts to RATTLE. In addition, hood is assembled using pop rivets which have a tendency to work loose! The control box was loose and missing a screw. UPDATE: After only a few months, the LEDs that are SUPPOSED to light up the stove, but were pretty weak to begin with, are just about burned out and give off as much light as a night light; NOT GOOD. UPDATE AGAIN: Here is what you need for the LEDs; Armacost Lighting 223411 LED Puck Light, Bright White. Theses are almost a perfect fit and easy to wire in place of originals; VERY bright and 100 times better than original trash. Use the mounting ride on the inside of the rangehood so the two pieces of the Armacost light puck "clamp" in the original LED's mounting hole. In light of this discovery, I have upgraded to THREE stars. No higher because of the "issues" I had to deal with; hate that protective plastic crud!

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 21, 2015
reviews.text: I read, with enthusiasm, the mostly rave reviews of this Regenerist Instant Fix Wrinkle and Pore Vanisher. I am 50 years old and, although I take good care of my skin and it has held up well, I have fine lines around my mouth and some on my forehead that I would like to see vanish. I tried a pricey product called Wrinkle Relax or something similar and it was flaky and awful. I was hoping that this product would at least blur the lines so they weren't so visible. Unfortunately, I am one of the few that didn't get great results from this product. It is thick and off white. You are supposed to apply your usual moisturizer first and let it absorb, then apply a small amount of this product directly onto the lines or pores that you want to fill. The consistency is like spackle which seems like it would be a great filler. I used it on the lines around my mouth and really didn't see much difference. Then, it started to flake and crust and looked like I was peeling. I washed my face and started over. Maybe I was using too much of the product. I again applied it to the lines, very sparingly with a slight tapping motion. I didn't rub it around or use a heavy hand. But I still got white residue showing up. I found that the best way for me to apply this product was after my primer which is silicone based. While my face is still a bit damp from the primer, I apply a tiny amount to the lines. It does nothing at all for my deeper forehead lines but slightly fills in the lines around my mouth. If I apply after my primer, I get much less flaking and residue although I still get some. I don't know if I am doing something wrong or if I am just too far gone to be able to use a product like this and get the good results others have had. It does fill in very fine lines a little bit and, once I found the best way to apply it, the flaking was minimal but I won't repurchase this product. I wish I could add my review to the many glowing ones here but, for me, this just didn't work out well. I will continue experimenting with different ways of using it to see if I find a more effective way to apply the product. If I do, I will update and rerate. For me, this is average at best. You may have terrific results like many others so I can't recommend that you don't at least try it.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on September 25, 2019
reviews.text: My previous desk was a hand-me-down from my brother and I’m pretty sure that thing was from the late ‘80s. As old as it was, it lasted me for over a decade and a half, but my new computer tower was just too big for it. I needed something cheap and small (with enough space on a lower shelf for the new tower) and this fit the bill. It shipped and arrived fairly quickly. When I pulled the pieces out, I was worried at how thin and light the panels felt. Some pieces were already installed like the tacks and dowels because I bought it used-like new. So, it only took me about twenty minutes to assemble before I was ready to flip it over and install the top shelf. Luckily, it felt much more sturdy once fully assembled. My only main concern was, the top shelf holes didn’t completely line up with the two back boards. I assume this is why it was returned ‘used-like new’ by the previous buyer. The person probably got nearly done assembling and then found the dowels and cam screw only lined up on one side. I was too cheap and lazy to send it back, so I just drilled new holes and it fit together fine and feels pretty sturdy. It’s definitely not a desk I’ll be climbing under in the event of an earthquake (not that I’d fit; the footwell is childsize,) but it does the job and fits in the space I need it to.

reviews.title: Solid build, clean finish, keeps towels warm and dry
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on September 6, 2019
reviews.text: We installed this about six months ago during a bathroom remodel. We have it set up on a timer (Century FD60) to run from 8pm-2am so that towels are warm before the evening shower, and then have some time to bake dry afterwards. The finish is a nice brushed stainless steel over the whole item, and the welds and joints look clean and smooth. The switch is covered with a flexible rubber cover to keep water and dust out. We installed it so that the left-side mounts are screwed into a stud while the right side uses wall anchors. This gives a nice solid attachment. The mounting is done by fastening four solid little SS flanges to the wall with a screw in each, and then the rack's legs slip down over those and attach to a tapered part of the flange with a set screw. Easiest method is probably to put the flanges into the legs and hold the unit against the wall so that the legs are centered over the stud or whatever you want the screw to go into. Then lightly pencil a circle around each leg at the wall. This will tell you where to drill and mount the attachment points so that they line up perfectly with the rack. They state that it's thermostatically controlled to 149F, something I've not measured but seems about right. (I'm guessing this is in open air.) It's uncomfortably hot to the touch but doesn't seem hot enough to cause a burn from brief contact, at least for an adult. The metal temp under a towel feels a bit hotter than the parts open to the air, which makes sense and is something to watch out for. Obviously they're trying to strike a balance between making a hot towel and creating a burn hazard. Overall we are happy with this product.

I like to keep my face brushes in the middle (as this compartment is slightly larger across (2.4") and I keep my eye brushes, fan brush, and concealer brush on either side (about 2" each at the widest point).

reviews.title: First Impressions...
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada 🇨🇦 on June 22, 2021
reviews.text: 1 - Is this real "Crazy Horse" leather: YES it is! thin leather but it is real, none of the PU b.s. 2 - Is the craftmanship on par with other leather brand names: No, it looks like some underpaid kid made the item in a rush... 3 - Does the manufacturer knows about this? Yes, according to their Costumer service: The imperfections on stitching , forming, etc. are due to "the employee's and inspectors' carelessness." 4 - What's up with the dark burned square on the inside / outside of the product? According to their Costumer service: They use HOT aluminum molds to shape the leather. However, that does not answer why the heck is there a burned square on the leather. There should be NO marks on the leather if the forming was done correctly. 5 - Does it fit correctly? Well, that is a mix bag of "hahas and hehes" it depends on the LEVEL of "the employee's and inspectors' carelessness." as put by the CS rep. My case is a little crooked and the USB port hole doesn't look correct... 6 - Does "white hand cream" cleans leather? As much as this page states to use " white hand cream ", you should be using leather cleaner NOT " white hand cream. " 7 - Does "facial oil" work on leather? Well, by now this seems like another bag of B.S. (if you've read the above recommendations by the manufacturer / seller ) You should NEVER use "facial oil" on leather. What you want to use is "Neatsfoot oil" or "Mink oil." 8 - Would you recommend this case as a gift for someone? NO, since QC and QA is not guaranteed... 9 - Does it come in a box? NO, mine came in a opened plastic bag with a different brand on the bag... 10 - What is "Contact's Family"? Not sure, but it seems to be plastered all over every product that "Hiram" sells. So, it might be a second brand and not some leftover material which was not saleable at the time... It is pretty weird to be expecting a "Hiram" product and when you open your package out comes a bag with a "Contact's Family" as the logo brand. Almost as if someone at Amazon has played a joke on you... 11 - Does it come with a "belt loop" as the info says? Nope, this case is too small for a 2 inch belt loop... BUT there is a tiny metal clip... 12 - Overall, impressions: This case is an "OK" product, just "ok"... If you got it for $10 - $15 then that is just about right, anything over that, you are better spending a little more money on something else that will have good QC/QA and won't have "the employee's and inspectors' carelessness." as part of the excuse... However, their CS assured me that 99% of their products are "good quality..." That still leave the 1% of "NOT FINE" products that are still sold... UPDATE: I had to return it... This case would leave blue dye on the Airpods case... I'll be looking for something better!

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on July 13, 2022
reviews.text: My daughter suffers with SAS short anagen syndrome where her hair is missing the smooth outer layer and also lacks a decent root meaning it is prone to falling out in clumps and easily breaks. As a consequence it also knots very easily and it’s a vicious cycle to get her to brush her hair. She won’t brush it because it’s knotty and it hurts. But it’s knotty and it hurts because she won’t brush it. I figured this brush, being Disney Princess, would perhaps persuade her. There are less bristles, they are very fine and very flexible with a very small end tip. We wash her hair once a week with a small amount of shampoo, then use conditioner, then use the L’Oreal 8 second miracle water, wash it it out. Follow with My Little Coco spray and curly custard and this brush literally glides through her hair. Not a single knot. We’ve found a routine that works and her hair is in brilliant condition. For any other parents with short anagen syndrome kids, I really empathise with you. Stick with it, keep trialling products and find what works for you. This brush had been brilliant for us but the down side is that she now wants more of the Disney Princess brushes.

reviews.title: Best pressure cooker there is.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 3, 2021
reviews.text: I previously had an instant pot, but absolutely hated it's lame interface. Neither my wife, nor my best friend could make sense of it's stupid controls. Then, one day, after plugging it in, it just went "Pop!" and smoke started coming out from the vents. Into the trash it went. I decided to give the Chef iQ a try, and bought it this past January. It's worked wonderfully, those gh the app has crashed in the middle of a recipe once (out of maybe 30-40 recipes cooked), and though after restarting the app, and it seeing the cooker was running that recipe, I was unable to resume it, without starting over from scratch, which was a nuisance, but I just stepped through it to catch up with the step it crashed at, and continued with no further issues. Aside from that one issue, this cooker has worked flawlessly. I'll come back to the app, and some of it's weaknesses/shortcomings , but first I want to address what a couple reviews mustated. First, to the user, Jude, who assumed the company is in china, and the device is full of spychips. The company, called RJ Brands, LLC, is located in Mahwah, New Jersey. Last time I checked, New Jersey isn't in China. Correct me I'm wrong (eye roll). The Chef iQ is designed in the US, and merely outsourced to China for manufacturing, as are the vast majority of products made the past couple decades. It's simply impractical to manufacture in the US these days due to the extremely high cost of US labor. Then there is the sheer absurdity of spying on your cooking habits. Some people drink way too much of the idiotic conspiracy cool-aid. They also have a VERY concise and clear privacy policy, so before jumping to absurd conclusions, do some research. Next, in regards to the overheat message. I have seen this a couple times, but I never had to add any extra liquid. I merely stirred well, and resumed. The error did not reappear. Simple. However, if the error were to reappear multiple times after STIRRING well AND adding liquid, the unit may simply be malfunctioning. Call their customer service. I have called a couple times with questions, and to find out about purchasing an extra inner pot and inquire about lids. They were super helpful, and pointed me to their website, which does offer these items for sale, but the "accessories" link is not in the nav menu, rather on the bottle m of each page in small print, where I just missed it. Oops. Not the best website design, but hardly the worst either. Now, back to the app. It's not perfect and lacks what I personally consider a key function: ability to create and save your own custom recipes. It also doesn't let you easily modify recipes. As an example, I love baked beans, and there is a good recipe for them, bit it is designed around canned, not dried beans. I prefer to use dried beans, which take a total of about 40 minutes at pressure to cook, with 20 minutes to parboil the beans, then saute the bacon, maple syrup, brown sugar, etc., then re-add the beans and continue pressure cooking another 20 minutes. Its just a minor nuisance to have to parboil the beans, then run the recipe, changing the cooking time from 3 to 20 minutes, but doing so made some of the best baked beans I've ever had, and didn't take 12 hours like it would if I cooked them the old fashioned way. Another quibble of mine is that you can't modify the number of servings in a recipe. I'd also love a more intelligent shopping list feature, but as it is, it's sufficient. If they address these minor quibbles, I'd give the Chef iQ 5 stars. I will say this though. I intend to buy another one this Christmas to cook more complex recipes side by side, instead of in stages, swapping out the inner pots as I do currently.

reviews.title: UPDATE: FANTASTIC REEL and OUTSTANDING COMPANY; HIGHLY RECOMMEND BOTH.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 12, 2015
reviews.text: UPDATE: 8/12/15 I want to post an update about this reel and about the company standing behind their product. My original review and the rating (1 Star) was about only the reel. I would like to make the point that this updated review is about the reel AND the company and I give both of them the 5 Star Rating. First and foremost, I want to let you know that the issue with my first reel and it being "DANGEROUS" has been completely resolved by the company. Megan Miller with Liberty Garden Products contacted me soon after my first review posted (see the comment on my review) and helped solve the problem right away. Megan acknowledged there was an issue with the reel and explained that someone at their factory changed the design, without authorization, and they didn't find out until the complaints started. Liberty Garden immediately stopped production and returned to the approved design. Furthermore, I want to applaud Liberty Garden for stepping up right away to the issue with customers and taking full responsibility for solving it. There are still good companies around and I believe Liberty Garden to be one of those. Speaking of the design, as soon as I received the replacement part, I knew the problem was solved. It's really kind of hard to explain, but if you look at the pictures I posted originally, you can see the bolt was stripped. The reason is that basically the bolt was enduring the entire weight of the hose, reel, handle and reel frame. The bolt was underneath the rotation knob (if you look at the company photo) and the motion of the reel caused friction and action on the bolt itself. NOW, the bolt is on top and there is a solid steel shaft that connects the reel portion to the wall mounted portion and the bolt does not endure any friction. I hope you're not confused, but I've have completely dismantled this reel and the approved design works nicely and I complete faith that it will hold up for its intended purpose. Lastly, I only have one issue with the reel now and to be honest, it really is not an issue with me at all. However, other reviewers have noted that the reel does not hold 125' of hose, as claimed in the product description. The truth is that it will hold the 125' but it really depends on the hose you use. And in all fairness to Liberty Garden Products, an average hose fits just fine. In fact, the hose I have is a heavy duty, very thick, 100' hose and it fits, but barely. In my original review I was thinking my hose was only 75', but since I had to change the reel I decided to measure my hose and it is actually 100' hose. The point is that marketing is marketing and we have to be fair on both sides and I think Liberty Garden Products is being fair in their claim of 125' hose fitting on the reel. If you're going to try to put 125' of some indestructible, super-thick never-kink hose on this reel, it isn't going to fit; and I believe it isn't fair to complain about that. My hose is 100', but it is also a heavy duty, thick hose and I have no complaints about it barely fitting. In conclusion, I give this reel the 5 Stars because I do love it. It really is awesome to just point the reel where I need the hose and almost effortlessly unroll 100' of hose. The action is smooth both ways, rolling and unrolling the hose. And while I am more concerned about functionality, this reel looks really nice on the side of the house. The reel is now sturdy and I can fully recommend it. INITIAL REVIEW BELOW AND MY ISSUE DETAILED HAS BEEN COMPLETELY RESOLVED BY LIBERTY GARDEN PRODUCTS: I would still advise anyone who has this reel to be sure and tighten up the bolts on your reel and pay close attention when you roll up the reel. If it is excessively wobbly when you reel it in, you probably have one of the defective units. It should NOT wobble much at all when reeling it in. This hose reel was nice for the two months that it lasted; but, this thing is junk. First, it does NOT hold 100' ft of ANY sort of "garden" hose. Secondly, if you put 75' of 5/8 hose, it will fill the reel to capacity. That might be ok if the substructure of the reel could hold up, but it won't. Those of you who have heavy hoses on this reel need to be very careful. At some point, this unit WILL FAIL because of a serious design flaw. For those of you who have mentioned this reel is "wobbly", you should be especially careful, because this thing might take off your toes or break your foot when it falls. See my attached pictures: What you see is the SINGLE and ONLY support for the entire weight of your hose, reel and handle that attaches to the other piece of this unit. Depending on this size of hose you have, that could be 40 pounds or more. Look at the manufacturer pictures... See the black knob on top, which is directly above the section that holds your hose? Directly under that knob, hidden underneath (I believe intentionally), is the piece you see in my photos. If you own this unit, you will have a hard time seeing this thing without taking the whole unit apart. You have to completely dismantle this thing to see how it's designed, but, this bolt you see in my pictures is the ONLY weight-bearing support you have for the reel and hose! The bolt you see is an 8mm bolt and is LESS THAN 1cm long; it is made from a VERY cheap, soft alloy. If you look close at the picture you can see that the bolt is completely stripped and is basically smooth. This is from only two months use. The reel came detached from the support and nearly hit my foot; and I was in flip flops... It's not IF this thing will fail on you, it's only a matter of time, when this thing will fail. And this is where Amazon sucks. This unit was bought from Amazon LLC...and they do not stand behind the products they sell. 30 days is a joke. I've been a Prime Member for several years and I believe Amazon should have a better return policy, and especially if they discover they are selling a dangerous and flawed product that is certain to injure someone at some point. I am pretty quick on my feet, but if an older person or a youngster gets themselves under this thing when it falls, they could be seriously injured!

reviews.title: Time and space-saver. Excellent customer service.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 13, 2018
reviews.text: I bought two of these. I love them. Re: Functionality: I was tired of having to hand-wrap my 75 ft hoses onto wall-mounted hose racks. I also tried one of those plastic containers, with a reel in side, that sit on the ground. It was unstable and wobbly and difficult to get enough torque to pull in a long, heave hose. These options were such a pain that I often just left my hoses sitting in the yard. The Liberty Garden Hose Reel changed all that. It is sturdy and functional. The reel swivels, allowing me to angle it in the direction that I'm going. I can quickly and easily crank the handle and reel in my 75 ft hose. Re: Defective Item and Customer Service: One of my reels was defective. The pin that slips into one of four holes, allowing you to angle the hose, would slip out of the hole I placed it in, with any movement. (Other reviewers indicate they've had the same issue.) In other words, as I was trying to crank in the hose, the pin would slip out, and the reel would swing back and forth. Cranking the handle was not an option. I basically had to turn the reel, using both hands--one on each side--to get the reel in. You can imagine I had no patience for that. The hose sat in the yard, unwound. Now, the defective reel was over a year old. It had sat, boxed in the basement. It went to the back of the house, and it took a year until I got around to installing it. So when I discovered it was defective, I thought I would have a problem getting it replaced. My Amazon return window had, obviously, ended. So I contacted Liberty Garden directly. I sent them a short video that showed the dysfunctional reel. Their response was immediate. They never mentioned anything about the warranty expiring, or not having a receipt. They said they had a fix, and sent me a replacement part. When I received it, I was disappointed. The part, I knew, was not going to fix anything. It was not a pin, and it was not a new piece containing the holes, into which the pin went. They sent me a replacement sleeve, into which a bolt went that held the reel hanger to the wall mount. (If you don't have the reel, you probably don't know what I'm talking about.) Anyway, I changed out the sleeves. It, obviously, did not work. I took another short video, and emailed it to Liberty Garden with a message that their "fix" was ineffective. They--without any question--said they would sent me a new wall mount (which contains both a pin and new holes--everything being one unit). They shipped it right away, I changed out the mounts, and now it works like a charm. In sum, customer service was great. The only issue was that they could have sent me a replacement mount in the first place. Re: Rust and finish: Some reviewers complain (excessively) about rust. The reel is powder coated, which is a very durable paint. However, where the pieces of the unit are welded or pieced together, you will get a bit of rust. It just happens. I assume the powder coating cannot fully cover all of the crevices and nooks and crannies, especially in these welded areas. Just spray some oil or WD-40 in these areas before setting outside so that the oil gets in their, covers any exposed steel, and prevents oxidation. Also put oil on the sides of the reel before you slip it into the sleeve of the reel mount. The connection is tight, and you (like me) might scratch some of the paint off. A little gear or mineral oil smooths the insertion. I think Liberty Garden actually recommends spraying the entire unit with a clear sealant. I thought about that, but was afraid that this sealant would, over the years, begin to peel or crack, making the unit look worse than a bit of rust at the welded points. The paint does dull, especially in direct sun. Everything eventually succumbs to UV rays. Perhaps a sealant with UV protection would help. I rubbed a bit of mineral oil on the item, and it shined right back up. It eventually gets dull again, however. Just the nature of something outside, in the elements. Re: Wobbling: Some reviewers complain about the reel wobbling when reeling hose in. There is a slight wobble, but nothing to worth whining about. Just make sure the allen screws and their lock nuts (that attach reel to hose mount) are really tight. This eliminates most of the wobbling. Re: Hose length the reel can hold: Liberty Garden claims the reel can accommodate 125 ft of 5/8" hose. No way in hell. I have 75 ft of a 5/8" polyurethane (poly) hose, from Eley, on the reel. I have hardly any room to spare. Poly hoses are as thin as, or thinner than the cheap vinyl hoses, and they're much thinner than the heavy-duty rubber hoses. Maybe I could fit a 100 ft of vinyl or poly hose on there. Maybe. No way could you fit more than 75 ft of 5/8" rubber hose. I think Liberty Garden made a typo. MAYBE you could fit 125 ft of 1/2" vinyl or poly hose onto the real. Maybe. But no way can you fit 125 ft of 5/8" hose on it.

reviews.title: This thing is built like a tank
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on June 29, 2018
reviews.text: I just received my Liberty Garden 710 Navigator rotating garden reel today, and it's already installed on my brick house. This thing is built like a tank, and although a bit heavy to install, I managed to install it without the need of another set of hands. You just have to take your time, and think things out before installing. I highly recommend using 2 1/2" long by 5/16" diameter lager bolts, as opposed to concrete tap screws of same dimensions, for installing into brick or stone...because like I mentioned, this spool is heavy duty, and with a 100' commercial 5/8" hose, it needs good anchorage. I did it using the lag bolts, and it's very secure. The spool is so easy to unroll and roll up, even my wife can unwind and roll up the heavy hose effortlessly. The fact that you can spool in the direction of the hose is a major plus. The quality of this unit surpassed my expectations, and I have a feeling it will last us a very long time. The connections are all brass, and once I turned the tap on, there wasn't a drop of water leakage anywhere, which I'm very happy about, because I just can't stand a leaky hose or connection, even if it's just outside in my driveway. There is a tension allen screw under the handle, which allows you to adjust the free spool, so that it doesn't over unwind when rolling out, and keep the hose taught at all times. You really can't ask for a better hose reel than this, and if I could give it 6 stars, ....I would gladly. Living in Ontario, having severe cold, I plan on detaching the spool from the frame every fall, and keep the spool and hose in my warm basement, which will definitely, prolong the life of this garden hose and the Liberty 710. Thank you Liberty for finally making a descent hose reel. No more fancy shmancy plastic reels, that you have to replace every 2 or 3 years. So I highly recommend this hose reel, which is built to last...and no leaks LOL. Good job Liberty.

reviews.title: A very good product for cooler/colder climates
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 13, 2022
reviews.text: At a property we have near the beach, I put in an outdoor shower years ago to clear off the sand, etc. Every winter I'd disconnect the water lines and turn the shower handle to 1/2 way so that all the water would drain and things would dry out. Eventually, that shower valve developed a leak so I replaced it with a new valve that lasted all of one season because water had collected, froze and broke an internal seal. Then I found this gotonovo product which I am already super pleased with. First it has two shower modes - the overhead shower via a large circular head, and the more European style hand shower which you can select via a valve lower on the unit. There is one handle to control water flow and temperature. So as an outdoor shower unit, it works better than anything I'd had to date. The BEST part is that it's easy to remove for the winter. There is a hex key (metric mind you) that holds the top of the shower head, and down below you can spin two nuts holding the bottom part of the unit and it comes right off. This means I can store it indoors where it won't freeze and I can just pop it on next year. Taking on and off is literally a few minutes. So, if you're trying to blow out your shower head etc. for winters, I suggest you take a look at this product as it works superbly as a shower unit and it easily removable for the colder months.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 2, 2018
reviews.text: Update 3-9-2018. Further below is my original review which was 5 stars. I am knocking off a few stars, mainly because I feel like for $30 it should do it's job pretty well and be done with it. It's not working as well as it did originally, and I'm thinking of returning it. It did work well at first (summary: I have 3 TV's all fed from yagi style long range amplified antenna in attic, which leads to omni directional controller box that came with it. The two upstairs TV's (one fed direct from the out on that box, and the other from that boxes second out to the in on the channel master dist amp and then the out from it) get all the channels I expect in clear HD. The downstairs TV being fed by by a long coax from this distribution amp seemed to get all the channels with the addition of this amp, and I was very happy. Without it (was using non-powered splitter) multiple channels were choppy and cut in and out. Well, now the same thing is happening even with the dist amp, but the upstairs TV's still get all get the channels fine (so it's not like signal fluctuation from antenna - if they still get all the channels fine). If I connect a TV from the same out port of the distribution amp that the downstairs TV is being fed from, with a shorter coax cable, it works. Basically the long cable is the issue. But I have to use a long cable since it's running from upstairs down. The point of this purchase, was to power the long run so it would work, but seems to be hit or miss. Sometime OK, sometimes not. I should mention, I bought another long coax cord (25 foot, making sure it was the RG6 and not RG5) to see if the long coax cord was maybe the issue, but it made no difference. Actually, that was the first thing I tried before even buying this dist amp. I'm thinking of getting a coax to HDMI converter and seeing if that will work. I'm hoping HDMI works better over a 25 foot distance than coax. If that does work, then I have another headache to deal with, as the converter boxes have remote controls, but I'd want to use a short coax from dist amp (or splitter if elect to return the dist amp) to the coax to HDMI converter, with a long HDMI going downstairs, so my downstairs TV would need to be controlled by a remote (on HDMI source) with a box that was upstairs. Not sure how I'm going to solve that one. Frustrated... -------------------- Original review This distribution amplifier is exactly what I needed and works exactly as I hoped it would. Our basic cable bill (for just the local ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX, PBS, CW,) had gotten out of hand with cable company. Way too expensive for just basic cable. I decided to get a long rang amplified antenna (roof or attic mount). We are in a valley 30 miles from nearest TV towers. A relative had tried a basic antenna at his home down the street a while back and was only able to pick up NBC. My long range amplified antenna did better even mounted in the attic (didn't need to mount on roof). I get all the previously mentioned major local channels (except Fox, but I knew that going into it - because their signal is super weak in our area). All channels are in crystal clear HD, and much better than the cable I was paying for. The coax cable from the antenna goes to a powered box (which came with the antenna) and provides amplification, omni-directional control, and two outs to split the signal. Both TV's get all channels off each out. So I tried a third TV downstairs with a splitter. I lost 4 of the channels on downstairs TV that way. So I tried using same the splitter and a shorter coax and it works fine on third TV. So, I suspected the issue was too long of coax cord. I bought this distribution amp and now the downstairs TV (being fed by a long coax cord) gets all the channels. I am very pleased. It does what it's supposed to do.

reviews.title: Broadcast Beauty
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on June 8, 2013
reviews.text: I'm a Boomer, so I'm old enough to remember that the promise of cable TV was, "no commercials". Since they haven't lived up to that promise they don't get any of my money. I have a rooftop antenna and its coax cable runs into my utility room where it then splits to 4 locations in the house. I had only a passive 4-way splitter, my signal had really degraded and I was not looking forward to scaling the second story roof to check the antenna, which is only 5 years old. But, even my strongest broadcast signals were only in the 60 -70% quality range and I'd completely lost a number of UHF stations. So, after reading a lot of reviews, I took a shot and bought a "Channel Master 3414 4 Outputs Distribution Amplifier" from Amazon. Choosing it because the reviews and the price, because the power cable was included in that price, where with others it was a separate purchase. I've had it installed for two months now and I could not be happier with it. I live in a major metropolitan broadcast market so with the Channel Master I am now pulling in 40 different stations. All of the VHF stations are now showing 100% signal strength and signal quality and most of the UHF stations are showing the same. Even the very weakest UHF stations, which I couldn't even watch before as they had less that 3% signal quality, are now showing over 50% signal strength and over 30% signal quality, which for a digital transmission still gives you good picture and sound. So, if you want to have great reception from a rooftop antenna that is split and routed to numerous televisions, while telling the cable and satellite folks to take a hike, I highly recommend the "Channel Master 3414 4 Outputs Distribution Amplifier" Don't forget, if you are not going to use all the ports you will need to cap any unused ports with an F Type 75 Ohm Terminator cap or you could have signal loss even with the amplifier. UPDATE June 30, 2014: It's now well over a year since I installed the Channel Master amplifier and it's still doing a bang up job. Recently I had some work done on the house and decided while there were pros up on the ladders to have them replace my 6 year old "airplane" shaped antenna with a new Terrestrial Digital DB8 Multi-Directional 'Bowtie' UHF DTV Antenna. The new antenna is mounted about 5 feet above the roof peak, which is about 20 foot high. Living 8 miles from downtown Chicago the Channel Master/Terrestrial Digital DB8 combination is now pulling in 70 channels and when you discount the duplicates broadcasting on two frequencies, one HD one not and the weaker ones, I have well over 50 strong, viewable, channels. The interesting thing is I get different channels depending on the brand of the TV or converter box. For example with my Toshiba LED TV's tuner I get a series of Channel 13s but not the series of Channel 22s I get with the Zenith converter box in the same room which does not get the 13s. I've actually gotten a little hooked on the subtitled Korean historical costume dramas running on one of the Channel 24s I get. My only regret is I wish I'd put another 5 foot extension on the antenna mast; I think if I had I would probably be able to pull in the Northern Indiana stations around Merrillville, Hammond and Gary. reviews.title: Works very well to restore signal quality
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada 🇨🇦 on August 12, 2020
reviews.text: When I first installed my OTA antenna, I already had the signal going to two TVs and got reception of 37 channels. According to TVFool, I got all the nearby signals that I was aiming for (CN Tower and Buffalo broadcasts), but not two Hamilton stations. When I split this into three TVs, I lost most of the Buffalo stations due to weakened signals. To resolve this issue, I got the 4-way distribution amplifier from Channel Master and hooked up the three TVs, leaving the fourth port unused (on a side note, I am using the pre-existing coax setup from my long-ago cable TV provider housed in an outside plastic case to pull in the OTA signal). The net result of this was that I got all of my stations back, and I got the two Hamilton stations too! So the Hamilton stations were likely too weak when I split it into two, but were restored when I used the distribution amplifier. The amplifier itself is sturdy and heavy with a smooth painted finish, so it would last even if it were completely exposed to the elements. I love that the input power is provided through a coax cable because you can use your existing coax cable installation to provide power to the unit without running another power cord into your box. I simply plugged the wall wart near one of my unused TV jacks, used a short coax cable to connect the wall wart to the jack, then connected the other end of the corresponding coax line to the power input of the unit. Very easy and I didn't have to use one of my outdoor AC outlets to power the unit. Just make sure that the power-providing coax line is completely isolated and is not connected (via splitter) to any other cables, then test the voltage (~13V DC) of the other end of the power coax cable before you screw it into the unit.

Well worth the investment IMO.

reviews.title: Si mejora la Señal de Televisión
reviews.date: Reviewed in Mexico 🇲🇽 on May 16, 2018
reviews.text: Tengo el servicio básico de televisión por cable y suele llegar débil la señal de los canales, y siempre se ven con estática o como si se encimara un canal sobre otro (se ven imágenes opacas de un canal en otro canal), por ello decidí comprar este amplificador de señal y realmente mejoro la calidad de la señal, ahora se ve sin la estática y sin imágenes encimadas, sin embargo, para que funcione el Amplificador se debe mantener todo el tiempo conectado a la luz eléctrica porque si se desconecta la señal se ve mal y con mucha estática pero cuando se conecta se ve muy bien, ademas no afecta el servicio de Internet por el contrario parece ser que ligeramente lo mejora un poco (el servicio de Internet es por cable). Si tienes interés en mejorar tu señal de televisión sin afectar tu Internet por cable considera comprar este producto, porque realmente es útil y funcional como Amplificador. Ventajas: -Mejora la Señal de Televisión (la Amplifica y se ve mejor la imagen del canal) -No hay perdida en la señal de Televisión o Internet por cable y ligeramente mejora esta ultima un poco (No es un divisor/splitter por lo que no disminuye la señal) -Es fácil de Instalar, tan solo se conecta un cable coaxial a un regulador de voltaje que el mismo producto trae, y después solo se conectan los cables al amplificador y a la luz para que el aparato funcione (trae un manual donde se muestran las conexiones, sin embargo recomiendo ver tutoriales por Internet para una mejor comprensión de su uso). -Tiene 4 salidas para la señal (Solo he usado 2; una para el cablemodem que es el internet y otra para la señal de televisión y ambas funcionan correctamente) - No se calienta en exceso, el Amplificador lo he utilizado dos días seguidos y su temperatura es lo que podría considerarse como normal (se siente tibio) Desventajas -Si el Amplificador esta desconectado de la corriente eléctrica la señal se ve con mas estática (Si no conectas el Aparato a la corriente electrica y lo quieres usar sin luz como si fuera un divisor de señal no te servirá, porque la imagen se ve mal) -Si se va la luz el Aparato no mejorara la señal, solo pasará una imagen de los canales al televisor con estática (Sin embargo si se va la luz tampoco funcionará la televisión) -Es un Aparato algo caro. -Necesita estar conectado a la luz eléctrica, o si - no la señal de Televisión no se observará bien.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 23, 2019
reviews.text: I tried to save a few bucks on cheaper versions over the years, they were all cheap junk that would overflow, save your money and buy the Nelson. The Nelson self filling bowl hasn’t given us any trouble in the three or so years we’ve owned it, the dogs always have fresh water. We used tapcon concrete screws to attach it to the house under our covered patio, then plumbed it to an outdoor faucet. I made a mistake and put it where it got sun half the day which made the water warm and the concrete underneath nasty with green mold. I relocated it in the middle of the patio where it doesn’t get any sun, no more hot water or mold. Great product. Worth every penny!

Fast-forward to the end of June…With a last-minute trip scheduled, I made the purchase at such a great price with quick shipping. Now we’re ba-ack from our first trip and happy together! Here’s why: The 360-degree spinners don’t add to the height of the luggage which is all-important for carry-on bags. They also were excellent for the necessary starting and stopping at the airports to navigate the TSA maze and so many travelers over the holiday while maintaining social distancing. In addition to the sturdy, maneuverable wheels and affordable pricing, I gave this set 5 stars because: 1- I wanted a set with classic lines that would still be distinguishable from other luggage in the overhead bin and on the baggage carousel without the loud colors and styles that are so popular today. 2- The design closely matches the overnight/underseat bag from my old set. (It’s pictured with the others from last night’s arrival home.) 3- Gotta love the bag tag that refers to shoes (always admired Madden’s shoes and accessories) because I pack so many on every trip! 4- The tassels are a nice touch. I hang them from the zippers for easy opening and I don’t mix up the open/expand zippers. 5- My TSA-approved locks slide right in the zipper holes. 6- The bags stack inside each other as they arrived for minimal storage space. ***Check out the pictures for all of the above*** AND, SO IMPORTANT: I had a minor issue with one bag. I reached out to the Seller and received an almost instantaneous reply from a Fashion Luggage rep who resolved it for me. I’m impressed with the product quality and the stellar customer service from this family-owned business based in the USA. I’d gladly do business with them again and look forward to many trips with this luggage, and I would recommend both to friends and family.

reviews.title: It's a great basic planner...
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 6, 2022
reviews.text: It has everything you need in a planner. I'm really happy with it. I generally like planners that are simplistic and aren't too flashy, or god forbid they have some cheesy message on it like "believe in yourself" or "today is a new beginning"! It's undated, and it's a very nice refreshing aqua blue color. The inner pages are decent quality, I don't see any part of the planner breaking or tearing apart over the course of a year. It has one good quality clear plastic pocket in the very back for additional document storage. It has 5 double sided "Notes" pages, and 1 one-sided "Notes" page. The "Notes" pages are blank rules pages for you to write anything down. It fits a maximum of 12 months. It has an elastic bookmark, that loops around, to keep your page. I also really like that it has a page listing all the holidays. I bought my planner in April 2022, and the holiday list came with holidays for the years 2022, 2023, AND 2024! The yearly overview shows for years 2022 and 2023. There's two pages for contacts, with columns for "Name" and "Address/Numbers". Slight Downsides: - I wish it came with monthly sticker tabs to add for every month so that you can find and skip to any month easily. It's not a huge deal though because I easily added my own little tabs, so I'm still able to get that easy access I want. - I wish there were more "Notes" pages. My last planner had a lot more and so I guess I was a little disappointed there aren't as many in this one. There's definitely enough for your basic desire, but if you are someone who needs to put lots of notes in the back, you might need a planner with more pages. If those two things won't be a big deal to you then this would be a great planner for you. Overall, I'm happy with it so far.

reviews.title: Great magnification, I wish the arm was longer for better reach
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 4, 2012
reviews.text: PRO: Price competitive product. Sharp chrome finish that fits well in my bathroom. Excellent 5x magnification provides extreme close up for personal grooming. 8-inch mirror size allows for full face/neck viewing. Easily mounts on the bathroom wall with two screws. CON: Extension arm is entirely too short for my personal needs. Overall this is a good product - I only use the 5X magnification side because that provides me with the close-up view I need for personal grooming, be that nose/ear hair trimming, shaving, blemish maintenance, etc. I've yet to use the normal magnification side of the mirror since I have this mounted next to a large mirror / cabinet in the bathroom. The chrome colour fits in well with everything else in the bathroom - so really not much to report there. Install is easy with just a couple of screws and so if you find a stud in the wall you're pretty much good to go. My complaint which removes a star from the product is that the extension arm is just not long enough to bring the mirror away from the wall and right up to my face without me having to lean into it. If you have a large vanity / sink then you're going to have to lean in if you want to see right up close to your face. This can be managed a bit with mirror placement and of course it depends on where your walls are in the bathroom, but I'd like to see something with an arm extension that is a bit more adaptable. Swivel of the mirror is smooth and unencumbered. The mirror rotates gently but is tight enough so that it doesn't move when you need it to be stationary. Good light reflection and is easy to clean with a wipe and some windex, or a glass cleaning pad. This is a daily use item for me and for the price was a good deal.

reviews.title: Perfect! Installs in minutes.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 11, 2020
reviews.text: So, I’m getting to that age, um where I look into the mirror with my reading glasses on and I’m like “holy cow” was my eye liner looking like THAT all day?? This mirror is perfect. It was SO easy to install. I just got it today and in 10 minutes I was done. Like other reviewers say, don’t use the cheap-o enclosed wall anchors. I wasted time starting with them but quickly threw them away. Tip: Use your own. Install: I figured out where I wanted it; made sure there wasn’t a stud; used the bracket to trace the screw holes; used a level to make sure they were level up and down; drilled the holes for the anchors; popped them in; screwed the bracket into the wall, mounted the mirror on the bracket, bada-bing, bada-boom, DONE! The mirror is very nice looking and goes with all the other oil rubbed bronze fixtures and the dark brown mirror frame in my bathroom. There is no distortion on either side. I’m very happy with it!

reviews.text: The mirror itself seems of decent quality, but there’s where the positives end. This anchor has no lip and will just be pushed back when inserting and tightening the screw. Buy a E-Z ancor for easy installation. Also, the swing arm is installed off centre and one has to compensate for this sloppy assembly, otherwise the swing arm will not be level.

reviews.title: Good value for adventurous quilters
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 19, 2021
reviews.text: I read all the reviews and decided to take a chance. I bought two bags last month. One contained 37 pieces of Sweetwater’s “Red Barn Christmas” fabric. The pieces were all 32” long but varied quite a bit in width. The widest piece was 2.5” and the narrowest was 1.5” (which includes the selvage edges). This bag weighed 10.05 ounces. Several of the pieces will be very narrow when put into a quilt but I’m okay with that. The second bag contained 24 pieces of Civil war colored fabric - a mix of “Folktale” by Lella Boutique and “Prairie Dreams” by Kansas Troubles. Every piece was a complete width-of-fabric with selvages on the short ends and each piece was exactly 2.5” wide. This bag weighed 9.75 ounces. This bag was like getting a little more than half a jelly roll for the price of one-third of a jelly roll. So I took another chance and bought another bag, which arrived today. This bag contained 31 pieces of “Figs and Shirtings” by Fig Tree. Each piece was 32” long, with the narrowest piece being 2.5” and the widest 3.4” (including selvages). This bag weighed 11.5 ounces. Every bag is great! The fabric is high quality and it’s fun to have a chance to use new designers in my work. I think these grab bags are generally a very good value for those who are willing to take a bit of a risk or are of the adventurous type. I’ll definitely buy more.

reviews.title: Gambling for fabric addicts
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 20, 2020
reviews.text: I've gotten several of these Moda scrap packs from different fabric stores/sellers, because I can never resist a low-stakes gamble. 😂 Most recently, I bought a pack here on Amazon and got 12.3 oz of selvage strips from Moda's Dwell in Possibility line, which is scheduled to be released in the coming months. I received 32 strips in 28 different prints, each strip is about 32 inches long. If you're thinking about buying a scrap pack, they can be pretty nice as long as you know what to expect! In each pack, I usually get an assortment of strips between 9-12 oz, some just barely skimming 2 inches and some a little over 3 inches wide. The prints are usually all from the same collection, usually recent or upcoming collections. Some people say they've gotten scrap bags with no selvages, but every pack I've personally received has been 100% selvage edges. When I'm lucky I'll get more of the selvage side that has the fabric print going all the way to the edge, so I have a little more useable fabric. Sometimes I get fabric from collections that I honestly don't really like and would never buy for myself, but it's all just down to luck. Moda always seems to have good quality fabric regardless of the print, so if you're not picky this is a great way to build up a variety of prints for scrappy projects. If you're looking for bigger pieces of fabric or you only like working with certain styles of prints, this may not be the right buy for you. But if you're looking for a little surprise to brighten your day, you might just find it in a scrap bag. :)

reviews.title: The Most Comprehensive Review of Rum Runners. My Tips and Tricks to Be Successful.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 5, 2021
reviews.text: This is the review for the guy/gal who wants the most comprehensive report on why these work, why they don’t work for idiots and the unlucky, and what other methods are available to sneaking alcohol on the ship. If you want the readers digest version, read paragraph 2 for my choice. I’ve read about 100 of these reviews, watched 20 or 30 different Youtube videos, read several detailed articles compiling data about rum runners, scanner machines, general human behavior, “wine” bottles, and bringing the massive generic looking shampoo bottles filled with booze and have come up with a few indisputable facts, as well as a few deductions based on probability. And obviously I’ve successfully sneaked alcohol on my cruise with these. Ultimately I chose a combination of the rum runner method and wine bottle method to hedge my bets hoping that at least one goes through and if both go through I will just have more alcohol when I get home (which both worked btw). I gave the rum runners about 80% chance of going through and the wine bottles about 80% chance as well based on all of the information I compiled which leaves only a 1 in 25 chance I end up with no alcohol on the ship. 1. Carnival is by far the WORST for sneaking booze on. I may have only read one product review that mentioned a cruise line by name that WAS NOT Carnival. Their profit margin must be more heavily weighed on sales of alcohol than other lines. 2. Rum runners are your BEST CHANCE for sneaking alcohol on other than wine bottles which you will pay a corkage fee for (about 15$ per bottle on NCL and 1 free bottle per passenger on Royal) 3. If you choose the wine bottle method, just know you’re taking a chance as far as the person you get who inspects your wine bottles. If you shake a wine bottle, wine bubbles look a bit different than vodka bubbles which can be kind of combatted by ensuring the top of the liquor goes just above the seal line so it takes them more effort to look if they care enough. 4. Only put wine bottles in your carry on as putting them in your checked baggage will cause them to search and find your rum runners (if you do both methods like I did) 5. Limited information about scanning machines was available but the most information I was able to find implied that a TSA type scanning machine, they aren’t necessarily able to see liquid, but faint outlines of plastic things. Also, they don’t scan from the bottom, only the sides and top which is why all of the reviews showed that the rum runners were placed on the bottom with other toiletries stacked on top so when the scanner is run, you see a top view and sides which should only show a slim version and disguises the rum runners with outlines of other bottles. 6. If you’re thinking of getting a TSA lock and using that, a simple amazon search will find that anyone can buy a key that only TSA is supposed to have. Also, they have no inhibitions in calling you down to the dark room in the ship where they will ask you to open up your bag to reveal your belongings. 7. The shampoo bottles seemed to have more mixed than polarizing reviews and my friend elected to try them because they came with “quality control seals.” They worked fine but I’m still not sold because this removes items you could bring on because who uses two shampoos and better yet, who brings 32oz of it with them. Also, everyone knows shampoo is thick, a simple shake even with the quality seal will reveal it’s a thin liquid…. busted. 8. Buy a couple of the same wine bottle and the wine sealers. A 30 pack is like 8 bucks with Prime. Don’t only buy 5 because you will mess up the first couple trying to figure out how long to boil them for. You’re paying pennies on the dollar for alcohol on the ship… Don’t trip over dollars to get to pennies. Do it right. 9. Buy two of the same wine bottle, preferably chardonnay. Chardonnay works best because it’s usually a tinted bottle and a couple drops of yellow food dye makes the liquid indistinguishable from real chardonnay. The only part I haven’t come up with a solution for is the bubbles. This is tricky. Shake a chardonnay bottle, then shake a chardonnay bottle filled with your liquor of choice side-by-side and see the difference in the bubbles. 10. Do NOT use a wine opener on the wine when you open it. Use the grocery bag method on Youtube. Whoever came up with this is flipping brilliant! I have seen stories of where idiots were caught because security suspected it was fake and they popped the seal on the wine to inspect the cork and they got caught because security saw the gaping hole from the wine opener in the cork. If you’re going to use Rum Runners, follow these rules 1. Place rum runners ONLY in your CHECKED BAGS. They will be found in your carry on bags. Open bags are much much more likely to be searched. 2. Try to turn in your checked bags in last if possible. I know you’re eager to get on your vacation but if your bags are among the last to be scanned, rest assured they will be rushing to get them done and everyone out to sea for an on time departure. 3. I decided to place a 20$ bill on each rum runner with the words “Free Money” on it so if found, hopefully they would just take the 20$ bill and let me have the alcohol and if they took the alcohol and my money, I would raise hell saying they stole money out of my bag which is 100% true. And if you’re about to complain about the 20$ just think on cruise day if its a choice between getting them taken, and “spending” an extra 20$ to get about 250$ worth of retail value on the ship of alcohol, I hope you would chose the latter. 4. Don’t go on Carnival. They are much more likely to search individual bags. This is a cheap cruise line with thinner margins than other cruises, and believe me the profit margin of cruise lines is already razor thin. 5. Don’t be that guy and not buy any alcoholic beverages on the ship, you could risk getting the alcohol you worked so hard to get on the ship, taken. Pregame in your room, get yourself a solid buzz, then get a drink or two while out. Don’t cheap out that hard. 6. Place them flat and stacked below your toiletries. If you have a rollaway, place them under the lining, they will disappear in the scanners sideways view because of the metal bars which you retract to roll your bag and will disappear from the top view because of the toiletries in your bag. 7. To understand why this works, download the airport scanner game on your phone and see what items actually look like in a scanner. 8. When filling the rum runners, get as many air bubbles out of it as possible before sealing it.

reviews.title: Carnival Cruise Inspiration
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 12, 2019
reviews.text: Just got home yesterday after a 4 day Carnival Cruise out of Long Beach! These actually worked! I was nervous about it even after reading so many positive reviews. I bought the 3 pack of 8oz and only a $12 bottle of Cuervo Silver so that if caught, the $20 total wouldn't be a bad loss. Anyway, I tested the "leak proof" durability of the bags for 1 week. They were 100% leak proof!!! I read reviews, I filled the bags about 80%, tilted the bags, spout up, and squeezed the pouch slowly, making sure all the air went out and tequila poured out as I capped the bag. I did this with each bag, multiple times, making sure that the only air that did end up in it was about the size of a pinhole. 2 of my bags were perfect, no air bubbles at all! Then I placed each bag into a sandwich sized ziplock bag. I folded one in between the pant legs of the only pair of jeans I brought. One went inside a sealed Halloween costume bag (Halloween time on our cruise!) And the 3rd went at the bottom of my makeup box with makeup, micellar water, facial scrub, hair care cream and jelly and perfume rollers packed all neatly on top and around it in the makeup box. I then had my travel kit with lotion, body wash, shampoo and conditioner. I decided that if any of the bags set off security bells, and they had to check, that they'd hopefully dismiss it due to all of the other things I had in there that definitely set off alarms. My luggage arrived late to my room and had definitely been gone through. Nothing had been found though!!! I can't use this as an example that they were undetectable in the luggage. But on a day when we left the ship and came back on board, I took one full one, untouched, to shore. Did not end up drinking down the streets so it was going back on board. I was again nervous about being caught. I took this bag and placed it in the waistband of my pants, went through the security check, no problems! I feel like overall these worked. My interference during the checked luggage didn't get to be proof, but maybe if you're like me and just want to take extra caution, place a few items in your checked luggage to purposely set off alarms and make sure the flasks themselves are well hidden. I will definitely use these again! And just a side note, that 1 bottle of wine per adult, to be carried on, was never searched/checked. My friend and I went through separate security checks and neither got checked. That means you could get a bottle with a twist off cap, fill it with alcohol and close it up again, put it in a wine bag, inside of a backpack, and send it right onto the conveyor belt as you walk through!

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on March 30, 2020
reviews.text: I bought this to secure a 5-shelf wire shelf to my wall. I used FIVE of these latches-- 2 on the top shelf, 2 on the bottom, and 1 in the middle of the middle shelf. Nothing particularly heavy is stored on the shelf, but we have a crawling/toddling baby, and I wanted to be extra sure that this shelf wouldn't tip over. Last week, I noticed one of the top latches had completely broken (the cable tie was still connected to the shelf, but the plastic piece attached to the wall was cracked and no longer even touching the cable tie). So over the weekend, I took everything off the shelf to move it away from the wall and replace that one piece, and I found that FOUR of plastic pieces were ALL BROKEN!! Good thing I checked! It has been <3.5 months of use. EDIT: After my initial one-star review, the company reached out to me and offered a refund for the product, which I did receive. At first I was told that the plastic straps are now thicker, but then after I clarified that the anchor pieces are what had broken, I was told that the anchor too is now thicker. I cannot confirm this (as I will not be buying this product again), but it is nice to have been told this, at the very least, and that someone contacted me with an apology.

reviews.text: So apparently these little things are the most fun you will ever have in your lifetime. Who knew. For Christmas this past December I decided to make my own poppers or crackers. I collected *18* toilet paper rolls and stuff these little guys into each one (which they don’t really fit into). BUT not before giving each one a number. I wrote little number on all of them. The numbers are very important. Ok so after they all got stuffed in their rolls I wrapped them up all pretty like normal poppers. Then I wrote down corresponding numbers on a piece of wrapping paper and put it in hat. I got everyone gathered around and told them to pick a number. So they did. Everyone had their numbers. I dumped out the poppers. Everyone had to find their popper. (I had the number written on the outside.) Everyone was trying to shake them and guess and trying to figure out what was going on. Once everyone got their poppers open they saw their little guy! With their number! Then it was...Off to the races!!!! We lined each of the little guys up at a start and a finish line (don’t make it too long-lol!) and wound them up and counted down and set them off! No one knew, including me, what they were going to do! Hop, walk, run, circle, or something we hadn’t thought of yet! I named mine and told him I believed in him but he still lost the first round. Well, he didn’t just loose he went into the negative because he went backwards. But that’s to be expected because that’s my life in a nutshell. The second round he actually won! So no telling what they will do! Everyone was very excited to play and made a great Christmas experience! So much so that my aunt and my great aunt went and purchased these to then go and play “the game” at their next party!

Read more Engineered By PRAZTECH Tools right at your Doorstep, with over 5 Decades of Engineering Expertise, Complete tooling solutions Read more Guidelines While Using PRAZTECH Single Point Diamond Dresser To use the tool to its optimum level, it would be wise to keep the following guidelines in mind: Praztech diamond dresser should be mounted firmly into the holder and, the distance between the diamond and the clamp should be reduced to the least, so as to avoid the diamond from getting ruptured due to vibration. Ensure that the diamond tool is never directed at an angle which is opposite to the direction of the rotation of the grinding wheel. To maintain a sharper point, it is essential to check that a drag angle of approximately 10 degrees to the horizontal wheel radius, pointing in the direction of grinding wheel rotation is maintained. It is important not to insert Praztech dressers into the grinding wheel at more than 0.001” (0.025mm) per pass. Cuts deeper than this may cause overheating and, thereby, result in excessive wearing of the diamond. A fast traverse dressing rate will produce an open wheel, enabling removal of large stock. On the other hand, a slow traverse dressing rate will impart a finish on wheel which is appropriate for producing a good finish on the work piece. In order to maintain a conical point, Praztech dresser should be rotated in the holder at an angle varying from 20 to 40 degrees. To avoid cracking of the diamond, use ample amount of coolant wherever possible. Always make sure that before beginning with the cutting activity, the coolant is turned on. In cases, where dry dressing is performed, do not apply the tool incessantly for longer time, in order to avoid high temperature. Allow the tool to cool naturally instead of doing it with the aid of a coolant. A sudden change in temperature can possibly cause fracture to the diamond, essentially not at the time of shock but in the future use of the tool. A diamond dresser should never be worn down to the shank as this might result in dropping out of the diamond. Unusually, a Praztech diamond dresser mounted in a dressing tool has more hidden points which, if desired, may be used by resetting. A crucial point to be remembered is not to allow a large flat to develop on the cutting point as this may deteriorate the economic life of the diamond.

I basically drilled a 1/2" hole thru a piece of scrap wood, and affixed another piece of wood underneath to slide across the tool rest. Of course, this requires that your tool rest has a straight edge against which the jig can accurately slide. The diamond point itself worked very well. It cut (dressed) the grinding wheel quickly and cleanly. Just don't slip, or you'll instantly gouge your grinding wheel and possibly damage the diamond point.

reviews.title: The figures arrived with no problems, excellent secure packaging, and they look amazing!
