reviews.text: I ordered from the seller Anime Books Store, and they did a fantastic job with the packaging of these figures. They came in a larger box than I thought they would, with "fragile" labels all over. I've had a few drop-kicked packages before by certain delivery services, so the extra warnings around the box may have been enough to remind them to gently place the box at the door. When I got the package opened, the two figure boxes were securely placed in the center with plenty of packing paper and bubble wrap to keep them from being jostled and impacted. The figure boxes themselves didn't have a single scratch on them. This was great, because I was hoping to keep the boxes, and after seeing a lot of figure reviews saying that their boxes arrived looking like a beast gnawed on them, it was a pleasant surprise to see them unscathed. The figures themselves are of amazing quality and capture the personality of the characters well. The paint jobs are great, too. I can't speak for any other seller at the moment, but if you do want to order yourself some figures or other anime/manga merchandise and have peace of mind knowing they'll arrive in good condition, make sure to look into Anime Books Store on the Amazon Marketplace. In the Wild West of the Amazon Marketplace, for me, it's comforting to know there are sellers that care.

reviews.title: Just As I Remembered
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 23, 2022
reviews.text: I had one of these sets as a kid and loved it. I've always loved marbles. Well, I had my nephews (5 & 8 yr old) coming to visit, and ordered this for them to play with. The 5 year old was a bit lost and didn't understand how to put the pieces together so the marbles flowed through, but he had a blast running them through it. The 8 year old enjoyed the puzzle of figuring out the run. We built it up together and used all the pieces and they had a blast dumping all the marbles in at once over and over again. It's fun, it's mesmerizing, it's soothing, it's satisfying. You have to tighten things up frequently. If you bump it, it will most likely fall over, but you just start again and make a new build with modifications. We had a problem because they started fighting over marbles and knocked it over a few times in the process of trying to take them from each other...sigh...

reviews.title: Glad I Chose This One
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 29, 2020
reviews.text: I read tons and tons of reviews for different marble runs before settling on this one. I agonized over the reviews that appeared on almost every different marble run, saying the pieces don't hold together and the structures fall apart. I ended up buying this one, despite a few negative reviews, and it works great! The pieces hold together very nicely, and my 7-year-old and almost-4-year-old love playing with it. When we first got it, they spent no less than 6 hours that day playing with it, and at least 4 hours a day for the next few days. It slowly petered out over a week or 2, and they gradually lost interest, but will still get it out every few weeks and play with it for an hour or so. Not bad for $40. I love that it comes with a handy, drawstring bag so we can pack it all away, all together, and the pieces don't get lost. It's also great that it came with so many marbles, because somehow those DO disappear, despite our best efforts. For the reviews saying structures fall over; this is not really a fault of the toy, in my experience. You do have to build with a little intelligence, setting the towers up in a triangular or square pattern (or any kind of staggered pattern, really) for stability, not all in a straight row, which would be easily knocked over. My kids learned this very quickly. My 7-year-old very quickly learned to build complex, fully functional structures. My almost-4-year-old likes to run the marbles down structures that someone else builds, or just play with the pieces, connecting and disconnecting them, sorting the colors, collecting and hoarding marbles, etc. He doesn't quite "get" the concept of making a functioning marble run on his own yet, but that is fine; both kids enjoy the toy a lot. Only 2 pieces in the whole set do not quite work properly; the two that look like curving roller-coaster tracks; they are just slightly warped, and the balls would stop running on them, so we stopped using them. All the rest work perfectly, and we are very happy with it.

reviews.title: Better Than Expected
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on April 19, 2022
reviews.text: Purchasing something for one tenth the cost of similar products always stirs up a good deal of anxiety. You spend extra time combing through the reviews comparing the good and bad ones. Initially I just wanted a 517 tip for my existing ancient sprayer but could not find a compatible one then I stumbled across a 517 that comes attached to a complete gun for less than a tip would have cost from one of the well known sprayer companies. The gun is heavier than expected, appears well made and despite others complaining the threaded fittings aren't NSP, they are and mate up just fine to the sprayer and existing hose. I like the fluid regulator using a double re-tractor mechanism. This gives a smooth, easy to regulate flow and is more durable than a single pin arrangement. All the components seem fastened securely and I am at a loss to understand other complaints about the trigger falling off or the lock mechanism flopping closed. Can't say anything yet about leakage issues with the hose swivel but I see it can be removed and either repaired or replaced with a non-swivel fitting. Something odd to close this out. The box clearly states on the front it is made in China however the the small card showing how the tip and saddle are to be installed has a German company name (Wacner) and address and logo that so closely matches a US company it cannot be coincidence.

reviews.title: I love this punch set
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 5, 2021
reviews.text: This punch set gets more use than I thought it would when I bought it. It functions well with little effort. The selection of hole sizes makes this set a must have when different size holes are needed for an array of stitches, snaps and eyelets. This punch made clean sharp holes, I have no complaint. Handy and stores well in my small craft room. I bought this tool in 2020 Nov. and have used it pretty much every day since. It does punch paper and yardstick. The trick I have learned is when punching paper or anything the base you punch on should be a hard plastic cutting board, (Dollar Tree Item) the reason for this is the base will get cut as well. Another trick is when cutting, rotate the cutter around the hole you're making to make sure the hole you are cutting is complete. One more hint, I oil the grove to making the pushing motion easier, cuts down on the pressure needed. I sure hope this helps out, I really like this tool. Now I want to buy an extra set of punches for mine as a back up. I would be lost with out this tool. I don't need another tool but, I will buy one just for the extra punches.

reviews.title: Awesome even in a small shower and 3/4 bathroom
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 8, 2020
reviews.text: The media could not be loaded. I took a leap of faith on this product because so many reviews said it wont work in a small bathroom. The bathroom in my moms room is a 3/4 bath, toilet, sink and shower and is tiny 6×8 if that. However the toilet sits across from the sink and next to the hall entrance door. There is nothing but the door to her bedroom in front of thr shower entrance. (I drew a crude diagram for a visual) This is what makes the difference. I think people who have a toilet or sink in front of the entrance to the tub or shower are the ones with the "not for small" bathroom problem. So please look at the configuration of your room, thay is what will matter the most. This product is excellent. I have enough room for my mom to take one step from the toilet to the chair, or from her wheel chair in the bedroom to the bathroom, which she can do, then I just slide her into the shower. And even though my shower stall is small I have plenty of room to slide her completely in and not get the floor wet. Being that she is only about 5"3 she still has leg room as well. The control you have to push in is under the seat and between the the persons legs but that is no embarrassment issue for us since I bathe her anyway. I have arthritis and it was easy to assemble and easy to slide. She weighs about 145. Pulled out it blocks her bedroom door but i can push it in when we are done and leave access to that door for the remainder of the day. But that room and the bathroom has two entrances so I can leave it slid out if I choose. It is an excellent product and will be a great assistance to us, she is 93 with dementia.

reviews.title: just what we needed-but measure carefully
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on February 20, 2014
reviews.text: I ordered this for my mother, who now needs assistance with bathing, after I had considered many more-expensive benches (all, but this one, with astronomical shipping fees) & finally crossed fingers and ordered this reasonably priced chair - which arrived very quickly and has so far proven to be an excellent choice. WIDTH OF BENCH: Our shower/tub (original 1959, all-in-one style) tapers down to an 18 1/2 inch width at the tub's base. Like most tubs, the sides curve into the base like a bowl. Of course, with such a tub, it's important to measure not at the opening at the top of the tub as it is several inches wider at top than at bottom; and I did not measure from side to side at the bottom either, because the legs will not be resting on the curve. Note where the tub's base becomes level (that is, where the inside-legs will situate themselves once weight is on the bench) to determine if this bench will work for you. (The 18-1/2" width I mentioned was obtained measuring tub's base: from outermost level point left to outermost level point right. If our tub's width at bottom was an inch or so narrower, I think this bench would be too wide. The chair would rest over the lip of the tub; the person bathing would have to spray water on the bathroom floor in order to fully rinse.) FEATURES: -The chair slides smoothly; securely; easily. -The bench does not slip; slide or budge while Mom is bathing. *The chair is steady & secure. After sliding and "clicking" into place, the chair holds fast and steady. *The suction-cups on the outside-of-tub legs hold well yet are also easy to detach by lifting their tabs. -I find the slide-release-button easy enough to access with Mom in the chair. -Mom likes the handle. She feels secure - especially when I slide the chair for her. -The seat is generous in size. My Mom is about 110 lbs.; we've tested the chair using people up to 170 lbs. It operates smoothly and effortlessly. -All water flows off all surfaces; no worry of mildew which forms quickly in our area. -It's light-weight; enough so that I can easily put it into the tub when Mom's done bathing & store it there till next bath. (Therefore, I haven't needed the folding feature so can't comment on that.) -I find it's easy to clean. I'm all around pleased with the performance of this item so far. We've only used it 3 times though. I am looking forward to seeing how it holds up with use and over time, and hope I'll remember to update this review with that information in future!

reviews.title: Width of slide and getting it to sit as close to the edge of the bath as possible
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on September 12, 2021
reviews.text: Overall, this product is good. My wife can now have a shower. Because our bathroom is small and the toilet is next to the bath, we figured out that we have to have the back of the chair against the hot/cold water controls so my wife is facing the other way. Otherwise, there was not enough room for her to sit down and raise her legs up when she slides across the bath. Second thing was the rubber feet on the side that goes into the bath were about 4 inches in diameter which, because the bath is curved as most batch are, it meant it would not go all the way into the bath, the chair was still protruding over the side of the bath. So, to fix this, i unscrewed the two rubber feet, bought two slip on ones that are a lot smaller from home depot and fitted them. The transfer bench now fits further into the bath and the chair no long sticks out of the edge. Other suggestions to the manufacturer, try making the legs more snug to the slide, they still stick out or make them so they can slide into the frame. A clip in piece of Perspex on the side where the bath is would be great in order to help reduce the amount of water going on the floor, the shower curtain has to be lifted up and pushed around and over the frame. Otherwise, it works great. I would still recommend this product, its light, and the legs fold in for storage.

reviews.title: Comfortable, lightweight, AND effective filtering???
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 17, 2021
reviews.text: I'm allergic to almost everything, especially perfumes and air fresheners, and I have to wear a mask all day when I'm working at the office. So I've bought a lot of masks and most of them fall into a couple of basic designs. This mask is actually a new design and new type of filter, and WOW I was impressed. First the positive: The mask relies on a removable filter, which allows the rest of the mask to be a very lightweight, soft, and stretchy fabric. It is super comfortable, and the little bit of fabric that goes under the chin really helps to keep leaks out. The filter itself is designed to fit perfectly in the mask and covers most of the breathing area, so you're actually breathing through the filter and not around it. I don't really understand how the nanofilter works, but it's very thin and easy to breathe through. BUT I know it is actually filtering, because my big issue is fragrances, and this keeps them out better than any other mask/filter I've tried. Seriously - other masks, even when properly fitted, will usually reduce the amount of perfume I inhale, but I can still smell it in the mask. With this mask, I was able to walk through the halls of the office and not smell ANYTHING until I got to a certain "danger zone" where the perfume is usually intolerable, but even with that, it still reduced the smell significantly. The negatives: The fabric covering the nose wire is very thin and looks like it could tear eventually. The nose wire itself isn't padded, and the mask comes with two adhesive foam pads, but neither of them stuck for more than a few minutes. The mask was definitely more comfortable with the extra nose pad, but it's tolerable even without it. The main annoyance is just how fiddly it is to get the filter in place. I appreciate that the tight design of the mask helps when you're wearing it, but to get the filter in, you have to do a lot of maneuvering of the thin and fragile filter, and once it's in place you still have to do adjustments to get the seam to line up with the front. It's a minor annoyance, but I like to wash my masks regularly and I dread having to take the filter out and then put it back in after washing. That being said, this is my #1 mask at the moment. It'd be great if they were able to improve the design somewhat, but even as it is, it's worth it for the comfort and great filtering.

reviews.title: This mask fits great, normal adult male face
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on October 29, 2021
reviews.text: Over the last 18 months I have tried several different masks as they wear out and this is what I am wearing currently and I really like it. Firstly the size, I am wearing an XL, which fits my normal adult male face perfectly. If you are someone that people would describe as having a large face, it won't be large enough. If you are female or smaller male face, you might want to go down to a L. Other masks will say large adult male, until you try them on and they are just too small. Secondly I really like the built in plastic guard that holds the mask away from your lips, combine that with the chin cup and it stays on perfectly in place while talking for hours. Thirdly the elastic adjustable straps, other masks use rubber elastic which will melt if you leave it in your hot car hanging from the turn signal, these are fabric elastic and while they don't stretch as much they won't melt either. Fourthly the fit and seal all the way around is good, you know this because air doesn't blow up towards your eyes, instead the whole masks bellows in and out with your breath, meaning it's going through the fabric not escaping around the edges, but the plastic guard is still preventing it from caving in all the way. Fifthly the fabric appears to be preshrunk, I have had other masks shrink in hot water washes afterwards, not this mask. Other things, no problem breathing in the mask at all, but I am also not using the optional charcoal liner. It also comes with a single optional charcoal liner, and you can buy replacements for that if you want extra filtration. Many different color and patterns available, rather than just boring old black. The only thing I don't like about this mask, and I am not sure it's an issue yet, is the moldable metal nose bridge. While the corners of the metal are rounded, they are starting to wear the fabric thin where it rubs against the corners. I anticipate it will wear a hole through the fabric, but it might be time to replace it by then.

reviews.title: Plays high well but dirty and not light
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 13, 2022
reviews.text: I’ll start with the reasons why I returned it and then turn to better details. The product name is incorrectly written as “ Bach Trombone lacquer(LT190SL1B)”. It came as a trumpet. The LT designation means light but this trumpet is about the same as other trumpets weight just north of 2.4lb(1kg). That might be a light trombone but is normal weight for trumpet. The instrument seems to have passed from buyer to buyer on Amazon for a long time. The silver plating has many groups of very slight marks around the valve and tubing near there. I could not clean it off. Microfiber plus a bit of water, the marks are still there, a bunch of hairline widthed marks. Plus the out side of the bell is dirty. I washed it with soap and there just is some kind of white residue that doesn’t come off even after a very hot soapy water bath. My only conclusion is that this instrument is a sample that people returned many times on Amazon. I’ve a much cheaper silver plated trumpet that I play daily for a year and it doesn’t have this kind of dirtiness that I can’t clean off. On the other hand, this trumpet does live up to its hype—high notes are incredibly easy to play, the trumpet “responds faster” like they say on YouTube—you can really hear the difference when playing 16th or faster notes. I didn’t notice very significant volume changes resulting from the Large bore size, but by the same token, I don’t feel more tired playing with more air. One Caveat for the uninitiated, it comes with a very shallow 3E mouthpiece which will take getting used to, but more importantly, a lot of the benefits of this trumpet disappears when you don’t use the 3E mouthpiece. The quick response disappears with anything heavier. The high notes, the volume… it seems to be very sensitive to everything. This is definitely a very cool trumpet to be tried at music store. They might even be able to clean up this grime better than what we can do at home. But I am not keeping this particular one from Amazon.

And the colour seems to be fading fast- I can tell the difference between the one I washed five times and the one I washed six times. And no I don't use bleach or harsh detergent or anything, I even wash in warm not hot water. Also, consider that the extra details that make a towel look cute in an ad can make it look busy in a home. I think the pattern would be quite enough on its own- the border on one edge goes too far and makes these look try-hard, as we used to say in the 90s. Personally I wouldn't have them out if anyone was coming over as I think they look silly. And when I use them I keep the edge with the border facing the wall. As for usability, they are nice. Soft enough but not so plush they're linty or take ages to dry. The crosshatch texture is lovely for slurping the water off your skin faster than a smooth towel, exfoliating mildly, and hiding minor stains. If only they had just the overall texture, no edge embellishment, and the seams were sturdy, and the dye more lasting, these would be fabulous. But alas they are too imperfect for me to want to buy more.

Also, I bought the 25' - 28' cover for my 24' pontoon which leaves a little extra, but I rather have extra than not enough. 11/1/20 My first 25’-28’ cover was ripped because the additional midsection stand I set up came loose and puncture the cover so I bought another cover 21’-24’ and it fits the whole length of my 24’ boat. reviews.text: After putting this on my pontoon for the first time, I am happy with it, so far. As you know, only time will tell how long a boat cover lasts, but it seems well built. The fabric is light, but fairly tough. It's plenty long for my 24ft pontoon, and I like the flap on the back that covers the outboard. I will be buying some bungee cords to make installation a bit quicker. Threading the enclosed rope through the hooks and under the boat is quite time consuming. Overall, I am happy so far. I will update my review after some time and I can see how well it lasts.

reviews.title: Great Value!
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on October 25, 2014
reviews.text: The material is very robust and beads water off like a duck. The seams are strong and well sewn. The rubber bungee at the bottom is tight. Most importantly, the D ring webbing material is very well fastened and strong. I would suggest that the plastic D rings could be improved to aluminum or galvanized metal for little cost but if they fail, you could easily replace it with a carabiner or the like. The photo implies that there may be some more reinforcement material where one would place supports. No matter, different structures could be envisioned. My boat is 26', so I ordered the the 25'-28' size with a lot left over to tie down; because the bottom stretches, I would be inclined to go smaller and get a tighter drum-like fit. But at the price this is a great buy and I would recommend it in a heartbeat

reviews.title: Exactly what I wanted, but not for bassheads
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 16, 2012
reviews.text: I ended up purchasing these after reading some reviews and opinions at Head-Fi, so I had a pretty good idea what to expect. I am extremely happy with the headphones, especially for the price. Obviously $35 is not going to buy you a $350 pair of headphones, but these are very tough, if not impossible, to beat on a quality-for-price basis and beat the pants off of some models I've tried that cost twice as much. However, bassheads beware: these are not a bass-centric or bass-enhanced headphone. That's not to say that the bass response isn't good, because it is. Bass is very tight and punchy without muddying the rest of the mix, which was a problem for me with the CX-300's these are replacing. But you are going to hear what the engineers put in the mix - nothing more. That was actually a huge selling point for me, but if you want your ears rattled off you need to look elsewhere. That said, response is good across the frequency spectrum, with possibly just a bit of a bump in the mids. Highs are sharp and responsive without creating a lot of sibilance or overpowering the mids - these are not tinny phones by any means. Lows are solid. Bass drums have a nice dull thud just like they should without overpowering the rest of the mix. Mids really shine. Guitar and piano-based rock and pop sound fantastic, and jazz is very pleasant. I have heard it said that fit is very important with these headphones, and that's true. If they are not fully inserted they can sound thin and tinny, and it is important that the ear pieces create good contact with your ear, both for isolation and for bass perception. The stock "medium" sized pieces that were factory installed work great for my ears, but they come with a good selection of alternatives, including 2 sets of double-flanged cups. Isolation is good but not great with properly sized ear pieces. I find I need to bump my volume a notch or two in noisy environments compared with my CX-300's. However, isolation is far superior to my MDR-EX90's or any outside-the-ear buds, and what these phones give up in isolation they make up for in a much more open soundstage than my previous buds. This is probably owing to the vented design of the E10 vs the closed design of the CX-300. I can't see isolation being an issue unless you spend appreciable time in very noisy environments with these phones. Comfort was a big concern for me as I sleep on my headphones just about every night. The CX-300 has a lower profile and rounded back that is very unobtrusive to sleep on, and I was concerned that the squared back and slightly longer length of the E10 might cause some discomfort. Surprisingly, these are actually, if anything, slightly more comfortable to wear lying down and haven't caused me any pain or discomfort while sleeping or upright even when left in place up to 7 hours at a time. Everyone's ear being different, YMMV, but I find them very comfortable to wear even for long durations. Build quality seems very good. Every tactile surface besides the wire is metal and feels sturdy. Accidentally dropping or sitting on these will not cause me a second of concern. The strain reliefs are short and low-profile with a hardened rubber feel, but seem to work effectively, and I don't anticipate shorts or breaks becoming a problem. The wire is a bit thicker than either my EX-90 or CX-300's, and microphonics are very minimal. By way of comparison, I never had a problem with my CX-300's before, but going back to them after using these the microphonics are really irritating. Cord length is good. I haven't found myself wanting for more slack or getting tangled up in excess cord. This was a welcome change from the CX-300, which has a very short cord that would occasionally cause the headphones to jerk out of my ear when shuffling my chair around my desk or turning my head too far away from my MP3 player. Overall, I'd say these are without question the best pair of in-ear headphones that $35 can buy right now. I started out looking for a replacement for my CX-300's that were inexpensive enough that I wouldn't have to worry about abusing them and sleeping in them, and I ended up with that and a lot more. I would have been extremely happy with the quality and performance of these headphones at double the retail price. For what I paid, I almost feel guilty. As I said at the outset, these are not a good match for a basshead, but they suit me and my listening preferences perfectly. As long as you know what to expect I can't think of any good reason you would be dissatisfied.

reviews.title: A balanced frequency response makes the E10 a good budget choice for most people.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 29, 2019
reviews.text: SoundMAGIC E10 In-Ear Headphone Review *Note: This is the first in-ear that I've ever reviewed and the most expensive in-ear I've yet purchased, so I won't have comparisons. This is just what I've heard with my ears and my subsequent conclusions. · Sound Quality: The bass on the E10 is present and not overdone. It's in the grey area where audiophiles may find it too emphasized but average consumers/Beats fans may find it to be not enough. It is very well controlled with decent detail. It isn't too punchy, it isn't too detailed, but it isn't boomy or muddy either. It's fairly clean and tight but could be more musical. If you're a basshead, you will want more bass, and if you are after reference/flat sound, you might want a bit less. I personally would have preferred the bass to be slightly more emphasized and punchier for a more immersive and musical sound. - It's worth noting that if you don't get a seal/correct fit, the bass on these will be quite thin and underemphasized. Make sure you have the right fit before you come to your conclusion. The midrange is balanced and clean. It's not too recessed or too forward, and has good separation from the bass. Vocals are nuanced and relaxed but not so much that they lose their presence. The upper mids seem a bit more emphasized than the low mids. The mids as a whole sound a bit thin. The treble at first was bright to my ears but now sounds pretty smooth and relaxed. It is slightly artificial but has plenty of airiness and space. The soundstage isn't very big but these are in-ears after all. Despite this, they do sound quite open, and never congested/thick. The isolation is good if you can keep the seal/correct fit. · Comfort: These aren't the most comfortable headphones. If you don't like things entering your ear, then you obviously will find these uncomfortable. My personal issue was trying to make sure the seal was in place. I never quite felt like they were in my ear enough, which meant I kept adjusting them to make sure I had the seal. Without a correct seal, the bass loses a lot of presence and emphasis and the headphones sound too bright. · Build Quality: I can't speak to the long term durability of these headphones, but SoundMAGIC says these headphones have a "Unique, all metal earphone construction," which is very impressive for the price. They also claim the cord is "tangle-free," which doesn't seem to be the case. The cable had lots of twists and turns and didn't lay straight after just a few uses. Overall, the build is good for the price. · Accessorization: The accessorization is quite good for the price. There are 7 sets of eartips to help the user find a comfortable fit. They also come with a cable clip and a nice small zippered hard case. · Summary: The SoundMAGIC E10 is a budget in-ear with a balanced sound. The bass is present but not ample, the mids are relaxed but not recessed, and the treble is smooth with just a slight brightness. Getting a correct fit could be tricky for some, and the long-term durability is unknown to me. For most people, these are 4 stars, but for me, they are 3 stars. I would prefer them with a bit more bass and a more comfortable fit. They're just not engaging enough to keep me listening. PROS: · Balanced sound · Airy treble · Good accessorization · Price CONS: · Bass could be more emphasized and engaging · Slightly thin midrange · Slightly artificial treble · Trouble getting a comfortable fit · Small soundstage

reviews.title: Really Nice for the price.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on January 29, 2017
reviews.text: Blown away with the performance of these for the price. I have quite a few in and on ear headphones by various brands such as Sony, AKG and some Grado and have paid ten times what these cost for some but I have to say they really are great for the money. I have looked at them in the past but not really knowing the brand decided to go with others but after owning a pair for a couple of weeks now I honestly think that in my opinion unless you are prepared to pay well over £100 I think you should definitely consider these. They sound nice and natural and can also produce a decent bass if it's supposed to be there, I prefer a natural sound and don't like certain brands that push out bloated bass. These can handle the bass on many of the tracks I have pushed them on very well. I mostly listen to FLAC audio files and they are great for this price and I've struggled to hear any difference between these and some £150 on ear headphones while listening to 16bit FLAC audio. My only gripe is I would have preferred a 90° plug on them but that's about it. There are many great sounding headphones out there and a lot comes down to personal taste but in my opinion for the money you can't go wrong with these gems.

reviews.title: Really great sound, and excellent bang for buck
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on January 14, 2017
reviews.text: Brought these a few years back on the strength of What Hifi's review on them. I was not disappointed at all. I would rate these very highly as the sound is brilliant in my opinion. I wasn’t expecting that much from these because of the £30ish price point. My reference at the time was from a set of Sennheiser CX300II’s (about the same price point) and these outperformed them by a country mile. The mids were rich, with good high notes and a decent base. Sounds were in abundance with excellent clarity. Even compared to a much dearer set of Bose IE2’s I had, these definitely held its own against them. Honestly. I was so impressed I brought another pair. I now have a set of red/back and another black/golds. They come with a zip closure carry case, clip for the wire and alternative size ear plugs for you to change if needed. Build quality wise, the wire is generally tangle free and the plugs are well made. I did manage to bend the jack on the gold pair I have but it still works perfectly. I would honestly recommend that you try these. They are to be the best value earphones I have ever owned.

reviews.title: Great, especially for the price
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on December 11, 2021
reviews.text: Have had these since 2014, and only just started to have the cable coating pull away from the earbud exposing the wire underneath - which is annoying, but considering their age, is something I'll live with. I've generally used these whilst at a desk doing work, not jogging with them or even walked at all I don't think - so they may not have lasted as long with other users, but they've been great for me and I'm only writing a review now as I'm considering getting a new pair. I have had only cheap, included headphones, that come with devices to compare to, so I'm not an expert -but I don't know how much better a headphone/earbud etc can sound at 'diminishing returns' levels of money thrown at them. There was a website I tested these on recently that plays a variety of sound files testing low level frequency, highs, stereo separation, etc. and these played the lowest bass sounds, didn't quite reach the highest (but my 40 year old ears are probably the issue) and generally performed highly in all the tests. The included hard case is still intact. The cable really is tangle free and the best cable I've used. For the price you can't really go wrong.

reviews.title: Absolutely Superb
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on February 11, 2020
reviews.text: I'm no audiophile, but I do like my music and my ears know what they like!! Like most people I've had all manner of ear pods, headphones, speakers (I'm old enough to remember vinyl the first time round!). I must admit, after all the reviews and awards, I was expecting a good pair of headphones, but I was blown away at how good these little gems are. The fitting was great due to the vast array of earpieces that come with the headphones, so finding a pair that fit, I popped on some tunes. Now, this is Spotify, so let's be fair, it's not CD quality, but even so, these headphones are wonderful. It's all subjective, if you want bass banging and not much else, look elsewhere. If you want balance and a lovely clear sound, with detail, crispness, no sharpness and a detail, bearing in mind the constraints of Spotify, these headphones are wonderful, no, they really are, I'm over the moon. Xavier Rudd to The Eagles, Little Peep to Rush.....yup, that eclectic.....for the money, they're amazing, go for it, I'm going to get another pair in case I forget to take this with me...did I mention I'm old enough to remember vinyl first time round....yeah...I forget things....have a great day

reviews.title: Not as good as before
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on September 30, 2022
reviews.text: Bought these to replace old E10s with a frayed cable as the sound quality on those were superb. What has happened? Muted top range, stereo effect is limited, bass end is weak and volume is quieter. My old pair still work and comparing the two sets, no comparison. This new set is inferior in every aspect. For the money they are OK and if I didn't have the old set I would accept them as they were but so disappointed. They are just "limp". There is no punch or power where before the old E10s would smack you and immerse you in a wave of sound that was a pleasure. These, just do a job. Going to try and repair the old cable and keep these as a back up. Overall , disappointing.

reviews.title: It is time to cut the cable.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 9, 2017
reviews.text: I live in a suburb quite far from the city and many of the broadcast station antennas. I purchased the GE 29884 antenna a couple of weeks ago from Amazon. Along with the antenna, I purchased a PCT 4 Port Cable TV/HDTV/Internet amplifier (model PCT-MA2-4P) just in case I need it. I have been trying to "cut the cable" and stop paying expensive cable TV fees for even local basic television stations. In addition to the fees, my cable company switched to a system requiring cable TV boxes that you rent from them for $6/month per box. I have tried other powered indoor antennas and have had miserable experiences with them. Few channels could be scanned and the picture quality was dismal, or heavily pixelated, especially in the daytime hours. The few stations that I could pick up were often unwatchable. So back to cable I went. I decided to try the GE 29884 antenna based on the reviews I read on Amazon. The antenna comes in a fairly small box labelled as Pro Outdoor/Attic Mount Antenna. The installation booklet is small with tiny "mice" type. So you might need to scan in the booklet in order to be able to zoom in on the text and illustrations. All the parts are nicely packaged and are easily identified in the instruction manual. A count of each part type is also given, Prior to installation it helps to layout all the parts including the nuts and screws, the reflector rods, dipole antenna parts, main mast, mounting parts, etc. The installation can be a bit tricky, if you follow the manual. However is you do a search on "GE 29884 antenna assembly", YouTube videos can be found that simplify the assembly process a great deal. It took me about a half an hour to assemble the antenna. One nice thing is that rubber end caps were provided to cap off the dipole rods. The antenna definitely seems to be a quality product. I mounted the antenna in the attic, as high as possible using the provided J-mount mounting hardware and supplied M5 bolts and nuts. I disconnected the coaxial cable from the cable TV provider, and connected it to the antenna's connector located on the main mast. Using a bedroom TV, I then selected "antenna" as the input, and performed a channel scan. A total of 106 channels scanned. Most were crystal clear. Perhaps 3 or 4 were pixelated. Sure many of the channels are trash or of no interest to me (shopping channels, religious, languages I don't speak, etc) but many great channels came in beautifully including all the local channels and sub-channels, movie channels, retro, public, etc. A few audio-only channels were picked up. And I didn't have the amplifier connected. I did wire up the amplifier simply because a signal splitter attenuates the signal from the antenna as you feed the signal to multiple TVs. The 4-port amplifier boosts the signal going to each TV. So far, I've had the antenna for a week and I have not been disappointed. All I can say is "bye bye cable TV company". It is time to cut the cable. The antenna and amplifier will pay for itself in a month or two. Update: 6 weeks later: This antenna works like a charm. I have cut the cord, get no more monthly cable bills, and could not be happier.

reviews.title: Great antenna for the attic
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on December 29, 2019
reviews.text: I am able to pick up a wide range of local signals with this antenna. On occasion when the atmosphere is right I can pick up US broadcasts from hundreds of miles away. It’s rare but it happens. I would not recommend this antenna for an outside installation because I believe it may not hold up well outdoors with the plastic parts it’s made from, but it’s an excellent choice for an attic. It’s a directional antenna and I live in an area where there are 2 transmission towers running north and south of each other. I’m off to the west so if you drew a line from my house to each tower it would look like the letter “V”. However, one transmission tower is much farther away and has weaker signal due to the distance. I chose to point this antenna directly towards the weaker tower so I get all of those channels plus it picks up the channels from the stronger (closer) tower from the side of the antenna. I’m getting all channels. I’ve tried lots of other antennas including a huge 8 bay antenna. This one is my favourite as it gives me the highest signals.

Do not expect this to produce enough signal to split to multiple TVs without a distribution amplifier. That is not the intent of it’s design. A great value. IMO, I would not mount this outdoors. The construction quality is ok but it would never last outdoors in my Canadian climate. I don’t suspect it would last anywhere for too long outdoors. In my attic it will last forever.

Our last one barely covered the edge of our mattress on the end and there was no extra to tuck under like we normally do. But these had plenty of room to tuck under the lip and make neat. The tag on the sheets says “100% bamboo cotton” which is confusing because they say it’s 100% bamboo, so what is the word “cotton” doing there? They are completely different materials. While sleeping in them, they do not have the nice cooling effect bamboo normally has. But what’s worse, is they honestly feel like wool. They are bordering on itchy. My fiancé and I both agree these are the worst sheets we have ever felt. On the plus side, the company was helpful and responded to us in a timely manner.

reviews.title: Not Bamboo!!
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on January 17, 2022
reviews.text: I have had many bamboo sheets in the past. We thought we’d purchase a different color from a different brand, since the brand we usually buy from didn't carry black for king size. HUGE MISTAKE!! I bought these based on the materials saying 100% bamboo viscose, but it’s not bamboo at all. This sheet set feels like linen and cotton mixed. It’s very starchy and rough. Bamboo is soft like butter and has a slinky texture it’s very malleable. My kids live in bamboo clothes I know the texture by feel. This company is robbing people blind by pretending that their sheets are bamboo based and charging prices accordingly. If you see the pictures the creases are imprinted in the material, bamboo doesn’t crease like that. The labels don’t even list the materials, it just says “bamboo sheet”.😡

reviews.title: These sheets are unbelievable!
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on September 15, 2018
reviews.text: I recently purchased these sheets after reading several other positive reviews. I was initially a bit skeptical on whether or not the sheets can really be THAT great, but trusted the other reviews and made my purchase. Let me tell you, they are INCREDIBLE. I've never felt such soft, comfortable sheets on a bed. It's immediately noticeable. The second your skin touches the sheet or pillow, you'll say holy sh*t! My wife (who is not usually one to agree with me on these types of things) very quickly said that she would buy these sheets for every bed in our house. This was after ONE night of sleeping on them. I washed them when I received them and put them straight on the bed. Had an amazing sleep. The quality is unreal, the comfort is incredible, you seriously can't find a better sheet for a better price. These are worth every penny. The king pillow cases are nice and long and fit the longer pillow really well with room to spare, the fitted sheet is easy to put on (you don't have to wrestle with it and the corners won't slide up (super annoying with my old sheets), these fit with a bit of room to play but stay snug and tight to the mattress). Honestly, if you want the softest sheets, buy these. You will not regret it. I'm definitely ordering more, and will not buy any other sheet for my bed again.

reviews.title: Great quality, so soft, best sleep!
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on July 29, 2020
reviews.text: The media could not be loaded. These are the most comfortable, soft, durable and nicely coloured sheets I’ve ever owned! And I’ve had 1000 tc pure Egyptian cotton before... I also have another 100% bamboo sheet set that is around 120gsm from Brielle and they’re great but these are better and a little cheaper by about 15$. These can get wrinkles but I spray a little wrinkle relaxer (which smells so good - I buy from melaleuca because I have sensitive skin) and run your hand over the wrinkled spots and poof! My husband has never cared about/was interested in what type of sheet sets he slept on until now. It’s bamboo all the way for us! We recently spoiled ourselves and got 2 bamboo sheet sets, a weighted bamboo blanket and we have a bamboo duvet cover for the weighted blanket on the way! I still use satin or silk pillow cases to sleep on for my hair and beauty (no wicking of moisture from the face/hair) but from now on I will be only buying these bamboo sheets from hotel direct! I can’t wait till hubby lets me buy more lol I want them in every color 🤩

reviews.title: Furinno 3-Tier Side Table - b/w with white tubes - good for the money
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on October 31, 2022
reviews.text: After buying and giving away numerous small chests of drawers to sit either side of the bed, I decided a table would be better. I tested this with a small table at home and it seemed to work so I began to look for something more appropriate. I landed on this sales page during my search through the options on Amazon. I liked the height - perfect for the side of a bed. I liked the size - not too large so would not get in the way (it isn't a huge bedroom). I liked the idea of a couple of shelves since it would mean I could "share" on different shelves what normally sits cluttered on the top. I decided to take the risk and order 2 of these tables in the black and white, with white tube legs. I felt having contrasting colours set against white bedding and a white headboard would fit nicely. I was right, the two-colour scheme is ideal. Delivery was naturally quick with Amazon and each table was housed in its own box. A quick slice around to remove the sellotape, everything seemed to be packaged neatly so I removed each item. I decided to first try with the black tops on the top and bottom, with the white shelf top in the centre (turns out that was a good choice in my case). Construction - if only all flat-packed furniture was as easy as this to construct. One glance at the instructions to find the order of putting things together and I didn't need them again. A quick dust of the shelves and the first one was ready to sit next to the bed. Perfect. For the second box I decided to time myself. Obviously the construction was identical to the first. From the time I started to open the box to the time I wiped surface dust away was... a mere 8 minutes. Like I said, if only all flat-packed furniture was this easy. The second table went on the other side of the bed, job done, boxes into recycling bin. Although plastic tubes for the legs, they are quite thick and the whole unit is very sturdy. Each piece screws into the one beneath it so it effectively holds itself together. I should imagine it would be just as easy to unscrew parts if ever I wanted to change the top colour of any of the shelves. Negatives - I didn't expect absolute perfection, not for the price these were. However, I did feel that the finish of the white binding could have been much better, especially where it meets white against white. As I said, for the price I didn't expect perfection but given that the binding is an integral part of the design, it could have been applied better. Thankfully, given where the tables are, I doubt if anyone would ever get close enough to inspect. There was a 6" "smudge across the middle of one of the shelves, on the black side. This was clearly done at the factory and no amount of rubbing would shift it. Fortunately, I could use this as a centre shelf with a white top, but it would cause problems if ever I wanted to have all shelf tops in black. As a result of the unnecessary "smudge" that should have been picked up by quality control, and the not-so-good finish with the binding around the shelves, I have removed one star from my review, simply because I felt it best to give future customers an idea of what to look for. Priced at £18.29 at the time of this review for each table, even with the slight flaws I have mentioned, I find the price to be acceptable. They were easy to construct, plenty sturdy enough for bedside tables, will easily hold whatever I need to put on them, and I do like the black and white colouring, it is quite striking. Even with the flaws, I will recommend this product, I doubt if you would get much better for the money and I am satisfied enough.

Many stern-drives have flexible gaskets, called ¡°bellows,¡± that seal the water out where the universal joint, shift cable and exhaust run between boat and drive. Their flexibility allows the drive to trim and turn while under way, but they can dry out and crack due to heat, harsh weather or age.

Bellows are rubber “boots” that seal out water around the exhaust, U-joints and shift cable, while allowing the drive to pivot and tilt.These can wear out and require regular replacement. Specific replacement procedures vary by model, but knowing the basic steps can empower you to change the bellows yourself.

reviews.title: Excellent! Get it.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 11, 2022
reviews.text: In the past, I've seen leather pants at stores for about $200. Way beyond what I care to spend. So, recently, I purchased faux leather pants on Amazon. But I sent them back right away. They squeaked, had an ultra shiny finish, looked like cheap upholstery, and the seams were shoddy -- someone in China even forgot to create the hole for the pants button. I searched Amazon for leather not thinking I would find anything within my budget. When I saw these by Alpha Cycle Gear, they were only 40% more than the faux leather ones. So I assumed they would be better, but not by much. To my surprise, these look like what you would expect for $200. The leather is thick, has a grain, and a matte finish. The button-snap and hook are secure. The inside is lined. The seams are tight. My wide leather belt fits within the loops. And, although other reviewers expressed a different experience, these are the same size as my jeans and they fit perfectly. When I first put them on, they felt a little stiff when walking and, especially, going up the stairs. But, as with any leather product, I can see that I will have to wear them for a while before they break in and start to conform to my shape.

reviews.text: Everything just clicks. I use superglue to secure the stitches after hemming them with a Fiskars scissors. The new flat hook plus snap dual closure sure beats the old single button too. Even came with a spare snap you’ll need a punch die to use. I run an industrial abrasive waterjet metal cutting machine so leather pants are ideal since I can just hose them off at the end of the day and head to a nice cafe. I treat such pants (second purchase of this brand) with Kiwi Scuff Cover every week or two to get rid of abrasion. Sometimes I use a belt but if that needs to be too tight then I switch to suspenders. Otherwise the belt pressure leads to stomach discomfort. This time I bought a size smaller and it was still a bit big so I’ll only need a belt. My old pants were $600 Schott but they were so heavy. No knee joint in the back either, thus the cost along with double thick leather. Not really needed for warmth, just burn outs on a highway.

reviews.title: Good for the price, definitely get value for the price
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 8, 2020
reviews.text: So these are a good value, not great but pretty good... They definitely run small, I am 6'1" 240lbs with a 35 in waist (been losing weight thanks!) In Jean's I wear a 36 waist x 30 inseam and they're baggy on me, so i ordered the 36 waist which says it has a 31.7 inseam and figured I'd cut an 1 & 3/4in or so off the bottom of the legs... the waist is a perfect 35 inches and inseam is a perfect 30 inches so no need to cut and I certainly recommend ordering up a size, also I INSTANTLY recognized what the other reviews said about the button it is NOT sturdy at all and I imagine it will pop off very quickly. They also have a weird cut to them - as tight as the waist is the crotch is a little low for comfort, not terrible but bad enough that it warrants mention. The last negative thing I have to say is that the leather is very thin... it's thick enough that with proper care - saddle soap, conditioner, and light quality waterproofing, I believe it will hold up, but I wouldn't suggest just wearing them right out of the box they will need attention at least once a year if you want them to last; I recommend bickmore saddle soap, bick 4 conditioner, and bickmore silicon free waterproof as a yearly regimen (bickmore is a quality made in usa brand available here on Amazon at reasonable prices). On to the positive points - the leather is, while thin, good quality and the stitching is top notch, the seams are exactly where they should be on a good pair of leather pants to avoid chaffing, one piece front panel no annoying seams at the knees, and the liner feels great against the skin, you don't notice the seams at all. The belt loops feel very sturdy, and I would trust them to hold a holster, even for a good heavy pistol like a full size stainless 1911. In closing - are there better leather pants out there that are thicker, better fitting, and sturdier buttons? Yes Will you pay $150+ for them? Yes you will So for $50 this is a pretty good deal, and if you want leather pants that are easy on the wallet and worth every penny you pay for them you should buy these, just order up a size, 2 if you want to wear denim jeans underneath, and get a good belt because the button IS going to fall off.

reviews.title: Good mouse for FPS games, but outdated in several areas
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 8, 2020
reviews.text: After a few more than a month with it I wanted to describe my experience and why I went back to my G305. Some pros/cons may be personal preference, of course: Pros: -Shape is pretty good. I have a G305 and I dislike how the sides of it are curved inwards and with no curves to assist a good, consistent grip. The S2 is heaven in comparison. I just feel the rear is a little too fat but it may just be the overall size of the mouse. -Feet feel pretty good. Comes with replacement. -Flawless sensor. -Great low profile looks. -No need to install software. Configure DPI and polling rate with the two buttons below the mouse. -Zowie clicks are said to be quite stiff and less crisp compared to other mice from, say, Logitech. They do feel a bit less crisp but they're almost as if not as light as my G305's, which amongst other Logitech mice are also already quite light. -The side buttons are so. much. better than my G305's and just quite good feeling overall. -The scrollwheel is very good when you bind it to something where you don't want to accidentally scroll two or more times since it's hard to do so. Cons: -Feet could be a bit thicker. If you press down the mouse too much (which I fortunately don't do) it could increase friction by a lot since they're so thin. Might last less too because of it. -The coating is a fingertip magnet. Even after thoroughly cleaning it with a microfiber cloth and a especial liquid to remove grease it has few small spots that seem permanently "tainted", and that's just after a month of use. Compare that to my 1 year old G305 that I could cheat someone into thinking it's 100% new. -I thought the slightly bigger size compared to the G305 wouldn't be a big deal and it kinda isn't but it's still a bit of a problem since it restricts me with vertical movement and horizontal movement to a lesser degree. My hands aren't even small, but medium and with a fingertip/claw grip. You would think one of the smallest mice Zowie could offer could fit that niche better since they're all about hand-size/grip variety but I must say they're lagging behind the competition. -Could be a bit lighter in my opinion, although most of the feeling (but not all of it) comes from the size. Even when using AA alcaline batteries with my G305 which puts it at 99g, it somehow still has lighter feel to it compared to the 86g S2. -The cable is outdated compared to many new mice (wireless/shoelace-style cables). If you're any kind of serious about FPS games and unless your sensitivity is very high, you NEED a mouse bungee and even then the cable may still feel annoying sometimes. -The scrollwheel is loud AF and the 16 steps makes it feel awful for scrolling web pages/documents. -70 dollars doesn't feel like a good price.

reviews.text: So i'm on a little mouse spree trying to find the right mouse for my everyday and i'm typically all ergo but i wanted to try an ambi or symmetrical mouse to try. i have a med size hand, i truly found this out when my EC-1b started to feel like i was pushing a dump truck. so i went for the EC-2b, sold by Addice, Inc,; btw super fast shipping! I did a little research and i decided to try the S2. At first i was hesitant about the 58cm width but i like the 120-125mm length so this hit that sweet spot. it's lower profile of 38mm vs the Ec2 was a nice change. it really is a relaxed grip and you feel your palm spoon the bum of the mouse rather nicely. very comfy. The clicks are awesome. The scroll wheel is zowie 16 click. the finish is outstanding. it has a grippier texture, so it's easier to grip off the pad. i really like the zowie models, they are solid and reliable. and all the buttons are on the bottom. So clean! they are a little heavier but for my use, excel can wait that extra sec for me to move the mouse. lol amazing mouse, would def recommend. yay no RGB too :)

reviews.title: Critical reviews are 100% accurate.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 23, 2020
reviews.text: I agree with most of the critical reviews on this mouse. Andrew Vo summed it up very nicely. Zowie isn't adapting fast enough to the market. At a whopping $70 I would expect additional features and improvements. While superfluous, it's always nice when mice have optional RGB. It looks pretty, there's no denying that. Software controls are nonexistent and really should be optional in this day and age. I found myself missing having customizability from my Logitech mouse VERY early on. Cable is the Zowie standard. It's O.K. but has been the same for YEARS. Clicks are nice and stiff, like zowie mice have always been. Side buttons are heavily improved from my previous Zowie mouse (EC2-B). Scroll wheel is abhorrent. It's incredibly loud, hard to scroll, but the click seems okay. Definitely stiff. 82g for the small S2 without cable doesn't match the competition. Mouse feet are decent, but are becoming below standard with Virgin PTFE feet becoming the new "meta." There's just way too much competition for this mouse to sell. Featureless used to be a feature for Zowie, but it's been years of stagnant improvements. If you're a die-hard Zowie fan, the mouse is okay. Bump at the back is particularly high for me, but is personal preference.

reviews.text: Update: the mattress is nice and firm and comfortable and will be very comfortable for a cot or RV bed, but it is clearly not meant for a day bed or a trundle. My wife read the description and ordered it without taking measurements, and now we have a mattress to go on a cot that we don't have, or in an RV that we also don't have. To make matters worse, went to return it and the box will cost $89 to return, bc the box they shipped it in is too small and cheaply made, and we can't compress the mattress well enough to fit it in. reviews.title: Excellent mattress... if you sleep on your back
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 27, 2016
reviews.text: First off, a few details. I'm male, 5'10", about 195lbs. I'm using this mattress directly on a carpeted floor (remodeling the house, longterm project, custom-built bed frame will come later). I am using this mattress every night for sleep, not as an occasional sleeper/guest bed. I learned quickly that results with this mattress will vary. I am a stomach sleeper. I always have been. When I first slept on this mattress on my stomach, I found that my upper torso and my legs were comfortably supported, yet for some reason my waist sank right into the mattress, making for an uncomfortable arch in my spine. The discomfort was subtle, and after a short four hours of being able to sleep, I awoke with substantial discomfort in the small of my back. However, if I lay on my back on this mattress, I am perfectly supported. In fact, if I were a back sleeper, this mattress would be just about perfect. Seeing how trying to return this mattress would have been a nightmare, I decided to keep on using it anyway. It's better than the 2" memory foam futon mattress I've been sleeping on! After about a week, I discovered that the mattress started breaking in some. Sleeping on my stomach, I still get some discomfort in my spine upon waking up, but it's nowhere near as bad as it was originally. I've been trying to convince myself to sleep on my back more, but I tend to roll over onto my stomach while I sleep. So. I can't fault the mattress for being what it is. It is adequately described as medium-firm foam. In order to get a higher quality mattress that would support me, I would probably have to go back to a spring-type mattress or something. But this will work for now. And if it breaks in better over time, I'll try to update my review to let people know. Other observations: It's 72" long. If you count the extra fabric used to sew the seams, it is right about 74". But the foam is only 72". The packaging was simple, no paperwork inside. The bed arrived rolled up tight in plastic and it expanded to full dimensions in about 30 minutes. If I just sit up on the mattress, my bottom sinks right through it, but there's enough springiness to it that although my tailbone touches the floor, most of my weight is offset so there's no pressure on my tailbone. This mattress does have some level of memory, as I stated above. It's 'breaking in' and becoming more comfortable for me to sleep on. But I can see no evidence of it becoming permanently misshapen, and I do sit on this mattress for a few hours every day in the same spot, not just sleep on it. The fabric around the mattress is soft enough that I'd be able to sleep on it directly, but I use a sheet just to keep it from getting stained up. Overall, I'd say the quality is good. Well worth the price for what it is. And as I said above, if I were a back sleeper instead of a stomach sleeper, this mattress would be just about perfect.

reviews.title: takes time to prep it right, but worth it.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on April 9, 2018
reviews.text: I ordered this mattress protector for my boyfreind who had a run-in with bedbugs a few years ago and is still a bit paranoid about it. He had just purchased a new queen sized pillow top mattress a couple months prior, and I figured this would be a good time to protect it and a chance to give him some extra peace of mind. To be clear, about the time this came in, we found what we think was a loner bedbug in or close to maturity, and I had gotten a few bites over the course of a week while staying there and sleeping on the new bed. Between these protectors (I bought one for the boxsprings and one for the mattress), a heat gun, and copious amounts of Diatemacious Earth (spelling? It's a fine dust of super small sharp particles that essentially cut into insects' joints and bodies, killing them), the bug was never seen again. I would highly recommend the dust to anyone fighting bugs, in conjunction with these covers. I would recommend opening the package and examining the seams - all of them, including the zipper - and look over the fabric for any defects. There were several reviews that complained about loose stitching or tears. These are made in huge factories on machines at a ridiculous pace - sometimes things get a little out of line at that kind of speed and scale, so it never hurts to check. Ours were both great. Also, some complained about the 'chemical' or 'plastic' smell. They are a bit strong, but running them through the washer and dryer first, as suggested on the package, takes care of that. We washed the two covers together, with nothing else. Initially, we left them zipped to avoid damage to the fine coil of the zipper, but in hindsight, I would say lust leave it unzipped all the way. When it came to the spin cycle, the closed zippers and the water resistance of the covers created giant flappy water balloons that kept throwing the washer out of balance. We unzipped them to release the water and it was all fine. They will take a ridiculous amount of time to dry. Just keep the heat low, be patient, and take them out to rearrange them in the dryer again to help them dry evenly. Some reviewers wrote about their covers melting or becoming brittle form drying - because they turned the heat too high. Just chill. You had to wait for the thing to ship to your house, waiting a couple hours with the dryer isn't gonna hurt you. We put them both on easily with two people, but with some patience and gracefullness, a single person may be able to do it. Having two people makes it easier to prevent tears in the cover after installing, while moving the mattress back into place. I gifted a protector for boxsprings and a mattress to my boyfriend for his new bed 4 months ago. He had a run in with bed bugs a few years that left him mildly traumatized. If you want a guaranteed rant, just ask him about it - On second thought, don't go there. We don't even go there. But, back to the covers.... I read a lot of reviews - mostly great, and several pretty bad - before purchasing. We had no problems with either of our covers. Here's what we looked out for based on the negative reviews (and common sense): - Check all seams for rips, loose stitches, and the like, one seam at a time so you don't miss anything. - Check over the fabric...all of it...for any rips, snagged threads, holes, or the like. Do this right out of the package so you can use the crease lines to help track your progress. - Run your covers through the washer with a bit of soap to neutralize the 'chemical' smell. Unzip it all the way to prevent the formation of a giant flappy water balloon that with try to strangle the agitator as your washer jumps about like a wild rodeo bull (yep, this happened). Unzip it all the way to prevent damage from the zipper getting pulled open, in case the two sides try to go opposite directions. - CHECK THE HEAT SETTING ON YOUR DRYER - Turn it down so you don't risk melting any of the synthetic materials. If it feels like you're taking a ridiculous amount of time to run it through and you're starting to feel like you're worrying too much, then YOU"RE DOING IT RIGHT! Take it out and fluff it and flip it around to help it dry evenly and (slightly) faster. I think we ran our covers through, like, 4 dryer cycles.... - Have two people to help put it on. It goes fairly easy and quick with a bit of teamwork and a plan, and will help prevent potential snags or rips from tugging. We slipped the cover over one end and slid it into place, then zipped one side before laying it down. We than lifted the zipped side up so we could straighten out the bottom of the cover in order to zip up the other end. Laid it down once more to zip the last side, and put the mattress/boxspring in place. - Be careful with the zipper. Gently tug your fabric into place so that the two sides of the zipper are close to each other and aligned. The zipper is small and fine so it can create a good bug barrier... Be nice to it, and it should zip just fine. Ours did have a couple "sticky patches" where it didn't quite want to zip. Just gently tug and coax the zipper pull, or unzip a ways and try again. If frustrated, walk away. It's not worth potentially busting that zipper after all the time and money you've spent on it thus far. - If you already have bedbugs, understand that this cover is not some magical kryptonite that eradicates bugs by simply existing in the same room. It can only kill bugs trapped inside, on an already affected mattress by trapping them in there until they starve (about a year or something crazy). Diatemacious (sp?) Earth will kill any bug it comes in contact with. Try using this in conjunction with your covers.

It's not a memory foam, it's not thin, it's a basic mattress and width, height, etc. We had another brand of recommended allergen (recommended by the doctor our child sees for allergies) barrier mattress protector. It did not zip all the way around actually - it was just one that fit on top of the mattress and well over the sides to underneath - good elasticity. It just wore out over time, because we washed it often. But we had it for years. It is no longer available through the supplier we bought it from so I ordered this one, and figured it would be great as it zips completely over the mattress. I can't really attest to the long term use of it - as it did not fit our mattress properly and just didn't seem to work well. The fitted sheet we use didn't fit well over it and with our bed (a loft bed) it just didn't really work out. It was also no where as durable (fabric wise) as the other fabric we were used to - this one felt thinner, and my son was sniffling the next day. We tried for a few days, running the air purifier and it didn't make any difference. Thankfully Amazon allowed us to return it. Just did not work out for us. My son's skin gets bad if he's suffering from his allergies and it was bad. This might be very effective for bed bugs I don't know. Our allergy doctor said we don't need the full encasement for allergies (dust mites) so I think I'll go back to finding a thicker one that doesn't cover the whole mattress. The shifting around and ill fitting cover (I get it has to fit various sizes) just didn't work here.

reviews.title: BEWARE!! No-Spill is NOT responsive to warranty claims!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 13, 2021
reviews.text: I have quite a few No-Spill containers, not all of which are pictured. They probably range from 3-5 years old. A few years ago I had a problem with the nozzle (lid) on one not screwing down tight for some reason - it acted like a stripped screw in that it would only tighten so far, then "slip" and start retightening again. Note that the nozzle doesn't fit flat on the can. I forget now whether I called or wrote the company at the time, but I *finally* got someone to respond, a guy who was 'on the road' and wasn't very responsive. After a few back and forths of "try this, try that" and un-returned contacts I just gave up and decided that I just wouldn't fill that can as full as the others. Eventually, although upset about the situation, I bought a new nozzle or two. NOW, I have a *few more cans* that are in the same predicament. (I seem to recall that the man I spoke a few years ago said that the plastic of the can and that of the nozzle are dissimilar and expand/contract at different rates once exposed to fuel) So I sought out replacement nozzles (lids) and saw them here on Amazon (less expensive) as well as from the company, so I bought four of them. Once they arrived I tested all four of them with full containers, both tilting them and turning them upside down - as as I often do when filling my vehicles. ALL FOUR leaked. (I also tested my years-old cans in the same way and none leaked) In addition, the new green button, which I didn't notice when I ordered the nozzles, is MUCH harder to push. So... I called Amazon and arranged to return them, telling them what I had done, and clearly noting that the nozzles smelled of fuel since I tested them. The customer service guy didn't consider that a problem, asked me whether I wanted to replace them or just return them, and I told him that I just wanted to return them. In the meanwhile, I still have at least three cans with nozzles I can't rely on/which spill fuel, so I thought I'd contact No-Spill and see what they had to say. I shouldn't have bothered. On December 28th I wrote to No-Spill via their web contact form, and ALSO left a message on their voicemail. By the way, here's what their website says about responsiveness: "Please use our Contact Form for questions or comments. All inquiries will be addressed within 24 hours." Yeah, right. Here's the note I sent: I own quite a few (around 20) No-Spill 5 gallon diesel and gasoline containers, every one of which was bought after 2010. In the past few years, I've had trouble with leaking nozzles due to the nozzles not fitting the top of the can properly - they were angled instead of sitting flat at the point where the nozzle meets the lip of the can. At that time I pursued the matter, but there was a notable delay in someone at No-Spill getting back to me, he was traveling, etc. so I ended up just buying new nozzles. More recently, I've started to have the same trouble with other cans, so earlier this month I decided to buy more nozzles since my leaking ones are out of warranty. I bought four new ones on Amazon because the cost was less than buying directly from No-Spill. I've just spent the last half-hour or more assessing the new nozzles (different, harder to push green button model) for fit and leak resistance. ALL FOUR leaked from the nozzle area when the cans were turned upside down. I called Amazon, and they've sent me a label to return them, but that doesn't solve my problem, since the old leaking cans (nozzles) leak when fueling our cars, and as previously stated, the new ones leak when turned upside down. My problem is this: I'm not about to reorder more new nozzles from Amazon (or directly from No-Spill) unless I have a reasonable expectation that the new ones won't leak. I'd like some help in getting a solution to my leaking nozzle problem. Please give me a call and thank you. P.S. - I've also left a voicemail message about my issues. ******** The other day I called and left another message, noting my earlier attempt at contacting them. As I type this more than TWO WEEKS since my first communcations, I still have heard nothing. BEWARE!!! Although when the cans/nozzles work, they're great, there's no way in (that really hot place) that I would buy any more products from No-Spill. If you decide to buy this product anyway, I **strongly* encourage you to give them a thorough test (including first pressing the button while the can is upright) before deciding whether or not to keep them. DO NOT count on No-Spill being responsive to warranty claims.
