reviews.title: Some Assembly Required
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 2, 2017
reviews.text: Before you order this scooter, make sure that you have all necessary tools, or buy it with sufficient lead time needed to take it to a bike shop for assembly. You may consider this a toy but it will very likely be used on Public Street and your child’s life may be at risk if not assembled correctly. Tools Needed: 1. 6mm Allen wrench 2. An adjustable wrench or 9, 10, 14 & 15 mm box end wrenches or sockets 3. Cable cutters or sharp scissors or utility knife 4. Air pump or compressor 5. Optionally pliers, super glue, lock tight, grease, small shrink tube lighter and gloves I paid for this scooter myself and was not compensated in any way for this review. First, it is much larger than a standard kick scooter. It will easily handle riders in excess of 150 lbs. It is a heavy scooter and may be too big for a child under age 7. The box clearly states “Age 8+”. There is no provision for folding and I have to put the rear seat down to get it in a standard hatchback car (Nissan Versa). Because it is bigger and has nice 12” wheels, it glides over most bumps, cracks, and irregularities. Large potholes and slotted storm drain covers are still serious hazards. Packaging was very good. The box indicated that it should not be placed on its side and did not show any signs of having been dropped or damaged. The scooter had all parts zip tied to the frame and was a little challenging to pull up out of the box. I used wire snips to cut off all zip ties and removed the paper and plastic wrapping to inspect the parts. The wheels are delivered totally flat. An air pump or compressor will be needed. Be forewarned, the clamp on my hand pump that holds the chuck on the valve stem would not fit between the hub and rim. I had to use my compressor. If your bike pump doesn’t fit, take the wheels to a service station for air prior to attaching them to the frame. Construction quality is on par with any low priced consumer good mass produced in China. In my instance, the rear brake pads were tightened out of alignment with the rim. You will very likely need to adjust the brake pads. As other reviewers noted the brake cable ferrules are not crimped correctly and will fall off. Put a drop of super glue in it and tap it in place or just wrap the wire end in electrical tape, or use a short piece of shrink tube on the end. The handlebars are not attached. You will need to remove 4 Allen bolts and position the handlebars. I was able to do this single handed, but a second person to hold them in place would ease this task. Once the handlebars are positioned and tightened the brake cables will need to be attached. There are two cables on the right for the rear brake and one coming up out of the stem tube to be attached to the left brake handle. Adjusting the brakes is not difficult, just take your time and tighten everything when done. 1. Loosen the nut clamping the cable at the rear calipers. 2. Route the two cables attached to the right brake lever through the handlebars and down to the upper cable stop. 3. Screw the alloy barrel adjusters all the way into the upper cable stop and slide the beaded end sideways into the detangler. 4. Hold the rear brake calipers closed against the wheel rim and pull the brake cable taught at the calipers. 5. Tighten the caliper cable clamp nut. 6. Adjust the brakes at the calipers, detangler and at the lever as necessary so that the wheel turn freely and stops easily when the brake lever is engaged. Now on to the front brakes, 1. Loosen the nut clamping the cable at the front calipers 2. Push the cable up into the head tube until you have enough slack to reach the left brake lever. 3. Screw the barrel adjuster most of the way in and align the slots in the barrel adjuster, nut and break lever. 4. Slip the cable end into the round opening under the break lever and feed the cable into the slot on the barrel adjuster. 5. Turn the barrel adjuster ½ turn. 6. Hold the front brake calipers closed and pull the cable tight. 7. Tighten the caliper cable clamp nut 8. Adjust the barrel adjusters at both ends until the front wheel turns freely and stops easily when the brake lever is engaged. Assembly took me exactly 40 min from the time the box arrived to first test ride. I provided detailed instructions on what is required to assemble this scooter so that potential purchasers are able to make an informed decision prior to purchasing. My daughter’s first scooter was a $20 scooter. This was to gauge her interest and ability. She didn’t use her scooter much until about age seven. In the past 3 months, she has been using it every day and has worn it out. Since this is not a review of that scooter, I will not go into detail. Suffice it to say she couldn’t keep up with her friends and small bumps caused tumbles that left her fearful of sidewalks and some streets in our neighborhood. Now with the Mongoose she has confidence and can keep up with her friends. All of the kids prefer her scooter over any other brand or style. As a parent, I would rate it 4 stars, for size and build quality but my daughter says “it is a solid 5” and since she is the one who rides it every day I gave it a five. After her first test ride I removed the axel pegs from the rear, as she did hit them occasionally with her ankle when kicking. I later reattached them to the front axle, but I am not sure if I will keep them on or not.

reviews.title: GREAT SCOOTER, BUT, ONLY IF you are an experienced bike mechanic.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on October 1, 2021
reviews.text: Once I finished assembling the scooter and getting it ready, it is a truly great scooter for the price. It is a thing of beauty (florescent pink), rock solid, steady and tracks straight. My 7 year old even prefers this one to her electric scooter. I weigh more than its weight limit yet it handles me with the greatest of ease (I needed to break-in the wheels' bearings/cones/races quickly). The price is VERY GOOD for it's looks, construction and selection of materials. It is an excellent scooter and will be very durable. BUT ONLY because I have worked on bicycles and scooters for over 50 years. Now here's the BAD news: It came well packaged in a well padded box. The manufacturer took great care packaging this little beauty. Once I started to put it together, I discovered that who ever assembled this thing at the factory must have been a totally incompetent employee. I needed a great of the Special Bicycle Tools I have to assemble, fix, adjust, modify and re-adjust to make this scooter go to its potential. A person who does not have a great deal of bicycle mechanic experience would have had to pay a pro to put this thing together. It took me several hours of labor to get this scooter functioning properly. So you may want to inquire what your local shop rates are before you buy. Here are some of the issues I encountered: 1) The headset bearings/races were very loose and needed special wrenches to adjust. The lock nut was loose too (safety issue). 2) The wheel bearings were seriously over tightened and the wheels would barely spin. It would have been a miserable experience for a child to get this moving and then it would not stay in motion when gliding. I needed special wrenches to loosen the cones to make it usable. Then after a few hours of use, I adjusted the cones again. Now it rolls like heaven (for the price range that is). 3) The brake calipers were crooked and I needed a special tool to align them with the wheels (it required a special tool to bend them safely). 4) The break pads were all either loose, crooked, and/or rubbed on the tires. The pads felt oily and would not have provided safe braking, so I used 100 grit sand paper to give them some grip for safe braking. The brake pads were a safety issue. 5) The brake cables both were grossly mis-set and they were not tightened to the calipers. One cable was 4 inches too long. Both cable end caps fell off into the shipping box. I had to use a cable cutter, put on new cable end caps, and use a crimper. The rear cable housing was pulled so far forward that it kinked at the adjustment barrel. The brake cables were a safety issue. 6) The brake cable adjustment barrels weren't even screwed in to the calipers! The calipers were not properly tightened to the frame and were mounted crooked. That means the brakes would have been always rubbing on one side of the wheel. It would be like having a partially applied brake at all times. 7) The handlebar stem bolts were partially inserted into their holes for shipping (and safe keeping until later assembly). Two of the bolts were cross threaded and crooked. Thankfully they weren't forced too far into the holes and I managed to get them in straight. If you are a bicycle mechanic enthusiast or pro, by all means, buy this scooter! Otherwise you will NEED to go to a bike shop for assembly and adjustments (repeated adjustments). Nothing says screw you better to your friendly local bike shop owner than buying online and then asking your local shop to fix your problems huh? Bottom line. Heck yeah I would get another one of these scooters. I am strongly considering the adult version of this for myself (for occasional use). If you are not a mechanic and try to assemble this one yourself, it will likely be unsafe and most certainly miserable for a small child get into motion and keep it there. Given the brake rub and over tightened wheel bearings, this scooter would not be fun for a child and likely end up just taking space in your garage. Nothing drives people away from cycling and scooter sports faster than mal-adjusted human powered vehicles. Good luck on your decision!

Voilà, ce sont de bons pinceaux mais je ne vois quand même rien qui justifie le prix actuel de 67,92 €, pour 4 pinceaux en poils synthétiques et de surcroît fabriqués en Chine, où la main-d’œuvre reste moins chère qu’en France. Je ne comprends pas ce prix, et suis bien embêtée pour mettre une note. Je mets donc « bien » : 3 étoiles.

Decent size and sturdier than I thought it would be. My daughter has about 6 clothes on the rod, some room for more, and lots of accessories and other clothes in the baskets, with additional room to add more items. Assembly: I would suggest sitting down and going over the assembly instructions and pieces before getting started. Make sure you're getting the hanging rod on the side of the wardrobe it's supposed to be on, etc. I had it put together in 30 minutes once I got started, but that was reviewing instructions first and laying the pieces out so I knew which way was frontward/topward on all the pieces (the assembly instructions don't identify top/bottom or front/back on the pieces). Save yourself some trouble here and do this as well. I saw several places once I got started building where things could've been put on backwards and wouldn't have figured it out until the very end. BUT, even if you put it together backwards, you can go with it and keep it that way as it would still function, but won't be as aesthetically pleasing (I think the stock pictures on this website are proof of putting it together backwards; if you look at the Emily Rose armoire, you'll see a piece that runs along the very bottom to hide the gap, this wardrobe has the same piece, as well as the other piece previously mentioned). The instructions also say to manually screw it together. Don't even try; you'll never get the screw into the rod for the clothes. Save yourself some time and trouble and break out the power drill.

reviews.title: beautiful ingredients; but didnt like the scent
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on March 23, 2016
reviews.text: * About the smell: It really doesn't smell much like roses. My first thought was that this smells like a cross between an artificial sweet candy and washing up liquid (like Fairy liquid soap). After use, it hardly leaves a scent behind; the only smell it leaves is a faint, almost imperceptible soapy smell with a slightly off-putting glycerin-y, ever-ever so subtle vomit-like smell. It's not the best smell in the world for me personally. I won't be ordering this scent again in the future. * About the consistency: The texture is quite runny / watery / liquidy, but a little goes a long way. Even if you put a small drop on your hand it lathers really nicely. * About the bottle top: Be sure yours comes sealed to ensure no tampering. The bottle top is a simple white plastic screw on top, with a pouring hole. A pump head would have been an improvement and would have been more user friendly for hand wash / body wash usage. * About the ingredients: This is the main reason I bought this soap: really health-conscious ingredients - no nasties in there. The only potential nasty, Potassium hydroxide, is only used for saponification and is entirely used up in the processing so that there is none of that chemical left in the end-product. Very happy with the ingredient list. * How it makes my skin feel: Washing my hands with it, it makes my skin feel waxy clean and a little dry-feeling at first, but that feeling dissipates within about 5 minutes and you're left with nice-feeling skin. * About using it: - Handwash: You can either use this as-is, using a small drop per wash, or you can decant this into a bottle, 1 part soap to 1 to 4 parts water (as desired). - Body wash: Again, you only need a small amount. If you use this in the shower, you'd only need small sploosh of the soap. For getting a good lather I found it best to use it neat in my hands rather than on a washcloth / shower-puff / loofah / sponge. If you want, you can decant a small amount of this soap into a bottle and a bit of argan oil and / or jojoba oil to it to make it a little more nourishing and moisturizing to the skin. - Dish soap: A little expensive for a dish soap, but if you don't like the smell on your body, you can use this to wash your dishes by hand. It's got healthier ingredients in it than your conventional mainstream dish soaps. - Shampoo: If you use this as shampoo it can leave a tangly feel. The official website recommends to pair it with an acidic conditioning rinse to avoid this. - Shaving lubricant: I read on a website to dilute one part soap with two parts water to use as a shaving lubricant.

reviews.title: Great oven, horrible instructions, HUGE price increase just before Christmas!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 10, 2020
reviews.text: I've had this toaster oven for about a month now and, after doing some scavenger hunting on the internet for instructions and a little trial and error, I think it's going to pretty much replace my regular gas oven. Let me save you a little frustration as to the lack of instructions, especially pertaining to the convection feature. If you select the "Bake" setting, the convection feature is activated. There is no way to turn it off, which is actually fine. What I have discovered is, if I'm baking baked goods (cookies, muffins, etc) you need to decrease the baking temperature by 25 degrees or reduce the baking time by about 25 %, or both. If you reduce the temp, start checking for doneness about 3/4 of the way through the baking process. If I'm baking a casserole, which contains more liquids or the like('cream of' soups, eggs, cheese, etc) I use the recommended temperature in the recipe and let it cook the full amount of time. I made a tuna noodle casserole last week and it was perfect using the recipe exactly as written. I haven't used the broil feature for meat yet, so I don't have a point of reference for that feature and, as I'm single and just make toast in a regular 2 slice toaster, I also don't have a review for the toast feature (I don't need 8 slices of toast at once.) What I LOVE about this oven is being able to use my regular pans! I had a smaller toaster oven before and got frustrated by having to buy special pans for it. I ended up buying a lot of disposable aluminum pans. With this oven, I can use all of my regular pans (I have several Pampered Chef ones that I wasn't able to use in the old toaster oven) except for a couple of my larger baking stones. So far, everything has baked so much more evenly than in my full sized gas oven that I'm absolutely thrilled. So, as far as the way the oven functions and the results I've had when cooking with it, I am very satisfied with this oven. The only negative comment that I have about it is that the instructions are almost non-existent. An individual shouldn't have to do 2 hours of research online and watch youtube videos to learn how to properly use this product. They really need to include an actual instruction manual, with a few recipes included for each feature of the oven, instead of a big sheet of pitiful basic instructions that are written in about a dozen different languages. I think that most of the negative reviews that I've seen could have been avoided if this were the case. Does the outside of the oven get hot? Yes, it's a toaster oven, not an insulated range, so move it away from the wall. The crumb tray slides into the slots underneath the OUTSIDE of the oven, it doesn't go inside and I believe this is the reason that so many people are saying it never gets hot enough. The convection feature comes on and stays on when baking, there's no way to shut it off. All of this could should be explained in an actual instruction manual. My last comment pertains to the price. At $67 in November, this oven was a great value. Less than a month later, it's $96!!!! Had it been this price originally, I'm not sure I would have purchased it. So, my review is A for the the oven itself, D for the lack of instructions and the $30 price hike just before Christmas.

reviews.title: Just received my third one!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on February 11, 2022
reviews.text: I have just received my third oven of this model. The other two lasted about four years each with everyday use. Not just toasting in the morning, but this is my actual oven for cooking. I never use my big oven. I am a baby boomer and I have come to terms with things not lasting like they used to. That being said, this oven has served me well. I got it originally for the wide oven capacity. For the two of us, this is perfect. I have read the other reviews, and yes when it was getting older, I noticed it became loud on the cooking part, not the toaster. And then finally the oven part went, and only the toaster worked. But I didn't care if it played a tune while it cooked, I still liked it. No glass ever shattered, and I didn't notice the temperature being subpar either. It cooked chicken, pork, casseroles, everything, or I would not have gotten a third one. For the most part I was quite pleased with it. I noticed they now have a newer version with a air fry option. Nope, I know better. I just stuck with what worked. I don't need any fancy add ons. Just one more thing to break. My guess is it doesn't air fry like a dedicated air fryer anyway. One more thing, I gave it one star because the grate cleans ok and the tray, which I cover with foil anyway. I stopped trying to clean the cavity of a toaster oven long ago, so no. Never bothered. I just bought new. So there you have it. UPDATE: I like honest reviews so I am going to put this here. Having had my new oven for several weeks now, I notice the cooking/baking selection makes a loud noise. Annoyingly loud. My other ones did when they were on the way out. This one is new and it is making the noise. The toaster, broil selections are quiet. Just the low sound of a ticking timer. Needless to say, after this one, I am going to try to find something else. It is too bad because I loved the width of this one. But I cannot listen to this oven. I have to put the TV on louder since my kitchen/family room is one area. I will not stop using it, but to say it is annoying is an understatement. So if this seems like something you can stand, go ahead. The oven cooks quickly, is wide and I like everything else about it. But it WILL be my last because of the noise. Color me disappointed.

reviews.title: Good but pricy dish rack.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 22, 2022
reviews.text: A good dish rack is one that is spacious enough, provides the proper grooves and slots to hold your dishes apart as they dry, is solid steel construction to provide the framework needed to hold said dishes, keeps the water flow aimed toward the sink drain, is itself easy to clean, and does not look like an eyesore. This dish rack naturally does all of that with the exception of maintaining the water flow toward the drain. I had to position the rubberized plastic drip tray at a steeper angle towards the sink by positioning the legs closest to the sink above the tray to get the water from collecting in the tray. The utensil cup slotted separator lid is a nice addition, but it does slide around a lot because it is held in too loosely. It is annoying that all the forks, spoons, and knives fall out all together if the one you are pulling out gets caught on the slot. Other than those hiccups, is the price point. It should not cost an arm and a leg to have a dish rack. Automatic dish washers are expected to be expensive, not a dish racks. I hope the price of Kitchenaid products in general fall. The premium brand name mark- up based on prestige alone is a big turnoff for me. Overall, the deal I got on Amazon’s Black Friday deals were decent enough for me to purchase since I was using an old rusty framed dish rack for years and needed something safer and nicer looking.

reviews.title: Not really worth it
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 5, 2020
reviews.text: Short version: The ONLY reason to buy these is if you're seriously committed to reducing waste. First off, understand you are not getting 3 filters, but 1 filter in 3 different versions: Coarse, Fine, and Very Fine. If you want a direct replacement for standard paper filters, the VF is the one you want. So you basically get 2 backup filters that aren't exactly what you want, but will work. Using these things is problematic on multiple fronts: 1 - They're fragile. So make sure you've got a place to clean & store them where they're not going to get roughed up. 2 - They're metal. Push 200 degree water through one and guess what temperature the filter is now? (see next two points) 3 - They add steps and complicate the process. Let's be honest, even if you love Aeropress (like I do), the downside is its got a lot of pieces and a lot of steps. Now you're adding 1+ pieces, another item to clean and keep track of. 4 - To keep things efficient, I like to 'pump & dump' immediately -- as soon as I push through the coffee, I dump the grounds puck into the trash and rinse the pump so its ready to go for next time. But now I can't just dump the puck because then I'm dumping the metal filter into the trash as well. But I can't pull the filter off because its 200 degrees! So I have to juggle half-dumping while trying to catch the filter in cap and then rinse all of it (including half the grounds) in the sink. Alternatively, I can set the pump in the sink to cool and come back later. Either way, its all just more work and more annoyance. So the real question is why would you even head down this path? Save cost? Ok, but you're spending more time/effort than you are saving money so I think this is a bad trade. Better flavor? Maybe. I sometimes think I get a better finish -- sometimes not. YMMV. Reduce waste? Well, there you are -- if that's you're goal, you've got a solution. While I like that goal, the complications in the process (and the fact I can't buy 3 of the exact filter I want) make it not worth it for me. One final note: If you use the VF filter, keep it clean. Otherwise it gets clogged and very hard to push. If you're not a cleaner, you may prefer the fine filter which takes longer to clog.

reviews.text: Generally I would only review an item if it is really good or terrible. Happy to report that this item is brilliant. reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on May 20, 2020
reviews.text: When I initially got these, I went straight for the mesh filter, which handles finely ground coffee perfectly.. Then I obtained some “Bird and Wild” coffee for the RSPB great birdwatch. When I came to try this, the water sluiced through the mesh, leaving a weak brew. I had an initial grumble, but then remembered there were two other filter sizes. Counterintuitively, the coarser filters stopped the sluicing (I’m assuming it’s because the larger holes trap the larger particulates, forming part of the filtering). Mystery solved! Coarse filters for coarse grinds, fine mesh for very fine grinds (I tend to drink lavazza, which is very finely ground). I’ve now had hundreds of mugs from these filters, and no sign of wear or degrading, and no damage to the aeropress either. The saving on paper is admittedly minor, but they’re great filters that give you the flexibility to get the best out of your coffee when used well.

reviews.title: Great for individual circuits in your load center.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on June 23, 2020
reviews.text: I always struggled to measure individual circuit current in crowded load centers (breaker panels). Clamp meters that can fit at the breaker are far and few between, so you're typically fighting to separate the wires AND trying to read the display at odd angles. With this CA-60, I can clamp the wire right where it leaves the breaker and view the reading on my DMM. And this was the primary reason for the purchase and I'm plenty happy. It is adequate for that purpose given the fact that without knowing the power factor, better accuracy isn't going to do any good. However, for electronics use, this may not be what you are looking for. The accuracy example given in the manual is a pipe dream! I experimented extensively and under certain tongue arrangements you can obtain some pretty good results, but I found it more of a case of maybe 2 out of 5 tries where I could get this to line up with reality (I have calibrated equipment that can accurately resolve better than 0.001mV and 0.001mA). Below 1A it really starts to stray and below about 200mA the readings are simply too random to be of any use. In almost all current ranges, it cannot output anything more accurate to your DMM than about +/- 5mV, which translates to +/- 50mA (0.05A). Real world, I think I would intrinsically trust it to within 100mA (0.1A). Yes, you can tease out much better results, but I'm not carrying tons of equipment along to verify the measurements every time! There is the popular UT210E which has a 2A range that is typically accurate in the single digit mA range. So if you need low-current capability, that might be a good choice. But it can't go where the CA-60 can... The overall quality seems good. The plastic feels solid, although the 9V battery door is a weak point. Made in Taiwan. UPDATE: I was able to obtain better DC results by following some specific steps: - avoid noisy (EMI) environments - zero the meter by holding the button down for about 5 seconds - make sure the wire being clamped is not floating, so have it connected to ground or similar. If it is floating, the meter will pick up interference from the wire when you go to zero the reading. - absolutely do not move the meter AT ALL once it is zeroed. With this I was frequently able to obtain 1mV (10mA) accuracy for low current measurements. High current measurements are still frequently off by around 0.1A as stated above. Picked up a Fluke 771 to be able to get the ultra-low range. It's a lot more expensive but is in a different league. For anything under 100mA, it is the way to go.

reviews.title: Totally worth the money in every way! Awesome set that is of super high quality!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 20, 2019
reviews.text: This set is pretty fantastic in every way, and it is one of the best tool purchases I have ever made. It was not expensive by any stretch of the imagination, at least not for this level of superb construction, design, and overall quality and so I cannot recommend it enough. The handle of the driver feels great in the hand and you can immediately feel that it is a solidly built tool that seems like it will last quite some time and put up with a good amount of use along the way. The turning action when you are actually using the device, combined with the magnetic nature of the tip of the driver and the bits, means that it is far easier to use with even the tiniest of screws than I could have ever expected prior to buying this item. It is awesome and incredibly effective in that respect. No more frustration trying to place one of those super, super tiny screws into place and get it threaded correctly in a confined tiny space, which is so helpful if you have big fingers like mine that are tough to get into the spaces needed to get the screws started. The magnetism of the bits makes quick work of that because you can put the screw on the bit ahead of time and then guide it down in to its correct spot, no fingers needed. Overall the magnetic aspect is just a nice feature and makes the process of doing any highly detailed work with tiny parts that much more intuitive and easy to complete. All the bits are machined with precision and there are literally no flaws in any one of them, nor are they made of such a weak metal that deform upon using them with some force to dislodge a stuck bolt or screw, like so many other less quality versions of this type of item are known to do. Even the most pointed, tiny little philips this kit contains is absolutely perfectly shaped, and as a whole the entire set of bits are definitely not built by a factory with marginal quality control standards. Someone took pride in what they were making, or maybe a precision machine made them automatically without any human input, but either way they are very high quality. The other accessories are of almost as good of quality as the driver set and bits are. I am referring to the tweezers, anti static charge wristband, the plastic pry tools, and other items included that are not in the actual center box that holds the driver and bits and extension part. There was one point of wear that I did notice and that was with the pry tools. The plastic ones that come in the set are made of a softer plastic than i expected, so don't do what I did and try to pry apart something that was quite difficult to do because it marked up the tip of one of them with some nicks and scuffs. The product worked correctly did exactly as it was supposed to, but it was more about the job I was using it for was probably better suited to something made of metal. I noticed a similar thing happen to the tweezers which one pair comes to an extremely fine (and sharp) point, and when I used the point to try and move something I probably shouldn't have, the super thin metal tips bent ever so slightly to one side. It was a super easy fix though as i just bent them back into place and they were good as new. Basically the point I am getting at is the pry tools and the tweezers are not made of indestructible materials and can show wear and tear rapidly if not used the way they are supposed to be used, which is precisely what I did before learning my lesson quickly and stopping short of actually causing any real lasting damage to the tools. I recommend this item wholeheartedly, and I have only ever written a few amazon reviews. This isn't typically my style or way of doing things on here. So for me to even write a review at all means it is something that I feel passionately enough about to take the time to write this all out. So you can see that it has to be something that I really would like others to know too and hopefully my thoughts on an item could help inform their purchase decisions if at all possible. Anyways, thanks for reading this and I hope y'all enjoy the kit as much as I do!

reviews.title: Both the precision screwdriver set and kit are both excellent values, but the kit is a better value
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 16, 2017
reviews.text: I bought this toolset when I needed a precision screwdriver tip that I did not have plus the ones I did have were a bit worn out. This kit certainly fixed that! The description calls this 74 in 1, but I count more. The precision screwdriver kit is actually 61 pieces counting the plastic case, the other tools number 17, plus the nylon organizer pouch make this a 79 in 1 kit. The precision screwdriver kit is available separately for $14, versus the $30 for this kit so the extra 18 pieces cost you $16, or, a little less than $1 per additional tool. Both the precision screwdriver set and kit are both excellent values, but the kit is a better value, especially if installing or removing small fasteners is all you need. All the tips are 4mm hex tips.. As you can tell from the photo, there nine bit holders, each with a capacity of 6 bits. Two bits I found loose at the top of the case giving 56 different bit drivers. Here is the inventory Hex 0.9, 1.3, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, and 6.0 mm Nuts 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, and 5.0 mm Flat 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, and 4.0 mm Torx T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, T10, T15 and T20 + 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.5 plus J000, J00, J0, and J1 5 0.8, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0 Sqr SQ0, SQ1, SQ2 Y 0.8, 2.0, and 3.0 Tri 2.3 U 2.6 X 1.5 Adpt 4 mm to 1/4" hex adapter The Phillips heads are included in the category "+", as well as the J series + bits that have a deeper + recess in the screw. The bits marked 5 look like a five pointed star of David. "Sqr" bits are square in shape. I assume that last 3 or 4 categories are only used as a manufacturers attempt to limit access.. The screwdriver handle measures 120mm. The handle has a comfortable variable diameter, a non-slip rubberized grip that, and the obligatory rotating finger rest for a precision driving tool. For reasons I do not understand, it has two 5 mm hex receptacles just beneath the finger rest; if it was 4 mm, it could have provided a way to turn bits. The bit holder adds 26 mm reach and can telescope to 43, 60, 77, and 94 mm and will fit through a hole a minimum of 8.2 mm. Using the flexible bit holder adds 138 mm to the reach, although the rotating sleeve requires a hole a minimum of 10.0 mm. A more likely use scenario is to bend the flexible bit holder, in which case this extension allows a screw or nut to be driven inside a box with an internal dimension as little as 75 mm versus 135 mm required with just the handle. Besides the precision screwdriver kit, the set includes Tweezers (3) - metal with conducting handle. Two of these have tips so fine that they could easily break your skin. Even the blunt tipped one has a finer tip than most medical tweezers. Splugers - 3 metal splugers with spade tip on one end, and rounded tip on the other. 4 plastic splugers for prying plastic cases, two widths. Probe - rigid black plastic (might be conductive), one end with a pencil point, the other with a flat scraper. Triangle plectrum - Pry a plastic case, or strum a guitar... your choice ;-) Retractable utility knife Metal straight edge/ruler, measures to 155 mm or 6" Suction cup with metal ring for handling LCD screens SIM ejector tool Anti-Static Wrist Strap with coiled grounding wire. Snap attachment to wrist strap and alligator clip Nylon case - Holds all 78 parts of this set. Two loops for hanging the case, plus, a wrist strap

reviews.title: Thickest donut bed yet!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 11, 2022
reviews.text: I have a 24 pound nervous Nellie! When she starts having a neurotic moment, she will lick the baseboards, carpet, I need a ton of grass. Last night was one of those nights, and we had just received our bed earlier in the day. One of the reviews that I read was from a woman who had purchased numerous beds from this company and use those for foster care of rescue dogs. Since dogs will mark their territory, she recommended putting the inserts in garbage bags. This also helps keep the pillow inserts from absorbing pet dander and stinking, which all dog lovers know about stinky dog beds! Well, when my girl finally decided to chill out in her bed, she was so relaxed that she snores even louder than our Great Pyrenees! I put the bed in place if her other one in my room for the night and covered her up with the matching blanket. I’m the morning, she continued to return to the bedroom to crawl in her bed. I brought it out next to the Christmas tree, and that is where she is still lying and it has been three hours! She loves it! The sides of the bolsters are very high. One side was not as fluffy and tall as the other. I tossed it in the dryer to see if it would fluff to the height of the opposite side but it did not. She doesn’t seem to mind, but I do. Also, the bottom insert that they lien is not very full. I know from past experience that I can compensate for the lack of filling but for this price, I was a little disappointed with that fact. I be will update my review if it slides not hold up as the company advertises. Overall, I would recommend the bed!

reviews.title: My dog loves this bed!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 22, 2022
reviews.text: Wanted to see if this would work for my pup. I have to say my dog does not like to be put in place or lay on his own bed in the living room. This came last night and we opened it up. My dog thinks all packages that come in the house are his. After a few minutes of him scooching it around, rubbing his paws and face on it he settled in. At first I thought it was too small but he just likes to stretch out. He actually stayed on it and seemed to doze off! I placed him a few times last night and he didn't freak out and cry. This morning while i was making his breakfast he wasn't in the kitchen as is normally the case. I turned around and he was waiting patiently in his new bed!! His kittens try to attack it because it is floofy. Super happy with the purchase and so is my Charlie.

reviews.title: Just arrived!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 10, 2022
reviews.text: Bought this to put in my corgi, Olive’s, den. She is on and off about beds because she’s super young and runs hot. Normally belly up on the hardwood floor is how I find her. When this arrived yesterday I unpacked it and went to take the box and plastic bag out to the trash, intending to return and wash it before use. Olive was pretty sick that morning, we had gone to the vet, and when I returned she was softly digging and nosing in the soft fuzz, while laying on it. I figured this might not be how she feels after a short while, so I moved it to her den. She slept on it the entire night. It’s a wonderful size: it’s even a bit big for her. She’s around 30lbs. It’s really lovely. The sides haven’t risen higher than the middle much, the center is so fluffy. You can see the ring around and I’m sure with wear the center will get flatter. This morning, when I opened her doors, she didn’t get up or move. I thought perhaps she still didn’t feel well, but it turns out she just really loves this bed. What a great purchase. Nice and big, fluffy and soft. It’s comforting while she recovers from being sick.

reviews.title: Soft
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 23, 2022
reviews.text: As a human I am giving this bed a 5 star rating. It's cute, soft and fluffy. My cat's gave it a "negative 25" star rating. They wouldn't go near it. So, thinking like a cat, I put one of our flannel sheets over this bed and "Voila", one of our cats settled down in the bed on her back with her feet sticking straight up in the air! The other cat, not so brave, but I will continue to work with her. I had ordered a white color and I'm wondering if that's what they don't like, because the flannel sheet I used is a dark blue. Do cats have color prefences? I think so, bwaaah!!!

reviews.title: A beloved bed for a beloved dog
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 9, 2022
reviews.text: Our dog loooooves this bed. He has never actually been able to own a bed before this--he tore one up, and tried to drag the other one we bought him around the house like a toy. But he discovered this magical bed at a friend's house and realized it was the coziest thing he'd ever laid in, so we immediately got one for him and he has been glued to it ever since. The fabric and shape is so soothing for him--he loves curling up in a ball and burying his head into the side walls. We've also added some blankets into it for him because the medium is a smidge too big for him (he's a 33-pound corgi mix) and the small was a smidge too small. With the added blankets, it makes for the perfect cozy spot for him to sleep the day away. We've had it for a little over a year and have washed it a half dozen or so times. It has held up well and is easily reassembled after washing. Overall, we're big fans of this bed!

Just when I was getting ready to return it or donate it, my dog decided to try it out and now seems to love it! She’s barely touched her other bed. I’m so glad I purchased this! reviews.title: Chemical Free Product - Works a Treat
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on March 14, 2019
reviews.text: I have tested this shampoo and conditioner on both mine and my daughter’s hair. We both have very thick, long hair and prone to knots and tangles. I’m always trying new hair products from Salon to the High Street. Both shampoo and conditioner are very thick, and you need to pump for quite a while before it starts coming out. For this reason, the push pump on the bottles is not necessary. They both lather into the hair really well and whereas I normally do 2 washes on our hair, I didn’t need to with this shampoo. After rinsing off the shampoo I applied the conditioner to towel dried hair for about 10 minutes. Both shampoo and conditioner felt silky soft and has a lovely gentle fragrance. We both don’t wash our hair every-day and I felt with this product our hair stayed cleaner even longer. We both use a tangle brush as well and the knots came out easier than normal. My daughter sometimes gets an itchy scalp and I have noticed she hasn't been scratching at all. Some shampoos and conditioners contain inexpensive chemicals such as Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) and these ingredients dry and damage your hair if you’re washing daily. I have checked the ingredients on the bottles, and they are chemical free - therefore it is all natural and can be used daily. The ingredients are a blend of a number of oils. I did however not see Argan oil displayed as an ingredient, so I dug further. I learnt that the ingredient Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil is, in fact, a plant oil PRODUCED from the kernels of the Argan tree and therefore Argan oil is the 2nd highest ingredient. I do think it is on the pricey side as you can get salon product for this price, but it is an excellent product and I would recommend it based on how well it works and how little I needed to use. I can feel a difference in how it conditioned and nourished my hair feels and how clean and lovely my daughter’s hair still looks after being washed 3 days ago!

It has a very pleasant smell and comes in plunger topped bottles. Even my hairdresser {who comes to my home} passed comment on this product and how it made my hair look and feel. So overall I would say Definitely give this shampoo and conditioner a thumbs up and I would give it a go if you want shiny, thicker feeling manageable hair, you definitely won't regret it.

reviews.title: Argan Shampoo
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on December 31, 2018
reviews.text: The argon shampoo and conditioner is contained in two 500ml bottle respectively with pump action tops for controlled quantity access. The information on the bottles is both detailed out ling ingredients used , how to use it and a description of argon oil infused formula used to wash and condition your hair. On the front of the bottle lists key ingredients including aron oil, avocado oil, jojoba oil, Canella oil, botanical keratin and green tea. It also indicates the product is both sulpate and paraben free and can be used on all hair types. I have found for me this is an excellent product thus far giving a clean feeling and makes my hair free soft after conditioning. The 500 ml bottle will last a long while given I only wash my hair generally every two three days, and only takes a small quantity to achieve a good result However, the product feels gentle enough I would imagine you could use it every day if need be without drying out your hair. I would recommend this product. However, after using it the initial time, I have since discovered the conditioner bottle does not pump the conditioner as its is very thick. I had to switch over the hose component with a wider hose in order to restore the pump action. For this reason I would only recommend 4 stars.

They sent me this 2.6 gallon container as a bonus due to an issue with spigots that they proactively contacted me about. As it turns out, I've been using this 2.6 all the time to carry drinking water from source to my campervan, on my motorcycle when I'm not close to a good potable hose source to fill my tank. Both the 5 gallon and 2.6 are well made with beefy handles and strong backside loop to balance when pouring. This is a great size to handle. The included extra flat sealing cap eliminates using the spigot tap cap for transporting. Spigot caps always leak regardless what container they come on. I'm thinking of buying a 2nd 2.6 size as a backup for when this one eventually starts leaking at a corner point. reviews.title: I’m on the fence, pros and cons
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 31, 2019
reviews.text: OK, I got tired of taking a big Coleman 5 gallon water dispenser camping with us, strictly from a portability standpoint. It takes up a ton of room in the car and we need every square inch of transport space when camping with the family of seven. So I saw this on Amazon and said hey, great idea, collapses, will not take up much space, winner winner chicken dinner! More or less, that is. Took it on our first trip and I was giddy at the amount of space it saved on the way to the campground! Once we got to the site though, I wasn’t quite as thrilled. *Pros: -Collapses, total space saver when storing or transporting. -Clear so always aware of water level, need for refill which was AWESOME! -Dispenser cap has an attachment to container so it does not get lost when filling. -Little red loop attachment helps to pull into shape for use. *Cons: -Difficult to get to fully expand, even with handy red loop- had to “blow it up” to fully expand at corners. -Small hole to fill with water so I needed to lift it to the faucet, became very heavy so we couldn’t fill it fully. -Had to poke a hole in top to allow for airflow, otherwise it would collapse inward as water was emptied from it. -Flow volume from dispenser is very slow. -To allow for collapsing, the plastic is not incredibly thick or rigid, so when it is full, it is both heavy and difficult to move from place to place. We transported it from the bathrooms where we filled it up to our campsite on a skateboard, and it tumbled off several times because it lacked an actual flat bottom surface. -There’s no real way to empty it fully or dry it out after use so I’m highly concerned with mildew forming during storage. All in all, I would say that if you desperately need to save space and are not terribly concerned with the speed of water flow, it’s worth getting. It’s a great idea in theory. For me, I think I will be going back to my old Coleman and figuring out a different way to conserve car space.

reviews.title: Good water containers
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 21, 2020
reviews.text: I purchased 5 of these collapsible containers to carry addition fresh water for my RV. They worked quite well. They were easy to carry. And when empty, they did not take up much space or add much weight to my load which is limited. The spigot works well, though I did use a knife and carefully increased the opening on the spigot for greater water flow. I am not quite sure why they have the regular caps attached at back of the storage container. I don't have a college degree, so I will have to find someone with a degree to help me figure that one out. I guess that I did not pass Logic 101. Relocating the regular caps was a challenge. A note of caution. It is wise to put the red cap on when transporting water in these containers. The blue spigots are handy when dispensing the water. Otherwise, keep the red caps on. Your spigot will not be accidentally opened and water spilled in areas where it is not desired. I add that as "Lessons Learned". These water containers are very sturdy and I think they will take a lot of abuse. They definitely serve my purpose and I would recommend them for anyone needing to store or carry an additional water supply.

reviews.text: The media could not be loaded. All in all, the product is reasonably priced and works fantastically. I'm building my daughter a loft in her bed room and this LED strip lighting adds wonderful "bling" that she already loves. The downloaded App on our iphones work perfectly along with the included remote. As for the strip lights themselves, you can dial in just about any color and the dancing to music or mere audio is "cool". For my application, I have but one small complaint that is worthy of mentioning for anyone doing an indoor visible project with these lights. Because I wanted a finished look since the light strip would be visible (not hidden behind a TV or up in a cabinet), I also ordered the Muzata track (Amazon recommended) which does give it a nice touch. The problem is making a 90 degree "flat" turn. I ordered the Amazon suggested P/N "JACKYLED" which allows you to cut the LED strip and turn it 90 degrees. That part was fairly seamless, but the JACKYLED connectors DO NOT fit with the muzata track, thereby making any 90 degree flat turn visibly undesirable an unusable with the Muzata track. Otherwise, it would definitely receive 5 stars... the video does not give the color hues justice as they look great to the eye...

reviews.title: Awesome lights, even better customer service
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 26, 2018
reviews.text: I ordered three 32.8ft strands and one 16.4ft strand of these Nexlux lights for my new house me and some roommates are renting. Two strands of 32.8ft lined the living room perfectly. We have the strands each on their own power supply since the power supply brick is not supposed to power more than 32.8ft. We found that 1 remote will control both strands at the same time as long as you have the receivers by each other. They’re super easy to set up and they look amazing. The white setting is bright enough to light up the entire room and give a nice even lighting. I then used the other 32.8ft strand for my bedroom, this is where I ran into problems. After testing the lights and then hanging them up, I realized when I press the off button the lights change to red instead of powering off. When I press the white button they turn blue and ‘Flash’ mode only runs the lights through 4 colors rather than all of them like my living room lights do. I saw tons of reviews talking about how good the customer service is, so I reached out and emailed Chris from Nexlux. He responded within a few hours and apologized and let me know they recently had a defective batch of WiFi receivers sent out, he then attached a coupon code for me to get a new wifi receiver for 99% off. I gladly accepted the offer and my lights have worked seamlessly since. These lights are definitely worth the money and customer service alone is worth 5 stars. I will be purchasing more in the future.

reviews.text: Been using this coffee filter for almost 7 months now and at first it was fine - sort of. You see, I made a New Years resolution to cut back on my coffee consumption and have been limiting myself to 2 - 3 7 oz. cups a day. The filter worked just fine when making this small amount of coffee. But recently I hosted a morning meeting and needed to make a full 10 cup pot. For my 10-cup Bunn this means grinding 1/2 cup of whole beans. The filter is not as big as a paper filter - at least it doesn't seem to be. It certainly doesn't expand (naturally) to fill the filter basket width-wise as a paper filter does and so the grounds are pushed up on the sides and coat the filter. This is fine when brewing a 1/4 or 1/3 pot, but with a full pot the grounds flow over the sides of the metal filter and clog the basket hole causing more coffee to spill on to your table top (and ultimately your cabinet face, floor, carpet, etc.) than in to the pot. It's a shame because I do like the idea of this little thing - it just needs to be a hair taller and about 1/4" wider, I think. Feel free to roll the dice if you have a coffee maker other than a Bunn (and yes, I did order the Bunn version) but I wouldn't even think of buying if you have carpet where you plan to brew!!

reviews.title: The thing about polyester
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 6, 2021
reviews.text: I usually use a wet cotton bandanna to keep cool in hot weather. But I was curious if 'cooling towels' were better. So, I got one to try, and on the next hot day, I tracked how long my cotton bandanna stayed damp, and then I switched to the cooling towel. I wanted to try to control for the temp and humidity to give them both a chance under the same conditions. Here's the results: the cooling towel stayed damp about 30 minutes longer than the bandanna, but because of its long scarf-like shape, I had it double wrapped around my head. The shape is a little unwieldy, actually. I want something loosely around my neck/shoulders or around my head, but this has to be worn like scarf. Hello, it's 107f, that's a nope. It kept dropping down onto whatever I worked on. Not great. So, both the bandanna and the towel need to be soaked again after two hours or so. But here's why the cotton wins out for me: polyester, for whatever reason, grows bacteria more easily than cotton. And if you use a cooling towel while working outdoors, or exercising, or doing anything sweaty, this towel will stink, quickly. And one of the awful things about poly is if you have a lot of it in your laundry, the smell can transfer to other stuff in the washing machine. So you have to do extra work to keep this thing fresh, by giving it a separate rinse or soak in whatever you use on smelly fabric. Plus, wet polyester gets itchy against the skin, I found it far more irritating than wet cotton. I ended up fussing with it, taking it off to give my skin a break, and repositioning it annoyingly often. Bottom line: I'm sticking with cotton bandannas. It comes down to preference. If you don't mind polyester go for it. As for me, IDK, maybe this could be soaked, frozen, and used as an ice pack?

reviews.text: Kim + Ono kimonos are so beautifully designed that they are really wearable art. I got the sapphire colored one with pink and lilac flowers and cranes. The satin's reflective qualities make the pink in the flowers of this piece look like deep mauve from one angle, a light blush from another, and yet another shade as you are looking at it straight on. The flowers and birds are outlined in gold and the sheen of the satin also gives the gold a metallic quality. The design, the colors, and the shimmer of the fabric makes this a stunning piece to wear either with a satin slip dress and pearls to go to a party or over casual lounging clothes to stay in or just go walk the dog. I live in Houston where it is semi-tropical and almost never cold enough to wear a sweater or coat, so this kimono is going to be my "go to" cover-up year round. I am soooo happy to add it to my wardrobe. I only gave it a 4 for comfort because satin has a side that isn't as soft on your skin as the side facing outward but the satin, machine printed version, of a Kim + Ono design is an absolute steal for this price! (They also make hand-painted silk versions that are priced over $200.) I was afraid this purchase would be a cheap knock off when I saw this being sold for this price, but the reviews said it had "Kim + Ono" tags, so I crossed my fingers and ordered it. (Amazon allows sellers to sell knock offs but show the real thing, but they do let you return it at no cost and have drop off returns close by.) I am 5'4. The hem just touches the ground with no shoes and bare feet. I may take up the hem an inch or buy a pair of healed or platform sandals to keep it from dragging the ground because I don't want to damage this piece! I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE, this kimono!!!

reviews.title: Once again I LOVE THIS ROBE!!! But be careful to order from Old Shanghai.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on June 17, 2015
reviews.text: August 2021: I’m still wearing my original pink robe from Old Shanghai, but I’ve purchased a replacement for next summer. Although the original is still in reasonably good condition, I think this will be its last summer of use. Excellent lifespan - I’ve worn this robe daily and washed it at least weekly about half of every year (all spring & summer & into early fall) since it was purchased in June 2015! And every one I’ve given as a gift has been a big hit because they look great on all body types. EDIT AGAIN, 16 May 2017: After contacting Old Shanghai directly, it seems when I clicked “Buy it Again”, then went to change the color, I was inexplicably shifted to another seller called Tigoof Online, and I inadvertantly ordered from them instead of Old Shanghai. For the better quality robe DO NOT ORDER FROM ANYONE EXCEPT 'OLD SHANGHAI'! After they realized what had happened, Old Shanghai sent a replacement robe free of charge, which is very lovely and to the standard I originally expected. I'm attaching photos to show the difference in the products. First is a side-by-side with Old Shanghai hanging on the right, and you can see even the Old Shanghai colors are softer, more elegant, while the Tigoof Online colors are harsher and cheap looking. Photos 2&3 and then 4&5 show some finishing details of the Tigoof Online vs Old Shanghai robes, and 6&7 are photos of the labels of each brand. I changed my rating back to 5 stars because of the excellent customer service of Old Shanghai. Edit 28 March 2017: I ordered another in black as a gift, and I'M VERY DISAPPOINTED. It is 4 inches shorter, the sleeves are a few inches shorter, and it has no interior ties - so how are you supposed to keep it closed while wearing it? It's marked as an XXXL, and does not have the Old Shanghai label, when ALL the others I've purchased are "one size fits most" and do have their label. Did they run out and go around the corner and buy an XXXL child's robe??? Changing my 5 star rating to a 1 star because of this. I needed it before a planned trip, and of course I can return it, but before replacing it I want to be certain I'm getting the correct robe, and Amazon has been NO help so far. Edit: February 2017: This robe has held up very well, and I continue to be impressed. I've ordered others as gifts and they have always been a hit. My 83 year old mother is the type of person who has always cared about her appearance and always dresses well. I purchased two for her, a long and a short version in different colors, for a recent hospital stay, and she loves them both. Both of my sisters have these now, and also love them. In my original review I mentioned ironing out the packing creases when it was new, and hoping I'd never need to iron it again. Sure enough, nearly two years later that is still the only time I've ironed it. Once those creases were dealt with, its been machine washed and dried (on cold water and gentle cycle) many times, and I've pulled it out of the dryer and it looks great. Easy care, in addition to being beautiful. I wear this every day during spring and summer, and yet for now I see no reason to replace it as it still looks great - in a year or two maybe it will be worn enough. A bargain for sure. :-) June 17, 2015: I LOVE this robe! I was looking for a very light summer robe, and this is just so perfect. I have a son and a stepson who are both grown men and are around all the time. I like to shower and change for bed early in the evening and then relax for the rest of the evening with family. Winter robes are easy but I needed a robe with complete coverage that wouldn't be uncomfortable in summer. This is it. This robe is so pretty; the colors are beautiful. I ordered the pink and it's a very soft, flattering color. This robe is so light I'd describe it as "gossamer", but the fabric isn't sheer - it provides total coverage. It looks like silk, but is EASY CARE! When I received it I washed it in cold water and dried it on low. It still had marks from being folded during shipping so I turned in inside out and ironed it on a medium setting to remove those few creases. Since it held those creases so well, now that I've ironed them out I don't expect to ever need to iron it again. For length, I am 5'6" and it comes to the top of my feet - almost to the floor. I am of normal weight for my height and it fits generously, folds and flows perfectly. I'll be ordering more of these, they're available in so many pretty colors and they are just so beautiful! These would be great gifts, too.

description: Product Description How to know what nose pads I need? With so many nose pads out there it can be hard to find the right pair. Start by looking at your frames to see what type of nose pads your glasses came with. This will give you a good place to start. There are several different mount types, shapes, and sizes. It will be helpful to have a ruler on hand that can measure in millimeters. Check out this complete comprehensive guide from GMS Optical to help you find the best nose pads for your frames! Mount Types The mount is the place where the nose pad connects to the glasses. Adhesive - PushIn - ScrewIn - SlideIn - ClipOn Shape Types There are many different shapes of nose pads your glasses may have come with. In some cases, when replacing your nose pads you do not need to keep the same shape; you can replace them with the shape you like best. It's an easy way to upgrade your glasses! Below we will discuss the different shapes and how to identify which ones you have. DShape - Symmetrical - Round - Oval - Butterfly - HalfMoon - Rectangle Silicone Types As nose pads evolve more and more Silicone types are used. Airbag nose pads are a very soft silicone that has air inside of them for maximum comfort, but you give up the firmness and durability. Airbags can be found in several mount types. Air Pillow has a pillow of Air in the center of the pad and is very soft, again the durability is ok. These are only found in the adhesive type. Hard Silicone is the most common nose pad and is likely what your reading glasses came with. They are the most durable and are commonly found in Screw-in, push-in, slide-in, and Clip-on mount types. Soft silicones are being used more and more and offer great comfort at the expense of durability. The soft silicone can be found in use in every mount type. The last time isnt a silicone at all but is a foam. Foam is the thinnest of all nose pads. They offer comfort and a good grip. They will need to be replaced regularly. Airbag - Air Pillow - Hard Silicone - Soft Silicone - Foam Why GMS Optical We are the experts. We were the first optical brand on Amazon.com to sell nose pads for your glasses. We have been innovating new designs through customer feedback since 2014. GMS Optical is located in the USA. We source only the best silicone and are quick to remove products from our catalog that do not deliver the best customer experiance. Just take a look at our 90,000+ happy customer reviews! _______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Mount Types -The mount is the place where the nose pad connects to the glasses. Adhesive These are typically used on plastic frames when there isn't a mount on the glasses. These nose pads adhere to the frame in the area where your glasses rest on your nose. Most of GMS Optical’s adhesive nose pads are made with 3M adhesive, which allows them to stick in place for longer. They come in silicone or foam materials, and several shapes which you can read about in the next section Push-In These are symmetrical pads. They have two long round edges with quick round ends to form an oval shape. They are interchangeable from left to right Screw-In If you look at your glasses and see a rectangle mount with a hole the size of a small screw, then you’re looking for screw-in nose pads. When you purchase new screw-in nose pads, they do not come with screws. Be sure to keep our original screws that came with your glasses to attach your new nose pads. Slide-In These nose pads are characterized by the lifted table top piece on their backside. This table protrusion has a little lip on the outer edge. The glasses will either have a round or oval shape mount that the nose pads pop into, or they will have a hairpin-like retaining structure the round protrusion snaps into Read more Shape Types - There are many different shapes of nose pads. In some cases, when replacing your nose pads you do not need to keep the same shape; you can replace them with the shape you like best. D-Shape These are some of the most common shapes. They are roughly shaped like a capitalized letter “D”. They have one long straight edge and one long round edge with round ends that connect the two edges. The flat side will mount toward the frames with the round side facing your face. These nose pads have a distinct left and right pad in each pair. Symmetrical or Teardrop Also referred to as Teardrops. These have round edges and are skinnier near the bottom creating a teardrop shape. These can be used on the left or right side of your glasses. Round These are easy to identify with their perfectly round shape. There is no difference between the left and right nose pads. They are often seen on children’s glasses or smaller frames. Oval These are symmetrical pads. They have two long round edges with quick round ends to form an oval shape. They are interchangeable from left to right. Read more Butterfly - Adhesive These are found in adhesive mount types. They have two “wings” with one being larger than the other. The larger wing attaches onto your frames where the nose piece rests on your nose. The smaller wing will wrap around the nose piece for extra adherence. Half Moons - Adhesive These are found in the adhesive mount types. These have a nice smooth long round edge from end to end. These are offered in thin and airbag styles. Rectangles These are less common than most of the other nose pads we have discussed. They will have two long flat edges and two short flat edges. They allow for even distribution of weight. They can be used interchangeably on the left or right side. Flat Foam - Adhesive Dont have a lot of room, but need grip and comfort. Foam adhesive nose pads are a great solution. Available in peach or black or brown. Read more ________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Size Types GMS Optical nose pads come in many different sizes to accommodate many different faces and glasses. Nose pads are naturally tiny, so we measure these in millimeters. This is where that ruler will come in handy! 1mm corresponds to approximately 1/32nd of an inch. Below we have broken down the sizes. We have them sorted into three different size groups: small, medium, and large. Because nose pads are so small, 1mm can make a big difference in how they fit! You should measure your current nose pads and consider how they fit before changing sizes. Make sure you use the exact measurement when purchasing nose pads, not the grouping of small, medium, or large. Small Sizes: These are recommended for small faces and children’s glasses. Often the round shape is the smallest nose pads, measuring just 9mm. Other small sizes include 11mm, 12mm, and 13mm. Medium Sizes: These tend to be the most popular sizes and fit well on most glasses. Not too small and not too big, just right! Medium nose pad sizes include 14mm, 15mm, and 16mm. Large Sizes: These are recommended for large faces and noses, or someone looking to better distribute the weight of heavier glasses. Large nose pad sizes include 17mm, 18mm, and 19mm. Material Types The material that makes up the nose pad Silicone: This is the most common type of nose pad material as it is superior to others, offering comfort, softness, and quality. Silicone nose pads are often referred to as “non-slip” nose pads. Silicone does help to keep glasses from slipping. However, the overall fit of your glasses and using the proper type and size of nose pad play a big factor in keeping your glasses from slipping. For most, silicone nose pads are hypoallergenic, but all users should consult a healthcare professional if allergies or skin irritation are a concern. Plastic: This type of nose pad is durable due to the plastic material and is more resistant to degradation from oils on your face. This material offers a more firm fit than silicone and is easier to clean. Foam: This material tends to be more affordable than the others. The foam is a light and comfortable alternative that still feels soft. They typically need to be replaced more often and are available in higher quantity packages. reviews.title: This device basically does the "standing outside on your tippy toes" to get a signal, for you.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 1, 2020
reviews.text: I bought one some months ago. For the layman, it's basically a repeater with some extras built-in. What you want to do is have the white out-door antenna higher up (in the attic or outside at roof or higher levels) where it can grab an existing better signal. The in-door antenna is basically just relaying that better signal into the house or RV. A lot of people have found themselves standing on their tippy toes and trying to hold their arm up in the air to get that text message out on a camping trip. Some people in more rural areas deal with this daily where they live. This device basically does the "standing outside on your tippy toes" for you. That's all. If you're in an area where there's no signal (middle of the ocean as a dramatic example), this device won't help, at all. It can't create a signal from nothing. In some applications where you can not place the out-door antenna at higher elevation (or elevation is not necessarily the problem - maybe the building is just a tin-can building), but you can get the out-door antenna in a windowed area of the house/building that does get a better signal, I recommend taking a piece of aluminum foil (12" by 12" roughly) and putting it on the side of the out-door antenna that's pointing into the building. Basically you want the out-door antenna to see and get the good signal from outside, but not feedback loop on any signals from inside the building. These things can suffer from "feedback" (like a microphone/speaker high pitch squeal because the sound from the speakers is playing back into the microphone over and over). This "feedback" is most likely to happen when the in-door and out-door antenna are at nearly the same elevation (which is why the instructions tell you that the in-door and out-door antennas are to be separated by ~30 feet or separated by elevation). By putting the aluminum on the side of the out-door antenna in applications where both the in-door and out-door antenna are at roughly the same elevation, you can block the "feedback" loop. This device does lower gain automatically to help prevent this feedback problem (this would be similar to if your church's audio system automatically lowered the volume output to the speakers if it detected a feedback loop), but then that's at the cost of gain or signal strength (volume) which is why you wanted this device in the first place. I suspect this is the angle where a lot of people complain that the device doesn't work or that it provided nothing better than what they already had, is that the device is automatically lowering gain to prevent a feedback loop issue because their installation wasn't optimal. In my specific use-scenario, the cabling is stretched out to the garage and the out-door antenna is in a window in the garage that stands around 7 feet in elevation - not an ideal elevation for this device because of the feedback problems it can cause from having both the in-door and out-door at similar elevation. To counter that, I have a 15" by 12" piece of aluminum taped to the side of the outdoor antenna. It's taped on the side that faces toward/into the house to prevent the "feedback". The fact that the out-door antenna is in-doors (the garage), but directly in a window is worth a small boost (radio signals go through windows easier than walls). The fact that the out-door antenna is probably 4.5 feet higher in elevation than what would be typical of me sitting on the couch on the phone is also worth a small boost. Using a phone app to see the DB on my couch, I go from 4G 1 bar of signal (*if that*) at -114db (without the booster) to a 4G 2-3 bars at -100db (with the booster) in my most used place in the house. It's a bit better than that the closer I am to the in-door antenna, and a bit worse the farther away, but it's enough of a boost that I never have to stand on my tippy toes to get a text or to send one and it's enough of a boost to watch a YouTube video without waiting for buffers.
