reviews.title: Black Flag Version 1.5/2 - 3.5 stars
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 21, 2021
reviews.text: This review is for the PS4 version. I started playing the AC series when I first played the Ezio collection years after they were originally release. So, after getting a late start, I played several other of the AC titles, quickly after getting hooked, including Black Flag. Somehow, I missed Rogue and didn’t realize that came out between Black Flag and Unity. Seeing this remastered version for the PS4 for 17 bucks, I grabbed it. With that being said, this could almost be called Black Flag 1.5 or 2 as it has a lot of similarities in gameplay, both good and bad. The game is shorter than BF in terms of size of the environments and missions. Like Black Flag the gameplay controls are a bit awkward as I tend to grab and jump onto/off something when I really didn’t intend to do it, as opposed to the smoother game controls that came about in Syndicate and games in the series since. Jumping and climbing can be a pain at times in the game and I really miss the smoothness and ease of jumping and climbing that I have gotten use to in the AC games. You would think they would have smoothed that out a bit with a remaster, but alas no. With all AC games, there is plenty to do with side quests and the collecting of things. It is interesting to explore the varies areas around the islands. There is a variety of different quests to do throughout but are pretty similar to what has been done before in the previous games so it does lack a bit in original game play. Like Black Flag, the game has ships and ship battles which are fun, but like Black Flag can be a bit clunky. The collecting of the animus items and songs are also back. They quickly get repetitive and is probably my least favorite part of the AC games. The songs are a bit of a pain to chase down, although you can pretty much stay where the chase starts to get it fairly easily when it returns. If you are familiar with Black Flag, you should be familiar with doing these. It took me a bit of getting use to the controls again, but quickly found my BF sea legs. The environment and scenery are well done and detailed considering the original game is 7 years old and the remaster at least 4 years old. The water is especially detailed and nicely done. The basic gameplay is pretty much the same as BF and lack the smoothness of the later games. The missions are ok and can be challenging, especially if you are trying to do 100 percent completion. Like the earlier AC games, there is still issues with glitchy camera views at times that make it hard to see and do things, such as the scenery blocking your view in the middle of a fight. I do think there is a lot of the sameness in the missions and seems to be more of an extension of BF than an original game. The Animus office scenes are back again and I am still not a fan of that in the game as I think it interrupts the pace of the game and the collecting of notes outside of the Animus is boring and seems a bit unnecessary to the game. Like BF the game menus are a little clunky but that could be because I got use to the way Syndicates menus were done. The story is decent, although not as good as other games, but does give a different perspective of the series. The ship battles are not quite as novel the second time around as the ship controls are a bit clunky and make the battles a bit harder to manipulate than they should be. For 17 bucks, there is still plenty of fun, especially if you are a fan of the series and worth playing, although lacking in originality and the remaster is lacking in improvements in gameplay. It isn’t my favorite in the series and falls more into average territory for the series, but it is ok to play. 3.5 stars

reviews.title: Did NOT have a halo or ahesion problem, fits well!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 7, 2020
reviews.text: It took a while for me to decide which screen protector to buy and I finally chose this one, despite seeing a couple of people with problems in their reviews. Well, I've waited 6 months to write a review to give it a fair assessment and it deserves the 5 stars I gave it. -No halo problem: First of all, the halo problem (meaning it doesn't stick well enough and the edges peel up or there are bubbles around the edge, etc) was a concern for me BUT there is zero and I mean ZERO halo on my phone. It is adhered extremely securely. This may be because I spent a very long and careful time installing it. I was as pinpoint precision as I could be whilst installing, and it shows. After being very careful I was able to get everything exact center where I wanted it, which wasn't a small feat which is why I debated between a 3 and 4 for ease of installation. I ended up giving it a 4 because everything I needed was included and the video was helpful. I won't dock them for me needing to be patient and careful. -The size is fine: It is noted and should be remembered that this screen protector DOES NOT GO ALL THE WAY TO THE EDGE OF THE PHONE! They call it "case friendly" but the reason is actually because there is a slight curve and if the glass were to go all the way to the edge you would have the problem where it would not fit straight against your phone. It will cover the on/colored portion of your screen when you CAREFULLY install it. If you are not careful it may be askew. -The adhesion is wonderful: Yes, I've dropped my phone. I drop it sorta a lot. I have a wallet type case which will protect the screen if it is shut... but it often isn't shut. I've dropped it on carpet, cement, and asphalt. Haven't done any damage whatsoever and it has not randomly "popped off." I don't have any scratches on it yet either. -No "rainbow screen:" Rainbow screen happens when the protector doesn't adhere all the way to the device and causes weird colors or warping. This is full adhesion and I haven't experienced any rainbow screen or touch screen trouble. -When they say it deflects water they mean it: Water will bead up on the screen and is easy to wipe away. I disinfect my phone with wipes often - that beads up and wipes away as well, whereas with some other protectors I've had it streaked. Yes, it does get fingerprints on it like everything else does. They just wipe off with the swipe of a cloth. In summation, you may feel safe buying this. It came packaged well for me - in a padded envelope was the box, and inside the box was some basic padding and all the equipment. I haven't had problems with the first protector as of this first six months, but if I do it is nice knowing there are more in there for the future. Update: Still gets 5 stars. I added a picture. I finally broke 1 of 3 by dropping it into an arcade machine (metal). Second one also installed with patience and no problems or halo effect.

reviews.title: The picture on Amazon is misleading, but still a wonderful plush
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 3, 2020
reviews.text: I have a funny little story with this plush... An ex boyfriend got me into the Sonic franchise by gifting me a Silver and Blaze plush a few years ago and ever since then, I decided to try getting plushes of all the characters I liked. Sonic was definitely on my list, but he was hard to find. I remember first coming across this exact plush on Amazon but the asking price for him at the time was around $164 US Dollars... Needless to say I passed on him at the time, assuming the price was so high just because he was the last of his kind (like a discontinued plush). Could I have settled for another Sonic plush from another plush maker? I could've. But I wanted a Sonic in the GE style. In the summer of 2019 I decided to randomly look up this plush again and BOOM - not only was he still on Amazon but he was now just $17 US Dollars and change, so I immediately scooped him up finally having a Sonic in my collection. He arrived, but I was disappointed by ONE thing... That one thing is that the picture of the plush on Amazon is slightly misleading. The pictures on Amazon (at the time of this review) show the arms as NOT being attached to the plush when in fact THE PLUSH'S ARMS AND HANDS ARE SEWN ONTO HIM. You can easily snip the stitching on the hands to separate the hands from the rest of his body, you *could*, but most probably don't plan on doing that intentionally especially since there aren't many other poses you can accomplished with a plush who has posed hands. But even with the posed hands and the hands being attached to his body, he's still a very well made plush. The pose he's stuck in is the Classic Sonic pose on the original Japanese box art of Sonic 1 - the classic finger wagging pose with the other hand on his hip. And this plush captures that pose perfectly in soft sculpture form! At first I was a bit turned off by the fact he was posed, but even with this pose in place, I've been able to take a bunch of silly pictures with this plush often with him pointing at humorous things and even in a "Draw me like one of your French girls" pose with the pointing hand supporting his head (the plush was placed on a bed). When it comes to posing this guy in a sitting position, his right hand (sewn to his hip) may look a little awkward, but that's nothing a good camera angle can't compensate for. He will look better when hung up from the gold string on his head (which is there to replicate the look and feel of arcade plushes), but the string may break if the plush is hung up for too long. Besides the pose, he's well stuffed, the arms have some thickness to him (so he won't be a stringy Sonic with spaghetti arms if you cut the stitching), he's a very canon accurate Sonic plush overall - especially for those looking to add a Classic Sonic to their collection. GE's Sonic plushes always aim to be as canon accurate as possible and they're usually aimed toward collectors, but this Classic Sonic is simple enough in his design that he'll survive being played with as a toy (I know he's survived being shoved in a bag and taken on kayaking trips). He makes a great addition to any Sonic plush collection and a perfect gift for Sonic fans and especially fans of Classic Sonic in particular. I also highly recommend him if you want a plush you can take funny photos with, as he's my most photographed plush!

reviews.title: A great toy that my kid has grown with
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 13, 2021
reviews.text: After seeing the other activity cubes listed here I decided to go with this Vtech option (there is another one) based on size, colors, and I thought the amount and type of activities it offered would keep my son entertained for a while. I was absolutely right. My son is generally attracted to lights and sounds, this cube certainly delivers on both. The front and top sides offer multiple options for him to push/turn/twist so that he can listen to a different sounds each time (he loves the monkey noise) as well as the piano keys which perform multiple functions (animal noises, songs, lights, find the animal). The other sides aren't quite as loud or bright but he still engages quite a bit. He thoroughly enjoys spinning the food/instrument shapes and turning the gears below (another noise maker). The sliding monkey, bird, bug side is his least favorite and just feels like this side should've been designed better (my only reason for the 4 star mark). The shape blocks are great, he just started putting the circle in the correct hole so it's really great to see the progress. Overall I would strongly recommend this product to any parent. It has kept my child engaged for over 6 months now and is a staple in his play routine. I would say this purchase is most useful once baby starts crawling or even more so when they can sit up. As with most Vtech products I'm very satisfied with this product and continue to look for their toys when making a new toy purchase.

Quality/Delivery: The machines are the best bang for your buck. Both machines arrived on time, in the original box, unopened. Model/Hardware: Both machines are the 2018 models with only the 1 bank for M.2 SSD (the 2019 model has 2 M.2 banks) and 1 2.5 inch storage bank for a total of 2 ROM slots. Gameplay/Graphics: At power on, the device only needed the basic profile setup. Both were immediately able to play Minecraft wShadres at 60FPS due to optional settings in the game settings. Gamers looking to play games like COD, GTA, DIVISION, etc. will be able to play these games with average settings. But they will be able to run smoothly but with mid level resolution. If you are looking for Ultra resolution at 200 FPS on games, this is not the machine for you and at this price it should not be expected to be. reviews.title: A very nice, reasonably priced set.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 9, 2011
reviews.text: The dishes are nicer than they appear in the photograph. I was grateful to find them. I had been looking for a new set of dishes for a very long time - several years. For one thing, I wanted a 5 piece setting, (cup and saucer), not a 4 piece setting (mug only). I also did not want to buy dishes by individual settings, so I was looking for a set, with serving pieces included. In addition, I did not want to buy anything made in China. This narrowed the range of choices to just about nothing, since I also wanted to like the pattern, at least a little bit. And oh, yes, I wanted something that could go into the dishwasher. (In this day and age, what morons decided to market sets of dishes that they recommend you wash by hand?) This set of dishes is lovely, It includes both cups and saucers, a few serving pieces; it can be used for everyday use or special occasions. Best of all, they are made in Italy, not China. I would have loved to have found something made in America, but, as far as I can see, dinnerware sets are not made in America. At least I couldn't find any. If I had to fault this set, I would say that it comes with 2 types of bowls, excluding the serving bowl: soup bowls and cereal bowls. But both are quite small; the soup bowl is wide enough, but it is very shallow. Some Lorenzo sets come with one bowl and perhaps those are bigger. All Lorenzo patterns that I saw on line are attractive. If I could have seen these sets in person, I might have chosen another pattern, especially if one pattern came with bigger soup bowls. Another minor fault is that they cannot be used in the microwave. But all things considered, the length of time I have been looking, the ultra reasonable price, and the fact that the set meets my other criteria listed in my first paragraph, I am extremely pleased. I am also relieved that I finally found something.

reviews.title: An Elegant and Unique Design
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on February 11, 2020
reviews.text: My wife has wanted a set of China/fine dinnerware for a long time. With the purchase of our new home last year, I felt the recent holiday season would be the perfect time to splurge on a good dinnerware set. What I found was a set from a reputable brand, with a quality I believe to be approaching fine China that usually costs at least 5x what I paid. I originally had my eyes on another brand/design with a princess lace border and silver inlay, for roughly 3x the cost. But when I stumbled upon the Lorren Iris series, I was sold! The Iris Collection has a design more reminiscent of Celtic knot/Nordic vine trim work. The combination of cobalt and gold leaf overlay provides a robust brilliance that not only makes the Iris Collection stand out uniquely from other traditional and contemporary fine dinnerwares, but it also represents the Irish portion of our family heritage. The overlays aren't as robust as more expensive dinnerware, so hand washing is a must, even though the product boasts to be dishwasher safe. Take care of it and be gentle, and I believe you will get may years of enjoyment from this dinnerware!

reviews.title: Lighter weight, nice flow
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada on January 20, 2020
reviews.text: The bedskirt I ordered came in today & I just put it on. It’s perfect! I ordered ‘off white’ & it’s what I was hoping for...halfway between soft white & apartment wall beige. The skirt isn’t fussy ruffly with too many waves & being made of a lighter* weight fabric, (as opposed to cotton which lays stiffer) the wavy flow is easy on the eyes. Yes, I had to iron it...I can’t imagine putting it on the bed without doing something. It ironed up beautifully & the fabric was a pleasure to work with. * It is not see-through or skimpy. No bugs, no smell in this package! I prefer this type of style that has the skirt sewn on to the sheet that lays across the boxspring. For those who complain that it’s hard to get on, take an extra 15 minutes, wiggle your mattress off the bed, stand it up against the wall. Then while you’re at it, pull that bed frame ( boxspring or not) away from the wall & dust off the baseboard & vacume the floor where you don’t usually along the head of the bed. Lay the middle sheet of the new pressed skirt over the box spring, line up the nicely finished edges of the skirt with the edge of the boxspring or frame. Now is the time to holler for a 2nd pair of hands, but if none is available, line the bed up with your standing mattress maybe 6” apart. Place your foot on top of the sheet/skirt to hold it in place, reach over & smoothly place as much of your mattress on top WITHOUT wiggling it. Move to the other end of the bed, again placing your foot in a spot to hold the skirt in place, lift the mattress up just a few inches while shifting it over. Repeat on each side. Should only take you a few adjustments to centre your bed & voila! Done! Why am I adding these extra tidbits? Because I’m 63 yrs old, & for anyone who wants to whine that they can’t do that, here’s how. I opened the package & less than an hour later I had it ironed & everything done including changing the bedding (might as well, the bed’s apart). Be aware of the length of your drop! Definitely recommend, especially for the price. Received quickly, adequate packaging & good quality.

reviews.title: Useful storage for large bags of food
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada 🇨🇦 on May 5, 2021
reviews.text: We had an older bin that was smaller and wouldn't hold a 30lb. bag of dog food. This one is very large, and has a bit of room to spare. It's a similar material to the opaque Rubbermaid tote-type containers, with a hinged latching lid. It comes with wheels that take just a few seconds to pop into holes in the bottom of the bin. We store the bin under the kitchen table and it fits perfectly. It's very easy to move around the kitchen at feeding time. The lid has a good latch that you need to engage to lock shut (it will make a definite thud against the lid when locked). It's easy to open and close. The lid opens completely for easy access of food or putting in/removing bags or pouring in kibble. We choose to keep the food in the bag and just put the bag in the bin. This is the first kibble our dog has been on, so in case we have to switch formulas, this will help make switching easier. We also don't need to worry as much about the food smell getting into the plastic. We keep the bag sealed inside, and this way the food is also protected from light (our kitchen is bright) The lid has a thick styrofoam-type gasket to help seal the bin. I would prefer that this be rubber or silicone so as to be put in the dishwasher if needed. Having a sturdier gasket would also guard against it getting damaged over time. I don't even know if the company offers a replacement gasket... I would hate to think that it be useless garbage if that can't be replaced. reviews.text: I really wish these types of sets had real Dupont IDC crimp type with retainer clip cables instead of this pulling apart a color coded IDC ribbon cable, stripping the wire, tinning it, crimping on male or female Dupont connectors’ contacts, soldering those together, and hoping you left enough slack in the ribbon cable to stuff the contacts in a 1 or 2 pin wide plain Dupont connector so that way you don’t peal away too much insulator somewhere down the line. But in concept It meets my needs perfectly, I have yet to trust this kit in that it will not be a tremendous amount of ass pain once I get started so I have not started other that stripping hand separable IDC ribbon insulator and a quantity of stranded conductor along with it which just pissed me off right away so I walked away disillusioned in how much difficulty this would be to do by hand. That’s not the fault of these connectors but rather the process method which leads you hope that you did all the prep-work right with the included IDC ribbon cable which you have to splay with an X-axcto knife and strip with a 10 year old cheap Radio Shack mechanical stripper that I have had 4 houses ago. I haven't brought myself to use it because it looks tedious, and trying to fumble with that kit pin by pin after having had neck surgery is still not a pleasant prospect. I can’t offer an unbiased review until I have actually tried to use it after getting over the process inducing initial frustration that happened right off the bat with using old strippers. Time to order me a new one of those I guess.

reviews.title: Champagne blush- here's what I wish I'd learned from reading other reviews.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on September 28, 2016
reviews.text: 1.) I ordered the champagne blush. It's gorgeous. The color is a soft, elegant pink- very subdued, almost neutral. It has a richness to it as gold does, but is cool enough to coordinate nicely with silver accessories. The finish is not over-the-top glittery, not exactly matte either. I have rented a comparable gold tablecloth that was much more glittery...this is more of a metallic finish than a sparkle fest. Exactly what I wanted. 2.) When I opened the package and shook out my tablecloth as directed, seven (7) tiny sequins came off. No big deal. 3.) The hem of this tablecloth is a simple surged edge. It is not a beautiful finished seam, but the thread used to finish it is a good match to the color of the cloth, and the overall result is unobtrusive. 4.) Speaking of seams, mine has two- each of which is about 6" from the long edge. So I suppose my cloth is composed three pieces, one long panel joined to two narrow panels to achieve the end width of 60". I don't mind this- it almost looks like an intentional edge detail, which is visible in the first photo I attached. 5.) The seller included a cute keychain with my order. It's a birthday bear. I can't be mad at that. 6.) I paid approximately $30 for this tablecloth and it looks like a million bucks. I ordered a navy blue openwork lace overlay to place on top, and I'm not even sure I'll use it. 7.) It costs $40-$50 to rent a comparable cloth in my area. You should buy this tablecloth. I had some concerns about color, and obsessed about gold vs matte gold vs blush vs rose gold vs champagne vs champagne blush spread out over a half dozen sellers (and honestly, any of them would have been fine with my table, but I wanted that perfect thing, you know?). If you want a gorgeous grown-up neutral pink, get the champagne blush. I'm glad I did.

reviews.title: Will Never Own A Different Brand! Pop Sockets Work Great Also, Just Need Some Extra Love
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 5, 2019
reviews.text: I just replaced my Galaxy S7 for the Galaxy S9 and instantly turned to Supacase's Unicorn Beetle! My Galaxy S7 stayed in its Unicorn Beetle for 2 years and was only removed to clean water that seeped through the cracks maybe a handful of times. I sold the S7 to my friend and removed the case and the phone was still in immaculate condition. Dust builds up around the openings but can easily be wiped away. Not even scuff mark's around the corners or anything! I dropped my S7 100,000 times and it never received as much as a scratch. I even got pushed into a pool once with it in my pocket and dropped it into the lake on other occasion and never had a single issue with it! My wife preferred the prettier cases and had her S7's screen replaced three times and the entire phone once, and spent the last 6 months with it cracked after not wanting to spend more money on it. Long story short, the Unicorn Beetle was the way to go! So far with the S9 I am getting the exact same quality! The case is great and perfectly protects my phone! I've dropped my phone a few times and not even the curved edges of the screen have been damaged. The back glass is still perfect, and after 2 months there isnt a scratch! The edges aren't raised above the sides of the screen which offers slightly less protection but with the case design a tempered glass screen protector fit underneath it and with touch sensitivity increased it functions perfectly! There are only a couple minor downsides to the case. Since the screen protector is plastic it scuffs up easily from just normal use, but after the first 2 weeks it's as bad as itll get and is only noticeable when viewed from certain angles or when the light hits it in specific ways and the phone is off. While on it looks great! It does tend to form some very small squares on the screen too that can be seen when using the phone from what seems like possibly moisture but I chalk it up as living in such a humid climate and something I'll have to deal with. It is also slightly bulkier than I'd prefer but a lot slimmer than previous models and still really nice looking! It is a little harder to remove than previous models once on the phone as well, but to me that just means it's better protected lol! Wireless charging also works but only when my phone is seated in a very specific position on a recently released Samsung Wireless Charging Pad. I haven't tried wireless charging with the towers that hold the phone upright though, they may work better. Regardless, I haven't managed to get reliable fast charging from the wireless charger even before adding the pop socket to the back. With the socket the chance or getting a wireless charge is likely close to 0%. *Note for Pop-Socket Users* because the back of the phone is beveled the entirety of most pop sockets wont be seated squarely and can cause them to easily come off. This was fixed very easily by applying a little super glue I stole from my wife that she used to put on fake nails underneath the socket on the left and right where it doesn't seat all the way. Since adding the glue I have not had a single issue! The positives greatly outweigh the negatives however, especially when compared to other cases and for far more than just the elite protection. For starters the finger print sensor is not hindered at all and works perfectly! The charging port cover is very durable as well and wont break like many other brands! Theres a lot of room around the headphone jack also so you'll never have an issue using headphones or an auxiliary cord! And just to boast about the protection again, when you decide to upgrade your resale value will still be very high because it protects from all scratches and scuffs to the actual phone! A simple wipe down and it looks better than factory restored phones straight from the dealers! So to sum things up, it's not great for the wireless charging pad I've tested, the screen will scuff a little but never onto the actual phone screen, and it may be a little bulkier than other cases but its overall protection makes it WELL WORTH IT! These phones are not cheap, so unless you've got a rock solid warranty or money to spend on numerous repairs then dont even second guess this case. I honestly didnt even opt into my phones warranty because I trust this case so much after its superb protection of my S7. I'd rival its protection against the Otterbox Defender Series any day of the week and for the price, I'd bet my life savings that this phone comes out on top. Its slimmer, lighter, more aesthetically appealing, offers, at the very least, comparable protection and the same protection for normal use people like myself (I'm not dropping my phone 100 feet, running it over, or going for a long swim. Max drop distance for me is probably 5ft or less), is a lot cheaper, and just as respected with A++ customer service! Dont think twice! BUY BUY BUY.

reviews.text: Never paid anywhere near this kind of price for a phone case (usually going with flip cases for my Galaxy phones). Read the reviews and decided to take the risk... I simply ordered an LK glass screen protector for £4.99 as seen here https://www.amazon.co.uk/gp/product/B07H2X26C3/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 I then removed the substandard plastic screen protector thats fitted to this case, fitted the LK glass screen protector and refitted the case to the phone and there you have it - an excellent combination of a rugged case with a decent glass screen protector...should anything happen to the screen protector then LK offer a lifetime warranty so simply contact them for a replacement so its win win and no more scratched screen as you get with the stock protector!

reviews.title: Not the Solution I'd Hoped For
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on April 5, 2022
reviews.text: I recently entered the world of acrylic pouring and it wasn't long before I had accumulated an insanely large amount of paint. Tubes and bottles everywhere! I was desperate for a better, more permanent storage solution so of course I turned to Amazon for help. I saw these and thought the wall mount option was a great idea, and so I took a chance and bought FOUR of them. But I was too eager and hadn't bothered to take measurements first, taking for granted that I knew the bins were customizable. Unfortunately once I received them I knew they just weren't going to work for me. The first thing I noticed upon taking this out of the package is that they smell HEAVILY of sawdust. Not really an offensive smell, just really overpowering. Even the next day it was just as strong. Just something I thought was worth mentioning. But that ultimately wasn't my biggest problem... So the compartments ARE customizable. There are dividers that you can remove to create more space. But the way it's designed would make it nearly impossible to wall mount if you were to remove any of the dividers, because then the products wouldn't be as securely snug. I got the impression that if you want to wall mount this, it's better to not remove any of the dividers at all. The photos I've included in this review gives some examples of what will and will not fit into the compartments. It seems 4 oz tubes of paint fit well, like Liquitex or Artist Loft, but 8 oz tubes are definitely too big (and I have a LOT of those). I had expected that when I purchased this organizer, but still wanted to give it a chance. Oddly enough, it depends on the brand when it comes to whether or not a 4 oz bottle will fit. In my photo you can see that a 4 oz bottle of Arteza paint fits perfectly, but a 4 oz bottle of Golden doesn't fit at all. When all the compartments are intact, it is not very flexible so there's no forcing anything in. Now like I said, the dividers CAN be removed so technically you can get any of these items to fit. Though in doing so it's better to keep it upright instead of wall mounted for safety reasons. But what I don't like is how limited customizing the compartments are. And that's where I had to deduct stars. If you need more room, you MUST remove one of the two "long" dividers. So it doesn't just affect the one compartment I need to be bigger, it affects the ENTIRE row. My photos explain it much better than I can in words, but it's just frustrating. I had to remove one long divider and one short divider in order to fit an 8 oz tube of paint. The compartment becomes so large that it actually fits TWO of the tubes. Honestly if this is what you have to do, you might as well just take ALL the dividers out because what's the point? Weirdly enough, the small compartment now fits the 4 oz bottle of Golden since removing some of the panels gives it more "stretch". So this type of customization, while it's cool that they added that feature, is not a good design in my opinion if it's designed for paint. Because while I gained one big compartment, it's TOO big, and the rectangular compartments you end up with are pointless. You CAN substitute one of the long dividers with a short divider, so you can get back some of the square compartments, but because of their length you will still end up with two, narrow rectangular compartments at minimum. Unfortunately I didn't take a photo of that before sending these back. I feel like this issue could be solved by adding more carved out "slits" for the divider panels. Both on the box frame and the panels themselves. It would certainly provide more freedom when it comes to customization. I don't know. I'm not an engineer, but there HAS to be a better way. Or, maybe create this organizer in multiple sizes so that it'll fit 8 oz tubes the way this fits 4 oz tubes. In any case, even if I was able to fit everything perfectly this organizer still wouldn't work for my needs. Because I mostly use tubes of paint, not bottles, and most of the tubes show the paint color near the cap, not the top. So I can't see the paint color unless I pull it out to check. Not an issue if you're using bottles, but for tubes it is. Maybe create this organizer in a second, clear color as well? Or something similar to a spice rack with 45 degree rows that can accommodate bottles and tubes of various sizes while keeping them secured to the wall.

reviews.title: - Great notebook for under $10 -
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on May 14, 2016
reviews.text: First of all, I would like to note that since this notebook is under $10, I didn't expect much. Second of all, a list of the Pros and Cons are at the bottom, for quick review (in case you would not like to read the whole review). I bought this book in the 'coffee' color. The color itself bears some resemblance to actual coffee, but is not as dark. The material catches the light in certain conditions, and the picture (of the product) shows that correctly. The material that the book is made out of is a man-made material that looks like leather (it is NOT LEATHER), but is really cardboard covered in a material that is kind of hard to describe - feels like cardboard (ish); on the inside it feels like a piece of felt that had most of the felt removed, and now it is not as soft but it is not hard. On the outside, the material is quite flat, shiny, and kind of boring. It feels plastic-y. If you look closely, you will see lines that resemble leather. The decal is a compass with lots of detail - it has the main 4 arms and some extra arms that are shorter. It looks like a compass rose you could find on a map, which is the point (I think, what else could it be?). I have seen some people (in the review section) having trouble that their decal is not aligned in the center, but I did not experience this problem. It seems that the company who is producing this notebook has stepped up their quality control, as mine was aligned correctly, and many others were aligned correctly (this data is based on what I have seen in the review section). There are 2 flaps - one is the big one with the decal, and the other, smaller (I would say about 2 x 7, but I'm only guesstimating here) flap. The smaller flap has 2 diagonal holes (you must poke them out on delivery) - I think they are for holding your pen/pencil/writing instrument. There are also vertical holes. I don't know their function, though as speculated in the question section (it could be the review section) that it is for a wallet, or something like that. The idea that the holes are for a wallet is improbable, because things don't tend to stay in the vertical holes. The bindings are simple, yet effective. The strap used to hold the notebook together (making sure the cover won't spring open) is the same material as the cover. It is effective, and it is the one that holds the steering wheel (?). The strap the holds the anchor is long enough to use as a book mark, but the anchor itself is too fat for that purpose. Both trinkets are 'washed' (washed is a term that means to cover an object with a specific color so that gravity pools it to a certain place that makes it look worn - at least, that is what I know of it, I apologize if the definition is incorrect) to look like bronze or copper (more likely bronze) and are made of a metal (I don't know which metal). Sometimes they make noise if you are carrying it around. Moving inside, the paper is connected to the notebook by a 6-ring binder clip. This means that if you wish, you can add more paper, or get refills if you run out of paper. Starting out, the notebook can hold more paper. The paper itself is a tan color, and feels thinner (to me) than regular printer paper, but is more durable. The tan paper (I could say browned) fits in well with the nautical theme. I don't know where to get refills, but If you poke around enough, I'm sure you'll be able to find some (meaning I forgot the link, I have been to the page where you can get refills). I have no complaints with the paper. Overall, this book is extremely good for just $7. While it does have its drawbacks (the material, strange holes..), it is great overall, and I would definitely recommend it. Pros: = $7 = Durable construction = Good color - doesn't fade, to my knowledge = Trinkets are nice - fits in with the nautical theme (Ship's Wheel, Anchor) = Paper can be taken out or added at will = Paper is nice quality = Bindings are nice - they don't come apart, work well with the theme = Compass decal is nicely designed - lots of detail Cons = The material that is made for the cover is plastic-y. Definitely man-made, and definitely NOT LEAHER (Don't be tricked) = Anchor is too fat to be used for a book mark = Might have a problem with the compass decal being off-center = Strange holes that don't have a use (or completely known function) NOTE: The notebook (as stated in the 'title' for the product) is 5 x 7 inches. This means that it is slightly larger than a mass-market paperback. I don't know if you plan to put it in your pocket, but it might not fit (depends on how big your pockets are)

reviews.title: This is a Durable, Vintage Journal that Deserves Five Stars
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 4, 2016
reviews.text: I love this vintage journal. I ordered the large size, dark green color. It is large only relative to the smaller sized journal and is more of a diary sized journal than a full sized notebook, but that is what it meant to be, a durable, personal sized vintage type journal. While it is made from imitation leather, it is high quality and has the feel and durability I would expect from a genuine leather product but at a reasonable price. This journal has a wonderful hand feel to it, from the soft suede feel of the cover to the lovely light brown tinted paper with a vintage appearance and feel. I write in mine using fountain pens with different colors of ink as well as sketch on occasion. I like that the pages are thin enough to feel like pages not craft paper, yet they are thick enough that the ink doesn't bleed through so I can use both sides of the page. I love the method of closure, where The cord with the sun token wraps around the journal. I figured out that when I wrap the cord in a particular way, and use the anchor token as shown in my picture, I can tell if someone has been peeking in my journal as I always wrap it a certain way that seems difficult for others to copy exactly. I am not sure if this is the original intention for the sun and anchor tokens, but it works for me and while it doesn't lock, it can be used to close your journal in a way that you can probably tell if it has been tampered with. I could't find any other obvious use for the anchor token as it is obviously meant to be on the outside of the journal and is too short and bulky for a bookmark. I still have no clue about the reason for the slits in the cover that I have seen some call a holder for credit cards. I couldn't use the slits for a pen holder and it makes no sense to me that a vintage journal would have a place to hold credit cards. The best I could figure for the slits might be to allow the book to close easily without bunching. I bought vintage paper refills for this as well and wrote a separate review for that item in addition to this review. Overall, I find this vintage journal more than meets my expectations and I look forward to writing in it every time I pick it up. I give this vintage journal a solid five star rating and will buy it again.

reviews.title: Good automatic card shuffler.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 13, 2012
reviews.text: If you are simply looking for an automatic card shuffler that does what it advertises, look no further. I have never used any other card shufflers so I can't compare it to higher priced models. With this one, you cut the deck, put 1/2 in one side and the other 1/2 in the other, press on the lever, watch as the cards are shuffled, 1 card upon another, until the deck is complete. Then you slide out the clear deck holder that is place over top of the lever...and you have your cards. You mainly need to make sure you have the deck as close to 1/2 and 1/2 as possible. Drawbacks....this product makes a lot of noise. I personally am not the type of person to care about this. I bought it for it's practicality. But everyone else at the card table complains about it, lol. It's often compared to a weed-eater or a remote control toy car. By the end of the night (and now before we even start) most people at the table want me to put it away. Let it be noted however that they are very traditional and would rather shuffle by hand anyway and also don't really understand the advantages of using an automatic card shuffler (less work having to shuffle and getting a more complete shuffle). This has been my experience with the 'toy.' You get what you pay for - it shuffles the cards well and I've had no trouble with it breaking or not functioning properly, etc. I didn't know what to expect and personally I am very happy with it. reviews.title: Works great for ONE DECK
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 26, 2011
reviews.text: IMPORTANT UPDATE: After going through a few of these from different sellers, DO NOT BUY the ones that take AA batteries. There is just not enough oomph to keep the thing running right. I don't know what it is exactly, but the AA ones will eventually start feeding unevenly. Eventually, we had to stack 1 1/2 decks on one side and 1/2 on the other. HOWEVER, do buy the one that uses C batteries. Look around Amazon until you find it. These have lots of oomph and have been working great from much longer than the AA ones. Here's my original review: I rated this a 4 because it is really a great convenience when you play multi-deck card games. Everyone in our card group loves it. Another benefit is it prolongs the life of the cards (this machine can't tear up cards). Consider that when you buy a game like Five Crowns where you can't just buy a new deck of cards very easily or cheaply. But the reason it lost a point in my rating is this: these things will not work for the max. number of decks listed. They are the right size for the decks, but the compartment that catches the cards fills up and when it gets too high, the cards start to jam up. The solution is to buy the 4-deck shuffler if you need a 2-deck shuffler, and a 6-deck if you need a 4. With the extra room in the catch-compartment, it works like a charm. Be aware it is noisy though. Anyway, just buy the next larger size and you'll love it!

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 5, 2020
reviews.text: I loved this. I am a pretty critical buyer, and I was thoroughly impressed with this. From the photos I was a little worried that the large center piece would be made from MDF, but it was solid wood. It's stained beautifully, and very well made. I saw some reviews about the game pieces not locking into place, but it's crafted like a classic and very nice game...so I think you have to understand that when you buy it. It's perfect for my 7 year old, but if you are playing with toddlers or little kids who are going to abuse it, then it's probably best to just go to a big box store and purchase the plastic game. I personally love the carrying bag. This was one of the features that attracted me to this set. The plastic version from the big box store comes with a very flimsy cardboard box that doesn't hold up at all. We ended up losing a ton of game pieces this way. This came with a plastic bag for such game pieces and they fit nicely inside a velcro pouch after you bag them. I didn't have any issues with the bar at the bottom. You need to slide it all the way in place though. That's the only way (besides abuse) that I can imagine would result in game pieces falling out. It came with 20 each of red and blue game pieces- which fills up every slot on the game board.

reviews.text: It's beautifully made. I exaggerate not... I introduced it to my three old who happen and said, "Wow, this is so nice," as he touched the wood. It has the nice wood smell, too. The negatives: The carrying case makes no sense. If someone is storing a game away, it is almost never in a canvas bag. You have to disassemble it to store it, and the legs still stick out exposed. I'll find another box to store it in so I can store it in the game closet. It's easy to assemble, but you have to pay attention to which leg connects to which side of the frame. Otherwise it won't fit. The sliding piece that releases all of the game pieces does come loose. It's not so loose that it is a deal-breaker for me, but if the game pieces hit it just right, the slider will slide right out and potentially ruin your game. I was surprised to find that the game pieces were made of plastic. Overall, very nice craftsmanship. The aesthetics is exactly what I wanted. I was surprised that the red and blue pieces were plastic. I thought they were painted wood, but I might've misread that.

reviews.title: Defective dimmer switch, put over by multi-layer Leviton scam
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 27, 2021
reviews.text: This Leviton LED/CFL “universal” dimmer switch is significantly defective, overwhelmingly not universal - and they evidently put it over on the market anyway by a multi-layer scam. It’s actually fascinatingly complicated and nasty, although not so wonderful for those of us who are its victims. The one bit of good news here is that Amazon very kindly completely fixed the problem for me - but that probably won’t help you if you too make the mistake of ordering this defective dimmer. In my experience, the main defect with this dimmer switch - as tried with three different kinds of bulbs, namely two kinds of LEDs and one of halogens - is that, almost always when the switch is turned on, it first flashes the lights on, at probably full-on brightness, for a fraction of a second, then dims back down to appropriate brightness as set by the dimmer control slider. This startling flash is like having a camera flash go off in your face, unexpectedly. This intense flash is particularly annoying behavior coming from a device whose entire purpose is to allow the user to set and control the light level and the mood at a desired level. Although, to be fair, in my experience, after this turn-on transient assault on the eyes, this dimmer actually works fairly well, does not (for example) flicker much thereafter. If Leviton just admitted this one bad defect, said yeah, we’ve got this terrible turn-on glitch in this dimmer, too bad, sorry, well then I’d probably just be moderately peeved, rate it say 3 stars and move on from there. But that’s not how it goes when you contact their customer service. First I should say that apparently all their front-line service people are very nice, sincerely trying to be helpful, although not very knowledgeable, and devilishly cleverly set-up by Leviton to put their product over on the market despite its severe defect and limitations and without their even really knowing. I also must note that this dimmer switch device includes, on its upper front face, a small 2-position slider switch, a selector. The instructions that come with this dimmer switch call this the “Bulb Selector Switch,” saying that one position of the switch is for CFLs (compact fluorescent lights), the opposite position is for LEDs and incandescents. They even explain that the CFL position “provides a pre-set kick-start to aid the lamp in starting” - which even makes some sense for fluorescents, since they do often require some kind of electronic kick-start. So, when installing this dimmer, I set its bulb selector switch to LED/Incandescent position (since I was using LEDs, duh!), found that I was getting this crazy huge initial flash of the lights when I turned on the dimmer switch, and called Leviton. The very nice, helpful, fairly-knowledgeable-sounding rep. told me that they had changed the selector switch - or maybe just changed the labeling and the instructions, they weren’t clear about this - but now one switch position was said to be for hard/fast starts, the other position for slow/soft starts. They couldn’t really explain what this meant and how in general to use it, but said that, if I didn’t like the starting/turn-on behavior of the dimmer switch, I should use the other setting of the bulb selector, that should fix the problem. So I tried the opposite setting of the bulb selector switch - which fixed nothing, just altered the length of the nasty flash. I looked around online, found another couple different versions of the instructions. At this point I had the printed instructions that came with the dimmer switch, and the different version information from the Leviton phone rep., and two different instruction versions online - all 4 of them different, each one contradictory of all the others. And all of them actually wrong. Because at this point I determined to watch closely and try to just plain see in detail with my own eyes what exactly was really happening with this dimmer switch, what exactly it was doing. And what I see this switch does at turn-on, as I mentioned earlier here above, is it initially turns on the light apparently full brightness for a fraction of a second, then dims it down to the normal, slider-set level. And, again, this might even make some sense for some kinds of bulbs. But it does it always, on either setting of the bulb-selector switch, where one bulb-selector setting causes this nasty bright flash that lasts just a smallish fraction of a second before it dims, whereas the other bulb-selector setting produces the nasty bright flash for around a second - but anyway almost always a nasty bright flash. You can see this all plain as day if you just try it and look and watch really close. And this all contradicts all the four different versions of instructions/information I have from Leviton. So I called Leviton again. This time the rep. - a different rep., but still nice and helpful - notifies me that I have to use bulbs from their approved list of “compatible” LED bulbs if I expect it to work. So I go away and look online and call back Leviton for a third time. I point out to them that they have at least two different compatible-bulbs lists for this dimmer switch, one list with 100 or 200 different bulbs, another list with close to 800 bulbs, the two compatibles lists almost completely incompatible with each other - but either way including only around 1% of all the enormous number of otherwise-suitable LED bulbs sold on Amazon. In other words, they are saying publicly, up-front that their dimmer is non-compatible with like 99% of all the bulbs on the market - and that that’s not their problem! Meanwhile, at the same time, they hugely lie and say, ultra-falsely, right in this dimmer switch product’s title, that it is “universal” - NOT! And, for my chandelier, which takes bulbs with so-called E11/mini-chandelier bases, a moderately common bulb type, their compatibles lists include not a single compatible bulb, zero, none. When I point out this too to the Leviton rep., then they earnestly advise me that I should replace my chandelier (a perfectly fine, $1,000 chandelier) in order to achieve compatibility with their ($16) dimmer! That was too much nonsense out of Leviton for me. So I contacted Amazon, which itself is officially the on-Amazon seller of this dimmer switch, and they very kindly, promptly refunded my money, so I can now go and try to buy a good dimmer switch. Meanwhile, regarding this Leviton dimmer switch, significantly defective, hugely incompatible, but bolstered by layer upon layer of Leviton scamming, I now rate it 1 star.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on April 20, 2020
reviews.text: I purchased this to replace 2 Lutron 3 way dimmers for my dining room chandelier. Installation was pretty straightforward because i was replacing an existing dimmer. The chandelier has 5 60W equivalent LED bulbs (Feit brand) and any attempts to dim results in incessant flickering. The light can only stay on at the max setting which kind of defeats the purpose of having a dimmer. I tried switching to incandescent bulbs and it still flickers with any attempts to dim. When I went to the Leviton bulb compatibility chart, there is not a single bulb that is listed a best for compatibility. Very disappointed and a waste of money. Stay away if you want a functional dimmer. Update I am updating my review to give the dimmer 3 stars. When I bought this, it came as a 2-pack. Since I was replacing an existing 3 way dimmer, I assumed I could do the same with this. However, any attempts to dim would result in flickering. After much online research and asking an electrician, I figured out that in order for the lights not to flicker, one of the 2 switches had to be a non-dimmer. I bought a regular 3 day non-dimmer switch that costs under $4 and replaced one of the dimmer switches. No more flickering! I can dim with the one dimmer switch and the other is simply an on and off 3 way switch. The only reason for the 3 stars is that the instructions never mentioned not pairing the 2 dimmer switches even though it was sold as a 2-pack. It looks pretty safe because the plastic extends beyond the wire, so it's practically impossible to touch the wire, but it's still technically in contact with air. I've tried Lutron dimmers which are a bit more expensive and they provide a single-cable cap to really isolate the 3-way cable if you don't use it. reviews.text: I am using one to hold my flashlight. As other reviewers have said, the spacers / shims that come with it do not do much to stop the clamps from slipping. The reason is, they are smooth hard plastic, and are useful as spacers, but for most applications they will likely take up too much space for how smooth and hard they are. I removed one side of the shim on the half of the clamp that goes on my handlebars, and made it nice and tight, and it is solid now. If it continues to slip, I can put a rubber band or something with friction between the clamp and the handlebars without issue. The other one I got, well, I had gotten a bike mirror from Amazon as well, but the clamp that came with it was not big enough to get around my handlebars. So, I seperated these double-clamps to have two seperate clamps, each one with a hole left by the attaching nut, this hole can be used to screw other attachments into to have those things be clamp-mounted, which I did with my mirror - I unscrewed its factory clamp from the mirror bar, and screwed the bar into this seperated clamp here. Now, I have an extra spare single clamp which is a useful thing to have an extra of. TLDR: Great value. Can be separated and used for other attachments where a bolt will hold it. The included shims are more like spacers, and you will likely need to get creative about stopping sliding and rotating, like using a rubber band on the inside for friction.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 24, 2019
reviews.text: Nice and cheap. Do hold single cell 18650 and 26550 flashlights to the fork of my bike with only simple modifications for the latter. Plastic inner shims kinda stiff and difficult to click into place, helps to warm them up a bit and apply a non petroleum based lubricant (I used refined cocoa butter, worked like a charm.) Can be ratcheted on the fly in ~ 8° intervals to direct a flashlights beam to the desired angle of attack. Quick release levers kinda fiddly and metal hardware seems to be chrome plated steel which rusts a bit with prolonged exposure to the elements. Update: For use with single-cell 26650 flashlights, recommended to open the channel-locks all the way and switch out the thick default click-lock shims with the single pair of thinner ones you’ll find loose in the box. These lack prongs to hold themselves in place when the clamps are opened, so my advice is to line with 3M VHB™️ double stick tape, trimmed to fit as shown in pic. The 3M sticks a lot better to its own plastic backing and to your fingers than it does to the shims so is a real PITA to work with but still worth the effort for the amount of frustration it will save you in the long run. Bonus, thickness and compressibility of the tape increases spring in the clamps when tightened around a flashlight, making the QR levers a lot easier to operate. If you’ve already lost the spare shims though or need better grip and compression around your flashlight, another alternative is to cut your own from 3M Electronics Self-Stick Rubber Anti-Skid Pads — marketed here on Amazon under the brand name ROOS. Their resilient composition, super sticky adhesive backing and grippy siliconized surface lend them ideally to this purpose. Just slice into strips 3/4” (20mm) wide and cut tabs/notches to match the interior halves of the clamps, peel off backings then press into place (see pic.) Easy-peasy. Do wish a similar mounting bracket were available in aluminum alloy with siliconized rubber shims, would gladly have paid triple the cost here for a higher quality device. Still, not bad for the price, especially with above mentioned mod.

reviews.text: I actually used these to mount a flashlight to my disc golf cart. At first I was disappointed they were all plastic and the orange pieces weren't already built into the inside of the clamps. After multiple uses these clamps hold up pretty well! I love the adjustable hinge. It really enables you to put them on many sizes of flashlights and poles. To stop the orange inner clamp pieces from shuffling around when opening the clamps, I left them shut tightly on the disc golf cart and a flash light. A couple of days later I opened the clamps and the orange inner grips stayed in place from having so much pressure on them for an extended period of time. I would still recommend to be careful when opening the clamps. The inner grips can run off pretty easily. Another thing about the orange inner grips is they aren't very grippy! Even at the tightest setting the clamps easily slides up and down the pole it's mounted to. I haven't had many problems with this, since it takes a little bit of force from your hand, but I just imagined it would be better. Bikers trying to use this would definitely have a problem with these shifting when they hit bumps. You can only tighten a full plastic clamp so much. In summary, know that it's all plastic, the orange pieces don't grip very well and run off on you, they are pretty durable for the price and being made of plastic, and they are e quite universal and inclusive. Overall glad I tried them and will continue to use then.

reviews.title: Like many, I was looking for an alternative to ...
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 15, 2016
reviews.text: Like many, I was looking for an alternative to the standard buckets and carboys for my beer and wine making. The idea of the Fast Ferment was sound and I started investigating. At first I was a little discouraged reading all the comments about leaks and clogging. Eventually I learned that supposedly the company had increased the size of the union valve and neck. This should address the clogging issues. I also planned to just hang any hops, fruit or other ingredients in a muslin sack from a stainless hook installed in the lid if I needed to add any of these items during fermentation or secondary. I figured that would also aid in clogging. As for the leaking, most reviewers noted that once they cleaned up the plastic flash around the threads things were much better and there were no issues. I am fairly handy and figured this wouldn't be much of an issue for me to correct. Finally after some time, I decided to order the product. Once it arrived I removed all the parts and laid everything out. I wasted no time following the instructions and installed and removed all the threaded parts numerous times to "break in" the threads and remove this flash. I did it at least double the recommended amount with very little success. There was still a large amount of flash and the threads did not operate smoothly. Therefore I proceeded to use a de-burring tool to remove the plastic flash from all molded threads. A person could use an Exacto or utility knife as an alternative as long as they only use light pressure and do not gouge into the threads. I then used some sandpaper to ensure all the flash was gone and the threads were very smooth and uniform. I like many, found the top of the conical where the lid attaches and seals to also have a raised flash or edge that prevented the lid from sealing. While completely sealing a vessel is not all that important for fermentation due to the CO2 pressure, it is important for secondary processes and after all, that is the main idea behind this product. Being sealed well is also good to help with monitoring the bubbles in the air lock. With a sanding block and a few minutes, I was able to create a very even and smooth surface on the top of the conical. Now the lid seals very well once installed snuggly by hand. The instructions mention to use 4 wraps of Teflon tape on various threaded fittings. They go on to mention you may need to add more to get a good seal. I would tend to agree that much more will be needed, especially if you do not clean the threads well. The thermowell is especially sensitive to this. I first applied 5 wraps of tape to it and installed it only to find it bottomed out in the hole before ever becoming tight. If not careful, a person could ruin the vessel here by continuing to tighten this. I then removed it and found I needed 10 wraps of tape to get the correct fitment. Ironically, these are some of the only threads that DO NOT have flash.... Finally I added a spigot as well for hydrometer samples. With the valve closed I "pressure tested" the fermenter by blowing into the airlock hole. PERFECT!!! It took some work and more than what the instructions outlined but I now had an air-tight vessel. I blew as hard as I could and not one bit of leakage. As soon as I pulled away from the airlock, the air came rushing back out the hole at me. Once I completed the remainder of the assembly and built a frame or stand to hold the fermenter, (I use an old freezer as a ferment chamber and mounting the arms to the inside of it is not an option) I filled it with water and left it for two days. Not one leak or issue. If you are on the fence deciding whether you need this or not, here is a breakdown of what I see as pros and cons as well as how it compares to other methods. Pros: - Reasonably priced - Similar cost to a good glass carboy, bucket, lid and basic siphon. - You can secondary in the same vessel - Many feel you don't need to secondary beer now a days, but if you do, this does make it easier to simply remove the collection ball and trub without having to transfer. I don't secondary ale beer anymore unless adding things like hops, fruit or similar. Lagers will still get a secondary of course. Wine also gets a secondary. - Thermowell - Get accurate temp readings and use with temperature controllers in applications like mine inside a freezer/chamber. - Yeast harvest is probably the biggest one - You can wash and harvest yeast from a bucket system also but this is cleaner and easier. Not to mention I can pull my yeast cake much sooner and maintain its health instead of waiting until I siphon the beer or wine off of it from a bucket. - You can bottle or keg right from the fermenter. I still prefer a bottling bucket though since bottling from this unit requires you to open the lid, pour the priming solution in and then stir it up. I fear this is more oxygen introduction than properly filling a bottling bucket from bottom up. Cons: - Needs extra work to get the best performance - It is plastic and if you use it as a secondary, especially for wine, you must be careful not to scratch or damage it during de-gassing which gives bacteria a place to grow. - More difficult to clean than a bucket but easier than a carboy. A bottle brush works well for the valve and conical neck. Collection ball is difficult to clean. Kind of awkward to clean anywhere other than a bath tub. - In order to fully clean, you must disassemble the union valve which voids any warranty and be careful upon reassembly to ensure proper function. - Takes up more space in my freezer. If I have something going in this, then I can't condition, lager or ferment anything else. - If you use it for primary and secondary your primary is occupied during secondary/conditioning phase, meaning you can't brew anything else or keep a good rotation going without a second unit. - If you do get a clog or leak, it's going to be a big deal and most likely result in a big mess or a contaminated batch as you insert rods and "things" inside to clear the clog. - Very awkward to move around or do anything with it once you fill it. This means you need to bring your brew kettle/pot to it or try to maneuver it into the final fermentation position after you fill it. In conclusion, I think this is a very good product once you put a little extra effort into it. But then again, what about this hobby doesn't require a little extra effort? I mean, it would be a lot easier to just go to the store and buy beer or wine right??? I give it 4 stars instead of 5 since it does require some extra work to get ready and a product purchased new should be ready to go. Personally, unless I don’t plan to brew anything else anytime soon, I use it as a primary only. Ales go into a bottling bucket, lagers into carboys for conditioning and wine into carboys for clarifying. This way I can keep other things fermenting while those are finishing. If I don’t have any other brews planned, then I will leave things in this fermenter until ready to bottle or keg as the reduced racking is nice. The biggest benefit for me with this product is harvesting the yeast sooner and maintaining is viability. Happy brewing!!!

reviews.title: Amazing features and value
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 12, 2019
reviews.text: I have 2 Fastferment conical 7.9gal fermenters, and I have been using them for about a year. This is the least expensive conical out there, and literally has the most features available regardless of price. SAMPLING PORT easily take samples for gravity readings and tasting without any danger of contamination and without having to use a wine thief (sampling port kit costs $14 on Amazon but once you've got one and have the drill bit, you can add generic sampling ports to subsequent Fastferments for much less) THERMOWELL A Metal - to metal connection goes straight into your wort giving an accurate reading without any danger of contamination. Thermowell is included but the thermometer will set you back $18 on Amazon. BALL COLLECTION VALVE This is the main advantage of conicals in general - great for dumping trub and harvesting yeast (also means no need for a secondary fermenter - just dump the trub and you're in secondary). One vessel means no racking and a lot of saved time!). This also means you can bottle straight out of the fermenter (again, no racking to a bottling bucket = saved time and reduced opportunity for oxidization) WALL MOUNT This is awesome for limited space users and this is truly unique feature. Wall brackets included. MILKY COLOR PLASTIC This means you can't see the fun swirling movement during fermentation, but it also protects your fermentation from sunlight. I still wouldn't leave it in direct sunlight but it doesn't need to be in a dark closet. GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE Fastferment's team is unbeatable. I stupidly drilled my sampling port too low and wrecked a vessel. Fastferment sent me a new vessel for just the cost of shipping. They did not need to do that and it goes to show how hard they work to do right by their customers. ONLINE VIDEOS Fastferment has made plenty of online videos to help with setup and use With all that said, there are some cons: SCREW TOP LID I have gone through 6 lids to find 2 that will seal to the point where my airlock will bubble correctly. The lid seals adaquately to prevent infection, but most of them are not an exact enough fit to get the airlock to bubble. This is just an annoyance since it is fun to see the airlock bubbling. Don't worry though - fermentation is still happening and luckily you can take samples via the sampling port which is the true way to check on your fermentation's progress anyway. There is a thick layer of C02 sitting on your wort protecting it from oxidization, and I do not think any nasties are getting in past the screw top even though the seal is not 100% airtight. TEFLON TAPE Setup is a little tricky because you need to use LOTS of PTFE teflon tape to make sure nothing leaks. The videos cover this very well, and if you follow them you won't have a problem. I recommend on going ahead and getting yourself some extra teflon tape right off the bat. That way you will be able to use lots and lots the first time you set up the fermenter without worrying about exhausting the 1 roll that the Fastferment comes with. EASILY SCRATCHABLE This just means you have to be careful cleaning the inside. I just fill mine with a PBW solution for a few hours, dump it out through the bottom valve, and then just rinse. No problems so far. BPA is just not as hardy as PTE or stainless, so you have to be extra careful with it. COOLING JACKET IS NOT GREAT I did go ahead and buy the Fastferment cooling jacket and I didn't love it. It works for getting the temperature down, but requires 2x a day frozen bottle changes and I don't think it reduces the temp as much as advertised. I'm still experimenting with cooling but the best option would probably be a stand-up freezer with a temp controller. I haven't gone that way yet due to space but I may in the end. Currently I'm working with a Brewjacket immersion pro which is good for getting above or below ambient temp by 15 degrees but not by the 35 degrees advertised. INCLUDED BOTTLING TUBE IS NOT GREAT The fastferment comes with a too-short bottling tube and a clamp for controlling flow. I upgraded to a 1/2' silicon tube and a 1/2" racking cane and it works like a charm. Bottling out of this thing is so quick and easy once you get your setup right! Overall I am super happy with the Fastferment and would recommend it to anyone. Eventually when I have the $$, I would like to upgrade to one of the ridiculously nice stainless fermenters on the market. For now though, the Fastferment is a great system that is meeting all my needs and allowing me to spend my brewing equipment money on other aspects such as temperature control, yeast management, and all grain brewing equipment.

reviews.title: The lid is the fermenter downfall.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on October 18, 2020
reviews.text: Using a conical fermenter is an excellent method for brewing and there are a few manufacturers who make them in various shapes and sizes. The FastFerment is made from a translucent plastic, which the manufacturers state prevents light from affecting the beer. It also means you can't really see if your brew is clear or cloudy before decanting it from the fermenter. If you buy the temperature jacket then light won't be a problem anyway. For me, a translucent fermenter is a disadvantage. The reason I gave the FastFermenter one star is due to the badly manufactured lid and poor customer support. The threads on the top of the fermenter are reasonably substantial but the threads on the lid are thin and practically useless. After screwing on the lid I can pop it off with thumb pressure. I contacted the manufacturer about this and let them know that I had spent a lot of money on every accessory sold for the fermenter. Their response was that I should go and find someone who can sell me another lid. The lids are probably injection moulded, so will a new lid have been manufactured differently??? My guess would be no. I am very disappointed that the FastFerment customer support is so indifferent. They have created a product that could be good but IT'S AS USEFUL AS AN OPEN TOP BUCKET. If bugs can get in through the lid then your brew will always, like this fermenter, be crap. Do not waste your money buying this fermenter.

reviews.title: Love my Fast Ferment
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on May 27, 2020
reviews.text: I’ve just finished my first brew in my new fast ferment. What a treat! I put it together easily using loads of the PTFE tape supplied and had no leaks whatsoever. I didn’t purchase the stand, but made Good use of Covid-19 lockdown time and a load of leftover plywood to build cabinet to house it (I insulated the cabinet to control temp). Being able to remove the sediment via the catching bottle without opening the vessel was brilliant, and apart from that I didn’t have to disturb my brew from the time I transferred it from my boiler, until I was bottling. This totally eliminates any risk of contamination if you’ve sanitised it well before adding the wort. I sampled the beer at that time I bottled it and it really is pub quality with no off taste. Bottling also so easy by using the length of tube supplied with one of those gadgets which fills from the bottom of the bottle and shuts off when you lift it out. Cleaning was also quick and easy. The only thing that is missing is a sampling tap so I have now bought one and will fit it before my next brew. I can see why a lot of people complain about the length of hose that comes with it. Seems to be neither here nor there as it’s only about 2 foot. When I first saw it, my first thought was ‘ why bother including it?’ But as it happens it worked out well for my set up I would say that It’s a little expensive for what it is. If you’re making your own beer to save money it would take you a long time to recoup the cost, but if your main thing is the hobby itself, then it’s definitely a great addition to your set up.

reviews.text: Works pretty good, hasn't broken or burnt too much and I've been using it quite frequently for many months for Japanese style sticks. If you're not using a bowl with ash or rocks or whatever, this is a good cheap alternative. Although one complaint is that I only use the three biggest holes, and the others are too small to fit anything really. Although I assume you could put incense with bamboo core in these smaller holes, given the small diameter of the product you're likely to get ash all over so it is probably better to use flat burners for those. Also to note that the top flower part comes off to give a wider base, which could probably be used to burn cones/coils on. Overall, a solid product that has earned it's keep many times over.

reviews.title: Cool design concept, poor execution
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 25, 2020
reviews.text: Going straight into the problems: The diameter is about 1"-2" too short. As the incense ash falls down, it lands right on the corner of those inner leafs, which can cause it to bounce off the entire collection tray. So you are going to want to put a plate under this if you don't want the ash piling up on the table you have it on. The point of this ash catcher, for me, was to catch the ash so I don't have to use a tray though, so it completely fails at doing its job because they made it too small. There are multiple sized holes for different sized sticks, which is a big plus, but if you put your stick in a hole that's a little too snug, then when you go to remove it it will pull the entire top layer of the catcher with it (this catcher is two pieces, one on top of the other) and if there's ash on that part then obviously it just creates a mess. So you will want to use a hole that is actually a little bigger than the stick, which then causes the stick to sit at an angle instead of straight up, which further causes problem #1 of the catcher not catching the ash. This could be fixed if the top pieces locked into the bottom piece. Aside from those two design flaws, I do like having multiple hole sizes so I can always trust whatever incense I get will fit, and the aesthetics is attractive. If I had to buy one again I would pick something else though, and I really wouldn't recommend this over other ones.

reviews.text: These are everything everyone said they were and more! Amazon win on this one. I’m writing this review specifically for a non-described use, because I struggled to find what I needed and I’m hoping this will help others from wasting time. I wanted glowing bottles for my Halloween display, I tried a number of products and internet suggestions that didn’t work. I started looking for UV reactive ink to try yet another internet suggestion and Amazon suggested these makeup tubes. The key in one of the reviews was how easy it was to remove when using it as makeup. That told me it was likely at least somewhat water soluble and might work to dissolve in water and make “glowing” liquid. It worked great! I did have to do quite a bit of shaking to get it to dissolve, but when it did it was exactly the look I was going for. It had a solid color without the black light and absolutely GLOWED with the black light. I could even adjust the amount of transparency by the amount of makeup I used. I was also able to mix the pink and blue to make my own shade of purple. It did eventually partially settle down to the bottom of the bottle which I took a picture of, but it took over two weeks for that to happen. It still glowed bright with it settled down at the bottom. This ended up being the cheapest and best option of everything I tried. Even better, there is still a ton leftover for any number of craft activities.
