reviews.title: Non è come sembra
reviews.date: Reviewed in Italy on September 1, 2018
reviews.text: Questa è una borsa di buon livello se la si guarda nel complesso ma non è cosi nel dettaglio. Partiamo dall'esterno: Ottime cuciture e materiali buoni ma non eccelsi. Il tessuto esterno, a prescindere dalla colorazione, risulta rigido e poco gradevole al tatto. Questo accade poichè i materiali usati non sono di origine vegetale, bensì, una miscela di plastiche varie, ed ecco perché risulta impermeabile. Le zip sono ben nascoste nelle cuciture ma oltre ad essere un aspetto positivo è anche negativo, infatti, sono difficili da aprire e da chiudere. La casa ha "risolto" aggiungendo delle cordicine che aiutano a tirare la linguetta per chiudere ed aprire le cerniere. Di fatto non sono comode. Interni: L'interno come l'esterno non è ne morbido ne comodo. Il tessuto è semi-morbido e per questo non garantisco un buon risultato per i piccoli graffi che possono presentarsi sulla scocca dei portatili soprattutto in alluminio. Per essere precisi non metterei mai un cellulare all'interno o un ipad senza la custodia perché sicuramente il vetro ne risentirebbe. Riflessione importante: La cosa che mi ha sconvolto maggiormente è che la borsa possiede la cerniera principale, quella che permette di aprirla, in basso e la maniglia nel lato opposto. Il risultato è che il fondo della borsa, aperto, lascerebbe cadere il portatile gravosamente nell'afferrare la borsa per la maniglia. Ora molti penseranno: "E come fai a dimenticare di chiudere la cerniera del fondo mentre afferri la maniglia?" Vi rispondo: La maggior parte di noi è abituata ad avere la cerniera dallo stesso lato della maniglia. In effetti è sempre cosi. In alcuni casi la cerniera è laterale ma MAI posta come fondo di una borsa. Giudizio finale: 2/5 come materiali adatti per accogliere le nostre amate apparecchiature 2/5 come concept fra cerniere e cattive disposizione delle stesse. Spero di essere stato utile a qualcuno prima dell'acquisto Saluti

reviews.title: Good mask, but could use some modifications
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 15, 2020
reviews.text: Looking at other sites that had the same mask, I was really surprised how well they looked on the reveiws, so I ordered one. As you can see, the original mask looks kind of "bland." At a close distance, it was somewhat obvious it was a mask, if someone was looking closely. There were no ear holes and creepy veins on the side of the mask's head. What I did to improve the mask was add hair, (from my cat. I know, kinda gross) eyebrows, and ear hair to the mask. This gave it a much more realistic touch, and hid some of the irregularities of the mask. The best way to disguise yourself is: a hat, glasses/sunglasses, a covid mask (unless covid is over in the future), and long sleeves with gloves. Also wear "old man clothes" but don't make it too obvious. If you want to add a cane, it adds a nice touch. The mask itself fits really well. I thought it was going to be too big, but it was a perfect fit. This mask probably wouldn't fit anyone under 12. If it is summer, the mask gets super hot and uncomfortable, but that's to be expected with any mask. Now you're probably wondering if the mask works, right? It absolutely does! I dressed up in front of my cousin, and he thought "it's pretty good." After I added hair, he said "it's now an 8/10." I also went to my aunts house, and she was blown away by how good it was. (that was before I put hair on). And last, I went into my dad's office and he had no idea it was me. At first, he thought it was an old man, probably asking for directions or something. But he ended up finding out it was me because he recognized my clothing. If he didn't recognize my clothes, he said he "never would have known." If you're in the market for a mask, I would definitely recommend this one. For the price it is absolutely worth it. It's more of a "base mask" for you to add other things onto like hair, glasses, etc.

reviews.title: Great product at a great value
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 13, 2018
reviews.text: I bought this vinyl window film to cover half of a bathroom window in a newborn’s room. The goal was to block out some of the sunlight that comes in in the early morning, while also providing privacy from the neighbors. Overall, I am very satisfied with the film and would recommend it to anyone looking for an easy and low cost method of frosting their window or glass panel. INSTALLATION Installation took about 45 minutes to complete for one window. I made a couple of mistakes along the way which slowed me down, so I think it could be done in less time if done properly. The instructions provided were clear, concise, and easy to follow. The film should be cut to be slightly larger than the window so that you can then trim the excess. The static cling of the vinyl is VERY strong so it is important to spray the entire glass with water. In my first try, I only sprayed part of the window which made it very difficult to align the edges of the film. After spraying the entire window, it easily slid into place. In my opinion, the most difficult part of the installation was cutting the excess film. Make sure you use a sharp razor with a clean edge. I originally used an old razor which kept pulling the film off if the window instead of slicing it. Once I grabbed a new razor, it was much easier to get a clean cut. I also recommend using a credit card or other straight edge to keep the film in place while cutting. This will prevent the film from moving during the cut. The end product looks great and I am very pleased. Because it is vinyl, it can be easily removed anytime without leaving and residue. I love it as a temporary sun filter until my child is a few years older. QUALITY The film is made of a high quality thick vinyl. It feels very durable and resistant to scratches and cuts. It also has a strong static cling which keeps it firmly in position. The prisms are very clean looking which makes it look more like frosted glass than a film application. The light diffusion allows enough light to come in to brighten the room while still blocking the heat and intensity of the sun’s rays. Overall, it is a great value for the cost and I would highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Very Good Printer - Tech Support is Excellent
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 22, 2022
reviews.text: I bought this printer a little over a year ago. First thing I noticed was how big and heavy it was. It set up easily, and the prints started out doing well. As I was still a beginner, there was a lot for me to learn, but overall, once I got settings dialed in, I am able to get pretty good quality prints. I have printed PLA, PETG, ASA and ABS. What I like about the printer is how easy it is to change extruder assemblies on it. If I want to move from a standard extruder/hotend to the all metal, it is just a few screws, drop in the new assembly, do a fast level to set the z height and I am good to go. Changing filament out is also pretty easy. The printer originally came with a high temp hotend as well as the normal one, but I had heard that the high temp had a tendency toward clogging, so I emailed QIDI and they sent me the new all metal for just the cost of shipping. It worked very well, though you have to be real careful changing nozzles on it as it can leak. I also ordered the PEI bed sheet from them, and abandoned the buildtak. It is much easier to deal with and to get prints off of. Again, they gave me a good price on that. This model is being replaced by the XMAX II, which has dual gear extruders, a filament runout sensor and comes standard with the PEI sheet. When I emailed QIDI, they sent me the new extruder assemblies, a new ribbon cable and carriage as well as the runout sensor. This way, I am able to mostly upgrade my original to the new II. This brings up where QIDI really shines, tech support. I have had many conversations with them and they have always been very responsive, and patient with my questions. They even sent me some replacement parts, even though the problems I had may have been my fault, under warranty. In other words, they have gone over and above what I would have expected. Is the printer perfect? No. No printer is. It has its weaknesses and design choices I question, but it is a very capable printer, and some of the weaknesses can be overcome with some mods. The one thing I wish it had, and can't because it uses a proprietary Chitu mainboard, is auto bed leveling via Bltouch or similar. It hasn't been a huge deal because there is a mod out there that allows you to use a dial indicator and get the bed leveled almost perfectly. Another thing I wish it had was the ability to easily add a Raspberry Pi. It can be done, but you must hook a cable up to the actual mainboard. All in all, I am happy with the printer.

reviews.title: Great Machine with even better customer service and ongoing updates
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 6, 2019
reviews.text: This is a fantastic machine backed by unbelievable customer service that continues to get better! We have used this machine 20+ hours a day for over a month. The machine came packaged very well in a thick box with plenty of closed cell foam protecting it. It came with a nice array of tools in a tool box, 2 spring steel flexible build plates and a full spool of red PLA. The included Toshiba USB thumb drive is a nice name brand drive and includes the best set of documentation and software I have ever seen with a 3D printer. It includes WiFi setup instructions, Qidi print slicer software and even a Simplify 3d Profile that they created. The Qidi print software has undergone several iterations since I first received the machine and it works very well. It is based off a CURA and allows for WiFi printing to the machine. When using Qidi print a preview of the object being printed is displayed on the printers display. It produces good results and the included profiles are very good. When using the software I found it was missing the Z offset feature found on Simplify3D. Since it has 2 build plates and they are slightly different in thickness I wanted to be able to create a profile with the correct offset for each plate. I sent an email to Qidi and less than 3 days later they updated the software and added the feature! I was amazed that a company cared that much to devote the time necessary to fix my issue. As time has gone by this was just the beginning of Qidi going out of their way to provide amazing service. So the slicer is good, what about the machine? The machine is heavy and fully enclosed. This printer is a 24V direct drive system running a 32 bit control board with onboard memory for WiFi printing, a full color touch screen and active chamber cooling. What originally caught my eye was the direct drive, H Bot configuration, enclosure and build volume. Unlike the common Cartesian machines the build platform does not swing back and forth in the Y plane but stays stationary. This allows for much better accuracy, less ringing, less noise and lower likelihood of tall prints being knocked over. The removable build plates are very high quality with a buildtak like surface on one side and smooth steel on the other. But, unlike any other machines I have used the second side of the plate can be used as another print surface for high temp materials! You simply apply some PVA glue (which is included) and your all set to print ABS or other materials that you want either a smooth bottom or even Nylons which I will get into later. I was skeptical that putting the print surface down on the heated bed would cause it to bubble and peel but many 15+ hour prints at bed temps of 100C and everything is still like new. The print quality of this machine really is spectacular. In the first 2 pictures you can see the printer torture test and a Marvin. The torture test came out fantastic even the 80 deg overhang! The Marvin is perfect. Both of these show how controlled the machine is and how well the part cooling system works. When using Qidi print you have control over both the part cooling fan and the 2 fans on the enclosure. This allows for huge amounts of part cooling but also where I ran into another issue. The part cooling fan and the chamber fans are controlled by the same header on the board. So if you wanted 25% part cooling you were also forced to take in 25% outside air which was an issue when printing PETG. I contacted Qidi about this and they have since changed the firmware and released a procedure to change which header the chamber fans plug into so now they are independent of one another. I have worked with Stratasys for over a decade and have never had them modify their machines based on my recommendations, I was very surprised to see them accommodate a request like this. This is where things started to get very interesting. Like most machines this has a PTFE lined hot end. Which is great for PLA, PETG, ABS and most other filaments but it is temperature limited to 250C. I contacted Qidi and asked if there was an all metal hotend available to which I was told they would look into it. 3 weeks later I was contacted and told not only did they have an all metal hot end but they created an entire assembly and new firmware that increases the max temp to 300C! I uploaded a picture of the all metal hot end with the original PTFE assembly on its left. It came fully assembled with an E3D hardened steel nozzle! It was a simple swap that required removing 3 screws and follow the quick bed leveling procedure. After that it was game on as all materials are now printable on this machine! Now they were clear that the all metal hot end is only for high temp materials as there was no part cooling fan on it but I wanted to put it through its paces. As any experienced operator knows the all metal hot ends have a hit or miss history of jamming up when printing PLA, PETG and ABS. This mainly comes down to the machining accuracy. I swapped over the part cooling fan from the original hot end and started testing. The next picture shows the bow of 2 benchy's. The left benchy was printed with the original PTFE hot end and the right one with the all metal. Same spool of PLA and the differences are minuscule. The surface is slightly less smooth but that is due to the hardened steel nozzle used. I upped the print temp 8 degrees and everything smoothed out. The next picture shows a chip clip printed in Filamentum Black ASA right into the back of build platform coated in PVA. 0 warp and amazingly clean. As good as the original hot end is with PLA this is just as good with high temp materials. After that success I really wanted to push this machine. In the past I had tried many times to print Polycarbonate on our Raise3D N2 Plus but always has jams. I loaded the filament and ran the heated bed for 15 minutes to heat the chamber. The resulting print is the picture of the 2 bears which left me speechless. A machine that we spent over 4k for couldn't print this material but this X-Max could, I had to look deeper. Upon a closer inspection I noticed that the all metal hotend assembly was not simply just a hotend swap but also a much stronger stepper motor attached to the extruder. So they engineered a high temp, wear resistant hotend assembly with a stronger extruder. Qidi is a Chinese company and I can only assume that some of these details are lost in translation but it showed to me that they know what they are doing and genuinely want to produce quality products. As a final test I wanted to print the most abrasive and hardest material I have used, Nylon X. Nylon X is very hard on any surface it touches especially nozzles. I have seen a brass .4 nozzle blown out after just 250 grams of this stuff. I loaded up a quick vase print. The resulting print was good but could have been better, you can see a de-lamination halfway down the print. I dried the filament for 5 hours before printing but it still had some moisture in it. I dried the filament overnight and gave it another go. Temps were 75 bed, 287 nozzle at a speed of 40mm/s and the vase came out perfect and is watertight. Since I had the material in there I printed out a 25mm cal cube to check accuracy, dead on! The only thing better than this machine is the Customer Service. We purchased this machine knowing it would be a good machine for PLA and ABS but it has been transformed into the best machine on the market for the money hands down. Where else can you get this build volume with material handling up to 300C for this price? I hope more companies listen to their customers like you have. In a market full of copycat printers this is truly a standout. Way to go Qidi!

reviews.title: It has all the traits of the new films but adds in far more Trek "flavoring" *Spoilers*
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 5, 2016
reviews.text: As I sit down to write this "review" of Beyond I'm listening to the soundtrack for the first time on Spotify, and I think the sentiments it's evoking are basically the same for the movie. It has all the traits of the new films but adds in far more Trek "flavoring" which seems very familiar to fans and should satisfy them even more. Far from making it more like Guardians of the Galaxy, the movie went the opposite direction, making it for fans..something I wasn't really originally expecting but may also be affecting it's box office. The 6 original films had a certain "feel". The Next Generation films had one film that felt somewhat like the older films, then 3 with their own tone. The JJ Abrams era began with a retro-original series reawakening of the Roddenberry mission statement from the series "Bible": action-adventure, but with a big budget, huge scale that couldn't have even been imagined with ST: The Motion Picture, the most epic of the original film series. Star Trek had come of age. No longer was it the bastard stepchild of the studio which was the product of complex cost-to-profit ratios that made the movies feel like glossier tv episodes. No one can say that the first two JJ movies do not have differences beyond all the callbacks to TOS however. In the roughly 2 hour run-time for Beyond, the entire world of Trek we saw in hundreds of episodes has to be distilled down from 4 hours of film. That's the entire backdrop of this new universe. It's ripe for all sorts of nit-picking just outside of the story. As such, the movies took awhile to get more quiet and intimate...to have our characters pair off, talk with each other more and really work as a team. So despite two great films in this new "trilogy", with the two over-arching themes being Kirk's development and Spock's trials and tribulations, the films were simply two very well made stand-alones. Beyond brings them both together. In his performance, Pine is now uncannily TOS Kirk. The development of Kirk is happening just as I predicted it: We have the brash, immature Kirk in ST09; the more seasoned but still petulant Kirk who acts on impulse in STID, he makes mistakes but learned from them at the end of the movie; to finally the more developed Kirk who would appear to us to be Kirk from the TV show. This is the exact impression I get from Kirk in Beyond. For all intents and purposes, he starts out in Beyond as the diplomat from certain TOS episodes, negotiating a treaty. His scenes with Bones recall similar soul searching from other movies and Tv episodes..he has gotten past the excitement of exploration and now, despite the technology and volume on a huge starship, he is feeling the oppression of being alone in deep space and encountering numerous dangers that take a toll on one's mindset: a theme that runs parallel to the other captain from Beyond: Balthazar Edison, but in a more extreme fashion. He is the quintessential crazy captain...another staple of the original series. This recognition near the end of the movie dramatically serves to strengthen our empathy with another captain who has gone rogue, but really is just a step or two away from the captains we identify with such as Kirk. Spock's story is less relevant to the film overall, but provides us with further character development as well as memorializing an icon of pop culture. That this film took time to have both a scene on Yorktown and also later in the film to honor Spock Prime/Nimoy is to it's great credit. Justin Lin's direction emphasizing Spock's "aloneness" as he came to grips with Spock's death is terrific. Quinto's Spock has a relevatory moment towards the end of the film as he realizes he doesn't want to leave the Enterprise for New Vulcan. It's one of his best acting moments. Other characters are well served and contribute to the plot moving forward but the real fun is watching them work together. This has really become a family and it appears the off-camera "team" gets along way better than the original actors. Of obvious note, McCoy gets more screen time here and is the heart and soul of many a scene. Jaylah is a welcome addition to the characters, and it's nice to see another female character take center stage. She's a renaissance woman! Engineer, ninja, tattoo artist, music fan. The plot here is not complex..it IS a revenge story so again with these things, it's the telling that's more important than the details. Is it any more or less compelling than Khan? Nero? Shinzon? Khan lost an empire and a wife. Nero, an entire world. Shinzon was emo. Krall couldn't adapt to a new way of life. He existed at the time of a great paradigm shift from a regional space culture with Earth centrism, to an interplanetary UN (ironically these points are more relevant than ever with divisive conservative movements all over the world trying to break up factions of human beings. The message of unity in this movie is so refreshing and a metaphor for the UFP itself!). He seemed to go along with it all, but when his ship crashed, and no one came to help him and his crew, he went off the deep end. His mind twisted by alien tech, loneliness and philosophical differences. Despite being able to leave at some point, his twisted mind led him to stay and plot against the UFP. Unlike some reactions to the film, I think this background to an "alien" character actually helps the film. When I saw Idris's face, I knew there would be more depth to the madness. To my surprise, Krall was in many more scenes of the film than expected, contrary to reports he disappeared in parts of the film..he is there throughout and very much an acting presence. Another thing I like about Krall and the Swarm: I'm just so happy it's not Klingons or Romulans and that both their appearance and tech are totally different. It's so different, the Enterporise is not equipped to handle an attack by so many ships at one time. It's truly an original sequence for Star Trek and rarely seen anywhere else on film. The attack on the Enterprise was much longer than I anticipated and a much better set-piece sequence than even the commercials let on. Never have we seen movement through and around the ship with such detail..crewman running through corridors seen from outside, panning, sweeping shots of relative positions of what is occurring. Yes we've seen ship destruction before, but again how was it accomplished? Surely this is better than any similar scenes we've seen before. So we have terrific character work, a good message and a good "villain". Does it pay off? Well there is a "MacGuffin". That's not a dirty word, and of course the popularizer of the term: Alfred Hitchcock, used them more than a few times. It serves well enough to provide character motives for the rescue mission and for everyone meeting up at Yorktown at the climax. It also provides us with one of the more graphic scenes in Star Trek: the torture and killing of several crewman with the new weapon and Krall's vampiric like absorbption of living beings. The main question here is a bit of a plot hole: Why does Krall need this weapon if his ships can already overwhelm the Yorktown defenses? Ultimately, he does wind up needing it because of what happens to his ships.. As someone pointed out on Twitter, Beyond is the first time there is a movie plot where a black man has been defeated by white rappers. Ironically, a review of mine online for the ST: Voyager TV show episode: "The Swarm" which has similar aliens and technological connection between their swarm-like ships, declared simply jamming the frequency between Swarm ships was too easy a resolution to the puzzle...and of course they used a similar solution here, but this time with VHF 20th century classics. This is one of the weaker points of the movie though the result is an epic chain reaction. There probably is very litle science behind ships bursting into flames from sound waves unless it somehow affected the mechanism used to generate them as they shut off abruptly. The final scenes in Starbase Yorktown were more compelling. Krall's fighter chase was thrilling with some of the most spectacular visuals in Trek history, and the scenes of the fight and chase in lower gravity between Kirk and Krall were something closer to what I would have liked for Kirk's death in Generations if the fight had boiled down to fisticuffs as it did. Another one of the best scenes ever in Trek history occurs at the end of the film..a time-lapse build of the NEW Enterprise-A. Off the new beauty sails into the darkness and mystery of space. The ending re-affirms both the Star Trek family, and symbollically, the theme of unity Yorktown represents. Both multi-cultural, both working together to make a better universe. A great, though not perfect film. Miscellany: Justin Lin was a great choice for director. By comparison, the outside "action" director Stuart Baird really infused very little style or nuance into Nemesis despite making the best looking film since STTMP. Lin is no one trick pony. The "look" of the movie was darker and more muted but still had a technological glow to it. We had some of the best scenes of Starfleet and Federation world-building ever. Starbase Yorktown was a revelation. A technological wonder. The cinematography was probably the best of any ST movie. Despite a different FX company, the movie continued and probably exceeded the very real looking, solid CGI work that we saw in Into Darkness. I might give a slight edge to the spaceship work of ILM, but everything else was probably better. The "Easter eggs" were fantastic, and definitely increased my enjoyment of the film because of the 50th anniversary. My favorite was possibly the nod to "Corbomite Maneuver" and the unexpected byproducts of exploration..complete surprise of the scale of a situation. The aforementioned soundtrack. It's simply the best one since the 1980s. Nostalgia fuel. My only decision...I rated it an "A" on a poll elsewhere, but I feel it's on parallel with ST09 in overall quality, so I had to decide if it will replace that as my number 1 film in Star Trek history. At this time I'm going to put it there, though I'll make a more concrete decision after I see it in the theater again. 1. STB 2. ST09 3. STID 4. STII 5. STFC 6. STIV 7. STNEM 8. STIII 9. STVI 10. STINS 11. STTMP 12. STGEN 13. STV

reviews.title: Best of the "reboot" Films
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 7, 2016
reviews.text: I enjoyed Star Trek Beyond tremendously when I saw it in the theaters but was surprised and dismayed to see the lackluster box office numbers. I felt that this was the best of the three “reboot” movies but the gross was soft enough that Paramount will probably go back to the formula of the first two films at best, at worst they may pull the plug on the “reboot”. So what in the world went wrong? I will try and look at the positives and the weaknesses (and there are a bunch) of the film and see if I can figure out where the film might have failed artistically. What the films really improves on from the previous two is characterization and dialogue. If Star Trek were just a science fiction show/movie it would never have reached the level of success it has achieved. It was the actors as well as the writing that overcame the miniscule budget of the original television show. The skills of the “reboot” actors are excellent and the dialogue, for the most part, has been fine, but they didn’t feel like the original cast. In particular, Chris Pine felt nothing like Capt. Kirk and it wasn’t Pine’s fault, it was the writing. The dialogue this time around is a HUGE improvement and Pine feels like Capt. Kirk. He even does the occasionally Shatner delivery but subtle enough that it doesn’t feel like mockery. For God knows what reason Simon Pegg and Doug Jung, just like the previous writers, do not seem to be able to get it through their thick skulls that Spock is not supposed to show emotions. So where does the movie fail? *sigh* Just as with the previous two films it is in the plot where things fall apart. Almost every Star Trek film is based around an existential threat and those that aren’t tend not to fare well (I’m looking at you Insurrection). Although the Yorktown contains “million” of human and alien lifeforms the movie never invests the viewer in its residence so why should we care if it gets destroyed or not. Even its placement so far out in space seems like poor planning. Krall’s motivation in destroying the Yorktown seems eerily reminiscent to Admiral Marcus’s from the previous film except Marcus, at least, had a moderately well-conceived plan. Spock does state that the Abronath MAY be capable of killing untold planets but it’s capabilities are so ill defined that it’s hard for the viewer to get too concerned. I would contrast it with the Genesis torpedo where the writers of Wrath of Khan very explicitly showed its destructive potential. How in the world did Krall build his unstoppable swarm fleet? We never see any evidence of factories or an economy capable of supporting such a formidable army, just one small base. We only see maybe a few dozen or so bees parked at Krall’s base but when they launch there appear to be millions and each bee seems to have a crew of two or three. I love the Beastie Boys going back to the 80’s but using Sabotage to destroy the swarm fleet made no sense. Even if I accept that they could jam their central control using a VHF signal, why would the ships blow up? Were they all bumping into each other? The bees could punch through starships without blowing up so why would they blow up from getting bumped if that’s indeed what’s happening. So many movies go for a cool visual over plot coherence and sadly Star Trek Beyond is one of those movies. ****SPOILERS**** So, the big reveal is that Krall was the Captain of the USS Franklin which crash landed on the alien planet over 100 years ago and is very much human. Captain Edison hates the Federation because he was a military man and the Federation is peaceful (except when it isn’t). He also felt the Federation abandoned him and his three surviving crew members. The planet was abandoned except for powerful technology and a drone workforce. Very convenient. The exposition dump comes way too fast and way too late in the film and viewers have to make a ton of inferences. How does Krall know about the Abronath since he seems to be sequestered on his planet? How does he know Kirk has it on the Enterprise? How did he take control of the drone army? Does he drain the drones in order to prolong his life? Manas is a perfect example of the films failure to establish characters and motivation. He’s Krall’s second in command and was one of his original crew who was transformed but you may never even notice him unless you’re paying close attention. He’s completely non-descript and has almost no dialogue so when he and Jaylah have their climactic fight few people watching the movie probably care. There are two deleted scenes on the disk but they add nothing to the backstory. If you pay VERY close attention Krall actually has an interesting motivation believing that the Federations soft peaceful existence is sowing the seeds to its own destruction but the message is so muddled and buried that I had to watch the film three times to catch it. Star Trek Beyond is a damn good looking film except for some horrifyingly bad CGI when Kirk and Jaylah are riding on a motorcycle. How that made it into the final product is beyond me. I enjoyed the film for the jokes and I felt that Chris Pine and Karl Urban stole the show. Less so with Zachary Quinto because he still doesn’t feel like Spock. But why can’t they nail down a plot? Keep it simple. Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country is a film with a similar villain motivation but the plot is SO much simpler. I wouldn’t even mind a more complex plot but clearly the writers can’t handle it. My opinion is this is a better film than the previous two even though it made less money and all three are good popcorn flicks. I just wish they could plug the gaping holes in the plot and STOP having Spock show emotion throughout the films.

If you need to install in a thicker sink buy the "TS Supply Nipple B-0425" They come in various lengths, then get elbow separately. FYI the correct sequence to install these is: Use both nuts on a single nipple as jamb nuts to tighten into faucet fitting. That's how you get the leverage that most people seem to be complaining about. Once the nipples are in faucet, Install washers and nuts and tighten to sink, lastly install elbows onto nipples. reviews.text: After reading a few negative reviews I wondered what the problem was with this product, some were whining about. There is no problem with the product at all...none! Just inexperienced people trying to play home plumber with no real trade experience. This kit is the cats ass. I hooked up my triple compartment commercial stainless sink with no issues, no leaks. Now for those that want to use this product, I'll give you some professional advice, I'm a steamfitter with over 40 years at it. Use Rectorseal, Gasoila or another soft set thread sealant on ALL of the threads, not teflon tape.. You'll have no problems. Remember to tighten all of the fittings with wrenches. Double nut the nipple when you install it in the 90 and tighten it until it stops, then install the 90 with nipple into the back of the sink into your fixture. It ain't rocket science folks. If you can't do it properly, hire a professional.

reviews.title: Reliable, but lacks out-of-the-box features
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 2, 2022
reviews.text: I originally ordered the Orbit 57950 B-hyve Smart 12-zone controller. It was much cheaper. And it came with WiFi capability and all 12 zones. However, it would not deliver the 24VAC to turn on/off each valve. And the WiFi signal was so weak that it was unusable on any of our devices. I returned it and decided to spend the extra money for this Rain Bird ESP4ME3. Unfortunately, it only came with 4 zones, and while it’s WiFi capable, it does not include the WiFi module. I spent another $86 for the WiFi module. And since I currently have 6 valves - I’ll need to eventually purchase a 3-port expansion module, which is $43. This brings my total purchase to $257. That’s $137 more than the Orbit B-hyve. But… the Rain Bird unit WORKS! One feature I appreciate is the backlit display, which makes it easy to see at night (the Orbit doesn’t have a backlit display). The Rain Bird controller is much heavier than the Orbit - and this probably means that the 24VAC transformer is able to source more current to the solenoids. In summary… I did not like spending $257 for a sprinkler controller. But the old adage, “You get what you pay for!” rings true here. The Rain Bird is a quality controller that I can rely on. And it should last a long, long time.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 20, 2018
reviews.text: A really handsome light at a great price. A few tips on installation as a replacement light assuming you know the basics of electrical fixture installation (if not it is definitely worth hiring a professional) and the necessary safety precautions. If putting this fixture on siding- check the size of your existing kit as the base of this light is just about 7" (I used this one: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0069KVZZ4/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1). Make sure you get the right one for your siding. I wasn't a big fan of the included mounting bracket I got with the light as it did not allow for horizontal adjustment. I used a nail set to crimp the ring when I had it set at the right position and also added a bead of silicone to fix it in place and to add a waterproof seal to the mounting kit. A hanger fashioned from a wire hanger is also pretty helpful unless you've got a willing assistant to hold the fixture while you make the connections- see the attached photo. reviews.title: Love it, not too heavy and not too light.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 31, 2017
reviews.text: I just got a chance to use this string this weekend. I purchased a new head that uses cut lengths of string, not a spool that autof-eeds. I have made a cutter to cut string to length so I purchase spools. I find this is easier and more cost effective than the old auto-feeder. I went through the left over spool after replacing the old head. I figured I should try some heavier string that is recommended by the new head so I ordered this string. I was changing the strings several times when trimming with the lighter string. I have refrained from trimming around my pond which is surrounded by canary grass, cattails and small willow trees that shreds lighter string. I have used plastic blades on this stuff and they broke after a couple of uses and took too much power. I cut for over 30 minutes and didn't have to replace the line once and it looked as good as when I started. Normally I would have had to change lighter string 5-10 times cutting that grass. I did use it on lighter grass and it worked great. I don't think that small trees would like stand up to it too well, but I try not to use a power trimmer on those anyways. It does take more power to cut, but my trimmer kept up where it didn't with the blades. Out performed my wildest dreams. If it stands up to the pond this well this spool will last several years.

reviews.title: Better than I even thought it would be.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 31, 2013
reviews.text: This stuff surprised me in several ways. First, it's softer than I expected, yet still durable. Maybe that's how trimmer line is supposed to work, but it surprised me. It felt very flimsy compared to the line that came on my trimmer, because it was so pliable. But once on and running it's tough and cuts better than the harder line. It also is quieter than I expected. I'm not sure if that's related to the shape of the line, but I don't hear it spinning through the air as much as the smooth line that was on before - not really a big deal (especially with a trimmer running), but interesting at least. And finally, the contrast of the orange color against green grass is easier to see while spinning, making it easier to tell if it's time to bump-feed more line and easier to see exactly the range of the line that's out. That might not sound like a big deal, but it's actually pretty handy and you can be more precise with your cutting. The only negative I've found so far is that because the line is kind of soft, when running at a slow speed it gets a little floppy and is easily knocked out of being taut and straight. Even tall grass, which it'll slice through like nothing is there when running at high speed, can cause it to just start spinning but not cutting.

reviews.title: Absolutamente geniales para un toque desenfadado!
reviews.date: Reviewed in Spain 🇪🇸 on July 25, 2021
reviews.text: ✷ Set de 3 muñequitos alpinistas para colgar en cualquier pared y que nos sirvan como unos percheros que, además de muy útiles, le darán a tu estancia un puntito divertido! ➤ Los colgadores, nos llegan muy bien presentados en una cajita con ventana para ver parte de su contenido. Llegan bien protegidos, cada uno dentro de una bolsita de plástico de burbuja, y se acompaña de un pequeño sobre en el que hay 6 tacos de nylon y 6 tornillos para poderlos sujetar a la pared. Han pensado en todo, y una cosa súper práctica que hay, es una plantilla de papel con los muñecos dibujados, para que podamos usarla directamente en la pared para marcar los agujeros donde taladrar (ver fotos que he puesto). ➤ La calidad que tienen es estupenda, están muy pero que muy bien acabados y su superficie de plástico es fina y de tacto gustoso. Miden 12.5 x 6.5cm y una vez puestos, la distancia que quedan con respecto a la pared es de 6.5cm (la zona de la cabeza) de modo que nos permite poder colgar hasta un abrigo grueso sin problemas. Cada uno aguanta hasta 2.5 Kg de peso, y te permite cogarle un par de objetos o 3, según el modelo (el blanco, tiene la cabeza y las 2 patas para poder colgar por ejemplo una chaqueta, el bolso y una gorra). 💢 Para colgarlos, los puedes poner como quieras, o en línea, o cada uno a una altura diferente, la distribución que más te guste. Al tener la plantilla, es muy sencillo pues solo tienes que superponerla en la pared en el lugar donde quieres cada perchero. A continuación, marcas ahí con un tornillo en los puntos clave para que atraviese el papel , se marque la pared, y ya tendrás los puntos exactos en los que hacer los agujeros con el taladro. Como puedes ver en las fotos que he puesto, cada muñequito tiene su punto se sujeción único. Una vez puestos, los brazos y manos de cada muñeco esconden los tornillos, de modo que queda visualmente perfecto, parece que estén trepando! 💢 Los hay en varios colores y la verdad es que son muy divertidos, tanto para poner en una habitación como si los quieres poner en el recibidor. Nosotros hemos optado por ponerlos en el recibidor y siempre arrancan una sonrisa a quien viene y los ve. 📌 Están pensados para colgar en una pared, y no en una puerta (a menos que sea maciza). La superficie de sus “manos” y “pies” es muy pequeña, de modo que si quisieras fijarlos con cinta de doble cara tipo 3M, no aguantarían mucho peso. ✪ CONCLUSIÓN FINAL: ⭐ Son geniales, de calidad, simpáticos, funcionales y muy fáciles de poner! Estamos súper contentos con la compra y los recomiendo sin duda alguna. 💬 Espero que lo que te he explicado, te haya sido útil. 👀

Until then, the crispness is a bit loud as you move around in them. Being cotton, these also are not wrinkle free. I just make sure to take them out of the dryer immediately and put them on the bed, smoothing them with my hands as I go, and it works pretty well. If you're looking for wrinkle free, cotton probably isn't the way to go for you. I also wish the fitted sheet had a thicker elastic on it. It does have elastic along the entire fitted sheet edge, which is great, but it's a thin one that I'm not sure how long it will last. It's not a deal breaker, but the pillow cases are open ended rather than envelope and I'd prefer envelope. Overall, these sheets are pretty good. reviews.title: Where have these been all my life?
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 1, 2021
reviews.text: My family always has a lot of open snacks and I’ve tried numerous ways to reign it in because the bottom-of-bag stuff always goes stale before anyone eats it. Those days of excessive food waste are over and I’m no longer throwing away stale chips. These containers have absolutely changed my life. There are a few things that bother me (I’ll get to that later) but overall, I wish that I would have made this purchase sooner. These containers are 100% dishwasher safe (container, lid, sealing ring, and even the chalkboard label - all safe after multiple washings!). The containers are durable, airtight, bug-proof stackable, and very easy to open/re-seal. They are so easy to re-seal that it can be done one-handed while not even sober! They stack nicely on top of the fridge so that available snacks are visible and I top them up from the bag or move them to smaller containers when needed. Because they are visible, they are more likely to get eaten before they have a chance to become stale. Another thing I’ve noticed is that the chips stay unbroken throughout the whole duration of the bag because they aren’t being crushed anymore (aka a lot less chip dust at the bottom of the bag so you get more product for your money than before). There is enough space on the label to write down the expiration date from the bag if you wish. You would be amazed by how freeing it is to be rid of all of the chip branding as well. I never realized that it mattered, but now that my snacks have no wild colors or branding, no crinkled 3/4 eaten unappealing bags, the entire bag is being used on a regular basis. They stay as fresh as the day they were opened and somehow it feels like less mental work to choose a snack. You can see the snack itself at a glance or just read the label, but either way it looks nice and consistent which is super pleasing to the brain. (I’m now looking into other ways to remove branding from my daily life because I love the effect it has had already.) All of that said, I do have a few annoyances: #1 - The sealing ring is best taken off before placing everything in the dishwasher. This is because water gets trapped under the ring and without removing it, water will get trapped under the ring and potentially allow mold to form. I wish that the set came with some kind of tool to pry the ring out so that I don’t have to risk damaging it by using other pointy objects. #2 - The tallest container sadly does not fit in my dishwasher, so I have to hand wash those. I’ve tried both the top rack and the bottom rack. On the bottom it would definitely block the spinning blade and on the top it just doesn’t fit at all. So if you hate hand washing, I recommend only using the tall containers for things that will continually be refilled (favorite chips or baking ingredients like flour) rather than snacks you plan to rotate out. #3 - I feel like I am in constant need of the smallest size container (or smaller!). I wish that I could purchase an additional set of those in this same brand but I simply do not see the option to do so. Despite those few gripes, I’m still giving these containers 5 stars because I feel that they deserve it. If I could give more stars than that, I would. Edit: Some additional things I forgot to mention: - The lids are all the same size, which I absolutely LOVE. No more digging through the cabinet to find that one specific lid. - The labels usually self-wash in the dishwasher and come out blank again, but when that isn't the case, I've found that using a spritz of glass stovetop cleaner works to wipe the chalk marker off pretty easily without damaging the label.

reviews.title: I am pleased with this purchase but it does have some issues.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on April 26, 2021
reviews.text: I actually really like this product. Has downloadable software on the seller site for the rgb, tho very vague in which version to download. I went with the "other" version, as the other serial numbers for software versions did not list my serial, and luckily it works with this board. Though to be fair the this software might ask to change your keyboard firmware warning was a bit scary, especially if I was downloading the wrong keyboard software and firmware, but it worked, so guess I dodged a bullet. Otherwise very customizable rgb via the software. Worst part about ordering this board on amazon and not the sellers site tho is that if you order the black on on the site, its fully customizable, including switch upgrades, keycaps, board size, but when you order it on amazon, its brown switches and brown switches only. I feel like they had a surplus of brown switch versions they needed to get rid of and they just dumped them on amazon. I ordered this before I knew you could get it on their site, and free prime shipping is what really made me order it, thought I think if orders are over 99$ on their site, shipping is free anyways, so not sure if thats really an issue, but as I said, I didnt know that before I got this keyboard. Things I would improve, the numpad stabilzer location. It comes with a switch remover but the stabs are very close together and angled with very little space to get into around the + sign and the ENTER key. It was hard to wedge in the provided switch remover to take them out, and I was unable to use my other switch remover to do this task, as you need a completely FLAT switch remover to fit into these very small clearance areas. I dunno if this is changeable but I would look into it. Its hotswappable so people are going to want to remove those switches, and man were they a pita to remove. I would also change lack of rgb lights when computer is turned off. My old keyboard and mouse both have lights when the computer is off, and both of the mentioned keyboard and mouse are from different companies, so its pretty easy to say that this is mostly a rgb standard among MOST companies, but NOT for this keyboard. Once the computer is off, keyboard is dead. There are no lights, no nothing, The lights themselves are not THAT bright. If you are using a keycap set that does NOT have see thru icon, then you will only get a light backlit rgb light, which isnt very bright. If you do use a keycap set that is provided with the build you will most likely either get the keycaps that have the see thru icons on them so rgb will be visible to see what the keys say, or you might also get the pudding caps which have the lower base white see thru bottoms that also show a lot of the rgb along with the see thru icons. Most keycaps in general tho do not have rgb icons and even the key cap sets they have that are on their site for sale do not have rgb friendly icons, though tbh they are fairly nice looking with gradient style colors. So just keep that in mind if you decide to swap out keycaps, cause you could be removing a lot of the rgb lights needed to make this keyboard look really cool. More about keycaps. These keycaps that come with the board have function key information built onto the keys. The board itself has some hard wired built in functions for rgb that you can use WITHOUT the software. Sure you wont be able to customize each key without the software but you can still use the function keys and pressing the right keys to input commands for the board to change colors and rgb style effects. BUT if you buy any other keycaps to customize the board, you will no longer have these marked labeled keys to know what to press to do what. You will be totally in the dark. The gradient keys offered on the site that they sell do not have any of the function commands printed on the keys for these keyboards. I know this cause I have them on this board. So the only way you will still know which keys do what functions is to keep the original keys or memorize it. There are two pages of commands for the function keys in the manual to tell you what keys do what, so good luck with that memorizing. Hope you really like those keycaps you are going to swap out for or at the very least you got the software installed and are set to use the board as is without wanting to change setting on the fly. If you take the board to another place and put it on another computer you will not have access to your saved settings either. You will have to use the function keys to really get any functionality out of the rgb settings, so having other keycaps on this board will be a problem. I have a mouse that has a usb mini drive that you plug into its wifi receiver that keeps all my stored setting in it, this might be an idea to implement with wanting to travel and keep your saved settings for your board at new location, but I dont know that they will really be so concerned to look into this. Maybe if it was for the smaller boards, that people travel with more, it might be something worth looking into. Or if you really were a rgb fanboy that wanted your board set up no matter where you went or go. Like to conventions or twitch cons, etc. then you might be more concerned with having saved settings at all time. Either way, its not currently an option to take your saved setting on your board. You can import and export your settings to the software, though there is no profile log in for specific users to access to save settings on a server or anything like that. But you could just reinstall the software on the new computer and bring a usb drive and import your settings? Wow just saying all that seemed like more hassle then I want to go thru for some rgb lights, so yea pass. I asked the companies discord chat where they say you can go for support, about this lack of rgb lights when computer was off, and was told that I didnt need lights when computer was off. Ok odd. Good to know you know what I need. I honestly went there just to find a hard answer of yes or no, if this was adjustable, I found neither of those. Most of the people responding to my question either ignored it or didnt know a hard yes or no as to why the lights were inactive, or if there was any way to activate them. Would be nice to know, hey this is deactivated for safety and not wanting the keyboard to overheat, or maybe oh there is a way to activate it, here do this. Or just NO its not possible, its hard wired into the board to NOT do this, but no, there were no answers, So dont hope for much support with this keyboard. But regardless of my complaints it does work as intended, and I do like the board.

reviews.title: Great keyboard, but not perfect.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 24, 2022
reviews.text: This keyboard is surprisingly good, but has a couple of flaws that I would like to highlight at the end. First, the good. The feel of the keys is outstanding, even for ABS keycaps. They have a subtle texture that is nice to touch that doesn't feel as sterile as a more smoothly finished surface. I am generally a fan of brown switches (quiet tactile) and the included Gateron Brown switches are perfectly solid. The switches themselves don't make much noise... most of the typing noise comes from the keycap bottoming out, so depending on how hard you type, you will experience more or less typing noise. The downloadable software allows you to change the polling rate from 250Hz up to 1000Hz. It came out of the box at 250Hz. It also allows you to change the backlight color scheme however you want, whether you want each key different individually, or just want to use the default color schemes that are included. Two flaws, however, one fixable and the other... not so much. First, as you can see in the photo, the formation of the legends appears... incomplete. You can see especially on the @ and the #, they are definitely malformed. This isn't a huge deal, but it just feels unpolished, and will be a non-issue for those of you who intend to replace the keycaps anyways. Because of this, I'm probably going to look at a solid double-shot PBT keycap set sooner rather than later. The second is that while the keyboard software allows you to set three different profiles for the backlight, you cannot switch between them without using the keyboard software, i.e. you have to launch the software every time you want to change it. There are no hotkeys or key combinations to change the profile. You can change the color scheme among the defaults with key combinations, but not any custom lighting you may have defined within the profiles. This seems like something of a overlooked item on the part of Glorious... not a huge flaw, but definitely inconvenient, and based on what I've read, not something they seem interested in addressing, as the software for this keyboard is older than the software for the GMMK 2 and Pro. I also wish the USB cable was detachable, and that there was USB passthrough, but that's just nitpicking at this point. Solid keyboard, otherwise, and a great value.

Would have been nice to have been able to pick the switches...but assume that would have come with a price tag for customisation. 2) would be cool to have a couple more rgb lights under the space bar, only 1 light where the switch is. Overall a great starter kit, with all the bits to get you started, was worth the £150 price tag. Sounds good, feels good, plays good, looks good etc etc

reviews.title: An interesting solidly built mechanical keyboard let down by bad software
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on January 7, 2022
reviews.text: For reference: coming from a Pok3r mechanical keyboard which was sufferring from poor key registration after many years of use. Rather than blowing cash on a bunch of new switches and digging out my soldering iron, I thought I would give this GMMK keyboard a go. Specifically interested due to the hot swappable switches. Pros: - good build quality for price, brushed aluminium on sides and top - swappable switches is an interesting idea: can take Cherry / Gateron / Kailh switches without having to mess with resoldering. Hopefully means this keyboard will last a while with minimal maintenance hassle. - RGB lighting customizable down to individual keys - lots of RGB preset patterns Cons: - No hardware layer support like the Pok3r or GMMK Pro (GMMK Pro is double or more cost of standard GMMK after you buy parts) - Only 3 profiles in software for RGB and key bindings - Software profiles can't be set with a keyboard shortcut - have to mouse click through multiple software menues - Software key bindings are janky. Not clear how modifiers work, and config is limited.

description: Product Description Tubigrip provides tissue support in the treatment of strains and sprains, soft tissue injuries, joint effusions, general edema, post- burn scarring and ribcage injuries and is also used for pressure dressings and arm fixation. Tubigrip provides lasting, effective tissue support with complete freedom of movement for the patient. Once the bandage has been applied, covered elastic threads within the fabric move to adjust to the contours of the body and distribute support evenly over the surface. Fitting is quick and easy and Tubigrip stays securely in place without pins or tapes, unlike other conventional bandages. Tubigrip can easily be reapplied after washing, without loss of effect. Tubular Bandage Applicators may be used to make application easier over bulky dressings or painful joints. If an applicator is used, Tubigrip is loaded onto the applicator, which is then positioned over the affected area. The end of the bandage is held in position while the applicator is gently removed, leaving the Tubigrip in place. Then form a double layer by doubling back the bandage. Ensure that the upper edge of the second layer is taken 2–3cm higher up the limb than the first. reviews.title: Worked well in my old repurposed grinder.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on May 4, 2022
reviews.text: I replaced my old bench grinder with a new one and decided to 'upgrade' the old one with a new wire wheel and adding a buffing wheel. The old grinder's housing was a bit too close (IMHO) to add a buffing wheel so I installed the EmilyPro shaft extension (the longer version). Fit and finish was (barely) acceptable - the interior of the extension staff was burred and had to be cleaned up before it would slide over the grinder arbor shaft. In addition the retaining nut (13/16 o.d.) did not thread onto the EmilyPro arbor shaft until I cleaned up the shaft threads. Quality control may not be quite the best I've ever seen. Once installed (simple installation, remove the old grinding wheel, remove the grinder's guard, slide the EmilyPro onto the grinder arbor shaft, secure with the included hex screw using the included hex wrench, install the included retaining washer, install the buffing wheel, install the second included retaining washer, and thread on the retaining nut. Note that the EmilyPro I installed was for the right side of the grinder. After reading reviews I was concerned about vibration but that turned out to be not a concern - there is some vibration but not enough to cause a problem. YMMV. I'd recommend the EmilyPro, but with the caveat that you may run into quality control issues so don't expect necessarily a plug-n-play solution. I'd also recommend not making any alterations to the adapter that would prevent you from sending the unit back in case there are vibration issues. Including the cost of the new wire wheel and the EmilyPro and I added functionality to my basement shop for about $40 - better than sending the old grinder to the recycle yard. Total time to upgrade the grinder (including cleaning up the EmilyPro threads and inside shaft) was about 30 minutes.

reviews.title: Decent Protector but Headache to Install
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 24, 2018
reviews.text: I just received the Julk case for my Apple Watch Series 3 and here are my thoughts: You receive two cases and two sets of wet & dry wipes in the packaging and nothing else. No installation instructions, no visual guides, nothing. They do give you the entire step-by-step guide on their Amazon site when you scroll through the product photos but if you were expecting anything in the actual product box, you will be disappointed. It looked simple enough to install, it literally is one piece of flexible, rubbery material that wraps around the front of your watch. The cutouts on the sides help you orient which way to put the protector on. However, there was a disconnect in the simplicity of how the product looks with the actual application of said product. After removing my watch straps and powering off my device, I wiped my watch with the wet cloth then the dry one to remove any dust particles and finger prints. I then took one of the Julk covers and worked my watch into it, button sides first to ensure they were lined up with the cutouts. This thing is a SNUG fit, which is what you want of course, but it makes it a beast to get the watch into it initially. Once I slid the device in and got it lined up, I went about stretching the Julk and squeezing my watch in. Because of the rubbery material, it would cling to the watch making any type of adjusting and sliding around nearly impossible. I literally had to stretch the Julk to the point I felt I was going to break it, to make it fit around the watch. All of this activity must have pressed down on my power button because at least 3 or 4 times the watch came on and I had to shut it off again. Once I got it around, it somehow didn't fit my device properly and trying to adjust it was a pain in the butt. I got frustrated and ripped the Julk off the watch and proceeded to use the second cover and try again after I wiped the device and dried it a second time. I repeated the same steps and got the one side of my watch in, ensuring proper alignment and stretched the Julk around. This time it was almost perfectly aligned around the entire watch but I still had to strong arm it and stretch it to the point of being scared I was going to rip the rubber, to get it to align perfectly. To this product's credit, the first cover I had ripped off my watch with some force, bounced back to its' original shape so it was able to take the abuse and "repair" itself without warping or stretching out permanently. After it was properly installed I began testing out how well it allows you to use your watch's touch screen and if it made it less sensitive to your touch. To my pleasant surprise, the watch is still quite responsive despite the rubbery type of cover on it, so I am pleased. There are instances where it is difficult to swipe away notifications and previously opened apps due to the rubbery-ness of the cover but it is not on every occasion. Since the Julk wraps around the entirety of the front and sides of the watch, I feel it is pretty well protected and the cover's clarity makes it so it does not detract too much from the watch's beauty. I have to see how well this material holds up over time, hopefully it will not get weirdly discolored or attract too many particles like similar cases I have had in the past for other devices made out of the same material. Overall I would give the Julk case a 4 out of 5 stars. It does fit snugly around the Apple watch and the cutouts align perfectly (once you get it installed properly). It offers decent protection in my opinion and it does not degrade the watch's performance. Will I keep the case long term? I am actually not sure. With other cases for my ipads and iphones, etc... when I knew I had THE ONE, I knew I was keeping it for the long haul and reordering the same exact thing once it became worn out. With this Julk case, I do not get that same level of absolute certainty that it is the case for me. I am actually ordering a pack of traditional screen protectors (the kind that clings to the surface) as back-up. They will not offer the same type of sude protection, but I feel they would be better as far as being unobtrusive to the watch's screen clarity and touch screen responsiveness. I hope this review is helpful to you folks out there!

reviews.title: A Good and Easier Way to Protect Your Watch
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on October 4, 2020
reviews.text: I tried a number of different screen protectors for my iWatch over the last couple of years. The type that adheres to the watch face by wet-application is the least apparent of watch face protections. Most of those adherent types are completely invisible once you get them on, but that process always requires no small amount of time and requires leaving the watch off the wrist while it dries (usually overnight). But they are very nice, while they last. I have found those adherent protectors to last anywhere from a couple of days to maybe a few months until they start to peel off. I really got tired of going through the process of applying a new one that frequently. Thus, I bought this product in May of 2020. I have returned here today to purchase another box of two having today replaced the first one with the second one. I'm going to stick with this type because overall it's just a lot easier to deal with and it does what it needs to do. Now that I have the new one on, it really is crystal clear and 'invisible' -- just like the screen wet-application type. The one I just replaced had turned slightly yellow, likely from exposure to sunshine during the summer months. After four months and some weeks, it was finally time to use the second screen protector in this package. That is a better replacement record than with the wet-application screen protectors. Plus, it's a lot easier to replace and requires no loss of wearing time. I have never experienced any trouble with watch usability with the Julk case on the watch. Once on --and especially when brand new--it is completely invisible like there was nothing on the watch. The touch screen is as usable with it on as it is without it on. If you do get dirt or pet hairs or whatever underneath the case, you can easily take it off and clean it gently with some water and maybe a drop or two of rubbing alcohol. I did that a couple of times and it looked nearly brand new after doing that. I noticed that some people have complained these are hard to get on. As mentioned above, I had removed the first one a couple of times to clean it, and I think with practice, you learn how to quickly get the case in place. The case is tight, but you want it tight. You have to tug and stretch the band a little to get it over the side of the watch, but if you work from the top of the watch, getting the alignment right and fitting it on down the watch, getting that last band over the side of the watch is really not that hard. Took a minute or two. If you've had trouble with the wet-application type screen protectors as I have had (I was so frustrated with the last package I bought where I was replacing it every couple of days or so!) I think you'll find this Julk Case a better way of protecting your watch. I like, also, that it covers the side of the watch, which wet-application surface protectors do not. The frame of your watch is thus protected from getting scratched, too. For the price, it's a good deal, even if it discolors and gets surface scratches (which mine did also) after three or four months' wear. Better the case than the watch. The surface scratches on the case were not so noticeable as to interfere with watch use but they do happen, I found out. The wet-application protectors do not show scratches, from my experience. However, the problem with them peeling off at the corners and needing constant replacement makes the Julk Case preferable for me, regardless of the minor scratches it eventually gets. So, I'm buying another pack to have on hand when I need to change this second one out.

reviews.title: Classic Subtle Brando!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 3, 2020
reviews.text: A sleepy noir romance that’s poignant and sympathetic to its characters. Sidney Lumet’s noir romance drama The Fugitive Kind (1960) is an enthralling adaptation of Tennessee Williams’ Southern Gothic play about love, loneliness, outsiders, sexism, xenophobia, and racism. Lumet’s direction is all noir aesthetic utilizing shadows, silhouettes, and close spaces for a hot Summer backdrop for The Fugitive Kind. Boris Kaufman’s cinematography makes use of dreamy close-ups and stark black space separating lovers. His wide shots outdoors are so mysterious. Kenyon Hopkins’ score is nuanced and romantic, apt for the disquieting atmosphere and loving vibe around the central characters. Tennessee Williams gives as much sympathy for his drifters, empathy for his housewives, as he writes disdainfully towards his racist figures. Tennessee Williams was a genius writer, whose poetic flowery language coated biting critique of American society. You can hear Williams’ voice condemning cruelty. violence, and hate towards women as he writes every man in this backwater Mississippi town to be ignorant and loathsome. Marlon Brando’s intriguing tough guitarist moving with the win named Valentine “Snakeskin” Xavier is the lone thoughtful man in The Fugitive Kind. Everything happens to him as he gets no agency and Brando brilliantly shows his frustration and disappointment in a subtle and romantic dramatic role like few could have played. Marlon could easily be a romantic lead as Val with his handsome features and cool appearance with his snakeskin jacket and muscular physique. We can thank costume designer Frank Thompson for that jacket and Lady’s gorgeous black dresses. But, it’s Brando’s quiet glares, judgements, and kindness that make Val such an engaging character as Brando carries himself with a heavy gait and undeniable gravitas. You are drawn towards his serious expressions and sincere line delivery. Anna Magnani is incredible as a miserable, middle-aged, wife left to look after her sickly husband’s store. Magnani makes her character Lady Torrance. I adore her Italian accent, gentle eyes, and desperation for affection. She is passionate without seeming needy and strong without having to resort to violence. I think Anna Magnani gives as powerful and moving a lead actress performance as Lady in The Fugitive Kind as I have ever seen in my entire life. She is remarkable! Joanne Woodward is fun as the lush girl Carol Cutrere, who willfully demands Marlon Brando join her on the road. She is genuinely funny and entertaining in The Fugitive Kind as the third wheel in Brando and Magnani’s love triangle. Her hysterical antics remind me of Vivian Leigh’s iconic acting as Blanche in A Streetcar Named Desire. Victor Jory is perfectly cast as the ugly, older, racist lecher called Jabe Torrance. He looks sweaty and filthy like his disgusting character Jabe. Maureen Stapleton is so nice and open as Vee Talbot. R.G. Armstrong is so quietly cruel and intimidating as the racist and corrupt Sheriff Jordan Talbot. The Fugitive Kind’s entire cast is nicely picked for each unique role so that you really feel like you’re looking at Mississippi in this past era. In short, The Fugitive Kind is pure deep feelings and emotional honesty for 119 minutes of riveting direction and heartfelt acting.

reviews.text: The Fugitive Kind is probably Marlon Brando's least effective collaboration with Tennessee Williams. A funky little melodrama (with its own full share of unintentional laughs), a brooding Brando is left adrift as a kind of snakeskin Elvis Presley variation. But without the occasional musical interlude to break things up. The film has its moments, but it just doesn't manage to come together. The sum of its impressive parts (writer, cast, director, cinematographer) fails to add up to the expected artistic powerhouse whole. An interesting failure, and a curiosity, for sure, but a long way from Brando's usual high standards of the day.

reviews.title: Vintage Williams; Near Peak Brando
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on May 27, 2015
reviews.text: This is a great film-play, though some critics considered it over-the-top. Tennessee Williams provided the fissionable material that enabled a great cast and a great stage director to make the film very special, in a way that transcended its flaws. Developments in the story were plotted for great emotional impact, as something was always happening. Brando gave a performance of confident physicality, as the jaded Valentine Xavierna who tries to build a new life. Anna Magnani was intense as a villain's wife, but the part was somewhat lightly written, so that her affair with Valentine has been criticized as unconvincing. I agree, but for me that did not prevent the story from moving ahead. It kept all of the characters isolated, living in their private worlds, and that seems to be how Williams felt the story. A young Joanne Woodward was excellent as the alcoholic nymphomaniac Carol who pursued Valentine. This was probably the most mythological element of the story, based on the play "Orpheus Descending," as she followed Val like a fury, to show that he could not escape from the law: "Wherever you go, there you are." Director Sidney Lumet handled pacing and intensity very well, and the sets were excellent. A film worth keeping.

reviews.title: Fake Widescreen - Buyer Alert!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 21, 2006
reviews.text: The aspect ratio is fake. The top and bottom of the regular full screen version has been cropped out of the picture to give the illusion your getting a widescreen - what your getting is less picture! The studios should label the DVD's as they did when they cropped VHS video picture " this film has been modified to fit you tv screen" as in modified to fit a 16x9 tv in this case. You have already lost one third of the picture when it was modified to full screen, now you loose an additional one third to one fourth of the movies image! The reason leterbox and widescreen has a demand, is that the audience or consumer wants to view the Movie as it was filmed and framed by the filmaker, and not loose out on portions of the movie that the director intended. In other words the idea to release in widescreen was for the intention of showing MORE not LESS of the movies image. The studios believe they can get away with this, since the average buyer does not have a full screen video version to compare with, or the consumer is just unaware. I compared this DVD to a full screen VHS version, and in many cases where some DVD's come with both Full & Wide Screen on a flip disc, compare them before watching, many of the widesreen sides are just chopped versions of the full screen. The picture quality is great on this and most DVD's, it is unfortunate though that it has to be a conciliation for cropped picture.

reviews.text: It is slow, beautifully photographed and Magnani smoulders as the unhappy wife of a vicious store keeper who falls for the drifter employed to help as husband is upstairs an invalid. The drifter is Marlon Brando and was he handsome - and sexy. It is based on the Orpheus legend cleaned up a bit for the screen - the Tennessee Williams play, Orpheus Descending, on which it is based ends with a castration, the film does not although it does not have not a happy ending, and while Magnani is magnificent she is Italian and fitting her, broken English and all, into a small town in the Deep South takes a little suspension of belief. Joanne Woodward plays a dissolute, unhappy girl who, like the drifter, is seeking something unattainable rather well. Not director Sidney Lumet's best movie perhaps but worth it for the performances of the stars and the photography.

reviews.text: This harness is really nice quality and I was excited to try it on my lab/mastiff mix. He currently has a more traditional fitting harness but I thought this might be more comfortable because it doesn’t go between his front legs. Put it on him and he wouldn’t move…he just stood there and cried a little. I had it fitted properly but the chest piece was maybe sitting higher than he liked? He’s very emotional about weird things and I guess this was one of them. I took it off and he sulked for about an hour before he finally forgave me. Honestly I loved the harness and was very impressed with the feel for the price but my guy wasn’t going to have anything to do with it!!

reviews.title: Sizing according to the product might be off.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 25, 2022
reviews.text: We've only had this product for a few days, but I wanted to write a review asap in regards to sizing because the chart doesn't seem to be accurate. We are looking for something safer than the mesh harnesses our pups can slip out of fairly easily. We have a 7 pound yorkie with a chest of 13.5 inches and a 12 pound morkie with a chest of 15.5 inches. According to the sizing shown, this should fit our yorkie and be too small for the morkie. It was too large for the yorkie even when adjusted to the smallest size. She is also a drama queen and did not like how structured it is. The harness did fit our morkie perfectly, and she doesn't seem to be bothered by the stiffness. She has an issue with pulling on walks, but it is something we are working on correcting through behavior modification. She has not slipped out of this harness yet. It is possible you will have to exchange for a different size or that your dog may not like how structured the harness feels. If you are expecting this product to stop your dog from pulling, don't. The only things that will completely stop this behavior are collars that could harm them or proper leash training.

After about three months of use, the porta filter has completely come out of the handle, as shown in the picture. But I fixed that with JB Weld quickset epoxy adhesive. I believe the heat from the machine just softens the adhesive that the manufacture uses and the handle separated. On the flip side, the shots taste good (I think). Price is affordable. I like the sleek polished stainless steel finish. It's not too big and fits on my counter in my coffee nook. Overall, I give it a solid ok. You get what you pay for.
