Besides that, you get a lot of functionality including two parametric EQ's, and EQs on every channel and built in FX sends that I have found incredibly useful and of great quality. One thing I also really enjoy about this mixer is I've found it to have far less noise than my other DACs. Which I assume is just the quality internals of an Alesis product I personally like to use this mixer to mix my drums and then send it's output into a seperate USB audio interface along with my other instruments/mics. This mixer has more functionality than I have mentioned, some of which I'm not entirely sure how to use yet! But I think any entry level recording enthusiast would enjoy this amazing quality mixer

reviews.title: Good for beginners recording themselves, not for bands
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 26, 2021
reviews.text: If you’re looking to record multiple instruments at once, look elsewhere. There is only one output through USB, and it combines all the inputs. If you’re looking for a mixer to power a XLR mic and headphones for discord/zoom/OBS, look elsewhere. Using a mic while using the USB to Output button (which you would need to in order to hear your PC sounds) makes the PC output go into your mic output. So your friends can hear themselves, and your audio will not pick up correctly. (You could fix this by buying a 3.5mm to 1/4in split cable, and hooking it into the line 3 inputs, if you really wanted to) There is noticeable noise, particularly when the effects are turned to 100 and there isnt anything playing. The effects sound good. If i was only recording a single instrument and vocals, id get this. But for recording a mic, a bass, and a guitar just gets too difficult to work with. This was for my case. I wanted separate outputs for each input, so that editing in my DAW was easier. You are unable to do so.

reviews.title: Great for the price
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 9, 2017
reviews.text: Pros: - Multi-XLR inputs for recording - Effects (Should you enjoy them) - Acts as a DAC in-itself - Treble/Bass EQ settings - Plug-n-play functionality - Good price for the functionality IMO Cons: - Effects are nearly trash (useless to me) - 16-bit signal chain (could tell a difference in defaults) I bought this for use with my new AT2020 microphone. Overall, I have to say I am very pleased with this purchase. I like how I was able to just connect it to my PC and it be recognized without any further configuration. My main complaint is that is that only supports 16-bit audio. When I first used it I could hear a distinct "distortion" in the audio quality. I found that that changing the bitrate setting in Windows from "CD Quality" to "DVD Quality" got rid of this issue. I still don't like that it doesn't support the higher bit-rates or bit-depths as other mixers, but for the price this is probably as good as it gets. I love the EQ settings this thing offers. It only as a treble and bass EQ, but that is all I need. I came from a Scarlett Solo, which has no EQ settings, but a higher bit-rate and I have to say I would choose the flexibility of this mixer over the solo. Maybe not the best for complete quality, but for flexibility it is awesome. The included effects are garbage. I didn't find a single one to be useful in any application. The only reason I bought this "FX" model is because the original model was discontinued. The effects are worthless unless you are just trying to impress a friend over discord. I really like the ability to plug in multiple Mics when trying to make a podcast and power them via phantom. That is the real selling point for me. The fact that this much flexibility can be had for =<$100 is amazing. That is why I give this four stars. Would be five if it supported a higher bit-rate.

reviews.title: Basic straight forward 4-input usb mixer - built like a tank
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on February 19, 2021
reviews.text: I'd spent a lot of time looking for a usb mixer and had real trouble finding one that had all the features that I wanted - at least 4 inputs, built in effects, usb out, phantom power and able to act as a stand alone mixer, on/off switch - and wasn't too large or too complicated. This Alesis mixer has all the features that I wanted and is only 18 x 22 x 06 cm. The first thing I noticed when I picked up the box was that it was heavy - this thing is built like a tank, steel facia and back, with plastic sides and the knobs and switches all feel quality. In line with most 4 track mixers inputs 1 and 2 have XLR and jack inputs and separate EQ controls and inputs 3 and 4 are just jack inputs and share one set of EQ controls. Inputs 1 and 2 have both gain and level knobs, as well as pan knobs, while 3 and 4 just have level knobs. Inputs 1 and 2 also have 80HZ low cut switches and input two has a guitar switch to accept high impedance signals. There are 15 effects - 8 reverb, 2 delay, 3 modulation (chorus, flange and rotary) and two multi (chorus and reverb) plus a bypass setting. Effects are dialled in via the selector knob and controlled by both a FX send knob on the inputs and a master FX return level knob. On the back are the power 18V power input, on/off switch, phantom power switch and the usb out socket. The unit comes with short, straight-forward instructions in English and I was very quickly able to get it up and running. Everything works as you would expect in a straight-forward manner, when connected to my iMac it immediately recognised the Alesis and I was able to transfer data. The gain and level knobs are a good feature and on most things that I've plugged in - electric guitars, acoustic guitars, ukuleles, mics, condenser mics etc - I've quickly been able to adjust the signal and get a usable sound. The headphone inputs works fine and there is also a mini jack input to connect mp3 players etc which I haven't used yet. The effects are quite subtle and don't sound synthetic, they are easily adjusted via the send and return knobs. All in all I am very pleased with this mixer, I had considered mixers with more inputs and controls and I'm so glad that I didn't go down that road, the simplicity of this Alesis mixer makes it so easy to use and when lockdown is over and I get a chance to use it in a live setting I'm sure it will come into its own on a dimly lit stage. There are cheaper mixers out there with more features but this does feel quality and I'm sure that it will last.

reviews.title: Old dog, new tricks
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 5, 2019
reviews.text: This is just the first day of using the bed. I was super excited to get the product ON TIME. I was previously using a cave bed that my Jack Russell Terrier could not fit into and used as a pillow (maybe because the product page failed to include important measuring requirements). At first my dog was like, Where by my bed at?! And I plopped this thing down and he took to it immediately. I wanted to call him off of it so he could see the little opening and he was actually reluctant to leave it. I think it is pretty clear he loves this bed. I considered washing it before use, but it smelled okay to me. I cannot comment on how easy it is to clean, but I will edit my review if I end up having difficulties. I did sit on it beforehand and it is soft with good cushion. It did not sink in like memory foam though. It currently supports his weight of about 12 lbs comfortably. He sleeps a lot so I think this is a good investment for him. *********TWO MONTH UPDATE********************* My dog who is 11 years old, finally figured out how to get under the blanket thing. I had given up on him and would hold it open for him at night. I guess I take too long to tuck him in and he figured out how to do it on his own. I have a stuffed animal I stick in on the side to prop it open a little. ********FOUR MONTH UPDATE********************* I removed the plastic tubing and the stuffed animal and my dog finally let himself in. What I think helped was that he knew it was possible and having a routine. Every night I brush his teeth and hold up the blanket for him to go under. Tonight I didn't bother because it’s warm anyway but I found he tucked himself in. So yay! It took him a while, but he figured it out eventually! The photo with the panda is NOT staged at all. 7 month update****** My dog started sleeping ON TOP of the cover instead of under when it got warmer, even though he knows how to get into it. So I removed the plastic frame. Then I found that he started to prefer the floor or the laundry pile. Tonight he was refusing to go to his bed, even though he knows the command. So I tried an experiment: I took his downstairs cat bed upstairs and put that on top of this bed and he immediately went for it. So maybe this bed is good for the winter...or maybe my dog just likes his smaller cozy beds with walls.

reviews.title: Thumbs up from this pumping scooter commuter
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on October 25, 2021
reviews.text: I'm a pumping mom who commutes to work by subway and scooter. I needed a compact, water resistant backpack that was easy to manage and had an insulated pouch for my lunch (morning commute) and expressed breast milk (evening commute). This bag delivered in so many way: Pros: Lightweight, well padded straps, fabric looks and feels nice and spot cleans well despite being a lighter gray color, good water resistance, well stitched and constructed with external zippers that glide very smoothly. The main compartment is double zip and the laptop compartment is single. The lunch section is a decent size and keeps things cold for a long time. It's easy to clean and keeps messes in, too. I had a leaky container of pesto pasta and nothing leaked through to the main compartments or outside fabric, which was pretty impressive to me. With an ice pack it keeps my breast milk frozen in the pump bags for at least 2 hours. I stick a flat icepack and up to 4 bags right in the internal mesh pocket (keeps things tidy and protected on my commute home). The size is perfect--not too big or small. It fits my 15" laptop, phones, chargers, and a spiral 5 subject notebook with no issues. I'm able to fit both my phones (iPhone 8S in Otter box and an Samsung S10), a pen and stylus, in the internal pocket, but those pockets are a snug fit. I have some room to spare in the main compartment. Once masks are off I will definitely be able to throw a makeup bag in there. I love, love, love the card pocket on the strap! Finding my MetroCard in a snap was always a struggle for me. I spent one too many mornings in a cold sweat, frantically searching pockets, the bottom of my bag, etc, thinking it was lost for good. With this feature this is no longer the case, thankfully! Cons: The pocket layout and capacity could be better, overall. Every pocket is constructed of stitched nylon with no elastic or extra fabric for give. I would have liked to see a larger computer accessory pocket made of elasticized mesh in the computer compartment, a zip pocket in the main compartment (there is none), and a larger zip pocket under the flap. The phone and pen pockets are decently sized, but they definitely won't fit some of the larger phones on the market today. It would be nice if they added a metal D-ring to attach keys and/or an ID to. I'm using that small zip pocket under the flap because there's no other good place for them, but it's cramped. Ideally I would put sunglasses in there, but I can't because they would get scratched up. On a functional note, I thought I would like the added security of having the zipper compartment under the flap but it just makes getting things out a bit of a pain. The handle is sturdy, simple and small. I would prefer it to be a bit bigger so I could slip it over my wrist while juggling security doors, my scooter, etc. Overall, I really like this bag. I give it 4.5 stars due to to the negatives I mention above. It looks like Matien makes another bag similar to this with larger handles and an exposed external pocket. I'll probably pick that one up instead since I'm super anal retentive, but I do feel that this is a very good bag that would exceed most people's expectations for the price (~$29 at time of purchase).

reviews.title: Well built, but poor separation between backpack and cooler compartments
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 4, 2022
reviews.text: I purchased this for the return to work. My company switched to a “open floor plan” during the quarantine, so now I only have a locker rather than a cubicle. I needed a way to carry my computer, office supplies and a few cold drinks. The upper flap is there for show only. Open it and there is a small zipper compartment underneath that isn’t really large enough to be useful. The lower flap is the insulated compartment. It’s important to know the compartment is soft-sided and shares the space of the main compartment- so if you use the insulated compartment, you lose space in the main and vice-versa. That is the problem, anything you put in the main compartment will crush anything you put in the insulated one once the bag is vertical. You pretty much have to load the main compartment, turn the bag upside down and shake stuff to the top - which opens up the space at the bottom for you to pack the insulated compartment. The insulated compartment is also wedge-shaped. Viewed from the side, it’s a triangle, not a cube. This limits how much you can pack in there quite a bit. The improvements the pack needs are to make the insulated section a cube, and provide a removable hard-side liner to protect the insulated area from the main compartment. Add a few pockets and loops under the upper flap for easy access items or office supplies and you’ve got a winner.

reviews.text: I’ve never seen a backpack that incorporated an insulated section before. I’m so glad that such a thing exists because this has simplified what I need to bring with me to work everyday. I thought the strap card pocket would be great, but in reality it is difficult to take my transit pass out while I’m wearing gloves so I haven’t been using it. These are minor complaints though. I do like this backpack, and I’m very happy with it. The size isn’t overwhelming and it holds a good amount. reviews.title: YES, THEY LEAK URINE...
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 20, 2018
reviews.text: ...BECAUSE THEY ARE SWIM DIAPERS. I am absolutely flabbergasted that so many people are coming here to complain that these SWIM DIAPERS do not absorb urine! They are SWIM DIAPERS. They are meant to hold solid waste only. If they were made to hold urine, they would absorb the urine like a disposable diaper does, and they would also absorb ALL OF THE POOL WATER. All swim diapers will "leak" if you are expecting them to absorb urine like regular disposable diapers. So yes, people...If you have been swimming in a pool where infants and toddlers in swim diapers have been swimming...You have been swimming in pool water that has urine in it. It won't kill you. On a more related note...These diapers do their job. No solid waste in the water. Thumbs up, Pampers, for creating swim diapers that work like swim diapers.

reviews.title: Good for more than one use if no poop in it
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 15, 2014
reviews.text: If your baby doesn't poop in these, rinse and wring the diaper out with his or her bathing suit and hang it up to dry and use again. We ended up with only three swim diapers at the beach, so we had to improvise. The pee was washed away in the pool or the ocean. We also washed a couple in the washing machine on gentle cycle, laid them out to dry, and used them the next day with no problem. We managed to get 2-3 uses out of each diaper. Since these diapers work exactly the same way as fabric swim diapers (keeping only poop in but letting pee out), we decided to treat them the same, and they worked just fine. As prior reviewers have noted, this diaper does not hold pee, so definitely don't put baby in a carseat while wearing one.

reviews.text: I am an avid Pampers fan so I purchased these for my toddler who is learning to swim. Regular diapers swell up and drag almost down to his knees driving him nuts. I gave these 4 stars, however, because they do leak more often than non-disposable swim diapers and don't hold as much pee. I know they're not designed to be very absorbent, but when I tested one it only held about 1/2 a cup of water without dripping. Ten minutes after putting them on my son had pee running down his leg.

reviews.title: It was an easy fix, since I ordered the iGrill2 from Amazon
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 7, 2018
reviews.text: Let me begin by saying that I never had the opportunity to use the old app so I can't compare it to the current version. I purchased mine in November of 2017 for $80 on Amazon. After using it for a few months, I found that a product review was needed for those interested in purchasing this. At the time, I was looking at the iGrill 2, iGrill 3 and the Thermopro-07/08. Out of the box, the unit comes with the basics to BBQ and grill. This included 2-tempurature probes, the unit, and other trinkets (e.g. sleeves to change the probe colors, a metal piece to adhere it a non-metalic surface etc.). The one thing I felt it lacked was the ambient probe. It was an easy fix, since I ordered the iGrill2 from Amazon, I also ordered the ambient probe for about $14 extra dollars. In my opinion I felt that the unit should have came with one meat probe and an ambient probe as well (total of two) rather than just two meat probes. When my unit arrived, my first cook was a whole chicken. i used the units presets to alert me when it was done. It worked great and was easy to set. I have put this unit to the test, BBQing at least 3 times a week. Over the past 2 months, I have used it for various cuts of meat. This includes, whole chicken, chicken quarters, chicken legs, beef steaks (various cuts), pork and beef ribs, pork butt and brisket to name a few. As a personal preference, I found that I occasionally use the pre-set temperatures and instead set the alerts to my liking. This is just because I noticed some of the preset temperatures were at a different temperature than my personal likings or that I wanted to pull the meat off prior to the preset to wrap or sauce. The presets give no option to setup this type of timer. The ambient probe is really good. It comes with a grill grate holder that it mounts in. It then lays about level with the meat you're cooking to monitor the meat. The other probes do what you want them to do as well (monitor the internal temperature). With two meat probes, I'm able to monitor two separate chunks of meat on the grill or (on a large piece) place them on both sides of the meat to ensure even cooking. As for the unit, it is very basic and can work without a phone (or other bluetooth device connected to it). If you don't want to use it with a phone or other device, you're limited to setting temps for each probe only. You also can also monitor each probes temperature from the iGrill device as well. Now, I'll talk a little about the app. Again, I've only used the current (as of this review) version of the app. I can't see a way to show what version my app is. It appears that it was designed by someone not into cooking/BBQing/Grilling. There are many features that I think the app could use to make it much more tailored to each user's need. One thing I would like to see in later features is the ability to 'modify' the preset temperatures. Another modification would be to add a search feature on the presets. As it is now, you need to choose the 'type' of meat you're cooking, then scroll through the alphabetical order list. One 'smart' feature that I think would be nice to add is for the app to notice a fast drop of temperatures (e.g. from 245 degrees to a fast drop to 110 degrees within seconds). This would be useful when you need to lift the lid and mop your meat or add some fuel (charcoal) to the grill and not want to have your app start beeping at you to warn you the temperature is too low. I know there are other additions that the app could use, but these are just my thoughts for now. Overall, if you're considering getting this Weber iGrill2 to add to your tools, I would recommend it. I would say that there are other probes and devices that do the same for less. Some are bluetooth and some are not. If you want to stick with the Weber brand, like I did, then go for it. I paid $80 (on sale from Amazon) for the unit and another $14 for the extra ambient probe.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 19, 2019
reviews.text: I bought the original iGrill 2 before Weber bought the product line (I think it was originally made by iReady?), and have used it since. I've been through all versions of the companion app from before its Weber days to it's most recent version. The probes can be inaccurate, especially the older ones, and you have to be sure to place them carefully or you will get a false reading. It died about 4 days ago after approximately 3 years of heavy use when I was using it on some London broil, so I ordered a new one (it's being delivered today). On occasions where the probes became inaccurate, I emailed Weber and they replaced them for me at no cost- even the ones from before they bought the line. However, that spooked me a bit so now when I do pork or chicken I use a quick-read digital thermometer, usually in place of (but sometimes in addition to) the iGrill. The ambient probe is very handy when doing a long cook where fire management is critical (such as smoking ribs or doing a roast). It gives accurate measure at grate-level, rather than at the top of the cover. The companion app is really handy and easy to use and has come a long way, but it still does NOT allow you to set one probe as ambient. I have asked for this feature on numerous occasions, and they still have yet to make it happen. Otherwise, it is highly customizable and very easy to use. The issue is that since it's bluetooth and not WiFi, I lose connection with the device when I head inside (I'm not going to sit outside and chain myself to the grill all day when I'm doing a large roast). It does reconnect as soon as I get within range, so I'm not sure why I'm reading that others had issues reconnecting. The base unit shows the temperature of each probe, which can be selected by pressing the arrow keys. You can connect up to 4 probes at a time. Within the app, you can set up the doneness of your cook by selecting type of meat or by setting custom temperatures and set timers (such as reminders to turn food, start veggies or check the fire). It also shows graphs so you can monitor the rate of cook and estimate with a fair degree of accuracy when your food will be ready to come off the grill. There is also the option to save cooks and share out to social media (I've never used that part, but it's there if you want it). It's actually quite a full-featured app, but it's also very easy to use. Weber's customer service is always quick, responsive and courteous. They have replaced 2 probes at no cost to me, both in just a couple of days.

reviews.title: Overly sensitive voltage selector and possibility of damaging sensitive equipment
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 7, 2021
reviews.text: This should be the perfect variable power adapter kit were it not for one very annoying problem and one potentially hazardous flaw. The Good: 1. Plenty of fitted barrel adapters are included with this kit to ensure a perfect fit to any device. 2. Turning the control knob on the unit immediately changes the output. It’s situated right next to a LED readout of the current voltage - with 2 decimal place precision (e.g., 5.75V). The kit will output a maximum voltage higher than the vast majority of people will ever need. The Bad: 1. The knob for selecting an output voltage is far, far, FAR to precise. There’s zero “give” when turning it. A slight brush can (and has) upped the output by several volts. 2a. The other downside to an overly sensitive control is setting the desired output. Dialing into an exact value, say 5.00V, takes finesse. It’s a game of tapping the control back & forth until it lands on the target. 2b. The control knob is an endless encoder (it spins around with no stopping point in either direction). There were obvious design choices which makes it precise to the point of annoyance. A slightly different set of components could easily allow the knob to work without frustration. The Ugly: The kit is in DIRE need of a “lock” to prevent the control knob from immediately changing output voltages. I understand these multi-adapter, variable voltage adapters are not meant as permanent replacements for an OEM adapter; regardless, it does offer quite a range of wonderful options. Before trying this kit on expensive electronics, I tested it on a rechargeable battery dock. Within the few hours, the two biggest problems became apparent. I barely touched the voltage control when sitting it on a table. It took a couple of hours to notice the batteries stopped charging. Upon further investigation, the LED readout showed the output was 4.86V instead of 5V - not quite enough to engage the charger. Later that day, the table was bumped, knocking the control unit off. From simply landing on the knob, it turned the output voltage up to over 10V! That’s when I decided this adapter would not go near equipment worth any amount of money. - - This would be perfect with 2 small hardware changes (until then, tread carefully): 1. Require at least one full turn of the knob per volt instead of the slight nudge it takes to jump a few volts. 2. Add a switch for engaging/disengaging the voltage knob to lock the adapter at a selected voltage. TL;DR: Do not get this for any sensitive equipment & stay mindful of how a slight touch can drastically change the voltage output. I’d be more than happy to update this review whenever the manufacturer adds a couple of glaringly overlooked safety features.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on October 6, 2015
reviews.text: I bought this item as our double pushchair (iCandy Peach Blossom 3) is short on storage - there is a decent size basket at the bottom, but when the pushchair is used in double mode it is very hard to access, and so not great for frequently needed items like beakers and wipes. It fastens via fairly strong velcro to the side of the buggy (the bars of the chassis that go up from the lowest part right up to the handles), and hangs downwards. The mesh material is sturdy, and after months of use is still in perfect condition. The Pros: It adds that extra storage we needed for frequently used bits and pieces, and can even be used to store everything needed for nappy changes if that's helpful (a couple of nappies, wipes, cream and nappy liners). It can stay fastened to the frame when it is folded up and stored (ours lives in our car boot most of the time, and so it's handy keeping this always on the frame, ready for use - the two velcro loops sort of bunch together when our pushchair is folded down, but you just pull them apart again the next time you put it up. It is sturdy and my kids haven't quite figured out how to get into it when seated in the pushchair yet! The Cons: It has quite a narrow, tight opening, so getting things in can take a second or two longer than you'd like, or require 2 hands (though this does make it harder for my toddler and baby to get into it, so no bad thing in some respects!). I personally find the mesh material a little scratchy, but I do have pretty sensitive skin, so that may just be me - my Husband doesn't have a problem with it. None of these cons are significant enough to take a star off the rating. If I used my buggy more (I'm now back at work full-time) I would buy a second one for the other side - between the Side Sling Cargo Net and the hook I have on my handlebar (for shopping bags), all my mobile storage needs are catered for.

reviews.title: Poor Quality and Missing parts
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 28, 2022
reviews.text: I’ve owned at least a half dozen hunting umbrellas over the past 30+ years. Some sold by this company (Allen), and also some other brands. I “assume” they’re all made by one company and marketed under different names. Regardless of that, they’ve all been flimsy, finicky devices at best. They’re made using lightweight materials (by design), and they definitely won’t stand up to heavy rain, wet snow, or moderate to high winds. However, if you hunt from a tree stand, ladder stand (or even on the ground), these umbrellas are an essential piece of equipment. My new umbrella arrived missing three of the six straps used to secure it to the tree. I should have received a short, medium, and long strap for each side of the umbrella. I only received straps for one side, which makes the umbrella 100% useless. Fortunately, I have some leftover straps from an older (failed) umbrella, so I’ll be able to use those in the future. The umbrella mounting bracket was also problem. The mounting disc/grip stripped the threads on the screw shaft the first time I tried to use it. Couldn’t screw it completely into the tree, couldn’t screw it back out of the tree. Useless. Of course, all this happened in the woods, in the rain! Shame on me for not doing a proper inventory and testing the umbrella before heading out hunting! Buyer beware. I’ve had similar issues with the screw-in mounting bracket with other umbrellas in the past. I was able to fix the problem by adding an additional locking nut on each side of the mounting disc, and applying a couple drops of permatex thread seal before reassembly (see picture). Chalk it all up to a crappy design, that has never been improved/perfected. However… the real question is… why market/sell a device that needs to be “fixed” by the customer before it can actually be used. Allen Company could just as easily add locking nuts to their product during assembly. As for the additional couple cents that would add to production cost…I’d be willing to pay an additional couple bucks for an umbrella I could use right out of the box. As for the missing straps…? Guess I’ll just buy a different brand next time. See if they know how to count.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 29, 2019
reviews.text: I'm an amateur woodworker trying to go pro. I *mainly* use the grits in the 80 through 400 range, with my 8 hole, somewhat low-powered random orbital sander (Harbor Freight "Bauer" model and an apparently identical model branded under "TACKLIFE"). In fact, I have yet to use the 40, 60, or 800 grit discs *on a powered sander.* However, the 80 through 400 grit range works fabulously under power. The discs are reasonably resistant to clogging (I recommend having one of those "sandpaper eraser" blocks, usually yellow, even with "clog-RESISTANT" abrasives), and they seem to start sharper and stay sharper longer than the crummy+cheap ones that came with my sander. Perhaps there are even better performing "premium" sanding discs out there? But I won't find out anytime soon. I'll probably purchase these exact same discs again for the 80-400 grit range, because 70 of my most-used grits for under $25 (as of 8/29/2019) is less expensive than the competition. And I'll continue to use the "leftover" 40, 60, and 800 grit discs, for random hand-sanding tasks. My only gripe *would* be that 220 grit and 240 grit are so close together in fine-ness, but to be honest, I don't mind because that's the grit that I use the most. So, kinda like getting 20 of one of my most-used grits instead of 10. All in all, a great purchase for my Benediction Works projects, and just great to have around the shop.

reviews.title: Almost Nine Years Now And Still Standing!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 28, 2014
reviews.text: I love this shelving unit! I bought it just over three years ago when I was moving into a new house and decided I wanted to store my shoes in a way I could easily see and grab them versus throwing them in an old laundry basket and having to constantly dig around searching for the other pair and ruining my nice heels too. Now, I will admit the materials used to make this unit are very cheap, esp. the wood and a couple of areas had already splintered when I received it, but I quickly remedied this by simply removing the splinters with my bare hands. It came with all the parts needed to assemble it, but it took a little longer to do this probably than it should have because I had to slightly wrestle with it to get/bend the shelves to line up with the wooden frames (either that or it also could have been the fact that this was the first time I had ever assembled anything and I was just a complete novice at it). Of course when I say "wrestle," I mean I barely used a little more muscle to put it together and I'm as weak as people come, so anyone else (but me) should have no problem putting it together in a jiffy. Once it finally was assembled, it was perfect! Today, I am storing 21 pairs of sneakers, heels, and sandals on it (the ones I mostly use) and I'm doing this by stacking some shoes on top of each other (this goes to show how much space is in between each shelf). I am even storing a pair of rubber sandals underneath the bottom shelf (the ones you use like at the pool that are cheap and flat). This storage unit has fulfilled every single need and want of mine and I'd buy another one exactly like it, if I had more closet space to put a second one in. Now, let me address some of the points mentioned in the negative reviews. First off, my unit was NOT defective when it arrived, i.e. it was not broken, warped, and the screws were not missing, as some people mentioned in their negative reviews, but all my returns to Amazon have been simple, esp. when a product was defective, so I don't think this would be a problem, so much as an inconvenience, on the off chance you received a defective one. Secondly, some reviewers have stated that this unit is cheap and they don't believe it will last for long or hold up to storing more heavier items. Well, I already addressed the cheap quality above and I don't know what they planned to store on it that they think would break it, but If you use it like it was intended for, i.e. shoes, clothes, purses, stuff of that lightweight, etc., then I would expect yours to last like mine has, which has been around for more than three (3) years now and still looks pretty brand new. I think I need to mention that I do not move mine much other than to occasionally vacuum underneath it and it sits on carpet, so it doesn't move on its own either when I remove shoes off and its never toppled over. Thirdly, some people have mentioned that the unit seems small and cannot store many shoes. Well, I don't know about men's shoes, but it holds more than enough of my women's shoes perfectly well (though I have no problem stacking a few of my older pairs on top of each other). The unit may be small for some people, but its size is absolutely perfect for my small closet and its fits really nicely underneath all my clothes. Lastly, a few reviewers have remarked that it is flimsy, weak, and/or too lightweight and while I do agree it is lightweight, I disagree about it being weak or flimsy. I wanted a unit that is light because this was going in my closet and I can't imagine why someone would need a heavier one unless your storing bowling balls or something else than what this particular unit was designed for. It being light and sturdy enough is ideal for easily pulling it out with shoes still on it to quickly vacuum underneath it and put it back without really bending over or straining one's self. Overall, I bought this closet shelving unit when it was just over $20 and I feel like I have gotten more than my money's worth since then. It does its job and it does it well and I would recommend this product to anyone who just needs a simple storage unit and intends to use it like it was meant for. Again, three years later and it's still standing! Edit: It’s been almost 9 years now (June 2020) and it’s still standing! Almost in as good as shape as the day it arrived. This is a solid buy!

reviews.title: The frame is wood, the shelves are shiny wire!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 25, 2012
reviews.text: Mine was easy to put together, as sturdy as one would expect, and attractive in a shelvy sort of way. Unlike some other commentors, I have the impression from the way the light shines off of the wood when the light hits it, that there is a nice layer of shellac or a related finish protecting it, and I have seen no evidence of splinters so far. Although I am sure it sits on a closet shelf very nicely, I have mounted it up on the wall in one corner of the small bathroom, hanging it from four long sheetmetal screws screwed at appropriately-placed points. This is an off-label use of course, and would probably void the warrantee if there was one, but so far it has show no sign of leaping from the wall and making a loud noise in the middle of the night, causing me to sit bolt-upright in bed in a startled confusion. It is important to note that the shiny chrome wire bars on the shelves are a significant distance apart, so that in the raw and unmodified form putting anything small or narrow on one of the shelves is likely to be unrewarding. A small container of dental floss, for instance, will easily slip through the bars. But here is a tip! If you put a few sheets of notebook paper, or a piece of stiff paper, or even a small piece of corrugated cardboard if that is handiest, onto the shelf, you can then put other things, even small things such as a container of dental floss, onto the shelf on top of that paper (or cardboard), and then the things will not fall. It will be as though the shelf did not have wide spaces between the bars at all! One reservation I do have about this product is that they provided only exactly the number of nuts and bolts that you actually need to put it together, rather than two or three extra as is often the case. If one were to be assembling the closet shelves for instance in the old boathouse down on the lake, where the water is visible between the old wooden slats of the floor, and you were to drop one of the nuts or bolts, there would be a good chance that it would drop between the slats into the water, down among the silt and muck of countless years, and then where would you be? Fortunately, this did not happen to me.

reviews.text: This review is for the 16 gauge round copper wire. Please note: this is pure copper wire. If you do not seal it with something, it very well might turn your skin green. That is what copper does (especially if it gets exposed to moisture, sweat, etc.). It also will tarnish if exposed to the air for long periods of time. Again, a property of copper. You can prevent this by storing in an enclosed container with anti-tarnish tabs, adding a patina, or sealing. Any copper would do this and it is not a defect of this item. The fact that it happens shows that you are getting real copper when you buy this! Anyway, I've bought a lot of copper wire lately but for some reason, I didn't have any 16 gauge in my collection (skipped from 14 to 18) so I purchased this. I am working from a lot of pattern and project books lately and I find it helpful to actually use what is suggested in the book, and sometimes 16 gauge is called for. This is soft and malleable, as it should be, but it hardens up as it is worked (and you can anneal it if you need to). It's only about 8 feet but that is sufficient to make several bracelets and pendants and similar items. I am not very good with wire yet but am finding this easy enough to work with. All my standard tools have been great (I try to use nylon jawed pliers when I can or else wrap a bit of masking tape around certain tools so as not to mar the finish). This shines up nicely. It is a bit thin for a bangle on its own (that's just my preference, anyway) but is good for wire wrapping and similar applications. Anyway, overall I'm pretty happy with this and would buy it again.

reviews.text: Did I really pay well over 20 GBP for this mat?.. It’s nothing special. Ultimately this left us with just a large black felt mat as a puzzle base. One that has attracted a lot of dust and hairs after the children spread it out on the floor at the start of their puzzling frenzy - that by the way soon abated. The inflatable roll is an interesting idea, but it started to deflate after a few days of having put the puzzle aside, endangering our meticulous puzzle effort. And of course it is sensitive to punctures. Moreover, we found that you can only start to roll up your puzzle when its about 3/4 completed. It just doesn't work and parts will move around or disintegrated. Also we generally sort and cluster loose pieces in certain areas, but you’ll find that disconnected loose pieces don’t roll up well. So we had to remove these first before rolling. It comes with 2 velcro bands as well to secure the roll. But really the combined set doesn’t warrant #22 we paid for it. The cost price of the few elements in the set is a fraction of what it is sold for and it really isn’t a very practical product. Granted, it comes in a full colour cardboard box. But the packing looked quite sloppy and creased in our case when it emerged from the envelope (!?) the seller thought convenient to use for shipping. Needless to say it wasn’t looking well enough to serve as a presentable gift to my daughter birthday. Maybe i’m just cranky because my daughter insisted on an almost pitch black 1500 piece puzzle that we now have to finish and it just lays there while we can’t really roll it up.. Should have sent it back but then i would have to remove the parts of the partly completed puzzle.

Amazon.com If you've seen "The Exorcist" lately, the folks at Parker Brothers would like to extend a heartfelt "Captain Howdy-Ya-Do?" courtesy of their newly luminescent classic Ouija Board equipment. It's the same traditional setup as it was decades ago: the alphabet-and-numbers board with "Yes," "No," and "Good Bye" spelled out in turn-of-the-century mysterious script; the heart-shaped "Message Indicator Oracle" with the readout window; the numerous coy references to Ouija being "only a game--isn't it?" reviews.title: Is it Evil or Good or just a game or something else????
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 12, 2005
reviews.text: I have done some research on Ouija boards trying answer the question is it just a game or is it something more? The more could be something good or evil. Some believe it's a conduit to HELL that lets demons in who want to eat your juicy soul and tell you lots of lies (since their dad is the father of you know what). Some believe it will contact a benevolent being aka goodie-two-shoe spirit high on life who wants nothing better to help and tell you swell things. Sometimes I think its all BS and sometimes it think it us connecting into the collective unconscious. Or something else all together? Do-do-do-do. Ouija goes way back (like 1000's of years) and its more commonly referred to as "talking boards" since their supposedly "talk" to the spirit world. They come in all shapes and sizes. One modern example is at a party I have used a beer bottle cap and notebook piece of paper with the alphabet scribbled on it. It "worked" just as good as the glow-in-dark game. Another tidbit is the word Ouija was a fusion of the French word "oui" for yes, and the German "ja" for yes.*. Cool huh? (...) After a few hours or drinking in graveyard we got bored. Just in case you were wondering we did respect the property and flowers of the graves we are not hoodlums here. Now on the other hand I can care less about the dead because well umm they are dead. This was a scientific event that resulted in only one notable event over several hours and users (people). I asked our lovely glow in the dark Ouija board what was yesterday's 3 Indiana pick 3 lottery number were. I ask that because this is something my trusted friend and I had no clue on since we don't gamble and it's something verifiable. It more or less answered "747" and the next day I looked up the real answer and it was 774. So while still wrong it, it was interesting. In conclusions I think it's a game. If Ouija really does tap into something its not an unknowable magical ghosts or sprits flying about. I think it's our unconscious mind and perhaps just perhaps it's everyone's unconscious mind connected together in some yet unknown way. If that is the case then its needs to explored and researched don't let fear of the unknown get in the way. It is not the dark ages any more. There are no more witch burnings. Religious dogma often has kept people in the fear of devils and persecutions. Did you know just in 1992, 359 years after the Galileo trial and 340 years after his death the catholic issued an apology, lifting the edict of Inquisition against Galileo? Perhaps the next big scientific break through could be a result of playing with the Ouija board?

reviews.title: More Like a Board Game than a Ouija Board-- Very Cheap!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on March 2, 2013
reviews.text: My friend loves Ouija boards, and I decided to get her very first one for her birthday. Quality: I read the other reviews and I was expecting it to be low-quality. However, expectations and actually seeing it are two different things. Once I took the board out of the shipping box, I was surprised. It looks exactly like any other board game; two cardboard pieces that form a box to hold the board and accessories. I was even more astonished that the Ouija board was also like other board games' boards; it was made of cardboard and had that glossy, laminated feel on the face. The planchette was hard plastic and felt the cheapest of them all. Since it was hard plastic, it was difficult to easily slide around the board. Aesthetics: I don't know how other people got the glow of the board to last as long as 30 minutes because ours lasted 5 minutes at the most. We put the board under a lamp's light for an hour, then turned off the light and it glowed very brightly, but only for a few minutes. The hour of lamp-light made the planchette glow longer than the board, but it only glowed for 10 minutes. "Does it work?": Other reviewers shouldn't have given it a bad review just because it "didn't work for them". The board itself isn't guaranteed to work, it's just a tool to help you communicate. We tried it once at my house at about 8 pm, but there was no activity on the board. This didn't surprise me because I didn't find my house to be haunted. However, since we used the Ouija board at my house, I have been hearing footsteps in the hallway outside my bedroom and in my bedroom, as well as on the main level of the house. I hear activity in the kitchen and my parents' voices when I'm home alone. Nothing bad has happened, it's just a little freaky. I do avoid my basement because I have a very negative feeling when I'm down there and like something is watching me. We've used a makeshift Ouija board (just notebook paper with writing on it) at my friend's house, and we had activity all night. Everyone in that household knows there's a person there whom they nicknamed Shadowman because they could only see a shadow of a man. However, after using the makeshift Ouija board, we found out that his real name is Allen. When we used the Ouija board that I bought, we didn't get any activity at all, and it was 10 pm. Now, I'm not going to say the Ouija board doesn't work because there are entities at my house now. I say if you're looking for a Ouija board and want to spend $19.99 or less on one, then buy this. It's definitely not like a classic Ouija board (except for the writing on the face) but it's better than using notebook paper.

reviews.title: Great Quality but Cleaning Something This Big is a Hassle
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on February 18, 2021
reviews.text: I got the giga size, big enough to cover all but a sliver of my desk. Construction, feel, and durability are all top notch. I let my cat hang out on it and she hasn't caused any damage to it with her claws. My only problems are with the practicalities of the thing. When you have big desk with three monitors, monitor stands, speakers, keyboard, mouse, usb hub, some audio equipment, and other assorted peripherals and doodads on your desk, getting this thing on or off is a real pain. Do you want to unplug every single thing on your desk and put it somewhere else or do you want to try to pick things up one by one and roll the mat out bit by bit under them(accidentally unplugging them anyway and having the cables fall under your desk along the way)? And then to clean this thing you either need a bathtub or driveway and a hose. My first time cleaning it there was a foot of snow outside so I had to use the bathtub, oh and I hope you have a pretty sturdy shower curtain rod to hold this thing up, its heavy enough when its dry and even more so when its waterlogged after cleaning. Letting it drip dry inside takes forever, it wouldn't be so bad if you could set it outside in the summer in the sun and the heat and the wind but indoors its going to take a long while. Just because this thing is such a hassle to clean I do it way less often than I should, I managed to push off cleaning this thing for over 7 months which was much longer than most people would care to as it was very dirty at this point. Then again, I work, study, game, play with my cat, and eat at my desk so yeah, if you keep a sterile workspace it won't get as dirty as quickly. If you want a nice clean looking mat all the time this thing is going to be a lot of work. If you have a minimalist aesthetic going on with your desk and not a lot of stuff on it then maybe it won't be so bad If you have a lot of stuff on your desk, its going to be work every time you want to clean it. If you are a clean freak you are going to be washing this massive thing all the time. If you get off on expending a lot of effort and time cleaning things you won't have a problem. If you are lazy and hate cleaning this thing is going to be a headache. Personally, I love and hate this thing, having a pad the size of my desk is both a blessing and a curse. Having it is freaking sweet, taking care of it not so much. I underestimated the responsibilities of owning a giga desk-sized mouse pad, I'm sure plenty of people won't have the same kind of problems owning such a thing as me, but, well, I am a lazy bum and realize now that I should have gotten something smaller and easier to maintain.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 10, 2014
reviews.text: Ok, so I don't do reviews very often, but hope this will be helpful to some. I am in my mid 50s, so please take that into account. Meaning that I wouldn't normally wear this type of earring at all. I got my ears pierced, higher up the ear, near the cartilage, and I was having a hard time getting them to heal. Sleeping is a nightmare because of where the piercings are, and they were becoming infected from regular earrings, with the push-on back. So, I decided to give these a try. Just let me say, if you don't have small fingers and thumbs, these are really difficult to get on! The ball is very small, and very slippery. I think I just got lucky and finally heard the ball snap in, after several attempts, and dropping the ball, no pun intended. On the second ear, I tried so many times, and just kept bending the earring without being able to get the ball attached. I finally gave up in frustration and waited for a second type of earring, which I ordered at the same time, to arrive. It was difficult to put in too, so I have two different earrings in, one in each ear ;-) So, if you get easily frustrated, and have no experience with the catch type of earring, you might want to pass on these! The depressions in the ball, which have to click in to the space between the wires, is very shallow, and you have to hold the ball just right to line it up, and then you have to apply pressure to try to make it seat. Not an easy feat, and probably took me an hour just to get one earring in! I wish you luck!!

reviews.title: Bright spot in center may not always be what you want.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 11, 2019
reviews.text: I've installed similar LED conversion units in PR-bulb flashlights before, and so far all of them have one common misfeature; the emitter has a focusing lens on it that concentrates most of the output of the chip into a narrow beam. Basically, any flashlight in which you mount one of these becomes a spot beam. While there is also a large illuminated circle around it, the light level there is far lower. Even if the flashlight nominally has a focus feature, you probably aren't going to get evenly distributed light from this. That said, if what you mostly want is that bright spot,. this will reliably provide it. I installed mine in a Ryobi 18V lithium flashlight that was provided with a cordless tool set. The original bulb in the light was a pitifully weak old-style incandescent, and by modern standards, it was a bad joke. With the LED upgrade, the flashlight is a lot more useful. Since the Ryobi did not have a focus feature to begin with, the spotlight result is maybe not always what's needed, but I think it's fair to say that this LED unit puts out more light in every part of the illuminated field than the old-style bulb did, albeit less evenly.

reviews.title: IMPORTANT!!! Quick Flash, Then Off? Flicker? NiCd Battery Flashlights Beware!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 13, 2021
reviews.text: Some buyers out there are claiming there is something wrong with the bulb because when you turn the flashlight on it flashes and then goes out. This is NOT a problem with the bulb! Some flashlights that originally came with incandescent bulbs have circuitry to shut off power when the battery gets low to keep from killing the battery (NiCd batteries). Two examples I know of: Milwaukee 49-24-0155 and 49-24-0165. When you turn it on, it energizes the bulb, but if the current is low it shuts it back off. If you have a bulb that draws very little current (like these LEDs), the circuitry thinks the battery is low and shuts it back off. Hence the flash. I bypassed the low-battery circuit (I'm an ET) and now it works great with this LED bulb. UPDATE: It was a pain to have to route around the low-current-shutoff circuit in my flashlight, but it was worth it. Came in very handy around the campsite.

reviews.title: Solid, good quality set from the top of the line brand
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 24, 2014
reviews.text: I used these bits to make maple trim pieces for my stairs using OF1010 router. Very nice bits, cut maple without effort and leave behind very smooth finish, both when cutting along the grain and across the grain. The box feels like economy grade plastic, but it is perfectly adequate for storage. I really liked storage in a foam insert because getting bits out of tightly fitting holes in wooden containers (e.g., a set which I got from a Chinese brand Woodland USA) or plastic (Freud - nice bits, nice looking individual bit boxes, but hard to get sharp bits out) can be a challenge. The bits arrived coated with protective layer of thin gel/plastic type compound which was easy to remove (no sticky oily substance as on cheaper brands). Beading set of smaller bearings is a plus, even though I did not need them. The advantage of having 5 different sizes in a set was that I could make samples using each of the bits, and then my wife and I decided what would work best. Compared to pricing of individually sold roundover bits available at woodworking stores, there is no much of discount for buying a set, but no premium for top of the line bits either. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Decent amp, quality control is questionable
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 30, 2022
reviews.text: It seems to do its power and can get your subs moving. I was pushing a 12" Skar SDR with it initially and it wasn't bad. Started having an issue with voltage on the output side and they shipped me a replacement with no hassles at all. I was impressed with the ease. I was up and running again and decided to upgrade from the SDR to a Skar 12" SVR. A bit off topic, but skip the SDR and get the SVR if you are going the budget route and wanting a Skar driver. Better preformance by any metric, more musical, hits lower, and seems to have better sensitivity. Months later, I was rolling around listening to my system and played a particularly heavy track and it cut out. I tried what I could with no luck. The amp seemed to power up and showed a normal power light rather than protect. The bass know wouldn't light up. I contacted them to ask if this was something to seek repairs for or if it would be possible to buy a new bass knob and that it would solve my issue. No response. I contacted several more times and never got a reply. I finally ordered a down4sound JP8 and put the Rockville in the closet. I was happy enough with it, you're always going to get used to how much power you have and want more. 625w will pound but you will get used to it and want more. I would recommend a 4ga ofc wire or better because of that. It will leave you room to upgrade a bit later without having to rewire because you went with 4ga cca. Williston Audio Labs on youtube runs a lot of amp dyno tests and is worth spending some time watching if you are new to car audio. In the end, this amp seems to do what Rockville claims.

reviews.text: I have got to say Marvel Legends is enjoying having the FOX Disney merger as they finally get to adapt the X-Men movie characters into action figures years after Toy Biz originally made them. In this case, Mystique from the original X-Men trilogy. This figure/character was made popular by the first movies in the late 1990s early 2000s with Rebecca Romijn playing the role with the later versions played by Jennifer Lawrence. Clearly, this figure is the Rebecca Romijn from the facial structure as well as the body shape. This is the form she uses the most when she does not shapeshift. But I remember the original Toy Biz version was set in a way that had her shapeshift into Wolverine. This should have been a much bigger set that had her transform into several people, but I guess Marvel Legends did not want to do that. The figure stands at 6.0 inches and with the same articulation as female Marvel Legends action figures. This figure includes an alternate set of hands as well as an alternate arm that is flesh-colored from the shoulder down. Not a bad figure but I wanted more. reviews.title: Pretty, Easy to Use, Lasting - we love them!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 20, 2022
reviews.text: I didn't have a ton of expectations going in to buying these lights. However, I had a couple things that I wanted the lights to accomplish: 1) I wanted lights to lighten our stairway at night without having the main lights on. 2) I needed something that didn't have to plug in because there wasn't a handy plug near the stairs. 3) I wanted to be able to adjust brightness so we could have it dim during sleep hours if we needed to get up for the bathroom or something, but brighter during the evening when we were still awake for aesthetics. The bonus really was the remote control and the other settings. The lights were SUPER easy to install and even come with little things to hold the lights in place if you have (I imagine) stucco walls where the adhesive may have a harder time gripping to (I guess this because stucco never lets me stick anything to those walls - could be wrong and this adhesives great to those walls). Regardless, in case the adhesive isn't enough for your walls, you have added flexible grip things to keep the lights in place. We haven't added them yet and the lights are staying up great all on adhesive alone. The installation of the lights was crazy easy. I just gradually pulled off the adhesive protection as I rolled the lights on the wall. Maybe took me 2 minutes in total. Depending on how often you use the lights, you may go through batteries decently quick. We leave our lights on for probably 8-12 hours every day. We also use rechargeable batteries with these lights as we are regular users of them. In the just over a month that we've had them, with regular use, we've switched out the batteries once. Not too much more to say, these work great for lighting and they look really nice. They would work great as under lighting for cabinets, but these aren't like fairy lights for decoration. They are nice, but I wouldn't say they are for centerpiece decoration or festivities, more background.

reviews.title: Very lightweight and the adjustability is great. Every rod I have found its own natural ...
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on December 7, 2015
reviews.text: Just bought and installed the two-section, 8-rod system. Very lightweight and the adjustability is great. Every rod I have found its own natural resting position so I was able to start at one end, lock one holder down, let the rod find its natural position, space the next holder accordingly, etc. Assembly tips: 1. The instructions say to install the set screws from the back side, i.e. the flat surface that will be inside the rail. The first set screw I tried screwing into one of the base loops did a few turns by hand then became difficult. I simply grabbed a pair of pliers, held onto as little of the set screw as I could in order to not damage any threads that would be making contact with the female threads, and spun the loop on lickety split. Every following loop and hook I'd try by hand first then go to the pliers as soon as there was any resistance. Only one set screw went in totally by hand. 2. Do not forgot to put the base loops and hooks into the rail before you mount the rail. I did for the first rail and had to take the middle connector off the wall in order to slide the loops on...duh! 3. Do not pre-drill measured holes like the directions state. The rail fits rather loosely over the end caps and you want a snug end to end fit. Mount one end cap but don't tighten it all the way down, insert the rail, then insert the other end cap and push it against the rail toward the other end so you've got a snug horizontal fit. Screw down the second end cap tight then tighten down the first end cap. Or if you got the 2-section, 8-rod system like I did it's first end cap loose install, middle connector loose install, second end cap tight install, tighten down middle connector, tighten down first end cap. 4. No, it doesn't come with mounting screws. As the directions state, use #8 x 1 inch screws corresponding to the mounting surface (drywall, wood, etc.)

reviews.title: Purchased Two Different Times
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on March 24, 2020
reviews.text: I first purchased these in early 2018. I found them to be wonderful and so incredibly absorbent. I swore I would never waste money on traditional kitchen towels again, as all they did was leave lint and push water around. The second time I purchased them was over a year later and something changed. I found the new set to not be nearly as absorbent as the prior set. I don't understand what could have changed. Their absorbency has not become better over repeated washings. I still have my originally set and there is a marked difference between them. The original set absorbs water off of plates and glasses wonderfully and yet still the second set doesn't. I have found little consistency with many products I purchase over the past few years. It doesn't matter if what I buy is a name brand or some unheard of fly-by-night Amazon mystery company. I don't remember it being like this years ago, but I find myself in the predicament of wasting too much money trying to rely on what I feel should be consistent and tried and true. I think, like many if not most of the sellers on Amazon, the products they sell are not really made by them. They all sell pretty much the same products made by the same factories somewhere. They simply contract with these same factories as all the rest. Then they package them in their own packaging with their logo and brand of the moment and market them as if they made the products themselves in their own factories. Which by now I would imagine most people on Amazon have figured out. In this case, you check the "Recent Reviews" and not the "Top Reviews" and you will see the real dirt that is either current problems that are being sold off. For instance, if you purchased these towels a year ago, and then noticed that you most recent purchase of these towels are thinner, not so well sewn, or dirty, or have wholes randomly. . . It may very well be because the brand selling them has recently changed factories and some other company is manufacturing them now. And quite often you will see the same exact problems, posted at about the same exact time by other reviewers who purchased another brand. So issues of quality control are moot, because these sellers are all purchasing their products from the same handful of factories somewhere in Asia. So you can spend days trying to compare one towel, one headphone, one this or that from another only to find that those same exact models are being sold by a ton of other sellers. The only difference is the brand sticker that is slapped on it by the factory the seller has contracted with. In many ways, it is an illusion that there are tons of models of a product, when in fact there may be just 200 sellers marketing the same exact 5 models of something. And can any of us afford to spend money to compare one so-called brand of flour sack from the tons of other sellers who've jumped on the bandwagon in the last few years?' The sad reality is that we would be kidding ourselves in believing that Amazon is this wonderful place to find anything. It may have been once a two decades ago, but sadly not so much no more.

reviews.title: Amazing little light... a personal 'always carry' must have
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 14, 2021
reviews.text: This flashlight is but mind blowing awesome... Everything is to like about this flashlight..... hang it from a belt loop .......and with the twist of a thumb and index finger you have light shinning on the ground before your feet at the intensity level you last used... ------ 3 intensities of light available..... just perfect..... ---- a very sure connection when twisted on... ( vs ...finicky threaded head / tail cap switch electrical connection others use ).... you get no light flickering whatsoever.. ..if you look into the head of the light you will see a gold connecting ring completely insulated from the head that mates to the polished surface on the barrel of the flashlight....this provides the ( - ) negative polarity to the head --- It won't draw power when off.. because .... when you twist the head to power off...you get a complete mechanical breaking of the circuit by the physical separation of these two surfaces.....you are in fact completely disconnecting the battery from the head which contains all the voltage regulating and memory circuitry ---- the last setting of the light will still be stored in memory when you turn off / replace battery ...etc .. because the memory used is non volatile ram / meaning.......doesn't require power to maintain settings ####### For anyone who may encounter a problem with the light no longer working... as some have remarked... I tracked the problem down with a volt meter... because after 6 months use.. it also happened to me... light is not busted... just needs cleaning pull out the spring with long tweezers or bent wire hook... get a piece of cloth ( wet with rubbing alcohol ) ..sized so you can twist and turn it down into the very bottom of the flashlight body to clean it... clean the spring also... then wipe the threaded part of the bodies shinny ring... that shinny ring contacts the gold contact ring in the head of the flashlight... twist and turn the cloth also into the head of the flashlight to clean the contact surfaces... after cleaning with alcohol... lightly coat all cleaned surfaces ... spring etc....with WD40 oil... ( keep clear of lens ) ... push spring back ...so tip points up...back into flashlight body... reassemble etc... the flashlight will now work and not require cleaning again.... the problem is caused by oxidation of the aluminum which forms a non conducting coating .... this flashlight has a voltage regulating circuit... and the coating causes low or no voltage....so it reacts by not shutting on to prevent damage / full discharge to rechargeable batteries... a regular flashlight would flicker... turn on intermittently ....if smacked against ones palm etc... I am going to try this... remove a thin strand of copper wire / or silver... from some multi strand wire.... wrap some turns about the bottom coil of the spring where when reinserted it should make a secure electrical connection to the barrel of the flashlight ... then run the rest of the wire up through the middle of the spring... and wrap some turns about the topmost spring coil where the battery will make contact with it... this way the wire will carry the current directly from the negative base of the battery to the barrel of the flashlight body ... should work.... / last solution... worked... pulled out the spring and put a slight bend outward at the end of the coil so that it digs securely into the barrel for a sound connection and at the same time increases the force of the rest of the coil against the barrel ... months now all good... I believe it's a permanent fix

reviews.title: Superb Keyring Torch - with a couple of slightly quirky features!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on June 23, 2019
reviews.text: Bought as a “keyring carry” torch, to replace a much used and abused, (and woefully dim in comparison!), Maglite Solitaire. The Lumintop EDC01 is an extremely well made flashlight. It is nicely engineered, IPX-8 waterproof to 2m, and has a real “quality” feel about it. A single AAA battery, (not supplied), is inserted, by unscrewing the o-ring sealed head assembly. At just 66mm x 14.5mm overall, it is incredibly compact, and weighing in at approximately 23grams (with battery), is a real featherweight! – (The battery itself weighs 12 of those grams!). It has 3 available light outputs: - Low @ 5 lumens, medium @ 32 lumens, and high @120 lumens., with claimed runt-times of 36-hours, 4-hours, and 30-minutes respectively. I have no means of accurately measuring the claimed light levels, but from experience with several other flashlights, have no reason to believe they are exaggerated or unrealistic. – At its brightest setting, it is every bit as powerful as the best of similarly sized models. My only (minor) quibbles with the EDC01 are: - 1). The rather strange choice of 5 lumens for lowest setting. (I think that a true “firefly” mode of 0.5 - 1 lumen or thereabouts would have been better for those times when one wants to avoid loss of accustomed night-vision). 2). The equally strange sequence in which the three output levels operate. (The torch doesn’t have a “memory”). It defaults to, and always switches on at medium brightness, from which level it can be adjusted to lowest, and then highest setting, and then back to medium again, to repeat the cycle. The EDC01 comes complete with a “glow-in-the-dark” diffuser, a small but well made “carabiner” type keychain, two spare o-rings, and full instruction leaflet. For the asking price of £9.99 (at time of writing this review), with the caveat of the two minor quibbles mentioned, and for its intended purpose as a keyring torch, there is little to fault about the EDC01. Overall though, I do feel that the similarly sized and similarly bright Thrunite Ti3, which although more expensive has a more logical low-medium-high settings cycle, just has the edge. – (See my separate review of that torch!). Accompanying photo shows the Lumintop EDC01, compared size for size with Thrunite Ti3, and Maglite Solitaire. NB: The battered, much abused (it was originally black!!!) and back-in-the-day “cutting edge technology” of the Solitaire at left of image is finally being retired, making way for today’s cutting edge technology!

reviews.title: Great pocket light
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on July 3, 2019
reviews.text: I’m a big fan of AAA battery lights. I have quite a few from top brands and this is up there with the best of them. The small, compact size means it literally disappears in your pocket. And wherever you are, an AAA battery is never far away. As for brightness, it’s perfectly adequate for most applications. Maybe not long range illumination tasks as it’s a wide spread, diffused beam more suited to closer applications. It always starts in mid mode and then cycles to low then high. I probably would chose low, medium, high mode order but it doesn’t bother me. High mode can light a small room adequately. Very impressive. This really beats lights much larger, such as the old Maglights. It comes with a small keyring attachment and a glow in the dark rubber end cap that turns it into a small lamp, great for camping. I probably won’t use this feature but cool nevertheless. I like the ridged machining on the body, can’t be a cheap thing to produce and looks great. Buy this light, carry it everywhere and always be ready to take on the dark!

reviews.title: Not as practical as I was expecting - very disappointed
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on September 18, 2022
reviews.text: It is a good small size which is what I was looking for, something that could sit in the pocket and not really be noticed. What let's it down is the on/off mechanism. It is turned on/off by twisting the bulb end and when it is off, it is not sealed, so not waterproof as claimed in the description. Turn it on/off quickly changes the light intensity so when using it a lot, you have to turn if off several times to use the maximum brightness (which is quite good). And, when it is off, bump the end of the light turns it on briefly so bouncing around in my pocket is going to be using up the battery. If this had been designed with a nice basic on/off switch, or button, with a single intensity setting, it would have been absolutely perfect because it is a lovely small size. But the switch as it is makes this impractical and unusable.

reviews.title: Very bright for its size, useful diffuser. Pocket-rocket torch for EDC and no reason not to buy it.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom 🇬🇧 on January 20, 2021
reviews.text: If you want a pretty bright torch on your keys, buy this. No questions asked. Comes with replacement O rings, keyring clip, and diffuser. Has three brightness settings that are changed by giving a quick 'on off' twist. The glow in the dark diffuser is also brilliant. Unroll its little turn over and slide it over the top of the torch. It does light up a small room when on, I tested it in the bathroom and it was as good as any camping lantern I've used. The brightest setting is great and puts a fair bit of heat out at the LED. Not along the body but like any LED lighting device, when its ramped up it can get hot at the light source. It'll be fine if you just dont touch it and use the torch in the proper manner. I bought this as an EDC on my keys, it's perfect in size, very bright, has controls and features that make it kinda invaluable. I'm going to buy another for my car. The one thing that is a niggle, is that the power is a screw top, so you unscrew slightly to turn off. This makes me question how waterproof it actually is once you slacken the seal to turn the torch off.

reviews.text: I had two Rev-A-Shelf tip-out trays installed in my dual sink bathroom around 2002, style 6571-63. These trays are now discontinued due to product design flaws. First, instead of the screws passing through the body of the tray, as they currently do, they went through two thin and easily breakable plastic loops that protruded from the sides of each tray. Second, instead of the current completely smooth, one piece design, each tray was made of three pieces: one large piece that comprises the front, bottom and back of each tray, and two glued on side pieces. The gap between the larger piece and the smaller sides collected dust, so the entire tray needed to be removed, soaked in warm soapy water, and scrubbed to get clean. Finally, the tray had non-functional wide horizontal grooves that also made cleaning difficult. Model 6581 is a vast improvement! Please note that if you substitute model 6581 for the older 6571-63, you will need to drill new holes, as the old holes in your sink front will not align with the holes in the new tray. If you tighten the screws until they lightly rest on the tray, you can easily remove the tray for cleaning. Not that I think this will be necessary, since the smooth design makes cleaning a breeze!

reviews.title: Great for the low price, for a Eastwood mig 250 amp.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on September 22, 2019
reviews.text: I can push it to 200 amps for 5-8 minutes before it overheats my aluminum .035 wire. I have to use .045 tips or the wire expands too much when it gets hot and starts rubbing too hard on the tip giving me inconsistent feed speeds. If you have 800-1500 to spend, you can buy a lot better than this. But for this price point, its great and I weld professionally and do a lot of aluminum. It won't run .026 wire as the feed wheels won't grip it. But .030 to .035 works great. I've bought 3 of them and worn one of them slap out. A common problem is the wire finds sharp edges to drag on and then won't feed at a consistent speed which is necessary for bead control. On all 3 of my spool guns I've had to go into them and file off the sharp edges on the barrel and feed mechanisms. Its a really cheap spool gun, but so is it price.

reviews.text: Great deal!!!! I have been welding non stop, almost one whole roll of wire on the same 2 tips. Took some time to learn first and now I am wright at it ! I am using it on 1/8 rectangle tubing over head and joints getting better all the time doing spay weld works good for me and I have tested them and they hold the weight. Using 4043 0.30 and 0.30 tip and wire from my local weld supply store. max volts 10 ++ and 8 wire speed 12 liters 100% argon. 20 amp breaker on heavy gage 25 ft. power cord,! also did 0.35 flat welds on 1/8 inch C channel first to learn. About 50 1 inch welds. 51/2 volt and 6 wire speed 7liters 100% argon with roll sent with spool gun. no matter what I had some black residue .I use a push weld, that's why, but it is cleaner on the drag method. but I am an old dog and find it hard to change lol.
