Despite the little cross bumps all over the mats, it's still smooth enough for us to move equipment when necessary. Our cats love these mats potentially too much. Even our grumpiest, eldest cat curls up in random spots on the mats to lay down and nap for hours on end. They keep clawing it up and, despite having basically chicken talons, they haven't been able to horribly tear them up to the point of pieces being shredded all over or being torn through to create holes. Easy to clean. We used our microfiber mop head and rung it out really well. Kicked on our central unit fan and it dried in no time. Our previously mentioned old cat has health issues and pissed on one section of the mats. The mats did not absorb the urine, nor did the urine get between the puzzle connection parts. The color of the mats have not changed. Cons: The smooth edging connections sometimes doesn't overlap properly with the edge piecing next to it and you might have to cut a slither on the edges for them to fit right. It's hard to explain without showing video of what we did, but it's an easy fix with a box cutter. Cats might enjoy clawing them up a bit too much and the sound does get a bit loud. So far, we're losing this battle, but we're getting there! If you have a cat that is basically a small dinosaur, be prepared for them to lay on the mat with you and bully you the entire time. They will let you know this is their gym floor, this is their mat, and you better do your best on it. They don't seem to come in more rectangular sizes to better fit rooms that are not actual squares. More diverse sizing would be helpful, but it's not the worst. The smell of the mats will fill the room. I've light mopped with a VERY well rung out microfiber mop and Pinesol. (This was due to cat accident and decided to disinfect the rest while I was at it.) The smell is still there, but not nearly as potent as before. It's not a bad smell, but it can be overwhelming. It's spring time for us, so we crack the windows for no less than an hour and it helps greatly. If the rubber gym smell gets to be overwhelming and you can't crack the windows, turning on a fan and putting a candle or other scent related things does reduce that rubber smell. Be mindful of the cleaner you use as harsh chemicals may cause damage, but Pinesol does not seem to be a problem after one use and one round of dish soap with the same microfiber mophead.

reviews.title: Very comfortable for your joints, but not quite perfect
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on August 16, 2020
reviews.text: I use this to do Tracy Anderson workouts which are a mix of cardio and weight exercises where you may be lying down or on your knees. The good: - does not move around on wood floor while doing weight exercises that do not have much movement - VERY comfortable cushioning for knees and wrists, lying down. Absolutely no knee pain. I do not need a separate mat to cushion my joints. I have tossed hand weights (note: less than 10 lbs) and worked out with a kind of heavy folding chair on these tiles and there was no damage to the tiles or even denting. - Easy to clean - good durability (I also roll my office chair onto some pieces as a floor protector and it holds up!) - no smell, does not absorb smell of sweat - hair does not stick to the floor (easy to clean up/vacuum) - good grip even when your hands are sweaty - floor absorbs sweat well The bad: - The tiles do slightly slide on hardwood floor when doing exercises that have more force and movement, like if you do a lunge and then quickly switch positions laterally - I did not need to glue any of the tiles together initially, but after about 6 weeks, I had to glue a single which had begun to expand away from other pieces due to frequently pushing down on that tile away from others (like doing a downward dog type of position, where you have opposing forces). The tile's pieces no longer quite matched up due to having stretched away. Eventually I had to glue together some other pieces. In about two months, I glued together 4 pieces in different positions. They were not damaged at all, but they had just started to kind of extend away from other pieces due to pushing down on them. - If your feet catch out the connecting seams of the puzzle pieces during a quick movement, you will push up some of the puzzle seams and this can be distracting - the pieces that come with the tiles to cover the edges do not allow you to necessarily do so seamlessly all the way around the edge. Some pieces need to be cut to fit against edges of another tile. Some other reviewers mention this. This is a cosmetic problem that is easily fixed, but mildly irritating. Do I regret buying this? No. I do not regret buying this because it gave me the chance to try my workout on a much larger surface area for a low investment (rather than be limited to a small regular exercise mat) Will I replace this with a solid piece of exercise flooring (like a large exercise mat)? Yes. This will also be way, way more expensive but I am prepared to do it after having used this for a over 2 months successfully. I just hate when my feet catch the puzzle seams.

Rather than spend a couple of hundred dollars on another monitor, I decided to look for a stand for my laptop. There are a lot of options available. Most did not go very high. The rest were made of plastic. Then I found the Husky Monitor Stand. I thought, for $16 how can I go wrong? When I ordered the Husky Monitor Stand I was surprised to see the cart show that the estimated delivery time was 8 days – with my Prime two day shipping. I considered other products, and tried to in vain to find the stand locally. Ultimately I decided that I really preferred the look of the Husky Stand, so I ordered from Amazon and prepared to wait. The height under the stand varies depending on the height you select, so you have 4.75”, 4” or 3.25” of clearance under the stand. I am incredibly pleased with this purchase. I find I have less neck fatigue – but more importantly, my set up now functions in the way I want it to. I am no longer considering a second monitor. I love how it looks, too. reviews.title: Simple, perfect size, and taller than most risers
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on March 14, 2018
reviews.text: This stand is affordable, basic, and strong. That's all I needed in a stand, and that's what I got. No fancy extra slots for phone holders, no acrylic or glass tops, no cross bars limiting the space underneath. Just a simple riser to get my monitor up higher and clear up desk space. I have a 12.5" Dell (Latitude 7280) laptop and docking station at work, so I arranged my desk so that they stay under the riser with my monitor on top. If my laptop happens to get hot, the holes in the riser are perfect for allowing heat to dissipate upwards. The laptop fits perfectly between the legs with maybe .5cm clearance on each side. I've included photos to show how much space is available underneath at the maximum height, as well as the size comparison to the 23" Dell monitor (P2317H) on top of it. For my use, it's the perfect size, and it's about 4" high, which is taller than most of the others I looked at on Amazon. My only complaint with the construction is that the design of the legs causes them to be a little wobbly when there is no weight on them. They probably have about 2-3mm of play. However, the weight of my monitor keeps them sturdy, so it's not a big deal. I tried shaking my desk with my hands, bumping into it, and pushing away from it while sitting on my chair to see if the stand was wobbly. No wobbles from the stand from any of those motions. If I shake the stand directly, it can be moved, but it doesn't wobble back and forth. This isn't 100% the best design for the legs, but since it was under 20 bucks and the weight of the monitor keeps it plenty sturdy for me, I'm keeping all 5 stars. Lastly, mine arrived with one of the legs missing its rubber foot. I contacted the manufacturer through Amazon, and they shipped out a new one immediately, along with a free HDMI cable. The missing rubber foot only adds about 1mm, so the height difference doesn't cause any wobble or balance problems; I was just worried about it scratching my desk.

reviews.title: One of the must have pedals!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 25, 2022
reviews.text: Added this to my pedalboard and immediately loved it. Tried my best to get the same sound on my Helix Floor but it just wasn't doing it for me. Immediately broke into some "Like A Stone" and got the settings near perfect and it's great. Very easy to figure out and the new ones are much better, no sound dip delay like the older TR-2 pedals. Not sure exactly what Boss did but they're now perfect!!! The wave forms are good too. A lot of newer boutique pedals have all sorts of gobledy gook mixed into them, all I want is a basic sound and this definitely fits the bill at a very affordable price. Even better, like every Boss pedal, it's built like a tank and will last you decades!

reviews.text: For the money I think this is a great pedal. I have little use for the CE-2 setting, but the S and CE-1 settings are very useable. I'd give it 5 stars but for one annoying feature. Like most of my other Boss pedals, it defaults to "On" when you power up your board. Before I play, I have to tap the switch to turn it off, unless of course I want to use the chorus right away. My Boss tremolo pedal and Vox delay are the same way. Not sure why some manufacturers do that, but it's a bit of a pain to have to play "Whack-a-Mole" with my foot before I start playing.

reviews.title: Classic pedal, must-have effect, great price
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on November 13, 2019
reviews.text: Great for subtle tremolo sounds. There are some wild and more pronounced ones in there but it takes a lot of fiddling to find those. I like extreme and weird sounds but also love finding new ways to use classic sounds. Tremolo has always been the one effect I overlook and this is my very first one (minus digital trem I had in an old multi effects unit and the built in tremolo of some of my amps). That said, I really appreciate this pedal and love the sound. I think it has plenty of options. Sure you may have to do a lot of tweaking to find the more extreme sounds but they’re still there and the classic sounds sound wonderful. It definitely does sound like vintage trem. It reminds me a lot of the vibrato setting that was in my old Roland JC-120. This pedal is less expensive than most out there and the effect itself is awesome. This is a steal at under $90. Even under $100 it’s a great deal. I’ve heard of issues with volume dropping when the unit turns on. This hasn’t been an issue for me at all. My level stays exactly the same when the pedal is on or off. The rate and depth knobs get a lot of love but don’t neglect that wave knob. It can make a huge difference no matter where the other knobs are set. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: I love the sound of this pedal
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on February 5, 2020
reviews.text: Reviewing pedals is so subjective, my 5 star could be your 1 star if we're looking for different things. All I can say about this one is if you want a deep, square trem, it knocks it out of the park. I wasn't even really sure I needed or wanted one, I was just looking for something to give my sound some variety and maybe write some new music around so I started thinking tremolo. I wasn't satisfied at first with what I bought, but I returned it and got this one and man, I love it. This one does both a round and a square trem, I can't say much about the round because I don't use it, but the square is fantastic and easy to dial in just the sound I'm looking for. I've gone from not even sure I want to trem to a regular sound used in my live sets all because of this pedal. Plus it's a BOSS so you know it's going to last forever. I love this pedal.

The effect is exactly what I was looking for. love it.

reviews.title: Excellent sounds.

reviews.text: Hands down, the best tremolo box out there.

reviews.title: Great Tremolo from Boss
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 30, 2012
reviews.text: This is a great Tremolo pedal. It is very quiet and when used correctly, there is absolutely no signal drop or volume drop whatsoever. You can blend the Tremolo type from a smooth sinuous pulsing waveform to a sharper edged "on/off" type tremolo. Tremolo varies the volume of the sound. It does not vary the pitch. You have control over the "depth" or "amount" of effect, and you can control how fast the effect pulsates the sound. A very simple, popular effect that I wouldn't want to live without in some form or another. Pretty teal green color. As with all Boss products they are built like a tank and generally last forever if they are not abused or damaged. I have no idea how fast this pedal eats batteries because I use a power supply. There is no on/off clicking when depressed. There is no added hiss, hum or distortion. The battery compartment is easily accessed without having to unplug anything. Simply a great effect and quality product from Boss and tends to hold its resale value well.

reviews.title: Gold standard tremolo
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on October 3, 2021
reviews.text: Such a simple effect, but executed perfectly by BOSS. Transparant effect, it does not color the tone at all, just makes whatever tone you have into a dreamy fluttering effect, or however else you use it. A bit wallet emptyingly expensive but worth it IMHO, after comparing it with cheaper ones.

reviews.title: Lovely, tweakable tremolo
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on April 18, 2016
reviews.text: Lovely, tweakable tremolo from a slight shimmer to square wave on/off throbbing. It's transparent and there's no apparent volume drop when the tremolo is on. I don't know what more you could ask for! It's true that it gets through batteries quickly, and for some reason the indicator LED is always dimmer than my other Boss pedals, but these are small things when it gets exactly the sound I'm after. My favourite setting for the Wave control is at about 11 o'clock - this seems to nail that vintage Tremolux sound :-)

reviews.title: BOSS comes up trumps again.....
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on October 5, 2016
reviews.text: Replacing an older DOD tremolo pedal. Needed a new trem pedal and have plenty of other BOSS pedals so this was the first choice. Your requirements may differ so yes, there are better tremolo pedals out there, with interesting controls and capabilities, but they are a lot more expensive. For the money this is a great pedal, you shouldn't be disappointed.

reviews.title: Good First Impression & Addition To Workout
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 7, 2021
reviews.text: I purchased the REEHUT Ankle Weights Set (2x 5lbs) to replace a 12 year old set of Everlast ankle weights that have started to leak their sand filling. The weights were delivered on time & in good condition. On the box is an email address for customer support if needed (contact@reehut.com). The stitching looked good on the pair I received, but the thread does not appear to be very heavy. Time will tell how they’ll hold up. If the stitching fails, I will be sure to update this review. The hook & loop attachment is generous & strong. These are the largest set of weights in the set & fit my ankles well (see pics). I wear a size US M 9.5. If you have an issue where they are not snug enough or you want more cushion, you could wear a pair wristbands underneath them. I’ve now had the opportunity to wear the ankle weights during 3 separate workouts. One workout I wore them for 2 hours & the other 2 workouts for 1-1/2 hours each. During these workouts I wore them while walking on an inclined treadmill, on my Max Trainer (elliptical/stepper), performing leg/knee raises/lifts/kicks, band & body weight work, strength & weight training w/dumbbells & kettlebells. During all these exercises & movements, the ankle weights were secure & comfortable. Shifting was minimal & I never had to adjust the hook & loop or fit. If you’re going to wear these on a treadmill, I’d recommend starting the treadmill flat (no incline) & much slower than you would normally walk & increase the speed in very small increments. As for wearing the ankle weights while performing sit-ups, if you wedge/brace your feet/ankles behind/under an object/bar & the ankle weights make contact w/them, I would advise against it to avoid unnecessary wear & tear. I would most definitely say not to wear these while riding any bike (indoor, outdoor, spin, recumbent etc), not just for safety on those requiring balance, but for unnecessary damage to the ankle weights as well. Some of the pics I’ve seen of small holes in ankle weights look like this kind of damage to me. The corners & bulging parts of the ankle weights will rub against the bikes crank arms while peddling & wear holes in them quickly. As I use these in the future, I’ll take note of any issues I may experience w/them & update this review. Thank you for taking the time to read my review, I hope you found it helpful.

reviews.text: I purchased these and a pair of Everlast ankle weights at the same time, to compare. I gave the Everlast weights 2/5 stars. I give these 3/5 stars. Everlast, while being more comfortable and easier to keep in place by far, began to leak material, taking it down from 5 stars to 2. I want weights to feel easier to use over time because I am getting stronger, not because they're losing material... I used the Reehut weights on both my wrists and ankles. They don't seem to leak (will update if this changes), but my god are these uncomfortable things. Unlike the Everlast weights, these don't stay in place and kind of hurt to wear on wrists and ankles, due to the tension being constricted at the band point as opposed to spread out over the entire piece of fabric. This may be because I have skinny wrists and ankles, but the pinching and the tension seriously distracted from my running and left bruises on my lower shins. Ouch. They seem sturdy enough, so if you're jogging in the winter, maybe wrap a thick sock around your ankle inside the weight... if you can tolerate it. No way I could wear these against skin or thin socks. I have the bruises to prove it. :( This sounds negative, but since I didn't rule out buying a higher weight value in the future, and they don't seem defective... I give them 3/5 stars.

reviews.text: First off, I didn't buy this mouse for gaming purposes; therefore, I cannot comment on its "game" quality. This was bought with price, number of buttons, and programmability in mind. The mouse is a little big for me, but this is a common problem with almost all portable/wireless mice I purchase. Therefore making this a very small issue. The mouse itself moves very smoothly! However, the different modes are jarring at first, as the first one moves so fast, but the last one is painfully slow. There is a good in-between if you're not using this for gaming and just as a normal (enhanced) mouse. The biggest plus for this mouse would be their customer service!! The mouse I originally bought seemed to tucker out a month in. I contacted support and let them know about my issue. Lucky was extremely respectful, understanding, and responsive. They decided they would send me a new mouse to replace my old one and, lo and behold, it has been working ever since!!!! Lucky was extremely quick with their decisions and responses!!! Summary: Unfortunately, I wouldn't call this the Number 1 gaming mouse. However, it is an excellent replacement a laptop track pad or portable mouse. reviews.title: Not that difficult but ...
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 13, 2021
reviews.text: Ok guys. Couple weeks ago was my girl's 50th and I wanted to make it special even during covid. I ordered a whole bunch of decorations and this was one of them. I read the reviews and wanted to give some clarity on things. First of all, don't be like other reviewers and wait until the day before or day of to check if your order was right. I ordered 1-2 months in advance and because of some other reviews I checked everything when I got it. My order was correct, I had the correct letters for "Happy Birthday." Secondly, don't wait until the day of to start getting things ready. Some of these take a little time to put together but they were not difficult or impossible and that's mainly why I'm here. I read about the "puff balls" and saw others complain about them. About a week before her Bday I put them together while watching a movie. They are awesome, worth it, and look great with the sign! Wash your hands because if you lick your fingers the paper comes apart very easily and I really didn't have to baby them. It's like tissue paper in the top of a gift bag ... you want it a little wrinkled. Also, don't cut off the long ends of the white string. Tie it off really tight to cinch the middle of the "ball," then tie-off the long ends to form a loop which you'll use to hang the dang thing. (I cut off the first 2 until I realized I needed them.) A course twine works great with the lettering because it will hold the letters in place ... fishing line won't. That will also take a few minutes to do. And the spiral swirl things - I had the ones in this pack and a couple other from other companies. They are all the same and will arrive flat in a little disk. You have to take time to pull them apart from themselves AND to add whatever you'll use to hang them. Fishing line worked great for that! I didn't even get to use the balloons as I had way too many decorations. I checked the balloons and if I remember correctly they sent the right number (24?) but not exactly the right number of each one. I was given more confetti balloons so I wasn't mad. Anyway, hope this helps. I was very happy with what they sent me and if you can take the time to do a little prep it will take some pressure off the day.

reviews.text: We had a kitchen mat that we liked, but the backing material eventually degraded and powdered away (made in China). I removed the rest of the degraded backing and coated the back of the mat with left over roof coating material that I had. This has worked very well, but the roof coating backing made the mat a bit "slippy" on the wood floor. I needed something like two-sided tape to non-permanently secure the mat to the floor so that it would not slip if stepped on at an angle. The "non-slip rug gripper" was purchased to solve this problem. So far, it has worked well securing the mat to the wood floor. I tried lifting a corner of the mat to take a picture but the rug gripper stayed stuck to the floor instead of staying with the mat. So it sticks better to wooden floors than it does to coated mat backing. I did follow the directions and put the floor side toward the floor and the rug side toward the rug. I have not tried removing the rug gripper from the floor but I really don't expect I will have a problem if I decide to remove it at a later date. The rug gripper package came with 9 pieces, 2 for each corner and an extra for boo-boos. I used just 1 piece on each corner at a diagonal to the corner (the mat is fairly small) and this seems to work well for the size and stiffness of mat that we have. Very satisfied with the product so far.

reviews.title: Cool beans!

reviews.title: Easy to install, great value, works great!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 22, 2019
reviews.text: We've had this for about two weeks now. After our old toilet seat broke we decided to give a bidet seat a try. There are so many to choose from! Basically, I was looking for something that had a good number of features (strong enough spray, front spray, dryer, etc) and was around the $200 mark. This seat has it all and then some! All I can say is I'm not disappointed at all with my purchase. The seat was easy to install, I think lining it up just right took the longest, but I had it all installed within 30 minutes and had no leaks, that includes a shut-off value I bought separately, just in case. As for operation, it works as I expected it too. I was worried that with the shut-off value the flow would be reduced and the stream would be weak but that wasn't the case. The water flow isn't blasting me off the seat but it's strong enough to get everything clean and that's the point, right? The dryer is warm and does an ok job, sometimes I run that twice and by the end of the second cycle, things are usually good. The controls are clear and easy to reach, I thought about going with a remote control type unit but with small kids, we decided something attached that couldn't get lost or used as a toy was probably a better choice for us. If I had to find a negative I'd say the seating area was a little smaller than we were used to, but that only bothered me for a day or two. Also, I find I have to shift around a little sometimes to get the spray in just the right spot but again, not a big deal and I imagine that's something you might have to do regardless of which seat you buy. The bottom line for me is that it gets everything clean, and it didn't cost a lot to do it! So hopefully between having to pump the septic less and using hardly any toilet paper, it will pay for itself eventually. 7/16/20 FOLLOW-UP So a year later still no complaints. I've found the shut-off valve was not a necessity for us, even with two Pre-K kids there have been no accidental sprayings! In fact, they are starting to use it now too, although I do find it isn't as effective for them as it is for my older child and the adults. One of the LED lights stopped working about 6 months ago but that isn't a big issue. I also found the seat doesn't seem to heat as much in the back, but I'm not sure if that's a failing or just where the heaters are positioned, again not a big issue for us. We will probably get one for the kids' bathroom soon, while I might not get this exact model I will certainly consider the brand.

It works well, it’s easy to refill, has a low medium high option as well as run time length of 2, 4, 6, and 8 hours or you can leave that alone and it’ll run until you turn it off. When plugged in and not in use the red light does flash, that part is annoying but not an issue. My first one came with a broke plastic piece on the inside and had to send that back and get a new one. I was bummed because I was really needing one ASAP however those things happen and it was handled quickly and easily aside from having to return the defective one. That was the most “hassle”. Aside from that, this has been working well for us for a few months now. It is very quiet. The blue led lights on the buttons aren’t too bright but are noticeable. There’s also a light you can turn on that will illuminate the water tank. It changes color.

reviews.title: It is close to perfect
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 8, 2021
reviews.text: The mist doesn't leave a puddle around the humidifier, but there is a bit of dampness. Not too bad. I don't feel it goes far enough into the room, but if I turn it higher, then I do get quiet a bit of moisture. You have to ensure that it's seated properly on the base or it will "leak" as some have complained. It only did it once to me but I discovered it was because I didn't carefully ensure it was put together properly. The controls - push buttons... I often have to press them several times before they register and react. BUT, until I set this up, every year, as soon as it got cold outside, I was like a walking lightning rod, getting zapped with static electricity constantly to the point I even hated touching my husband because I knew I'd get a shock! That has not happened yet this year! It runs for quite a long while, but I don't set it on the higher output because it does cause moisture around the base (because the mist doesn't go up and out into the air like I hoped it would. It's also VERY easy to fill and I think that's the very best feature!

reviews.title: Works well until it breaks.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on December 5, 2022
reviews.text: I loved this humidifier but you have to either bring a big pitcher to refill the tank by hand or unplug the machine to physically take it to refill. That creates a mess and water typically gets all over it. This eventually led to the electrical portion malfunctioning and no longer working because of the exposed portion of electrical wiring at the base of the humidifier. It should have lasted a lot longer for the price.

reviews.title: It's quiet, easy to use, easy to clean!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 8, 2022
reviews.text: The best thing is you can shut off ALL the lights so that your sleep is not disrupted by any light at all. The only thing that I can say is that if you use the timer, apparently it emits a short beep when it shuts off. I haven't heard it but my husband did. So we just decided to leave it on all night. The "night light" feature is awesome - it will change colors which can be relaxing. You may hear a trickle of water from time to time but this is not at all disrupting or annoying. Cleaning is a breeze there are TWO pieces the top and the bottom and both are easy to clean. I have not used the essential oil tray so I cannot speak to that but it looks easy enough. Would definitely buy this one again.

reviews.title: Really impressed with this powerful little humidifier!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on February 14, 2021
reviews.text: I am so impressed with this humidifier! The first unit I received arrived damaged due to rough handling by my post guy but the seller replaced it quickly. I've tried a few high end humidifiers but didn't really care for them. Either they were too complicated or too large. The functions on this relatively small humidifier are simple and straightforward, and it has a nice fine mist. The mist nozzle has two holes in it that can be rotated so you can customize where your mist falls. I keep them pointed in separate directions so I can have plants on both sides of the humidifier. The mist is a nice density so it doesn't create water droplets on the leaves, but can increase humidity for a good sized area. A full tank of water lasts a few days for me, keeping it on 24 hours a day. I like that there are 4 timer settings. The only improvement that I would suggest is a 12 hour timer function. I like to keep my grow lights on for 12 hours and it would be nice if I could sync it up with them. The unit is very lightweight are SO easy to refill and clean, since it has a wide top opening. Overall, I am really impressed with this humidifier, especially for the price!

reviews.title: Amazing purchase, highly recommed!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 29, 2021
reviews.text: I purchased this product about 2 weeks ago now and I have already seen a great improvement. I am using it primarily for my houseplants, its winter in New England and with the heat up in the house its SUPER dry and my plants are highly dissatisfied. I looked for a humidifier that was on the cheaper side that would throw out some real moisture and this did the trick! Before I purchased the humidifier I was witnessing dry browning edges on the leaves of some of my more finicky houseplants and I haven't had a single brown edge since I plugged in the humidifier. I'm a fan of the time limits you can set, I turn it on in the morning and let it run for the longest setting (8 hours) and when I go up to bed I turn it on again. I fill it every other day or so and honestly its been doing such a good job I plan to buy another one for a different area in the house. OH and how could I forge to mention how quiet it is, it makes zero noise. Highly recommend if you are in the market!

reviews.text: I've had this case since November 2019, so there is 1 year and 3 months of experience going into this review! Photos are without the phone in the case, since, well, how else could I have taken them? Pros: - Perfect fit for the Samsung Galaxy S10E! No misplaced port holes, the side buttons work perfectly, and the cutout for the fingerprint reader is just the right size with a nice impression that your finger naturally fits into. - Sturdy! I'm hard on phones and this case has held up 100% to drops from every angle, often onto concrete. The case has never cracked, and the phone has never popped out of it. It fits like a glove and has absorbed all impacts with NO damage to my phone. - THE RING! This is a COMPLETE game changer. It's flat enough that it doesn't really make a difference in the size profile (i.e. doesn't catch on pockets); it rotates 360 degrees, but rather than spinning freely, it 'snaps' into 12 different positions, making it easy to hold your phone at different angles (and fun to fidget with); and the edge is flat, making it much sturdier as a stand than a literal ring would be. Makes pop sockets look like cheap junk! The ring pivot also had a magnetic centerpiece, making this case compatible with any magnetic phone mounts (not pictured - I'll get to that). Cons: - The magnetic piece i mentioned fell off after about 4 uses with the magnetic mount in my car. I guess the mount's magnet was stronger than the glue that held the piece onto the case, so I pulled my phone off the mount and the piece from the case was just still stuck to the mount. This is the only reason why I only rated 4/5 on durability. - As pictured, the black finish has worn off from EVERY corner and edge, from heavy use and constant drops. Personally I don't care, but it is worth mentioning that the finish will wear. Apart from the magnetic piece coming off (which I'm sure I could just superglue back on myself) I could NOT be happier with this case! 8/10!

reviews.title: Locking Instructions for Spraypainting
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on January 6, 2021
reviews.text: These stencils are decent. The plastic is thin, but flexible, and I didn’t have any problems with it cracking, even when trying to lock the tiny tabs together. The seller sent me six 9’s (instead of three 6’s and three 9’s). The number shapes are identical, but the locking tabs aren’t. (I think you can flip them vertically, but you can’t rotate them or flip them horizontally and have them lock correctly. I was able to cut off the tabs on the upside down 9’s and still have them spaced correctly, though.). The seller's locking tab instructions are incomplete. Better instructions below: 1. Make sure your letters are right side up (The more finished, kind of bumpy, matte side seems to go down. The less finished looking, but smoother, side goes up. When they are correct, the tabs on the left side of each letter should be the outward facing/further apart tabs, with the inward facing/closer together tabs on the right). 2. Line up the letters you wish to lock together. 3. Slide the right side stencil of the first pair down (toward yourself) until the shorter, cut end of both letters’ top tabs are aligned. (See pic #1) 4. Push the tabs of BOTH stencils downward (toward the table/medium) until the cuts are separated cleanly (don’t crease them). 5. Nest the tab cutout holes of the two letters together by sliding the stencils together (toward each other). The top corner of the right letter will be on top of the left stencil, but most of its edge will be underneath. (See pic #2) 6. Slide the right stencil up (away from yourself) until both stencils’ top edges are aligned again. (See pic #3) 7. Gently curve (bend, but do not crease) the right stencil, holding its top corner in place, until you can align the shorter cut edge of the bottom tab with the left stencil’s. (See pic #4) 8. Nest the tab cutout holes of the two letters together by sliding the stencils together, again. 8. Release the bend in the right stencil so it flattens, and guide its edges until both stencils’ top and bottom edges are aligned. The bottom corner of the right letter will also now be on top of the left stencil, but most of its central edge will be underneath. (See pic #5) 8. The stencils are now locked. If you look at the back side, you will see the locking tabs have a kind of ‘arm-in-arm’ (think square dance) effect. (See pic #6) Using the locking tabs makes it easier to align and spraypaint the letters, but it also makes them stick up a tiny bit off your medium, so the edges won't be quite as clean.

reviews.text: There are a lot of one-star reviews that complain about rusting in water. It's important to note that these balls are made of 52100 chrome steel which is NOT STAINLESS STEEL! This is a moderate hardness steel deisgned for water-tight, low-impact, non-thermal environments such as the axle hubs of bicycles. 52100 chrome steel will absolutely corrode when exposed to water and oxygen, so these balls are not suitable for use as paint or polish mixers. 304 stainless steel, the same stuff used to make silverware, would be the best for wet environments like paint containers, but you may have to look harder to find ball bearings made out of it. 440C stainless steel is a more common ball bearing material that is more resistant to corrosion than 52100 chrome steel but not as resistant as 304 stainless steel.

reviews.title: A fancy blender to give you cognitive dissonance
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 19, 2018
reviews.text: This past spring, my husband and I got on a much needed health kick. We decided to incorporate daily smoothies into our new kick and the 20 year old blender we have wasn't cutting it. After a lot of research, we went with the NutriBullet Pro. Since May of 2018 I have been making 32 ounce smoothies every morning for the two of us. I've never used ice but I do blend frozen fruit just about every day including hard as rock strawberries. I add water or coconut milk as the liquid, always up to the fill line, you can add more after your initial blend if you need to. Some Pros and Cons: Pros: -Very easy to use -Convenient - makes me want to make smoothies every morning which is great -Small, takes up very little space/storage space -Powerful, will blend just about everything Cons: -Super difficult to clean! You'd think it's just soap and water and that's it! No. These plastic cups stain and hold smells just like any plastic food container. The four ridges that run down the cups to aid in blending, forget it. I use a green scrubby, a bottle brush and a regular sponge to get these areas clean and that's after a nice super hot water and soap soak. Still doesn't get them clean all the way. Seeds, little bits of fruit and veggies get caught up in there. I use a toothpick to really scrape them down if I need too. Toothpicks have quickly become my friends. A yellow tint has formed on both cups - they are stained and you can smell the 'leftovers'. I've tried all the tricks, the dishwasher just bakes it on so it's not worth putting these in the dishwasher. -The Blades: Cleaning the blades is fun. I clean this part right after I blend. If you use chia seeds, they will stick to the plastic. The blade also has a gasket, this gasket will pop out when you try to remove the cups from the blender if there is too much resistance. You'll have to either smush the smoothie covered gasket back into place or clean the entire thing before blending again. I recommend cleaning rather than smushing. Basically - if you blend anything that's too frozen or thick, the gasket tends to come dislodged and you will have to fight the blade cap to get it off the cup. Toothpicks help scrape the junk off the gasket and from the little tracks around it as well. When you do finally get the blades off the cup, you'll hear a little 'phizzzzz' letting you know there was some pressure building up in there. Please google bullet explosions for details on that one. Whatever you do, don't hold it by the plastic cup's top while blending. Always hold it by the base for obvious safety reasons. -Travel Caps: These are an awesome nightmare. Great for travel, my husband tosses his cup with this cap into his backpack, he takes his motorcycle to work. Never a spill, the cap's mouth piece locks perfectly and tight. The rubber gasket in the mouth piece part is easy to clean, pop it out with a fork tine to give it a good wash. The gasket around the base of the lid is a bit tougher to clean. Like the blade gasket, these are just overall really difficult to keep clean in general. The lid gaskets are also tough to get out to clean. Again, toothpicks are great for scraping the junk here. -Timer: No timer so you have to watch the clock to make sure you're not over-blending. No biggie the only downside is the longer you blend, the more pressure you have leading to potential problems. YOU DO NOT WANT TO BLEND MORE THAN 60 SECONDS! Seriously. Be careful. -If you blend heavy stuff or really frozen stuff, the blades tend to stick. Stop the blades, add more liquid and try again. I found this to be the best solution. Sometimes you'll be like, What the Heck? I don't have anything in there that should be causing this issue!? And you really don't! It's just the nature of the beast. Try the add more liquid deal, it's not failed me yet. -Oh last thing - bad UX design of the cups 'Max' line. It's in black and it's so hard to read once you fill the cup up. Unless you have it full of lightly colored food and liquid that is. If you're like me and use a lot of leafy greens and veggies and darker fruits - good luck. I will spin that cup around looking or the 'max' line over and over again. My husband will stand there watching like it's a game until one of us screams - I see it! The prize? A smoothie! Another one in a lighter color elsewhere on the cup would be super helpful. A larger line would be helpful as well. I can see how someone could easily overfill the cups because of this. Please don't let my cons persuade you against buying it though. I do really like our NutriBullet and it's been wonderful to have fresh smoothies every morning, we've noticed the positive difference to our health over all. So far, everything has run smooth enough for me not to hate the thing, it just bugs me a little but so does the dishwasher and the fridge so... The pros far outweigh the cons and my biggest complaints are cleaning ones, not function or quality. If you take care of your NutriBullet and follow the blending guide, it should last you a few years. That's not to say there are defective ones out there! It happens. I would recommend this to friends and family and I have. Of course I do tell them what my cons are, what kind of friend or family would I be if I didn't? In general, none of these machines are perfect, they all have their issues. What it really comes down to is what is right for you. For us, this a great little machine that hasn't failed us yet.

Even with our 65lb dog laying his full weight right up against the side panel, the tarp clips and suction cups didn't budge. The suction cups cost me $3 and the tarp clips were $6; even considering the cost of these the price of the cover is well worth it as you are really able to create an inexpensive custom cover. Our youngest pup doesn't do well on long car rides and ended up getting carsick four separate times over the course of the trip. This cover not only protected my seats but was easily cleaned on the go with bottled water and some napkins from my glove box. When we got home, I tossed this cover in the washing machine on the delicate cycle and it came out perfectly. I hung it up outside to dry and it looks brand new. I could not be more impressed with this cover. This was the first time that the pups had ridden in this vehicle and I was terrified that they were going to scratch the door panels or puncture the back of the leather seats. reviews.text: I have had the apron for three days and use it in my woodworking shop. It replaces one I have had for decades. The weight of tools supported by my neck had become too uncomfortable, so I ordered this one with shoulder straps. It helps, but is not as comfortable as I had hoped. Of course, I do not know if I am wearing it correctly because it came with absolutely no instructions or any other documentation. (It did come in a nice gift box which seems silly and wasteful.) Not knowing any other way, I crossed the straps and threaded them through grommets on the sides and then tie the ends behind my back. Owing to the shortness of the straps, either the apron is right below my chin or there is just barely enough slack in the straps to tie them behind my back. The straps cut right across my shoulder blades, which is not very comfortable. My wife may sew a loop onto the straps to force them to cross a bit lower on my back. I suspect I am not wearing the apron as intended, but, without instructions, I have no way of knowing. The fabric is heavy, which protects me from flying debris, but it is pretty hot, too. There are plenty of generously sized pockets. The jury is still out on this purchase. I am certainly not getting rid of the old shop apron any time soon.

reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 5, 2015
reviews.text: I have a neck injury and can't lift weights or do a lot of things I used to do with my arms because those things pull on my neck and cause great pain. I wanted to find something I could do to keep my arms toned without hurting my neck. I was torn between buying the UB Toner and buying another Easy Curves Kit . I had lost my old one during a renovation of my house but had loved it. For variety though, I went with this. This little unit has no adjustable resistance. The resistance level is not too hard but it requires a little effort. There are a number of ways to hold this wishbone shaped device and to push it closed and open it. I could definitely feel the resistance when I first got it. I did all the exercises which were laid out on in the enclosed booklet and my arms felt a little fatigued and I did feel the work in my chest. However. the next day, my neck ached. I wasn't sure this gadget caused it but after five or six times using it and waking up with a monstrous neck injury related headache, it was obvious. I bought another Easy Curves Kit and that caused me no issues (and works great for me). Still, I do find that this can be effective for toning the arms and chest a bit. Once you "outgrow" the level of resistance though, it is almost useless. It's good for those who are weak, recovering from injury, want to use something while watching TV, or just want to add a little variety to their upper body routine. If you can lift light weights, I believe they are more effective than this gadget as it doesn't get the backs of the arms and other vital areas. It is good for the biceps, chest, and even forearms. I use the UB toner now and then to see if I still get a headache and I do. But that won't happen to you unless you have a neck injury. This clearly pulls on my neck and causes it to flare. It appears to be durable and has not lost its tension of acted funky at all. If I could use it more, I absolutely would. I am going with 4 stars even though, for me, it wasn't the best choice. It's fine for people who are starting out or jumping back into toning. You won't get huge muscles but you will work your arms and chest muscles and it's really quite easy to use.

reviews.title: Sadly not quite what I was looking for.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on July 20, 2020
reviews.text: I bought the Tablet Arm Mount with the sole intent to use it for my Nintendo Switch. On my desk it works great, but I had hopped to use the mount horizontal on my bed's headboard, so I could use the system in bed. As this mount was not intended to be used in this way, this simply didn't work well. Assembly: You might not know this from simply looking at the product page, but this mount is essentially three pieces, that you the buyer are given instructions to assemble. The "Hand" grabber, has a ball joint that you need to unscrew and insert the "ball-stick" into the gap, then screw in the fastener. Then you attach the "Hand" onto the end of the Arm via an easy to attach grip joint with a fastener. The Vice is able to be attached to whatever surface you desire before or after attachment to the Arm, via a simple screw brace. Pros: +Easy to assemble. +Relative ease to set up. +Small when compacted and disassembled, for easy storage. Cons: -Limited application outside of store page example positions. -The Vice to Arm screw brace (labeled as 360°) is clearly the weak point on the Mount, and this is where the device falls short for me. -Misuse, by horizontal setup, can quickly lead to damage of the Vice to Arm brace unit, and reduce it's life. Conclusion: While the mount can still be used in the recommended way, I have sadly made some damage to both the weak screw brace, and the metal arm that you insert into it. I fear that if I continue to misuse the device this way that that joint will fail completely. That said, because the whole thing is easy to split back into three pieces, I am still using the "hand" of the mount to hold the switch after rigging the "Hand" into a PVC pipe with a hole drilled into it with support. So I can still use the one part of the whole in bed, and then as needed pull it out and place it back into the complete mount on my desk.

reviews.title: Does not do Dolby Digital
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada 🇨🇦 on July 7, 2021
reviews.text: I didn't want to spend a couple hundred bucks for a new receiver, so I got this instead. It works very well, but it will soon be obsolete like the technology it converts to because it won't work with Dolby Digital technology. "DD 5.1" is what streaming platforms use nowadays. You will be able to play console games, you will be able to watch DVDs and blu-ray discs, you will be able to watch older movies that weren't made with the DD 5.1 audio technology on streaming platforms, but forget about all the most recent releases on Netflix, Amazon Prime and other streaming platforms. "The Boys", one of Amazon Prime's most popular series, for example, is in DD 5.1 so the audio will not work. More recent movies like "Venom" also use DD 5.1, so forget about it too. For this reason, I think this particular device is not the kind of thing you should buy as a long-term solution. One workaround you can do is to connect your AV/RCA cable on your device ( ex: a PS3 ) while having the HDMI plugged in as well, and connect your colored cables directly in your receiver - you won't get DD 5.1 audio, but you may ( or may not, depending on your device ) get audio. The fact that DD 5.1 is not working with this thing is a big negative to me, but the fact that they don't mention anywhere it does not support Dolby Digital 5.1 is the worst. By saying it works with Dolby 5.1, one will assume it works with DD 5.1 too. It doesn't. This is why I'm lowering my score to 4 stars instead of 5. Other than that, it works perfectly and is very easy to use. It's almost a plug-and-play thing. You just plug the required cables, plug the power, switch the audio channels accordingly and it's good to go.

reviews.title: Fast enough, too "flashy", odd MAC address behavior, and radio silence
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on October 24, 2018
reviews.text: I purchased two of these adapters, with the intent to convert two laptops from 2.4GHz wireless g to 5GHz wireless ac. Fast enough: I have 120Mbps service from my ISP, and once this adapter was up and running, speed tests show that it was able to achieve that speed most of the time. So, for a 120Mbps connection to the Internet, it's fast enough. Too flashy: This adapter has a very bright blue LED on top that flashes slowly when it doesn't have a wireless connection, and flashes very rapidly when it does have a wireless connection. It flashes rapidly even when there is absolutely NO network activity. And the pattern of flashing isn't consistent...it looks like it speeds up and slows down randomly. At first, I had assumed the rapidly LED was a network activity indicator, and that the LED would be steady on with no activity, as is often the case for most network adapters I've used. So, when I saw all this constant/fluctuating flashing, even though I wasn't doing anything to generate any network activity, I thought perhaps there was some surreptitious transmissions going on. Scary. So, I shut down all processes that could possibly be talking on the network, fired up Task Manager, and fired up a network monitor. There was absolutely no network traffic, but this adapter was still flashing with a very fast and random pattern. I concluded that this is just how this adapter behaves, and have convinced myself that it's not tied in any way to actual network traffic. It's just trying to be annoying, but it's nothing that a little well-placed electrical tape can't overcome. (Suggestion to the manufacturer: Slow, steady flashing when it doesn't have a connection is fine. A connection with no activity should be on, with no flashing. Rapid flashing should indicate network activity.) Odd MAC address behavior: When I got these adapters, I initially tested them both on the same laptop, just to make sure they worked. My router uses MAC filtering, so I have to record each adapter's MAC address and enter it into the router. I was surprised to see that both adapters reported the exact same MAC address 00:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF. My initial reaction was that I wouldn't be able to use two of these in the same network, because their MAC addresses would conflict. But after some experimentation, I realized that when either of these adapters is installed on another computer, it reports a different MAC address. I switched adapters on the other computer, and the new adapter had the same MAC address on that computer. So, the MAC address appears to be generated when you install the software for the adapter, and that MAC address is tied to the computer, not to the adapter. This is different from any network adapter I've ever worked with. Nevertheless, it meant that I was able to use both adapters in the same network. UPDATE 6/14/2019: When I upgraded in-place from Windows 8.1 Pro to Windows 10 Pro, with this adapter attached before, during, and after the upgrade, the MAC address of the adapter changed. So, when I initially booted Windows 10 Pro, it couldn't connect to my router because the new MAC address didn't appear in the router's list of allowed MAC addresses. It was easy enough to change in the MAC Filtering section of the router, but this is another example of MAC address oddness with this adapter. Be aware that if you perform an OS upgrade, the MAC address of the adapter might change. The adapter had some trouble reconnecting to a network that doesn't broadcast its SSID, even though it was set to connect even without the SSID broadcast. I had to keep reconnecting to the network manually. Once I changed the router to broadcast the SSID, the adapter consistently reconnected automatically without any intervention. UPDATE 6/14/2019: Even with the SSID broadcast, the adapter has started to occasionally (twice a week, on average) lose the ability to see and connect to any wireless networks. The blue LED flashes slowly, and no available networks appear in the list. I can force the adapter out of this state by disabling and then reenabling the adapter in Control Panel | Network and Sharing Center | Change Adapter Settings. Once this is done, the adapter springs to life, sees its preferred wireless network, and connects automatically. The fact that this behavior started recently makes me think it's starting to fail. But it still seems to work, in spite of this occasional issue. The software installation, on Windows 8.1 Pro and on Windows 7, required the included mini-CD-ROM. The included "manual" contains some conflicting information, but the software installation process worked, but was a bit klunky. There were several periods during installation when nothing appeared on the screen, even though the installation was still proceeding. At one point, while installing on Windows 7, the installation choked and reported the amusing message "Your local administrator is no longer working." Since I'm the local administrator, I almost took that as a cue to go on vacation. But instead, I rebooted, reinstalled, and all was well. There doesn't appear to be any web-based support for downloads, troubleshooting, etc. I contacted the manufacturer, and they supplied links to an updated driver. The device shows up as a RealTek 8811CU 802.11ac NIC. I'm not happy that I had to experiment to discover the MAC address behavior, I had to experiment to discover the true meaning of the constantly flashing LED, the documentation doesn't point to a web site with drivers and support (I contacted them through Amazon, and they then directed me to contact their sales email at inamax.cn), I had to set my SSID to broadcast to get the adapters to reconnect automatically, and the software installation was klunky. If it weren't for these issues, I would have given the product 5 stars. But once I got beyond all that, the adapters do the job. Update: Radio Silence: A few days after posting this review, the adapter frequently and spontaneously entered into a state in which it couldn't see any networks at all. The LED flashed slowly, indicating no connection, and the list of available networks it saw was empty. This has happened at seemingly random times...it's connected and working just fine, and then suddenly drops the connection and can't see or reconnect to any wireless networks. The ipconfig command sees the adapter with the expected MAC address. Windows reports "no networks found" on this adapter. The included software shows that the radio in the adapter is turned on. I made sure that the router was working properly, that all other clients could see the expected wireless networks, and this was the ONLY adapter that has lost connectivity. (I've had this happen multiple times on both of the adapters I purchased.) There is no unusual interference in the area, nothing changed in the wireless network configuration when the problems occurred, and other wireless adapters used in the exact same location (e.g., same distance and direction from the router) see a strong signal and the expected wireless networks. It wasn't losing connectivity at all during the several days of using these adapters. Nothing changed in the router, network configuration, location of the adapter, or anything else. To resolve the issue each time it occurred, I had to physically eject (through Safely Remove Hardware and Eject Media) and reinsert the adapter to get it to see any networks. When I do this, it almost immediately sees all the networks it should, and connects to the correct network. After this action, the connection might stay up for anywhere from 10 minutes to a day before getting back into this "radio silence" state again. Frustrating. The seller worked with me through email to troubleshoot the problem, but was not able to resolve it. They issued a refund, and I will move on to find a different set of adapters.

reviews.title: No nano for this old beast
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 30, 2021
reviews.text: I have a vintage 2008, Dell Latitude E6400 laptop. It's a manly beast. This thing was made back when laptops were built like brick shi ....well, you get the idea. What's so cool about "This Old Dell" is you can get under the hood and "hot rod" it a bit ...fer cheap. Max out the RAM, stick in a new CPU ...lotsa stuff. One of the obvious things I needed to improve on was the WiFi card; the original card offered up transfer rates at the heady speed of 54Mbs. I think I could improve on that. Enter the AC600 Mini Wireless Network WiFi Dongle. This dongle is not like the tiny little dongles you find that just about disappear in their USB ports. No sir. This is a big dongle. Standing out and proud from the side of my beastly laptop. So why did I choose this impressive dongle? I noticed there were a lot of comments from owners of lesser dongles complaining that, when push got to shove, their teensy dongles, with their "nano technology" ...fried themselves and failed to satisfy. Size matters; I was not about to put anything on my manly Dell that had "nano" in any part of its description. No sir. I wanted effective and big. This dongle is made for the long haul, for the heavy load and to stand strong. Unlike the wimpy "nanos" this dongle is equipped with "cooling ports". Yes, it can go the extra mile, take a lickin' and keep on tickin' and not go limp when it counts because ...it is air cooled. Through the magic of convection, cool air is drawn in through the ten, ample-sized, cooling ports on the bottom of the dongle and hot air escapes through slots integral to the oversize USB male plug. A small LED on top lets you know this dongle is workin' hard. And performance? Night and day different. Don't be caught with "nano technology" on your laptop. Go big, go strong, or go home. Okay, sorry, I couldn't help myself. This is a great device, highly recommend. It comes with a mini CD with the drivers and software ...that's how I installed mine as the Dell has a CD drive. Follow the instructions. My install went without a hitch. Oddly, the software and drivers are Realtek. And while I may have engaged in a little tongue in cheek, the overheating issue seemed to plague a lot of the smaller nano tech dongles reading reviews. This one does have air flow through it to some degree. Not the smallest but it works.; big improvement over the old WiFi card. At 15 bucks a no brainer.

reviews.title: Great Purchase!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on November 10, 2022
reviews.text: Easy install, looks great, super bright, Quality product! Fantastic headlight for the money. The beam is precise and not scattered compared to the OEM headlight and other LED bulb replacements. No one mentioned but the Halo is an important element in most bikes that have the parking light mode. Although the Halo is designated by the lamp’s manufacture exclusively for the DRL (Daylight Running Lights) mode, most bikes have the low and high beam lights running all the time by default. The Halo light runs together with the Hi/Lo beam all the time, but a separate wire (red) is dedicated for the parking light exclusively when turning the ignition switch to parking (on most bikes). Fantastic headlight for the money.

reviews.title: good quality and great at blocking out the light!

reviews.text: I bought these because I get migraines and sometimes just need the darkest room possible. The curtains themselves are fantastic they block out light, however I will need to look at changing how I hang them because light does escape from above because the curtains are not flush with the wall due to my curtain rod. I find the curtains all hang quite nicely together (I have 4 panels) and I can set them up so there is no light that leaks through its one nice solid wall of no light. I think these are fantastic and would definitely recommend them to others. I have included 2 photos, you can see where the light gets in from the top because of my curtain rod I have at the moment, but that also gives you a good idea of how much light these curtains are blocking out because under that is just darkness. First photo is without flash and the second photo is with a camera flash. (the photos were taken just after I unpackaged them and hung them, the wrinkles you see worked themselves out over time and now hang nicely) I don't know if it helps with noise cancellation or energy savings or any of that, but it works perfectly for what I needed it for, which is room darkening.

reviews.title: Looks awesome, sounds good, works for our 4000 square ft home.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States 🇺🇸 on March 29, 2017
reviews.text: Call me crazy, but I installed this in a 4000 square ft home with 4 bathrooms. It is just 3 of us though. So I think I can answer some questions people have in a larger home. I gave this thing 4 stars originally because of the lower power, but then UPDATED moved to 5 stars since it does so well for us. It looks awesome, sounds good, small, light weight. Most people in reviews talk about showers. Well our household take primarily baths. For filling a bathtub, you need to play with the settings. At 48 degree F water here in MI, I found turning water heater down to 1.5 gpm works. I set the temperature at 131 degrees at the water heater. By the time it gets to my huge Jaccuzzi, it goes down to 115 degrees. That is hot, so I was able to add a tiny bit of cold and got a Jaccuzzi tub full at 97 degrees in about 30 minutes. Not too bad. Plus it is hotter and can fill to any higher level than my previous 50 gallon water heater. Next test, a regular small bathtub, but at the far end of my house. The water lines run through the garage ceiling. By the time it gets there, it is at 106 degrees and takes about 10 minutes to fill the tub. This small tub actually was the hardest to get just right. Originally I had the water at 2.4 gpm, and it was fine for the big tub, but terrible for this far smaller tub. This is why I set the flow to 1.5 gpm right at the water heater. I think I will just leave it there, rather then keep having to adjust. Ok, 1.5 gpm is really low and 2 people cannot fill a tub at the same time, but it works for us and you can fill the 2nd tub immediately after. For your closer bathrooms, you can get a bit more gpm by adding some cold water. We had a 50 gallon direct vent gas water heater. This was not perfect either. We could never get more than 1/2 a tub before cold water started coming out. So even though this tankless water heater takes a longer time to fill a tub, it can keep going until it is full. So we just set the timer on the Jaccuzzi to 20 minutes and then come back and check on it. Compromises but the benefits are how efficient it is, how it never runs out of hot water, and since it is lower power, it has to be safer. It is safer than having a tank, that is for sure. Check water heater mythbusters on yout. So I am not necessarily recommending someone with a 4000 square ft house to buy this. Although for a conservative family that has no problem with compromising a little time for filling a tub for efficiency, you can definitely get by. Next test, faucets. You can run 2 faucets at the same time at my settings. I imagine at 2.5 gpm maybe 3 faucets but I do not want to keep changing the flow rate. I really love the touch screen and the looks are nice. Btw plan on a dozen trips to buy pipe parts. I also bought more exhaust vent. The exact same. Basically China makes these vent kits the exact same size so I can extend mine. Under 20 bucks online. Also plan on spending another 300 bucks on pipe parts. This is because you have to get the pipes from where your tank water heater was to where your tankless water heater is. I think it is worth it. It will save $250 a year. Btw, it felt good getting rid of that big bulky and ugly tank water heater. 7/6/2017 Update: I just want to add that as the summer comes, I was able to lower temperature on the water heater to 113 degrees. So in the summer this thing has extra capacity available. I still just leave it at 1.5 gpm. Use of this water heater has become normal for us.

reviews.text: When it worked it was good. I purchased the first one in the USA Idaho. It lasted about 14 or 15 months started leaking water in the heat exchanger and shorted out the control panel. So I bought the exact same one from Amazon, mainly for ease of installation, 14 months later the heat exchanger started leaking and shorted it out. Contacted them about warranty, sent all the information they required pictures, invoice etc( keep in mind this has taken three weeks trying to get answers) on hold on the phone twice for at least 15 mins only to have them hang up. Multiple emails stalling me. Then today they told me no warranty because it’s my fault because of condensation, I’ve had issues with warranties before, but never like this. So my recommendation to any person purchasing a demand tankless water heater, run away from Eccotemp as fast as you can heaters only last over a year and their warranty isn’t worth the paper it is written on. If I had any say at Amazon Eccotemp would no longer be a supplier. I may even close my account at Amazon because of the way I have been treated by Eccotemp. The tech support guy treated me like i was stupid, not professional at all. (I’m a certified auto mechanic for 50 years and a certified auto parts person, so when it comes to hot water heat exchangers I’ve lots of experience, every vehicle has two at least, in all my time I’ve never seen one leak from outside condensation) BUYER BEWARE OF ECCOTEMP PRODUCTS

reviews.title: It works but could be improved
reviews.date: Reviewed in Canada 🇨🇦 on September 24, 2020
reviews.text: I installed this at my off-grid cabin to provide propane-based water heating for dishwashing, and in future, a shower. Given the price, it is an affordable means of adding hot water facilities in an off-grid setting. The fan that comes on when the heater is operating is very loud. Not a huge concern for me but it might be for others. My biggest issue is that the heater will only engage when the water throughput is at least 0.6 gallons per minute. There is no means to adjust this. You therefore cannot run the hot water slowly to do dishes, for example. 0.6 GPM is actually quite a fast flow of tap water and when you are relying on collected rainwater and have limited water storage, you don't want to be running the tap wide open just to wash a few dishes. On the positive side, it works and it is reasonably priced.

reviews.title: Kingston Tub Faucet is a Winner
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 28, 2017
reviews.text: Make certain that the spacing between the faucet holes is correct before you order. There are different sizes. That said this really works great. I had a plumber help with the installation of the shut-offs. He said that Kingston Brass was the best, I'd have to agree. The plumber had to leave so I did the rest of the install myself. The drain pipes have to be cut to fit. I used a tubing cutter and filed the edges after the cut. Where the drain fits under the tub I used 3M scotch-brite sanding pads to remove any scale or rust. I got a "drain insert tightening tool" with 4 prongs from Ace hardware just to install the drain. This is a speciality tool that you will need. The drain has a rubber washer that fits under the tube to provide a flexable seal. I used Locktite #2 Form-a-Gasket to adhere this to the tub. I installed the drain from the bottom and the strainer from the top using the 4 prong drain tool form Ace. I used flexible stainless supply lines (hot and cold) from Home Depot and installed the Kingston faucet with no trouble. Worked the first time with no leaks. It's been 3 months now and no problems yet.

reviews.title: Excellent for small clean-ups in open areas.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 18, 2013
reviews.text: This is a review of the Rubbermaid Commercial FG421588 Galvanized Steel Brushless Mechanical Sweeper, 10.5" Length x 9.5" Width x 44" Height, Black , Model No. 4215--the expensive one. It's worth the extra dough. When I was a kid, we had one of those big old Bissel carpet sweepers, and I've always thought they were an ingenious alternative to the cumbersome, noisy, electricity-consuming vacuum cleaner. Of course, they won't do everything a vacuum will do, but for a lot of clean-ups on bare floors or low-pile carpets they're just what the doctor ordered. I didn't know what to expect of the Rubbermaid sweeper's rubber squeegees, which take the place of the Bissel's (and cheaper Rubbermaid models') rotary brushes, but I've been very happy with them. They seem to pick up dirt, dust, and cat litter quite as well as brushes, if not better; and I imagine they'll also do a good job on wet spills, though I haven't had to test that hypothesis yet. I hesitated to give this sweeper five stars, because it's not much use in close quarters (such as on the bathroom rug in a New York City apartment's tiny bathroom), but I decided it wasn't fair to knock off a star for that, considering how the contraption works. Still, buyers should understand this inherent limitation: *You have to have room to move the entire sweeper head roughly a foot in a straight line, or it can't do its thing.* The rotary squeegees, which are two or three inches behind the leading edges (back and front), have to pass over the dirt while turning, or they can't sweep it up. The little stationary, downward-pointing brushes on the corners are presumably intended to reach dirt along the baseboard, where the squeegees can't go (because those are enclosed by the body of the machine), but they're not very effective. That's not a huge complaint, though. If there's dirt right up against the wall, you can use a broom or hand-brush to sweep it out into the open, where the sweeper can get it. This sweeper isn't meant to replace the vacuum cleaner or the broom altogether--it's just easier to use on the jobs it works on, and it works on a lot of common jobs, particularly little spills, tracked-in dirt, and various messy accidents--as long as they're more-or-less out in the open. And it might very well replace the dust pan. The construction of the sweeper seems good. The materials feel sturdy, and the moving parts operate smoothly, without wobbling, squeaking, or other indications of sloppy manufacture or assembly. I've seen complaints about the handles of other manufacturers' sweepers, which are made up of sections that are supposed to hold together by friction, but reportedly don't stay together very well. This machine's handle is sectional, too, but the sections are threaded and they screw together. (Note that the cheaper Rubbermaid models also have friction-fit handles. I have no idea how well or poorly they stay together. Reports vary.) As long as you're careful not to get the threads crossed, this handle should go together and stay together fine, and it feels very solid, once assembled. (Useful tip: To avoid cross-threading, always turn any threaded parts backwards, as if you were unscrewing them, until you hear or feel the click that means the threads have engaged properly.) The rotary squeegees sweep dirt into trays under the front and rear edges of the sweeper. Transparent ABS plastic covers let you see when the trays are getting full, and when you're ready to empty them, you just hold the sweeper right-side up over the trash can and push down on a little tab at the corner of each dust tray. The tray opens downwards, dumps the dirt into the trash can, and springs shut again. These assemblies feel sturdy, and work smoothly and firmly. The sweeper is about as good-looking as anybody can reasonably expect--an unobtrusive shape, and no garish colors, just basic black (though it looks like yellow trim is available if you like garish). It folds flat for easy storage. It's easy to clean, and the squeegees are less prone than traditional rotary brushes to get hair, thread, etc., wrapped around them, which I consider a big advantage. I can't say how durable the parts are, because I haven't used mine very much yet, but I don't anticipate problems. Note that Rubbermaid considers this a "commercial", not a "home", product, so information about it is to be found on the Rubbermaid Commercial web site, at [...] This isn't the cheapest sweeper on the market, but my advice is always to save up and buy the best quality you can possibly afford. A year from now (unless you're in such bad shape that you shouldn't be shopping on the Web in the first place), you won't miss the extra money you spent; but each and every time you use the thing, you'll appreciate having something that works properly and makes your work easier, rather than harder. I'm glad I spent the extra money for this well-made sweeper, and I'm happy to recommend it.

reviews.title: So far so good...
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 2, 2013
reviews.text: I did a little research and then ordered this item partly based on cost - $36 or so and free shipping from Amazon. I was concerned about the bad reviews but so far (just received it today) I think it does the job. I was also concerned when I received it - I was hoping it would have natural boar bristles but it does not - they are completely nylon. I was worried this would mean it wouldn't generate enough static to pick up dust/debris. We have a (very) low-pile carpet which it seems to pick things up on and it definitely is working on our wood floors (which are most of what we have in our house). I wanted it to be able to keep up with sweeping (without using a broom which ends up kicking up dust and pushing a lot of the dirt into the cracks between our floorboards), the carpet and I wanted to make sure it would pick up kitty litter. It does pick up kitty litter on our wooden floor. Not perfectly - but quickly and much easier than having to pull the vacuum out. ---- UPDATE I just wanted to add - I've had this for a couple of weeks or more now - that this seems to pick up thing that a normal broom doesn't. While a broom might get some more of the fine dust than maybe this gets - this picks up a lot more hair. I am usually using it to pick up little things that I see - crumbs, kitty litter, ext - but when I empty it I am surprised to find it full of hair (both mine and my cats) that I didn't realize was even on the floor. One word of caution - it says to tip the broom upside down to empty it. When inspecting it (with kitty litter inside) - as I tipped the whole thing at an angle what was in side dumped out! (And I wasn't trying to empty it at that point). I found that you can pretty easily open up the trap doors still holding it upright and it seems best if you don't tip the whole thing around too much if you don't want things to spill out. I will do an update if my opinion changes. The nylon bristles are a bummer (I think) but not worth paying for the more costly versions I don't think...

reviews.title: Sweeps Week
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on January 24, 2019
reviews.text: The Dual Action sweeper is fantastic on tile, not so much on carpet. Low pile carpet will be fine. Did a kitty litter test and on tile, the first pass got everything up. For the money though, I think I'd rather have invested in a Fuller. With Fuller you get a smaller cleaning area but this is why they are so good ironically. Although the Dual Action sweeper does a good job, it just doesn't say "quality" to me. The rubber wheels that engage the brushes when pushed back and forth seem a bit cheap and appear as though they will wear quickly. The Dual Action works well both forward and backward equally. The front brush is thicker than the back although this hasn't seem to make a difference in results. The nylon(?) bristles are lightweight (more so than I would've thought) and I would imagine, within due time, they would fray. I will update this review (posted on 01/23/2019) if and when that were to ever happen. The handle is broken down into 4 threaded pieces, which screw on together. I have noticed this is cause for the handle coming loose at times and need of re-tightening. Don't tighten those down to tight as it seems possible the threads will strip. Four stars, it's good if you need something a bit bigger than most. If you want a quality sweeper that will last a long time, get a Fuller.
